# MONTH OF NOVEMBER

Having 30 days.

*November 1: Holy Wonderworkers and Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian of Asia:*

*At Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," stichera of the saints, on 6.*[^6]
*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

Having laid aside all earthly care, and placed their hope in the heavens, the saints laid up for themselves an unstolen treasure. Freely they received, freely they give healing unto those who are ailing. In evangelical manner, they possessed neither gold nor silver; and unto men and beasts alike they imparted benefactions, that having become obedient in all things unto Christ, they may pray with boldness on behalf of our souls.

Although they were disgusted by corruptible things upon the earth, yet like heavenly citizens in the flesh they appeared as angels, companions of one mind: a holy pair of one character and of one soul. Therefore, unto all who suffer they grant healings, freely giving benefactions unto those who are in need; whom let us worthily honor in this yearly feast, as with boldness they pray unto Christ on behalf of our souls.

Having welcomed the entire Trinity to dwell within themselves, the ever-memorable pair, the divinely wise Cosmas and Damian, pour forth streams from the life-bearing source, even the waters of healing. Their very relics heal passions by touch, and their names alone drive afflictions away from men; for all who run to them in Christ they are saving havens, and with boldness they pray on behalf of our souls.

Having rejected all tyrannical passion, and having trampled down every calculation of the wicked serpent *(Fol. 1v)*
in Christ, O holy unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian, you appeared in radiant form, illuminating the whole universe like luminaries, always driving away darkness by divine signs and dispelling diseases by grace, appearing as saviors unto all who with unwavering faith celebrate your glorious memory, O all-wise ones.

*Glory, in Tone 6. By Anatolius:*
Endless is the grace of the saints which they received from Christ! Therefore their relics also unceasingly work wonders by divine power; and their names, when invoked in faith, heal incurable diseases. Through them, O Lord, also deliver us from spiritual and bodily passions, as Thou art the Lover of mankind.

*Both now, Theotokion: "O Theotokos, thou art the true vine..."*
*Or Stavrotheotokion:*
*Podoben: "Having laid aside all" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*
When of old the undefiled ewe-lamb and spotless Lady beheld her own Lamb upon the tree of the Cross, she cried out maternally, and wondering she exclaimed: "O sweetest Child! What is this new and most glorious sight? How has the ungrateful assembly delivered Thee over to the judgment seat of Pilate, and condemned unto death the Life of all? Yet I sing Thy unutterable condescension, O Word!"

*At the Aposticha, of the Octoechos.*
*[Rubric: But where there is a temple of the saints, or if anyone desires to chant the Polyeleos to the saints, then at the Aposticha chant the stichera; and at Matins after the Kathismata, the Sessional Hymns; and the Canon of the Theotokos, and two Canons of the saints, and the Praises, and the Great Doxology.][^7]*
*At the Aposticha, stichera, Tone 2:*
The pool of healings[^8] healed only one person in a year; but the temple of the unmercenaries heals the whole multitude of the ailing, for the wealth of the saints is inexhaustible and unfailing. By their prayers, O Christ, have mercy on us.

*Verse: God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel.*
*By Theophanes:*
Having lived actively in divine love and in yearning for future things, you made straight the saving paths. Therefore, having kept the purity of your souls undefiled, you resisted material things unto the end; and having been gilded by the Divine Spirit, you freely grant healing unto the ailing, O sacred pair, radiant union, enlightened divine couple, unmercenaries, visiting us in afflictions and illnesses, and freely curing the diseases of our souls.

*Verse: Unto the saints who are in His earth (Fol. 2r)*
...the Lord has made all His desires marvelous in them.[^9] *By Germanus:*
Having been accounted worthy of great gifts, O all-praised ones, you lived in a humble manner upon earth; and traveling everywhere, healing freely the passions of the ailing, you appeared as companions of the angels, Cosmas with the wise Damian, fair brethren: heal our passions also by your prayers.

*Glory, in Tone 6:*
Always having Christ working within you, O holy unmercenaries, you work miracles in the world, curing the infirm. For your medicine is an inexhaustible fountain: when drawn from, it overflows all the more; and when poured out, it abounds; emptied daily, it increases; granting unto all and remaining unfailing; and those who draw from it are filled with remedies, while it remains unexhausted. What then shall we call you? Healing physicians of souls and bodies? Healers of incurable passions, freely healing all? Recipients of the gift from the Savior Christ, Who grants unto us great mercy!

*Both now, Theotokion:*
None that runs to thee departs from thee ashamed, O most pure Virgin Theotokos; but he asks for grace, and receives a gift according to his profitable petition.

*Or Stavrotheotokion:*
*Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*
Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, she that bore Thee cried out: "What is this strange mystery that I behold, O my Son? How dost Thou die in the flesh, suspended upon the tree, O Giver of life?"

*Troparion, in Tone 8:*
Holy unmercenaries and wonderworkers, Cosmas and Damian, visit our infirmities: freely you have received, freely give unto us.[^10]

*At Matins, after the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn of the Octoechos; or of the saints, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Having acquired a life well-pleasing unto God in the world, O richly radiant ones, you grant the joy of healing unto us who receive it, honorably having learned the curing of wounds for the saints; for you appeared as glorious physicians of the sick, with Christ cooperating with you, O Cosmas and Damian, holy unmercenaries.
*Twice.*

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
We hymn thee, O Bride of God, Mother of Christ God, glorifying thy incomprehensible childbirth, through which we were delivered from the deceit of the devil and from all afflictions, O Lady Theotokos, and in faith we cry out:

*(Fol. 2v)*
"Have mercy upon thy flock, O only all-hymned one!"

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "What was commanded mysteriously" (Повелѣ́нное та́йнѡ):*
Performing wonders from unmercenary treasures of most pure graceful gifts, you appeared divinely in zeal, having received heavenly wealth and left behind earthly glory. Therefore we offer a hymn unto the Creator of all, Who granted unto you the grace of healings.
*Twice.*

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
Having given birth unto the immutable God, O good Lady, strengthen my heart which is ever altered by sin, through thy maternal prayers, that I also may cry unto thee, O Theotokos Mary: "Have mercy upon thy flock, which thou hast acquired, O all-immaculate one!"

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
You appeared unto all as givers of healings and wonderworkers, and light-bearing lamps of miracles, through spiritual grace; for by faith you cool the flame of passions, and you warm the understanding of the faithful therein. Therefore, having acquired your divine church as a medicine for souls, running thereto we cry out: "O God-bearing unmercenaries, entreat Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate your holy memory with love!"
*Twice.*

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
As a Virgin and unique among women, who without seed gave birth in the flesh unto God, all generations of mankind call thee blessed; for the fire of the Godhead dwelt within thee, and as an infant thou nourishest with milk the Creator and Lord. Therefore, angelic and human kind worthily glorifies thy most holy childbirth, and with one accord we cry unto thee: "Entreat Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who venerate thy most holy childbirth in faith!"

*The Gradual Hymns, the 1st Antiphon of the 4th Tone.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
*Unto the saints who are in His earth, the Lord has made all His desires marvelous in them.*
*Verse: I beheld the Lord ever before me...*
*Let every breath.*
*Gospel according to Mark, pericope 23.[^11]*
*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 2:*
Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity in the Holy Spirit,[^12] as the divine forefather David said: with unfeigned love, and unwavering faith, and true word, like golden fringes, each to the other *(Fol. 3r)*
clinging to one another: Come now, let us bless the Lord, Who has given unto us His holy unmercenaries, Cosmas and Damian: physicians of the sick, luminaries unto those in darkness, expellers of demons. Through them the sick are healed, through them the dead are raised, through them lepers are cleansed, according to the voice of the Lord: "Freely you have received, freely give healing unto the sick." By their prayers, O Christ God, enlighten our souls!

*Both Canons of the Octoechos, without the Hymns to the Martyrs;*
*And the Canon of the saints, on 6.*
*[Rubric: But where there is a temple, the Canon of the Theotokos with the Heirmos, on 6; and both Canons of the saints, on 8.][^13]*

*Canon 1, whose acrostic is:*
*"It is fitting for earthly ones to hymn the glorious physicians."[^14] Tone 6.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
When Israel traversed the deep on foot as upon dry land, beholding the pursuer Pharaoh engulfed, he cried aloud: "Let us sing a song of victory unto God!"

*Troparion:*
Illumined by divine glory, O divinely radiant unmercenaries, illumine our souls, dispelling the darkness of passion, that in faith we may honor you.

*Troparion:*
Having first refrained from corruptive passions by the transformation of diseases, O wise ones, you alleviate our grievous illnesses, and relieve bodily and spiritual sicknesses.

*Troparion:*
From the Master of all you received the gift of miracles, O holy ones: heal our many and incurable passions of the flesh, we pray.

*Troparion:*
Offer supplication unto God, O unmercenaries and physicians, that He may deliver us from many temptations and afflictions, and from the trembling and dreadful torment of that time.

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth contrary to the laws of nature, O pure one, unto the Lawgiver Jesus the Deliverer: entreat Him, O Theotokos, to deliver us from our many iniquities.

*Canon 2, whose acrostic is:*
*"With hymns I honor the wise unmercenaries."[^15]*
*The composition of John Damascene.*
*Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us, all people, sing a song of victory unto Him Who delivered Israel from the bitter bondage of Pharaoh, and guided them dry-shod through the depth of the sea, for He has been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Illumined by the grace of the primal Trinity, the marvelous and honorable pair freely grants healings unto all who approach in faith, *(Fol. 3v)*
ever pouring forth streams.

*Troparion:*
Mystically instructed in the life-bearing words, shining forth in the world like luminaries, you easily dispel the gloom of passions by the warmth of faith, O all-blessed ones.

*Troparion:*
Submitting unto the law of the Savior, O all-glorious ones, you rejected carnal voluptuousness; and illuminating your souls most radiantly with virtues, you excelled in the world, O right-marvelous ones.

*Theotokion:*
He Who dwelt within thy womb, O Mother of God, ineffably clothed Himself in all mankind: the transcendent Son Who shone forth agelessly from the Father; unto Him let us sing, for He has been glorified!

*Ode 3, Canon 1. Heirmos:*
There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established us upon the rock of Thy confession.[^16]

*Troparion:*
The world ever hymns your many benefactions, O holy ones, and the multitude of your miracles: wonderworkers and physicians, peers of all the angels!

*Troparion:*
We pray unto you both, O light-givers, stars mystically set on the height of the Church, Cosmas and Damian: illumine the hearts of the faithful!

*Troparion:*
Ever pouring forth drops of healing, O holy ones, wash away the defilement of soul from all, and stop all the torrents of the passionate flesh.

*Troparion:*
Lo, the people have gathered from everywhere, O holy ones, within your church to hymn your great gifts: fulfill therefore the supplications of all!

*Theotokion:*
O holy and pure Theotokos, who didst give flesh unto the most holy Word by a word: deliver me from irrational passions, O all-immaculate one, as in piety I hymn thee with divine words.

*Canon 2. Heirmos:*
Establish me, O Christ, upon the immovable rock of Thy commandments, and enlighten me with the light of Thy countenance; for there is none holy above Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Let us all worthily hymn the fountains of healings, the streams of divine gifts, the most radiant receptacles of immaterial light!

*Troparion:*
Healing both bodily and spiritual passions and diseases of those who come unto you, O all-honorable ones, you now heal them zealously as benefactors.

*Troparion:*
Adorned with fruitful virtues, you manifestly cast aside all corruptible worldly sweetness, unceasingly looking toward the beauty of God.

*Theotokion (Fol. 4r)*
*Theotokion:*
In our likeness He Who was formerly invisible appeared from thee, O Parent of God! Having united Himself unto flesh, the Godhead joined Himself within thy womb, O Bride of God!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Having divinely drawn streams of miracles from the abyss of the fountain of Jesus, O holy ones, by mystical showers you drive away the dark clouds of passions, and grant healings unto ailing men. Therefore, having obtained sound rejoicing through you, O most glorious ones, in wonder we cry: "O God-bearing unmercenaries, entreat Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate your holy memory with love!"
*Twice.*

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
As the all-immaculate bride of the Creator, as the unwedded Mother of the Deliverer, as the receptacle of the Comforter, O all-hymned one: hasten to deliver me from their wickedness, seeing that I have become a defiled dwelling for iniquity and a plaything for demons in my understanding; and make me a radiant dwelling of virtues, O light-bearing and incorrupt Lady: drive away the cloud of passions, and account me worthy of communion with the Most High and of the unwaning light, through thy prayers!

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding upon the Cross the Lamb, Shepherd, and Deliverer, the ewe-lamb cried out weeping, and bitterly lamenting she exclaimed: "The world indeed rejoices, receiving deliverance through Thee; but my maternal heart burns, beholding Thy Crucifixion, which Thou endurest for the tender mercy of compassion, O longsuffering Lord, abyss of mercy, and inexhaustible fountain: take pity, and grant remission of transgressions unto those who hymn Thy divine Passion in faith!"

*Ode 4, Canon 1. Heirmos:*
Christ is my power, God and Lord, the honorable Church divinely sings, crying out with a pure mind, feasting in the Lord![^17]

*Troparion:*
Truly fruitful is the divine branch of the divine vine: let us bless the wise unmercenaries, who distil mystical wine in gladness.

*Troparion:*
You appeared as a weapon distressing invisible enemies: deliver us also from their arrows, defending our life, O wise unmercenaries.

*Troparion:*
There is no man who has not acquired you as good intercessors before Christ, O holy unmercenaries: entreat Him to deliver us from eternal fire.

*(Fol. 4v)*
Whosoever calls upon you, O blessed ones, is delivered from all distress both on land and at sea: therefore deliver us from the surrounding assault of the adversary!

*Theotokion:*
Having taken up His abode within thee, O pure one, the Lord reveals thee, His holy dwelling-place, as a fountain of many healings and a cleansing of passions, O Theotokos ever-virgin.

*Canon 2. Heirmos:*
I understood Thy dispensation, O Almighty One, and with fear I glorified Thee, O Savior.[^18]

*Troparion:*
Manifestly following the divine saying,[^19] O godly ones, you acquired neither the brilliance of gold nor silver.

*Troparion:*
Shining with divine miracles, the unmercenaries bestow benefactions upon all, imparting grace.

*Troparion:*
You appeared as wise physicians for the diseases of passions, stretching forth healing hands.

*Theotokion:*
Let the faces of those who do not confess thee to be the Theotokos now be smitten on the cheek, O most pure Lady![^20]

*Ode 5, Canon 1. Heirmos:*
By Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine, I pray Thee, with love the souls of those who awake early unto Thee, that they may know Thee, O Word of God, as the true God, Who calls them from the gloom of sin.[^21]

*Troparion:*
They drew unto themselves divine enlightenment, whole-heartedly having loved the fountain of radiance, and with the beams of their miracles the renowned ones ever enlighten us.

*Troparion:*
A strong pair, O wise holy ones, having tilled the furrows of souls with divine signs continually, reaping passions like weeds, while health brought forth fruit an hundredfold like an ear of corn.

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by the might of Christ, you destroyed all the power of him who was strong in malice: deliver us from his tyranny, O unmercenaries, our vigilant protectors.

*Troparion:*
Strengthen us, O holy ones, to walk the upright paths and to do the will of God, calming the passions of our hearts and relieving the ailments of our bodies.

*Theotokion:*
Deliver me, O good Lady, from the temptations of the enemy, and from the torment of Gehenna, and from the captivity that holds me fast; and put me not to shame, who sing praises unto thee.

*Canon 2. Heirmos:*
Rising at dawn from the night, we hymn Thee, O Christ, co-beginningless with the Father, and Savior of our souls: grant peace unto the world, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Like divinely flowing torrents, you pour forth benefactions unto the faithful, *(Fol. 5r)*

the waters of action; healing together diseases of both soul and body: O glorious unmercenaries!

*Troparion:*
Having opened the fountain of grace, O honorable unmercenaries, you distribute health unto all who now run to you with faith and love.

*Troparion:*
As radiant and all-wise stars that have manifestly made earth like heaven in the likeness of angelic brightness, they unceasingly illumine us.

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast been revealed as higher than all, O Virgin Mother, having conceived the Creator of all, Who is co-beginningless with the Father, and having given birth unto the Savior and Lord of the world.

*Ode 6, Canon 1. Heirmos:*
Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, and fleeing to Thy calm haven, I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O greatly Merciful One![^22]

*Troparion:*
Living joyfully in the heavens, O martyrs, hasten to come into your honorable temple, and heal our bodily infirmities and the passions of our hearts.

*Troparion:*
Having been beautifully clothed in divine splendor as in a double garment, O holy ones: divinely clothe us who are naked of virtues, and now strip us of the dishonor of passions.

*Troparion:*
As you are ever clothed with the adornment of miracles, you appeared as saviors unto the world: deliver us all therefore from worldly harm, O holy ones, and from the passions of impiety and torment.

*Troparion:*
Having put to death all the death-bearing passions of the flesh by grace, O holy ones, through life-creating applications of miracles you bring to life those who suffer, and deliver them from the gates of death.

*Theotokion:*
Jesus, being Fire, came forth from thee in the flesh without burning thy womb: pray Him, O pure one, to deliver from fire and every torment those who hymn thee in faith.

*Canon 2. Heirmos:*
Thou didst save the Prophet from the sea monster, O Lover of mankind: lead me up also from the depth of transgressions, I pray Thee![^23]

*Troparion:*
Let us zealously honor the divine Cosmas and Damian, the God-wise benefactors and healers of saving things.

*Troparion:*
Having preserved chastity and being adorned with understanding, the divine Cosmas and Damian rejoice with Christ.

*Troparion:*
Having lived in like-mindedness and fasted with one soul, you were together entrusted to give healings unto us.

*Theotokion:*
Having in the flesh given birth unto the unapproachable Light, O most pure one, Who enlightens the whole *(Fol. 5v)*

world with the beams of the Godhead.

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "The firm" (Тве́рдыѧ):*
Having received the grace of healings, you extend health unto those in need, O physicians and most glorious wonderworkers; but by your visitation cast down the audacity of enemies, healing the world by miracles.[^24]

*Ikos:*
The word of the wise physicians surpasses all understanding and wisdom, and they impart knowledge unto all; for having received the grace of the Most High, they invisibly bestow health upon all. Therefore grace has also been granted unto me to recount in song how, as God-bearing pleasers and ministers of Christ, they grant a multitude of healings; for they deliver from all diseases, healing the world by miracles.

*Ode 7, Canon 1. Heirmos:*
The Angel made the furnace bedewing for the venerable youths, while the command of God burning the Chaldeans persuaded the tyrant to cry out: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^25]

*Troparion:*
You gave wings to your mind toward the heavens through the addition of good deeds, and became partakers of divine gifts: being winged eagles, you traverse the whole earth, continually working miracles.

*Troparion:*
You shone like fine gold, O unmercenaries, by the divine grace of healings, enriching multitudes. Therefore show mercy unto us who are held fast by temptations of grievous assaults.

*Troparion:*
Having committed your pure spirits unto the Lord, O unmercenaries, you received from Him the gift ever to drive away unclean spirits: from whose bitter malice deliver all of us.

*Troparion:*
You fell asleep righteously in the appointed sleep, O wise unmercenaries, and are sleepless intercessors on behalf of the faithful. Therefore continually lull to sleep the grievous passions of our souls and bodies.

*Theotokion:*
Pray unceasingly unto God our Lover of mankind, O all-spotless one, that we may receive utter forgiveness of evil deeds, and obtain in the heavens the good things prepared for those that love Him.

*Canon 2. Heirmos:*
We the faithful perceive thee to be a spiritual furnace, O Theotokos; for as the Supremely Exalted One saved the three youths, so He wholly renewed the world in thy womb: the praised and supremely glorified God of our fathers![^26]

*Troparion:*
You were revealed, all of you, as receptacles of God; for you left the whole world for God's sake, divinely following the footsteps of the Savior, *(Fol. 6r)*

O all-glorious ones, honoring the God of our fathers.

*Troparion:*
Supernaturally, O most excellent physicians, you heal all the wounds of the infirm with mystical operations of your hands, drawing saving remedies from divine treasures, and singing of the most glorious God.

*Troparion:*
With the crown of Thy kingdom, O Master, and with a radiant purple robe Thou hast splendidly adorned those who exceedingly loved the incomprehensible loveliness of Thy beauty, O Christ, and hast shown them unto the faithful as common benefactors.

*Theotokion:*
Unto the Orient from on high[^27] that appeared upon the earth, O most pure one, thou hast been revealed as a splendid and all-radiant door, illumining the world with beams of purity, and continually sending forth beams of miracles unto the faithful.

*Ode 8, Canon 1. Heirmos:*
From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew for the venerable youths, and by water didst burn the sacrifice of the righteous one; for Thou dost all things, O Christ, only by willing them: Thee do we supremely exalt unto all ages![^28]

*Troparion:*
Being warriors against every kind of disease by the aid of the Holy Divine Spirit, O holy ones: soothe the sicknesses of our souls, and relieve the pains of our bodies.

*Troparion:*
Being now truly beholders of the beauty of the Lord, visit this beautiful, God-bearing temple of yours, and make it a fountain of many miracles.

*Troparion:*
Flowing forth like two rivers from the fountain of Paradise, you water the whole face of the earth with streams of healings, drying up clouds of diseases.

*Troparion:*
Having received blessed hope, you are worthily called blessed by all; for as blessed accomplishers of the divine desires of our God, you appeared, O unmercenaries.

*Troparion:*
O unmercenaries, physicians of incurable passions: heal our incurable passions, soothe the tempest of temptations, and disperse the clouds of despondency.

*Theotokion [Triadikon]:*
With the holy angels let us hymn the Father, and the Word, and the Holy Spirit: one Godhead in three Hypostases, one Kingdom, and one Dominion.[^29]

*Canon 2. Heirmos:*
In the furnace the children of Israel, as in a crucible, shone more brightly than gold with the beauty of piety, saying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing ye of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^30]

*(Fol. 6v)*

*Troparion:*
Having died to the beautiful things of this world, and cut off the disease of the love of money, you were named by all as unmercenaries, O wise ones, crying out: Sing ye of all the works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Manifestly you became partakers of eternal life; for you left all the beautiful things of corruptible life, crying out in harmony: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing ye, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Deliver all from grievous diseases, O Master Christ, by the prayers of the unmercenaries, and vouchsafe us ever to cry unto Thee in harmony: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing ye, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
Rejoicing, all we faithful, and being strengthened by grace, who through thy childbirth were delivered, O pure Virgin Mother, unceasingly cry out: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing ye, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9, Canon 1. Heirmos:*
It is not possible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-pure one, the Word incarnate was revealed unto men, Whom magnifying with the heavenly hosts, we call thee blessed.[^31]

*Troparion:*
This temple of yours is most splendidly adorned with miracles as with bright stars, and rejoicing in harmony it ever calls you blessed and piously celebrates your honorable memory, O honorable unmercenaries.

*Troparion:*
Like light, like two great suns, you adorn the spiritual firmament, O unmercenaries, and with the rays of signs you enlighten the hearts of all the faithful. Therefore we cry aloud: Dispel the darkness of our passions, we pray you!

*Troparion:*
Being settled in the heavenly mansions, O holy ones, have mercy invisibly to be in the midst of us who in the midst of your divine temple send up songs unto the Almighty, and who diligently call you blessed, O all-praised ones.

*Troparion:*
Earth rejoices with the heavenly hosts on your radiant divine feast, O holy ones: deliver us who celebrate it from darkness, diseases, and every constraint, and from grievous torment in Hades, O wise ones.

*Theotokion:*
Having a terrifying childbirth, O all-pure one, I pray thee: in the fearful day of trial deliver me from the dreadful reckoning, and make me a partaker of the standing of the saved, who faithfully sing of thee, O full of God's grace!

*Canon 2. Heirmos:*
Thee, the radiant candle *(Fol. 7r)*

and Mother of God, the most marvelous glory, and higher than all creatures, in hymns do we magnify.[^32]

*Troparion:*
In hymns we unceasingly call blessed the wise pair of the noetic Light, flashing forth the dawn and imparting enlightenment unto all.

*Troparion:*
Working the strength of spiritual health for the faithful, you heal bodily passions entrusted unto you as saviors: therefore also you are continually praised in song.

*Troparion:*
As most radiant luminaries, spiritually pouring forth light in the sky of the honorable Church, now imparting light, they unceasingly illumine us.

*Troparion:*
Praised by the Honorable Trinity, the divinely called pair pours forth gifts of healings unto all that ask, who in love call them blessed.

*Theotokion:*
Thee, the cloud of light, the holy ark, and the all-radiant door of the noetic Sun: as the Theotokos do we magnify in hymns.

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во ст҃или́щи):*
Having received the grace of healings from God, O blessed unmercenaries, to heal the infirm and cure all who faithfully flee unto your divine temple: therefore in harmony do we worthily call blessed your honorable memory.[^33]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst give birth, O all-pure one, unto God the Word of God, Who accomplished the saving, excellent dispensation for the whole world. Therefore all of us worthily hymn thee, as thou prayest unto Him that we may be delivered from diseases and all afflictions.

*At the Praises, stichera on 4.*
*Tone 4. By Anatolius:*
Having received the grace of healings from God, freely and warmly do you heal the passions of our souls and bodies, O universal unmercenaries: therefore Christ granted health unto the faithful through you, having revealed you unto the universe as unerring luminaries. Entreat Him that our souls may be saved![^34]

*Tone 4:*
Having drawn an abyss of healings from the Providence on high, you pour forth healings unto all the faithful, O unmercenaries; for supernaturally, through mystical operations of your hands, offering saving remedies from the treasures of the Spirit for the passions of the ailing, you heal those who suffer. Therefore, having become an honorable temple of the Life-Originating Trinity, for in you It manifestly made Its dwelling: pray to It that our souls may be saved!

*(Fol. 7v)*

*Tone 2. By Germanus:*
The choir of the saints rejoices unto ages, for they inherited the Heavenly Kingdom: the earth, having received their relics, breathed forth a sweet fragrance; they were servants of Christ, having settled into eternal life.

*Tone 2:*
Physicians of the infirm, treasures of healings, saviors of the faithful, O all-glorious unmercenaries: heal those in need who cry out and are ailing, entreating the Good God together with Theodota,[^35] that we may be delivered from the snares of the enemy.

*Glory, in Tone 4. By Theophanes:*
Having the fountain of healings, O holy unmercenaries, you bestow healings upon all in need, having been accounted worthy of greatest gifts from the ever-flowing fountain of Christ the Savior. For the Lord said unto you, as unto equal-zealots of the Apostles: "Behold, I have given you authority over unclean spirits, so as to cast them out, and to heal every disease and every infirmity."[^36] Therefore, having lived well in His commandments: freely you received, freely you give, curing the passions of our souls and bodies.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "As one noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
Rejoice, refuge and confirmation of Christians! Rejoice, heavenly ladder! Rejoice, treasure of virginity! Rejoice, O Theotokos, noetic ark of divine glory! Rejoice, boast and confirmation of the whole world, recall of the fallen, all-radiant tabernacle, holy and all-beautiful!

*Stavrotheotokion:*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "As one noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
Beholding Christ, the Lover of mankind, being crucified, and His side pierced with a spear, the all-pure one weeping cried aloud: "What is this, O my Son? What have the ungrateful people rendered unto Thee for the good things that Thou didst for them? And dost Thou hasten to leave me childless, O most dearly beloved? I marvel, O Compassionate One, at Thy voluntary crucifixion!"

*[Rubric: But if there be the Great Doxology, then at the Praises append also these two stichera, that there may be 6. But if not, at the Aposticha of the Octoechos.]*
*Then the verse: Behold now, what is so good or what is so pleasant as for brethren to dwell together in unity?[^37]*
*Tone 6:*
The bright and enlightened memory of the unmercenaries of Christ has shone forth today, brightly illuminating the world with the rays of miracles throughout all the earth. Come then, O feast-lovers, let us faithfully keep festival; come, let us all zealously run to the relics *(Fol. 8r)*

of the saints, that we may abundantly receive swift healing from them; for freely unto all they impart the gifts of healings by the operation of the Holy Spirit.

*Glory, in Tone 8:*
Who will not marvel? Who will not glorify? Who will not faithfully sing of the wonders of the wise and all-glorious unmercenaries? For even after their holy departure, they richly grant healings unto all who flee to them in faith; and their honorable and holy relics pour forth the grace of healings. O holy pair! O honorable heads! O wisdom and glory of the grace granted unto you by God! Therefore in hymns we cry unto God our Benefactor, Who revealed them for the healing of our souls and bodies.

*Both now, Theotokion: "Receive into the haven..."*
*Or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy martyrs, O Lord" (Мꙋ́ченицы твоѝ):*
"I cannot bear, O Child, to see Thee asleep upon the Tree, Who bestowest wakefulness upon all, that Thou mightest grant divine and saving vigilance unto those who of old fell asleep in the sleep of perdition through the fruit of transgression!" the Virgin weeping said, whom we magnify.

*At the Liturgy.*
*The Beatitudes of the Octoechos, on 4; and of the canon of the saints, Ode 3.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
*Unto the saints who are in His earth, the Lord has made all His desires marvelous in them.[^38]*
*Verse: I foresaw the Lord always before me, for He is at my right hand, that I should not be moved.[^39]*
*Epistle: To the Corinthians, pericope 153.[^40]*
*Alleluia, Tone 2: Behold now, what is so good or what is so pleasant, as for brethren to dwell together in unity?[^41]*

*(Woodcut headpiece: Foliage cartouche)*

*On the same month, the 2nd day: The Holy Martyrs Acindynus, Pegasius, Aphthonius, Elpidephorus, and Anempodistus:*[^44]
*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*

Let us hymn the fivefold choir of martyrs: the wise Acindynus, Pegasius, Elpidephorus, Aphthonius, and Anempodistus, valiant sufferers and fervent defenders, who pour forth unhindered grace, and grant unslothful hope safely unto the pious.

Neither famine nor affliction, neither life nor death, neither the boiling of cauldrons nor chasms in the earth, nor the mouths of wild beasts were able to separate your patient-minded valiant deeds from the love of Christ;[^45] for looking unceasingly unto Him, and desiring Him alone, you conquered the adversaries.

Being filled with sweetness and replenished with light, having inherited eternal life: deliver from afflictions those who flee unto you, and from bonds and prison in the place of affliction, O God-wise ones, having boldness toward God and showing compassion, as true imitators of Christ.

*Glory, in Tone 6:*
Today the five-rayed choir of martyrs, shining forth unto the faithful like a constellation of luminous stars, calls us unto mystical gladness. Today the ministers of the spiritual Sun and destroyers of Persian traditions guided unto piety those who honored the sensible sun and worshipped fire. Having abundantly drawn from their passion-bearing chalice, and been crowned by the blood poured out for Christ's sake, they call upon us, lovers of piety, saying: "Come, feast upon our struggles, and behold our crowns and honors! For he that endures unto the end shall be saved,[^46] as Christ the Truth declared, that you may become partakers of our crowns, and have us as intercessors before the Lord!"

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion:*
*Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*

*(Fol. 9r)*

"The most lawless people unjustly nailing Thee to the Tree!" beholding Thee, the Virgin and Thy pure Mother, as Symeon foretold, was wounded in her heart, O Savior![^47]

*At the Aposticha, of the Octoechos.*
*And the sticheron of the saints, Tone 4:*
*Verse: God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel.[^48]*
The five-rayed beams of the martyrs have shone forth, equal in number to the decades: for beholding their images we are illumined, partaking of their memory. Therefore by their prayers, O Christ God, safely deliver our souls from enemies; and by their supplications preserve our life unexhausted, as Thou continually pourest forth Thy rich mercies upon those who unceasingly glorify Thee; and unto those who have hope in Thee, by their prayers grant great mercy unto our souls.

*Glory, in Tone 2. Idiomelon:*
Come, let us rejoice in the Lord on the memory of the passion-bearers, O lovers of feasts! Come, let us praise them, mystically singing their praises: Rejoice, Acindynus! Rejoice, Pegasius! Rejoice, Anempodistus! Rejoice, Elpidephorus! Rejoice, Aphthonius! who plunged idolatrous delusion into the abyss, and clearly proclaimed Christ the Lord in the midst of the stadium: therefore, O all-blessed and much-suffering ones, unceasingly pray on behalf of our souls!

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion:*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
Beholding Thee, O Jesus, nailed to the tree of the Cross, the unwedded Maiden weeping said: "O sweetest Child, why hast Thou left me alone who bore Thee, O unapproachable Light of the Father before all eternity? Hasten and be glorified, that they who glorify Thy divine passions may receive divine glory!"

*Troparion, in Tone 2:*
O passion-bearers of the Lord, blessed is the earth that was drenched with your blood, and holy are the dwellings that received your bodies; for in the stadium you conquered the enemy, and with boldness proclaimed Christ: entreat Him as good, we pray you, that our souls may be saved![^49]

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos; and of the saints, on 4.*
*The acrostic whereof is: "By the supplications of Thy multitude of martyrs, cover me."*[^50]
*By Theophanes. Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
I shall open my mouth, and it will be filled with the Spirit, and I shall utter a word unto the Queen Mother, and I shall be seen radiantly *(Fol. 9v)*

keeping festival, and rejoicing I shall sing of her wonders.[^51]

*Troparion:*
Having the never-setting Sun of Righteousness,[^52] Christ our God, Who enlightens you with immaterial light, O holy ones: disperse the clouds of my ignorance.

*Troparion:*
Safely and without hindrance pouring forth grace, O holy ones, you grant it unto those who come in faith, calming every affliction, every despondency, tempest, and turmoil.

*Troparion:*
Having girded yourselves with invincible strength, O holy ones, you took no thought for bodily weaknesses; but manifesting a fearless disposition, you boldly went forth unto fire and torment.

*Theotokion:*
Thou alone, O Bride of God, didst bear in the flesh Him Who sits on the shoulders in the highest; for from all ages thou wast revealed as a worthy receptacle of the Almighty.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Not in wisdom, nor in power, nor in riches do we boast, but in Thee, the hypostatic Wisdom of the Father, O Christ; for there is none holy save Thee, O Lover of mankind![^53]

*Troparion:*
Being strengthened by the power of Christ, O most excellent ones, with a steadfast resolve, suffering through fire and water you passed over unto heavenly realms.[^54]

*Troparion:*
Being established by the unbreakable hope of future things, with a most courageous mind, O all-glorious martyrs, you disregarded present afflictions.

*Troparion:*
Being of like mind with the three youths, O all-praised ones, you appeared extinguishing the fire of Persian madness, being bedewed with the dew of the Spirit.[^55]

*Theotokion:*
Having acquired thee as a sure protectress, O Mother of God, placing our hopes upon thee we are saved, and fleeing unto thee we are preserved.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Safely in their struggle did the glorious ones run the race of piety, suffering in hope, strengthened by crowns; for having destroyed the adversaries unto the end, they accomplished their unhindered victory. Therefore they ever abundantly pour forth a multitude of healings unto those who ask in faith, unto whom let us cry out in harmony: Pray unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who in love honor your holy memory![^56]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
As the Virgin and only one among women who without seed gave birth unto God in the flesh, all generations of men call thee blessed; for the fire of the Godhead took up Its abode within thee, and as *(Fol. 10r)*

and as an infant thou nursest the Creator and Lord. Therefore, angelic and human kind, worthily we glorify thy most holy giving of birth, and with one accord cry unto thee: Pray unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who with faith bow down before thy most holy birthgiving!

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding the Lamb and Shepherd and Deliverer upon the Cross, the Ewe-lamb weeping exclaimed, and bitterly lamenting cried aloud: "The world indeed rejoices, receiving deliverance through Thee; but my womb burns within me, beholding Thy crucifixion, which Thou endurest for the tender mercy of Thy lovingkindness, O longsuffering Lord! O Abyss of mercy and inexhaustible Fountain: have compassion, and grant remission of sins unto those who in faith hymn Thy divine passions!"[^57]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Sitting in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, on a swift cloud came Jesus the Supremely Divine, and with an incorruptible palm saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ![^58]

*Troparion:*
Enlightened by the beauty of most noble suffering, you appeared as radiant luminaries, O martyrs of Christ, illuminating with most radiant beams those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

*Troparion:*
The blood of the martyrs became a purification, and truly a most sweet-smelling offering unto God, granting without hindrance and pouring forth unto all an unfailing fountain of healings.

*Troparion:*
By your prayers which are directed unto Christ, you turned away the assault of various temptations and perils from those who zealously celebrate your all-sacred and all-festal memory, O richly marvelous ones.

*Troparion:*
Having cast down the godlessness of the deception of idols, manifesting by deeds the life-creating operation of the God of all, you cried, O most blessed ones: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

*Theotokion:*
We set thee forward as a most mighty weapon against enemies; we cast off the harm of every affliction and grievous assault, and we escape the turmoil of heretics, O Mother of God.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
The ungodly shall not behold Thy glory, O Christ; but we, waking early out of the night, hymn Thee, O Only-begotten One, the Radiance of the Father's glory of the Godhead, O Lover of mankind![^59]

*Troparion:*
Thou drewest even thyself unto Christ, O Aphthonius, having valiantly rebuked the godless malice of the tormentor, O glorious one, and thou rannest rejoicing unto the light of faith.

*(Fol. 10v)*

*Troparion:*
Emulating the passion of Christ, O Aphthonius, for His sake thy head was nobly severed; for thou didst hasten unto unchanging joy and an immortal resting place.

*Troparion:*
Established upon immovable hope, and having spat upon the beautiful things upon earth, O all-wise Elpidephorus: unwaveringly didst thou traverse the stadium of suffering.

*Theotokion:*
Having shone forth from thee, the Noetic Sun extended the radiant rays of His Godhead unto all, O Lady Theotokos. Therefore we all glorify thee.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
"I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord," the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood which for mercy's sake flowed from Thy side.[^60]

*Troparion:*
Having despised corruptible passing things, you were accounted worthy to behold incorruptible things. Deliver therefore from temptations and perils those who call upon you in faith, O all-praised ones!

*Troparion:*
O most glorious martyrs, by your supplications incline the Unoriginate Trinity to show compassion, so as to release those who are grievously bound and unceasingly kept in prisons!

*Troparion:*
Having delivered themselves up unto death for Thy sake, O my Savior, the valiant ones obtained immortality, and became deliverers of those who are in afflictions, temptations, and sorrows.

*Theotokion:*
Tear up the handwriting of my transgressions,[^61] O Maiden, granting release from the sorrows and passions that hold me fast, and ever preserving me unharmed, O good one!

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "The firm" (Тве́рдыѧ):*
The pious and God-bearing martyrs, who left all things upon earth, Thou hast received into the enjoyment of Thy good things and rest: Acindynus, Pegasius, Anempodistus, and with them Aphthonius and Elpidephorus, O Thou Who alone art Supremely Good![^62]

*Ikos:*
Open Thou my lips, O my Christ, that I may hymn and praise the honorable contests of Thy passion-bearers, O Lord! For having left all things, and having loved Thee, the Creator of all, they counted all things upon earth as corruptible; and having thus made the honorable sign of Thy life-creating Cross, the valiant martyrs zealously stood before the king as armed soldiers, crying unto Thee: O Thou Who alone art Supremely Good!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Thou Who savedst Thy Abrahamic youths in the fire and slewest the Chaldeans, whom justice righteously ensnared: O supremely praised Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^63]

*(Fol. 11r)*

*Troparion:*
As Thou didst deliver the three pious youths from the flame, even so now Thou hast preserved the sufferers in the fiery furnace, as they cry unto Thee in God-wise manner: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Thou givest abundant gifts, and pourest forth the working of wonders through Thy passion-bearers, O Christ, working and cooperating as Compassionate, and revealing unto those who sing unto Thee: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
A multitude of martyrs, truly united by faith, you were brought unto Christ, working the manifestation of most glorious wonders, and singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Delivered through thee from the ancestral curse and having passed over unto everlasting delight, we cry unto thee: Rejoice, O supremely glorified Theotokos, who hast given birth unto God incarnate for our sake!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The birthgiving of the Theotokos saved the pious youths in the furnace: then prefigured, but now fulfilled, it raises up the whole inhabited earth to sing unto Thee: Hymn the Lord, O ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^64]

*Troparion:*
The most pious festival of the martyrs has come joyfully; illuminating the world, it made all glad, and brightly adorns those who sing in faith: Hymn the Lord, O ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto ages!

*Troparion:*
Against wild beasts and pits and grievous torments you dared, O most noble ones, having the Lord of glory as an invincible helper, unto Whom we now cry: Hymn the Lord, O ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto ages!

*Troparion:*
Having you as a strong rampart, O sufferers Acindynus, Pegasius, and Anempodistus, and again Aphthonius, and ever-memorable Elpidephorus, we sing of the Lord and supremely exalt Him unto ages!

*Troparion:*
Adorned with the crown of victory and shining with the diadem of beauty, you received at last the never-setting radiance in the heavens, O blessed martyrs, crying: Hymn the Lord, O ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto ages!

*Theotokion:*
With lips and mind professing thee as Theotokos, we hymn thee in song, O all-immaculate one; for thou, O most pure one, didst bring forth in the flesh the Creator and God and King Christ. Therefore we sing of thee, O Virgin, and supremely exalt Him unto ages!

*(Fol. 11v)*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Eve indeed, through the disease of disobedience, brought in the curse; but thou, O Virgin Theotokos, through the blossoming of bearing in the womb, didst make blessing to blossom forth unto the world. Therefore we all magnify thee.[^65]

*Troparion:*
Your labors upon earth went before heavenly gladness, where the choirs of martyrs and divine hosts, and the whole assembly of the firstborn rejoice together, O all-blessed ones.[^66]

*Troparion:*
Deliver all from grievous bonds and afflictions, O all-blessed ones, who celebrate your holy solemnity in faith, asking for peace and tranquility, and salvation, O blessed ones!

*Troparion:*
Illumined by rich light and shining with grace, O passion-bearers: entreat the Benefactor to grant remission of transgressions and sorrows unto us, the children who flee unto you, having struggled together with you!

*Theotokion:*
Eve indeed was driven away from the tree of life, being forbidden communion; but thou, O Virgin Theotokos, didst give birth unto the Pre-eternal Life, granting by faith unto the world life-bearing operation.[^67]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены̀ ᲂу҆слы́шите):*
Let us crown with hymns Acindynus, Pegasius, and Elpidephorus, together with Aphthonius and Anempodistus; for having rebuked the vain-minded Persian deception, and having endured scourgings and wounds for the sake of Christ, they received ineffable glory.[^68]

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, palace of God! Rejoice, overshadowed mountain! Rejoice, unburnt bush! Rejoice, throne of glory! Rejoice, divine table! Rejoice, all-golden jar! Rejoice, fiery-radiant lampstand! Rejoice, swift cloud, O Virgin Mother Mary![^69]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos; and stichera of the saints, Tone 2.*
*Verse: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and out of them all the Lord shall deliver them.[^70]*
Having crimsoned thy body with streams of blood, safely didst thou traverse the path of martyrdom, O passion-bearer Acindynus! Therefore, having girded thyself with divine strength, thou didst cut down the crafty plots of the enemy. Pray unto Christ God for us, that our souls may be saved!

*Glory, in Tone 4:*
The five-rayed luminary of the sufferers, as with an axe in a forest of trees,[^71] according to David, cut down the deception of the enemy; having confessed Christ before kings, they unceasingly pray for our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
When Thine Ewe-lamb and Mother beheld Thee nailed to the Cross, O Lord, she was filled with wonder, and cried aloud: "What is this sight, O Son most longed- *(Fol. 12r)*

-for? Have the faithless and most lawless assembly rendered these things unto Thee, who enjoyed Thy many wonders? But glory to Thine ineffable condescension, O Master!"[^72]

*On the same month, the 3rd day: The Holy Martyrs Acepsimas the Bishop, Joseph the Presbyter, and Aeithalas the Deacon;*[^80]
*And the Dedication of the Church of the Holy Great-Martyr George in Lydda, wherein his honorable body is laid.*[^81]

*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera of the martyrs, Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*
O most marvelous wonder! The comely Acepsimas, minister of the martyrs, is crowned today with a headband of hymns; he sets forth God-bridled sufferings and wounds the bodiless enemy. O what bountiful grace he received! Through his prayers save our souls, O Christ, for Thou art merciful.[^82]

O most marvelous wonder! The star from Persia, the noble Joseph, by the Spirit destroyed the sorcerous abomination, and with streams of blood quenched the godless worship of fire. O the strength of his soul, which cast down demons! Through his prayers save our souls, O Christ, for Thou art merciful.

O most marvelous wonder! The steadfast Aeithalas is revealed as a champion of suffering true to his name:[^83] an ever-blossoming orchard, being cut he blossoms with wounds, and even when put to death he begins to live! O the fortitude of nature which he endured! Through his prayers save our souls, O Christ, for Thou art merciful.

*Other stichera, of Saint George, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
O passion-bearer George, companion of angels and dwelling place of martyrs, ever the refuge of the sorrowful, a haven of calm: be thou also unto me who sail upon life's sea, and direct my life, I pray thee, that with undoubting faith I may call blessed thy supernatural contests!

*(Fol. 12v)*

Preserve me when sailing upon the sea, when walking on the way, when sleeping in the night; when waking, enlighten my mind, O George, and guide me to do the will of the Lord, that I may find on the day of judgment release from the deeds done by me in life, having fled under thy shelter, O glorious one!

Having protected thyself with the breastplate of faith, with the shield of grace, and with the spear of the Cross, thou wast invincible to the adversaries, O George; and as a divine warrior, having conquered the demonic ranks, thou dancest with the angels; and preserving the faithful, thou overshadowest and savest them when called upon.

*Glory, in Tone 6:*
Worthily hast thou lived according to thy name,[^84] O soldier George; for taking the Cross of Christ upon thy shoulders, thou didst cultivate well the earth grown wild with diabolical deception; and having uprooted the thorny idol-worship, thou didst plant the vine of the Orthodox faith. Therefore thou pourest forth healings throughout the whole inhabited earth unto the faithful, and wast revealed as a righteous husbandman of the Trinity. Pray, we entreat thee, for the peace of the world and the salvation of our souls!

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*
Beholding our Life hanging upon the Tree, the all-immaculate Theotokos, weeping with maternal lamentation, cried aloud: "O my Son and my God, save those who hymn Thee in love!"[^85]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*
*Glory, of the saints, in Tone 6. By Ephraim of Caria:*[^86]
The three youths who were preserved unburnt in Persia were a figurative forerunner of your three-hypostatic like-mindedness and of your martyrdom in Christ, O sufferers of the ineffable Trinity and Supersubstantial Unity! For as they, daring against the flame, did not offend God, even so you refused not to die, not sparing yourselves for the love of Christ. But as the Fourth Who appeared among them bedewed them in the flame,[^87] so also Christ, Who is One of the Trinity, received you into a place of refreshment, O Acepsimas with Joseph, and Aeithalas, pleasing unto God: pray for our souls!

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*

*(Fol. 13r)*

Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, she who gave birth unto Thee cried aloud: "What is this strange mystery that I behold, O my Son? How dost Thou die in the flesh, hanging upon the Tree, O Giver of life?"

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God; for having Thine invincible strength, they brought down the tormentors, and crushed the feeble audacity of demons. By their supplications, save our souls![^88]

*Glory, of Saint George, in the same tone:*
As a liberator of captives and defender of the poor, physician of the ailing and champion of kings: O trophy-bearer and great-martyr George, entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved![^89]

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion.*
*At Matins, one canon of the Octoechos, with the heirmos on 6; and of the martyrs on 4; and of Saint George on 4.*
*Canon of the Martyrs, Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
I will open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I will utter a word unto the Queen Mother; and I will be seen keeping festival radiantly, and rejoicing I will sing of her wonders.[^90]

*Troparion:*
Equal in number to the Most Holy Trinity, O all-wealthy ones, you were revealed as Her honorable adorers; and you stand before the Trinitarian throne, fervent protectors of those who run unto you.

*Troparion:*
Adorers of the Tri-sunned Trinity, O sheep,[^91] you destroyed the deception of polytheism, O holy ones, having endured varied torments and unjust death, O divinely blessed ones!

*Troparion:*
You passed over the deep sea of martyrdom without tempest through faith, O blessed ones, and reached the sorrowless life, the haven of heavenly radiance, entering into ineffable glory.

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast been revealed as the Mediatress of joy unto us, O all-immaculate one, as having received the fullness of all the Godhead.[^92] Therefore we all cry unto thee with one accord the Joy of the Angel: Rejoice, thou that art full of grace![^93]

*Another Canon, of Saint George.*
*Whose Acrostic is:*
*As a husbandman for God I glorify thee, O blessed one.*[^94]
*Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
O Thou Who wast born of the Virgin: drown, I pray Thee, the three parts of my soul in the depth of dispassion, as of old the mighty captains,[^95] that in the mortification of the body, as on a timbrel, I may sing unto Thee a song of victory![^96]

*(Fol. 13v)*

*Troparion:*
Thou wast revealed as an abundant husbandry of God,[^97] nourishing the faithful, an example of imitation unto the pious, O passion-bearer George, who brightly celebrate thy light-bearing memory and warmly glorify thee therein.

*Troparion:*
Divine love truly inflamed thy heart, O passion-bearer; therefore of thine own accord thou camest unto the tormentors, consuming the deception of polytheism, and flashing forth the understanding of the brightness of salvation.

*Troparion:*
Confidently as a lion didst thou stand before the tribunal,[^98] clearly proclaiming the incarnation of Christ, whereby the world was delivered from the ancient fall and received its first fruitfulness, O thrice-blessed George!

*Theotokion:*
Delivering us from the ancient condemnation, the Son of God became the Son of the Virgin as man. Therefore in two essences and two wills,[^99] we glorify Him with an orthodox heart.

*Ode 3, Canon of the Martyrs. Heirmos:*
Not in wisdom, nor in power, nor in riches do we boast, but in Thee, the hypostatic Wisdom of the Father, O Christ; for there is none holy save Thee, O Lover of mankind![^100]

*Troparion:*
Not in the wisdom of Hellenic light, O wise ones, but by divine understanding did you rebuke the Persian godlessness, reproaching their madness.

*Troparion:*
Enlightened by the divine anointing of the sacred hierarchy, O holy Acepsimas, thou didst adorn thyself with the blood of martyrdom, O divinely blessed one!

*Troparion:*
The crushing of thy limbs, O ever-memorable Joseph, crushed utterly the wiles of deception, O martyr, and mediated for thee incorruptible glory!

*Theotokion:*
Having found thee to be a most pure dwelling place, the Wisdom of God was incarnate of thine honorable blood, and revealed thee incorrupt even after giving birth.

*Canon of Saint George. Heirmos:*
The bow of the mighty has waxed feeble, and the weak have girded themselves with strength; therefore my heart has been established in the Lord.[^101]

*Troparion:*
Having joyfully stripped thyself of the glory of thy lineage and fatherland, thou didst follow Christ, and wast revealed as a most comely citizen of the Sion on high, O martyr!

*Troparion:*
That thou mightest be revealed as a noble heir and an obedient son of the living God, thou didst endure the wounds exacted by the tormentors, O valiant martyr!

*Theotokion:*
Clothing Himself with the whole of Adam, He Who for mercy's sake became the New Adam from thee, O all-immaculate one, is the One Creator of men.[^102]

*(Fol. 14r)*

*Kontakion of the Saints, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Blamelessly didst thou initiate into divine mysteries, O wise one, and becamest an acceptable sacrifice, O divinely blessed one; for gloriously didst thou drink the cup of Christ,[^103] O holy Acepsimas, with thy fellow sufferers, praying unceasingly for all of us.[^104]

*Ikos:*
Who among the faithful can ever worthily hymn the all-wise priest Acepsimas, the luminary of Christ? For he destroyed the deception of idols and put to shame the demonic wiles by the mighty power of the Savior Christ God, instructing us piously to worship the Most Holy Trinity, to revere the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit in one Godhead: praying unceasingly for all of us.

*Sessional Hymn of the Martyrs, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
The valiant ascetic Joseph, Acepsimas the destroyer of deception, and Aeithalas the glorious invincible sufferer, radiant stars, let them worthily and truly be praised today by the faithful in hymns! For they blackened the deception of the Persians, sacrificing neither to the sun nor honoring fire. Unto them let us cry aloud in love: Pray unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who in love celebrate your holy memory![^105]

*Glory, of Saint George, in Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*
Having spurned military service upon earth, O martyr, thou didst desire glory in the heavens, and thou didst endure afflictions and a cruel death; therefore today, celebrating thine all-sacred memory, we offer praise unto Christ, O thrice-blessed George![^106]

*Both now, Theotokion:*
O Hope of Christians, Most Holy Virgin, Whom thou didst bear as God beyond mind and word: pray unceasingly for those who hymn thee, that He may grant remission of all our sins and correction of life unto us who ever glorify thee in faith and love!

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The undefiled Ewe-lamb, beholding dead upon the Tree the Lamb and Shepherd, weeping said, crying aloud in maternal lamentation: "How shall I bear Thine ineffable condescension, O my Son, and Thy voluntary passions, O God Supremely Good?"

*Canon of the Martyrs, Tone 4. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Sitting in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, on a swift cloud came Jesus the Supremely Divine, and with an incorruptible palm saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ![^107]

*(Fol. 14v)*

*Troparion:*
Having despised things below and looking unto abiding things alone, they obtained the dwellings thereof: let the valiant Acepsimas, and the glorious Joseph and Aeithalas, be praised!

*Troparion:*
Thy thought stretched forth unto the Master alone at the time of suffering, O martyr, wrought for thee relief from unendurable torments, O steadfast Joseph, passion-bearer of Christ worthy of marvel!

*Troparion:*
Thine honorable testimony, embraced as a fruitful vine, pourest forth wine of compunction unto the faithful, O passion-bearer Aeithalas, gladdening those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

*Theotokion:*
The Holy Theotokos, in whom the Father's and equally divine Word was well-pleased to dwell as in a sweet-smelling temple, corrupted not her purity nor caused grief; for she gave birth unto Emmanuel, God and man.[^108]

*Canon of Saint George. Heirmos:*
For the love of Thine image, O Compassionate One, Thou didst stand upon Thy Cross, and the nations melted away; for Thou, O Lover of mankind, art my strength and praise![^109]

*Troparion:*
Thy body put to death by torments, O blessed one, depicts the passions of the Word Who was put to death, Who granted thee eternal life.

*Troparion:*
Protected with the true shield, by a steadfast mind thou didst utterly destroy the champions of falsehood, O God-wise George!

*Troparion:*
Through thy holy limbs was the Word glorified, Who clothed Himself with the weakness of earthly men; therefore we eternally glorify thee, O George!

*Theotokion:*
He Who granted being unto men, also granted well-being unto them that had become corrupt through transgression, O most pure one, having become man.[^110]

*Canon of the Martyrs. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou, my Lord, camest as a light into the world, a holy light turning back from dark ignorance those who sing of Thee in faith![^111]

*Troparion:*
Calling upon the great and honorable Name of the Lord, rejoicing didst Thou fill the cup of salvation of sufferings, O Acepsimas![^112]

*Troparion:*
The heavenly food received thee who wast called by wounds, O Joseph, and the choirs of martyrs received thee, rejoicing with them.

*Troparion:*
An ever-blossoming orchard, nourishing the ends of the earth with the fruits of thy contests, wast thou truly revealed to be, O blessed Aeithalas!

*Theotokion:*
The Timeless Light, the Father's Radiance, didst thou bear for us under time, Who in the goodness of His wealth became man, O all-immaculate one![^113]

*Canon of Saint George. Heirmos: (The same).*

*(Fol. 15r)*

*Troparion:*
Having entered manfully upon the contest of martyrdom, thou didst strike down, O passion-bearer, the demonic cruelty of idols, though being crushed in body.

*Troparion:*
The Master set thee as a radiant stone in the crowns, O passion-bearer, shining suitably upon His Church.

*Troparion:*
Offered as a lamb, depicting the death of the Good Chief Shepherd, thou didst offer thyself upon the heavenly table as an undefiled sacrifice.

*Theotokion:*
Save us from dangers and sorrows, O all-immaculate Theotokos, and deliver us from future torments by thy supplications!

*Ode 6, Canon of the Martyrs. Heirmos:*
"I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord," the Church cries aloud unto Thee, having been cleansed from the demons' blood by the blood which for mercy's sake flowed from Thy side.[^114]

*Troparion:*
When thy head was severed from thy body, O Acepsimas, it joined thy soul unto Christ by faith unswervingly, O martyr, being ever enlightened by the radiances there!

*Troparion:*
Slain with stones like the Protomartyr,[^115] O martyr, thou didst not deny Christ the living Stone, passing over unto the radiant mansions there!

*Troparion:*
Unmercifully wounded with rods, thou didst rejoice, having the Cross of the Lord as a rod of strength and boast,[^116] O passion-bearer Aeithalas, God-wise and all-wealthy!

*Theotokion:*
The bush prefigured the great mystery, surpassing understanding, of thy childbirth, being wholly wrapped with fire yet in no wise consumed, O all-hymned Virgin!

*Canon of Saint George. Heirmos:*
I have entered into the depths of the sea, and the tempest of my many sins has engulfed me; but as God, lead up my life from the depth, O Plenteous in mercy![^117]

*Troparion:*
Doubly broken in pieces by the sufferings of the body, O martyr, thou didst manfully destroy all the wiles of the enemy's malice, O all-blessed George!

*Troparion:*
Neither the sharp blades cutting thy body and the wheel, O martyr, nor the ignited fuel of the furnace didst thou fear at all, being kindled with love toward God!

*Theotokion:*
A holy temple for Him Who rests in the saints wast thou, O Mother of God; therefore thou sanctifiest us who faithfully hymn thee, O Ever-Virgin!

*Kontakion of Saint George, Tone 4, Podoben: "To thee, the champion leader" (Возбра́нной):*
Having fled unto thy championed and speedy protection, we the faithful *(Fol. 15v)*

pray, O passion-bearer of Christ, that those who hymn thee may be delivered from the snares of the enemy, and from all tribulations and afflictions, that we may cry: Rejoice, O martyr George![^118]

*Ikos:*
So great in intercessions hast thou been shown upon earth, O pleasing servant and friend of the Lord; for overshadowing the faithful people, thou ever savest them, O glorious one! Therefore with faith and love we cry unto thee, O much-suffering one:
Rejoice, through whom the world is enlightened!
Rejoice, through whom the army is illumined!
Rejoice, deliverance of the faithful from captivity!
Rejoice, speedy defense of prisoners!
Rejoice, O height unto those who warmly run unto thee in faith!
Rejoice, enricher of those who love thee, and joy in afflictions!
Rejoice, for thou art the wall of protection for the king's son![^119]
Rejoice, for thou dost cause victory to lie beneath in battles!
Rejoice, O star enlightening those who sail!
Rejoice, unlooser of every affliction!
Rejoice, unto whom every faithful one flees for refuge!
Rejoice, through whom the Creator is praised!
Rejoice, O martyr George!

*Ode 7, Canon of the Martyrs. Heirmos:*
Thou Who savedst Thy children of Abraham in the fire, and slewest the Chaldeans, whom justice righteously condemned: O supremely hymned Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^120]

*Troparion:*
Having received dew from God amid the fire of martyrdom, you quenched the flames of the adversaries by your endurance, O passion-bearers, crying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Those who worshipped fire were shown to be heirs thereof; they compelled those who serve the Sun of glory to serve fire. But these cried aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Acepsimas, Joseph, and Aeithalas, three luminaries of the all-honorable Trinity, shining upon all the ends of the earth with the radiances of piety: let them be honored unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
Blessed is the Fruit of thy blessed womb, Whom the heavenly powers and the assemblies of earthly beings bless, Who delivered us from the first curse, O blessed one!

*Canon of Saint George. Heirmos:*
The three youths in Babylon, turning the tyrant's command into folly, cried aloud in the midst of the flame: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers![^121]

*Troparion:*
Thou becamest a living sacrifice, O martyr, unto Him Who was offered for us as a sheep; and being strengthened in Christ, thou didst abolish the sacrifices offered unto demons by thyself!

*(Fol. 16r)*

*Troparion:*
Thou didst appear fruitful as a vine, bringing forth for us clusters of endurance, O glorious one, dripping divine wine that gladdens the hearts of all the pious!

*Troparion:*
Thou gavest thy limbs zealously to be cut in pieces for Christ, yet thou didst remain inseparable from His love, O all-blessed one, and an heir of all good things, rejoicing!

*Theotokion:*
All creation offers praise unto God, Who was born of thy most pure womb, O all-undefiled Maiden, and Who delivered us all from the ancient curse.

*Ode 8, Canon of the Martyrs. Heirmos:*
The childbirth of the Theotokos saved the pious children in the furnace: then prefigured, but now fulfilled, it moves the whole inhabited earth to sing unto Thee: Hymn the Lord, O ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^122]

*Troparion:*
Having become receptacles of the Word, and bearing His wounds, through the cruelty of the tormentors you were laid as a lifeless burden upon beasts,[^123] brought unto the trial of greater torments, O noble martyrs, supremely exalting Christ unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Mediators of ever-existing glory, adorned, ever-memorable martyrs, you joyfully walked the glorious path of testimony of Him Whom you loved, crying: Hymn the Lord and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Neither fire, nor wounds, nor beasts, nor sword, nor pit, nor death could separate Thy martyrs from Thy love, O Lord,[^124] Fountain of blessings, Stream of inexhaustible love! Praising them, O Christ, we bless Thee unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
The only unwedded Mother, and the only one surpassing all creation, the most holy mountain, the all-golden table, the Theotokos, praising in hymns we cry: Hymn the Lord, O ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Canon of Saint George. Heirmos:*
O Almighty Deliverer of all, having descended, Thou didst bedew in the midst of the flame those who acted piously, and didst teach them to sing: All ye works, bless and hymn the Lord![^125]

*Troparion:*
An excellent pilot for those who sail, a great helper in afflictions wast thou revealed to be, O George: thou savest those who run unto thee in faith and with an undoubting heart.

*Troparion:*
Thou wast revealed as a champion of truth and an accuser of falsehood, and moreover a confirmation unto us, O passion-bearer, who cry in faith: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*(Fol. 16v)*

*Troparion:*
By the sprinkling of thy blood, O George, thou didst quench the coals of deception, and didst fill the hearts of the faithful who faithfully hymn thee and celebrate thy glorious memory!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst bud forth from the root of Jesse, and didst uproot the wicked root, having sprouted the Creator of creation, O Maiden, unto Whom we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^126]

*Ode 9, Canon of the Martyrs. Heirmos:*
A cornerstone was cut out from thee, the unhewn mountain, O Virgin, even Christ, without hands, Who united the divided natures. Therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Theotokos![^127]

*Troparion:*
Let us praise the pious luminaries and destroyers of deception, the sweet-smelling flowers of noetic paradise, the honorable vessels, the beholders of God's beauty!

*Troparion:*
Having received inwardly into your hearts the Coal which Isaiah of old beheld,[^128] and illumined by its radiance, O martyrs, you abolished the dark kindling of fire!

*Troparion:*
Adorned, you now stand before the Life-originating Trinity, and enlightened with the beauties of crowns, O blessed ones, make remembrance of those upon earth who ever commemorate you!

*Theotokion:*
Save me from despair, O Virgin who conceived the Savior and bore Him in the flesh! For weighed down with the burden of sins, in pain of heart I cry unto thee: Make haste to help thy servant!

*Canon of Saint George. Heirmos:*
Eve, through the disease of disobedience, brought in the curse; but thou, O Virgin Theotokos, through the budding fruit of thy gestation, didst blossom forth blessing unto the world. Therefore we all magnify thee![^129]

*Troparion:*
As the dawn, as the sun, thou didst radiantly shine forth and enlighten creation, O passion-bearer, with unsetting radiances and with manifestations of many wonders, O George, joy of the martyrs! Therefore in love we call thee blessed.

*Troparion:*
A drop of divine sweetness wast thou shown to be, O George, taking away our bitter passions and ever sweetening the souls and hearts of those who bless thee in faith, O worthy of glory!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst sanctify the earth with thy blood, and with the spirit of gladness didst fill the heavens, O martyr. Therefore every soul of the pious loves thee as a close pleasing servant of the Lord, and inscribes thee as a helper!

*Theotokion:*
We offer unto thee the voice of divine Gabriel's gladness, crying aloud: Rejoice, joy of the whole inhabited earth, having given birth unto the Destroyer of sorrow, *(Fol. 17r)*

and taken away the reproach of Eve: Rejoice, O unwedded Virgin![^130]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ въ ст҃и́лищи):*
As one bodiless didst thou endure unendurable torments, O all-praised Acepsimas, glory of priests, together with marvelous Joseph and admirable Aeithalas the deacon, initiate of Christ's mysteries; at the pains of whose sufferings the ranks of the bodiless angels ever marvel![^131]

*Glory, of Saint George, Podoben the same:*
With streams of thy blood, O blessed one, thou didst quench the flames of deception, and didst utterly destroy the cruelty of the tormentors, and didst glorify Christ, O passion-bearer George. Therefore thou didst receive the crown of incorruption and life from the right hand of the Most High!

*Theotokion:*
There is in me no hope of salvation at all, O Virgin, for evilly have I fallen into the depths of transgressions, and I await the threat of fearful torment and the portion of the goats.[^132] But have compassion upon me before the judgment, as thou art a fervent protectress, O Theotokos!

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos, and of the martyrs. Verse: The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them.[^133]*
*Sticheron, Tone 2:*
O pious holy ones, who steadfastly contended for Christ, you put to shame the cruelty of the tormentors, and plunged the haughtiness of idols into the abyss, O Acepsimas, Aeithalas, and Joseph! And now crowned in the heavens, dancing in chorus, pray for our souls!

*Glory, in Tone 4. Idiomelon, by the Studite:*[^134]
Let us spiritually praise, O brethren, the endurance of the noetic adamant, George the glorious martyr! Whom, burned for Christ, misfortunes struck, and torments sharpened, and varied tortures wore out his body, corruptible by nature; for desire conquered nature, urging the lover by death to pass over unto the desired Christ God, the Savior of our souls!

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "As one noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
When she beheld Thee nailed to the Cross, O Lord, Thine Ewe-lamb and Mother was filled with marvel, and cried aloud: "What is this sight, O beloved Son? Did the faithless, lawless assembly render this unto Thee, having enjoyed Thy many wonders? But glory to Thine ineffable condescension, O Master!"[^135]

*At the Liturgy: Prokeimenon, Tone 4: To the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath been wonderful; all His desires are in them.[^136] Verse: I beheld the Lord (Fol. 17v)*

*before me always, for He is at my right hand, that I may not be shaken.[^137]*
*Epistle: To the Ephesians, pericope 233.[^138]*
*Alleluia, Tone 4: The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them.[^139]*
*Verse: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and the Lord shall deliver them out of them all.[^140]*
*Gospel: Luke, pericope 106.[^141]*
*Communion Verse: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous: praise is meet for the upright.[^142]*
