*On the same month, the 4th day: Our Venerable Father Joannicius the Great;*[^143]
*And the Holy Martyr Nicander, Bishop of Myra, and Hermas the Presbyter.*[^144]

*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera on 6. Of the venerable one, 3, in Tone 4, Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*
When illumined with divine light, having through purity of mind looked upon and fittingly discerned the unstable things from those that abide eternally: then, having received fire into thy heart, like a hart didst thou burn with divine love;[^145] and forgetting flesh and blood, thou didst prepare thyself for ascetic contests, whereby thou didst subject the passions of the body unto thy soul! And thou didst receive the gift of prophecy, to behold distant things as though present, and to foretell future things unto the faithful. Therefore as a divine teacher we glorify thee!

The assaults and darts of demons didst thou powerfully blunt by the configuration of prayers, and prevailedst over them by the power of God, O worthy of glory! Thence He Who is marvelous in blessings granted honors unto thee, O father, resting upon the humility of thy heart; therefore also thy precious relics pour forth sweet-smelling myrrh, for thou wast revealed as the sweet fragrance of Christ, O Joannicius![^146]

Unto the ascent of the height of divine mountains thou didst remove, not humbled by the needs of this humble body, O father Joannicius; by vigilant standings and all-day prayers, united unto the Good One, thou wast enlightened, *(Fol. 18r)*

*Other Stichera of the Martyrs, Tone 6, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
Having received a name answering to thy calling by divine providence,[^147] thou didst confirm it by deeds: for the multitude of warriors and the assembly of tormentors didst thou conquer by thine endurance. Therefore having received the crown of victory, thou didst cry aloud in faith: Glory to Thine unconquerable dominion, O Lover of mankind!

Most sweet-smelling myrrh of healings dost thou pour forth for us today, O Nicander, on thy divine commemoration; and thou drivest away, O wise one, the gloom of afflictions and the bodily passions, and fillest with rich grace the assembly of all who cry unto Christ: Thou art the inexhaustible Myrrh that perfumes those who hymn Thee!

Having boldness toward Christ Who alone is glorified in His saints: pray thou unto Him, O venerable Nicander, for all who lovingly celebrate thy memory and praise thy righteous deeds, that by grace we may become partakers of those ineffable good things and incorruptible glory!

*Glory, in Tone 6:*
O venerable father, into all the earth has the sound of thy righteous deeds gone forth;[^148] therefore in the heavens thou hast found the reward of thy labors. Thou didst destroy the demonic ranks and attain unto the angelic orders, whose blameless life thou didst emulate. Having boldness toward Christ God, ask peace for our souls!

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*
Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, she who gave birth unto Thee cried aloud: "What is this strange mystery that I behold, O my Son? How dost Thou die in the flesh, hanging upon the Tree, O Giver of life?"[^149]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*
*Glory, in Tone 8. Idiomelon:*
We honor thee, O our father Joannicius, as the instructor of multitudes of monks; for by thy path we have learned truly to walk uprightly. Blessed art thou, having laboured for Christ, and having exposed the power of the enemy! O companion of angels, fellow-partaker with the venerable and the righteous: with them pray unto the Lord that our souls may be saved![^150]

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*
Beholding Thee nailed upon the Cross, O Jesus, and voluntarily accepting passions, the Virgin and Thy Mother, O Master, cried aloud: "Woe is me, O my sweet Child! How dost Thou endure unjust wounds, *(Fol. 18v)*

O Physician Who healedst human infirmity and deliveredst all from corruption by Thy tender mercy?"[^151]

*Troparion, Tone 8:*
With the streams of thy tears thou didst cultivate the barren desert, and by sighs from the depth didst make thy labors bear fruit a hundredfold, and becamest a luminary unto the whole inhabited earth, radiant with wonders, O Joannicius our father: entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved![^152]

*Glory, in Tone 4:*
Thy martyr, O Lord, Nicander, in his suffering received an incorruptible crown from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, he brought down the tormentors, and crushed the feeble audacity of demons. By his supplications, save our souls![^153]

*Both now, Theotokion.*
*At Matins, one canon of the Octoechos; and of the venerable one on 4; and of the martyr on 4.*
*Canon of the Venerable One.*
*Whose Acrostic is:*
*The Forerunner praises thee as an imitator. Joseph.*[^154]
*Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
I will open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I will utter a word unto the Queen Mother; and I will be seen keeping festival radiantly, and rejoicing I will sing of her wonders.[^155]

*Troparion:*
Illumined with the light of grace, O venerable one, enlighten those who celebrate thy memory in faith, and deliver them from the darkness of sin by thy supplications, O Joannicius!

*Troparion:*
Upon the path that leads unto the heavenly city didst thou walk without turning back, O Joannicius; for the Holy Spirit guided thee, resting in thy heart!

*Troparion:*
An obedient humility didst thou possess, O Joannicius; therefore we pray thee, O venerable one: have compassion on our lowliness, and heal all the diseases of our hearts!

*Theotokion:*
Thou art the restoration of the fallen and the confirmation of those that stand, O all-undefiled one; therefore I pray thee: set upright my mind that has fallen through sin, O Sovereign Lady, that I may glorify thee!

*Canon of the Martyrs, Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The choirs of Israel, having passed through the Red Sea and the watery deep with dryshod feet, seeing the horsemen, the captains of the enemy, submerged therein, sang with gladness: Let us sing unto our God, for He has been glorified![^156]

*Troparion:*
The honorable feast of the honorable sufferers, the hieromartyrs, their sacred memory today, *(Fol. 19r)*

sacredly celebrating now with sacred hymnody, the most sacred Church of Christ is adorned with hymns, honoring them!

*Troparion:*
Anointed with the precious ointment of the priesthood faithfully, O hierarch Nicander, thou didst make it yet more precious with the shedding of thy blood, crying aloud in joy: Let us sing unto our God, for He has been glorified![^157]

*Troparion:*
Having run the path of martyrdom, visibly manifesting true joy therein, you were enriched with the grace of wonders and heavenly gifts, O martyrs, crying aloud in unison: Let us sing unto our God, for He has been glorified!

*Theotokion:*
He Who is uncircumscribed in the Father's bosom is bodily circumscribed in a mother's bosom, even Christ, Who after childbirth preserved her truly a Virgin beyond understanding; unto Whom we cry aloud with a loud voice: Let us sing unto our God, for He has been glorified![^158]

*Ode 3, Canon of the Venerable One. Heirmos:*
Establish Thy singers, O Theotokos, thou living and inexhaustible Fountain, who have formed a spiritual choir; and in thy divine glory vouchsafe unto them crowns of glory![^159]

*Troparion:*
Passing things didst thou exchange for those that abide, prudently taking up thy cross, O Joannicius; and ascending the mountains that climb toward heaven like Elijah the Great, thou didst abide there![^160]

*Troparion:*
The maiden showed thee the path of the fathers, exceedingly desired by thee, whom thou didst find hidden in the mountains for very many years, enlightened by the prophetic gift, O blessed one![^161]

*Troparion:*
Shaken by varied passions, we run in faith unto thy protection, O Joannicius; through thy holy intercessions visit us all, praying unto the Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:*
By the sprinkling of thy mercy, O Virgin, quench the coals of my passions, O divinely graced one; and kindle the extinguished lamp of my heart, O all-golden lampstand, all-undefiled one![^162]

*Canon of the Martyrs. Heirmos:*
"As the barren woman from the nations has given birth, the Church, and the assembly that was rich in children has waxed feeble," unto our marvelous God let us cry aloud: Holy art Thou, O Lord![^163]

*Troparion:*
Spreading noetic nets, working wonders, thou didst catch those who were in deception, offering them as a manifold fruit unto Him Who shone forth from the Virgin, O Nicander![^164]

*Troparion:*
A most fruitful branch of the garden of Titus, the luminary of Crete, wast thou,[^165] bearing noetic clusters that pour forth saving sweetness unto us, *(Fol. 19v)*

O blessed Nicander!

*Troparion:*
Together with the divine Hermas, you cultivated cold hearts with the plow of the Cross, O wise ones, and made them fruitful with grace; therefore you are called blessed!

*Theotokion:*
Not even the heavenly mind can recount thy childbirth beyond understanding, O Maiden! For in thy womb, O pure one, thou didst conceive the Word of the Primal Mind, Who by a word established all things![^166]

*Sessional Hymn of the Venerable One, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Having cleansed the gloom of passions, receiving truly the light of Christ's commandments, thou didst blossom in fasting; and having mortified the body, thou didst live by the Spirit, trampling underfoot the snares of the enemy, O blessed one! Therefore thou becamest a partaker with the heavenly, bodiless angels by the grace of the Spirit, O Joannicius our father: pray unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who in love celebrate thy holy memory![^167]

*Glory, of the Martyrs, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йся):*
Enlightened by the divine anointing of the true priesthood, and truly by the sacred blood of martyrdom, O glorious ones, you joined yourselves rejoicing unto the ranks of the bodiless angels. Therefore we celebrate your honorable memory, praying that cleansing may be granted unto all through your supplications![^168]

*Both now, Theotokion:*
By thy divine childbirth, O pure one, thou didst renew the mortal essence of earthborn men that was corrupt in passions, and raised all from death unto the life of incorruption. Therefore as is meet we all call thee blessed, O all-glorified Virgin, even as thou didst foretell![^169]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
A sword pierced thy most holy soul,[^170] O all-undefiled Mother of Christ God, when thou beheldest Thy Son and God voluntarily crucified: Whom do thou not cease to entreat, O blessed one, to grant us remission of transgressions!

*Ode 4, Canon of the Venerable One. Heirmos:*
Perceiving the unsearchable divine counsel of Thine incarnation from the Virgin, O Thou Most High, the Prophet Habbakuk cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^171]

*Troparion:*
Having reached the highest mountains, thou didst by humility bring low the exalted summits of demons, O wise one; and thou actedst manfully upon them, O glory and confirmation of monks!

*Troparion:*
Armed with the fear of Christ as with a two-edged sword,[^172] thou didst noetically and sensibly cast down the apostate serpent, O blessed one!

*(Fol. 20r)*

glorified by sacred victories.[^173]

*Troparion:*
All inflamed with the Divine Spirit, O father, thou didst endure frost, dwelling for many years in the deserts, seeking the Lord, Who warmed thee with divine grace.

*Theotokion:*
Thee, the purification of all earthborn, with faith I beseech, and falling down, O blessed one: make the Judge, even thy Son, merciful unto me, that as is due I may glorify thee!

*Another Canon [of the Martyrs]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Sitting in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, on a swift cloud came Jesus the Supremely Divine, and with an incorruptible palm saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ![^174]

*Troparion:*
You appeared as a chariot of the Word, bearing Him in mind; therefore, bound unto horses and cruelly dragged, you did not deny Him nor were you conquered, being manifestly directed toward the heavenly path.

*Troparion:*
Drawing near unto prisons and bound with cords, you saved the city and the people from the bonds of deception; and you bound yourselves with the bond of love for the sake of Him Who was bound in the flesh for our sake, O all-blessed ones!

*Troparion:*
Shut up in prison, they glorified the Master together with the angels, nourished with heavenly bread, O all-blessed ones; therefore you took no thought of bodily pains, having become stronger than wounds,

*Theotokion:*
He Who sits fearfully upon a high throne sits as an infant in a mother's embrace, restoring the fallen image, and granting deification unto those descended from Adam.[^175]

*Ode 5, Canon of the Venerable One. Heirmos:*
All creation was amazed at thy divine glory: for thou, O Virgin who knewest not wedlock, didst hold in thy womb the God over all, and gavest birth unto the Timeless Son, granting peace unto all who hymn thee.[^176]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst walk the narrow and sorrowful path, O venerable one, by divine ascents of the heart, enlarged by contemplation and deified by adoption; therefore thou becamest the confirmation and adornment of monks!

*Troparion:*
Because thou didst cleanse thy thoughts, O venerable one, the grace of prophecy was given unto thee, so that thou spakest of future things as though present, and beheldest distant things as though near, O Joannicius, dwelling-place of God!

*Troparion:*
Deliver me from the pains of sins and sorrows, assuage the pain of my heart, and grant remission of transgressions, having God the Benefactor Who listens to Thy honorable prayers.

*Theotokion:*

*(Fol. 20v)*

Heal the distractions of my mind, O all-immaculate one, wither the passions of my soul, and drive away the darkness of despondency: that I may hymn thee in song, O ever-blessed, all-praised Theotokos!

*Canon of the Martyrs. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Send down upon us Thy enlightenment, O Lord, and loose us from the gloom of transgressions, O Good One, granting Thy peace.[^177]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst guide the people into the enlightenment of faith; and having driven away the darkness of idol-madness, they became children of light through thine intercession, O Nicander!

*Troparion:*
Shining with the illuminating rays of the Spirit, you traversed the night of martyrdom unharmed, dispelling the gloom of godlessness, O glorious luminaries!

*Troparion:*
Having been filled with the waters of Paul, Titus showed himself as a river nourishing thee,[^178] drowning the turbid streams of godlessness, O Nicander!

*Theotokion:*
O Virgin who didst bear the Lamb and Lord in the flesh, sole undefiled tabernacle, divine ark, honorable lampstand: illumine my soul!

*Ode 6, Canon of the Venerable One. Heirmos:*
Celebrating this divine and all-honorable feast of the Mother of God, come, ye divinely-wise, let us clap our hands and glorify God Who was born of her.[^179]

*Troparion:*
Having withered the bodily passions, thou wast seen as a high-crested tree, bearing most sacredly marvelous fruits and honorable corrections, O divinely blessed one!

*Troparion:*
The Lord healed thee through the appearance of Eustathius the Martyr,[^180] when thou hadst drunk all-destructive poison by an unrighteous hand and wast in peril, O all-blessed one!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst share in myriads of sicknesses, remaining infirm in body, O Joannicius; therefore in faith I cry unto thee: Assuage the pains of my heart!

*Theotokion:*
Sole help of all, help us who are in distress; stretch forth thy hand, and lead us unto the havens of salvation, O Maiden graced of God!

*Canon of the Martyrs. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Prefiguring the three-day burial, the Prophet Jonah, praying in the whale, cried aloud: Deliver me from corruption, O Jesus, King of powers![^181]

*Troparion:*
With their bodies pierced with nails, the martyrs showed themselves imitators of the passions of the Savior, Christ Who was nailed upon the Cross and saved the world from corruption.

*Troparion:*
You crossed the deep of torments, O martyrs, steered by the All-powerful Holy Spirit; and unto the divine haven, being filled with glory, *(Fol. 21r)*

being filled with glory.[^182]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst conquer every opposition of murderers, O man named after victory,[^183] O ever-memorable hierarch Nicander; and standing before God, thou hast received crowns of glory!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst destroy the reproach of the first mother, O Maiden, having borne Him in the flesh Who crowned us with blessings; and thou didst turn her sorrow into true joy!

*Kontakion, Tone 8, Podoben: "To thee, the champion leader" (Взбра́нной):*[^184]
Thou appearedst as an all-radiant star, enlightening the world, and shining upon those who are in the gloom of passions; and thou wast revealed as a most mighty physician. But as thou hast received the grace of healings, grant healing unto those who ask thee, that we may cry: Rejoice, O father Joannicius!

*Ikos:*
Another physician and protector hast thou been shown to be for those possessed by infirmities and sorrows, O marvelous Joannicius, healing all who run in faith beneath thy divine protection. Therefore from us also thou hearest: Rejoice, branch of a good father's root! Rejoice, bough of a good mother! Rejoice, thou who cast away their love! Rejoice, thou who accepted God alone! Rejoice, for thou didst abandon earthly soldiering! Rejoice, for thou didst cast down barbarian pride! Rejoice, having become a wall and guardian of the Church! Rejoice, revealed as a weapon and pillar unto the world! Rejoice, thou who destroyedst the battles of the heathens! Rejoice, luminary radiant with miracles! Rejoice, protector of the naked! Rejoice, deliverer of the captive! Rejoice, O father Joannicius!

*Ode 7, Canon of the Venerable One. Heirmos:*
The divinely-wise worshipped not the creature rather than the Creator; but having manfully trampled underfoot the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers![^185]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst make thy heart an abode of the Trinity, having built three churches;[^186] in which by divine grace, O Joannicius, thou pourest forth myrrh, unto the enlightenment and purification of those who come unto thee in faith!

*Troparion:*
Thy soul, ever embraced by the light-radiance of the Divine Spirit, beheld the intentions of the deeds of those who came unto thee in faith, O blessed one, sacredly marveled at for prophetic discernments!

*Troparion:*
Quickly deliver me by thy holy prayers from the infirmities of soul and body that hold me fast, O blessed one, and make me to sing:

*(Fol. 21v)*

"Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"[^187]

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth unto the Immutable One, the only Lord, O thou who art full of the grace of God: pray unto Him, O pure one, that by His right hand my mind may be changed unto better things, which is grievously perverted by worldly cares.

*Another Canon [of the Martyrs]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The Abrahamic children of old in Babylon trampled underfoot the flame of the furnace, crying aloud in hymns: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^188]

*Troparion:*
Having crimsoned thy sacred vesture, O blessed one, with the crimson dyes of blood thou didst make it more radiant, O Nicander, crying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Drawing near unto the fire with unhesitating love for the Creator, you were not consumed, crying aloud, O blessed ones: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
The furnace flame prepared for you for torture you transformed into dew by the all-wise Spirit, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Thou gavest birth ineffably unto the Incarnate Word, O pure Virgin, Who delivers from death those who cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Ode 8, Canon of the Venerable One. Heirmos:*
The birthgiving of the Theotokos saved the pious children in the furnace: then indeed prefigured, but now in reality active, it gathers the whole inhabited earth to sing unto Thee: Works of the Lord, hymn the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages![^189]

*Troparion:*
Standing high upon the mountain as a lamp upon a lampstand, O venerable one, thou didst enlighten the thoughts of all by faith, most excellently showing by words and deeds the path of life, and leading them by the divine word unto the height of dispassion!

*Troparion:*
With a mind cleansed by dispassion thou didst converse with the Lord Almighty; taught by Him ineffable things, O venerable one, thou didst prophesy beforehand, enlightening souls as one of the greatest prophets; therefore in unison we, the faithful, praise thee!

*Troparion:*
Grievous wounds have overtaken me, and various sicknesses trouble me; deliver me from them, O father, as I pray unto thee, for from God, O Joannicius, thou hast received grace to heal passions and to lighten the diseases of the faithful!

*Triadikon:*
Together with all the heavenly hosts, hymning the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Undivided Trinity, the Uncreated Godhead: Holy, Holy, Holy, let us cry aloud in joy: One *(Fol. 22r)*

Power, Principle, and Kingdom![^190]

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast shown to be higher than the angels, having ineffably given flesh unto God; Him do Thou entreat, O tenderhearted one, that through the height of humility my mind may be higher than bodily passions, as I hymn thy most great grace!

*Another Canon [of the Martyrs]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
O All-powerful Deliverer of all, having descended in the midst of the flame, Thou didst moisten the pious youths with dew, and didst teach them to sing: All ye works of the Lord, bless and hymn the Lord![^191]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast an honorable priest, by no means entering with the blood of others, but with thine own blood, O Nicander, entering into the temple on high, and singing: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Glorifying the Lord as a priest of priests,[^192] glorious Hermas, adorned with the blood of martyrdom, cries: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Sacredly celebrating beforehand the holy things, you were shown to be honorable sacrifices, and were offered unto the Lord as an odor of sweet fragrance, crying aloud: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord!

*Theotokion:*
Dry up the abyss of my evils, O thou who didst give birth unto the Abyss of tender mercy, the Deliverer and Lord; unto Whom we cry aloud, O Virgin: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord!

*Ode 9, Canon of the Venerable One. Heirmos:*
Let every earthborn mortal leap for joy, enlightened by the Spirit, and let the nature of the bodiless minds celebrate, honoring the sacred solemnity of the Mother of God; and let it cry aloud: Rejoice, O all-blessed Theotokos, pure Ever-Virgin![^193]

*Troparion:*
Be strengthened, since thy mind was confirmed to restrain passions! An angel in the flesh wast thou therefore, O father, and with the angels in heaven thou dwellest ever, standing before the throne of glory and filled with unwaning light!

*Troparion:*
As in heaven, thou didst dwell in mountains and caverns, O venerable one; therefore wild beasts were tamed before thee, when thou hadst subjected the passions of the soul, O Joannicius who didst overcome sicknesses and becamest righteous; therefore in faith we honor thee!

*Troparion:*
Thy sacred and holy relics lying in the tomb drown diseases and ever burn up demonic hosts, O wise Joannicius; by the grace of God they pour forth healings unto all who ever bless thee in faith!

*Troparion:*
Now drawing near unto Christ more clearly and purely, remember those who commemorate thee in faith, O Joannicius, asking for us remission of sins, deliverance from all diseases, and an abode in the Heavenly Kingdom!

*Theotokion:*

*(Fol. 22v)*

Illumine the eyes of my soul, O pure one who gavest birth unto the Light, lest the most heavy darkness of sin overtake me, nor the abyss of despair cover me; but save me and pilot me unto the haven of divine will![^194]

*Another Canon [of the Martyrs]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Eve indeed, through the disease of disobedience, brought in the curse; but thou, O Virgin Theotokos, through the blossoming of bearing in the womb, didst make blessing to blossom forth unto the world. Therefore we all magnify thee![^195]

*Troparion:*
Patiently stretched upon the tree, O wise martyr Nicander, and burned with torches, thou didst receive heavenly dew from an angelic hand; and by thy life-bearing prayers thou didst show the burned to be dead.

*Troparion:*
You were seen as a fearful sight, stripped and bound unto brute beasts, and dragged over many places, O passion-bearers, yet shown to be unharmed, drawing near unto fire and remaining unburned, preserved by the Divine Spirit!

*Troparion:*
Today the sacred Metropolis of Myra celebrates with a loud voice, calling every city unto gladness upon this your memory, O all-praised ones, in which you accomplished your sacred suffering!

*Troparion:*
Heaven was opened unto you, and the angels clapped their hands at your ascent; the ranks of the venerable and the righteous rejoiced, and the martyrs leaped for joy: with whom dwelling, remember those who commemorate you, O holy ones!

*Theotokion:*
Enlighten me with thy light, O all-immaculate one who gavest birth unto the Unapproachable Light, dispel the clouds of my soul, and pluck me out of darkness, I pray thee; and vouchsafe unto me divine salvation, O most pure, sole Ever-Virgin!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во ст҃и́лищи):*[^196]
The grace of God abounded in thy soul, O wise Joannicius, living as one bodiless; therefore deliver those who honor thee from the dark clouds of passions, leading them unto the quiet haven and driving away the demonic hosts!

*Theotokion:*
Truly the Pre-eternal Son wrought great things with thee by the Father's counsel; for thou gavest birth impassibly unto Incorruptible Life, and didst remain even as before birth, escaping a mother's birth-pangs, a Virgin; and again after birth remaining a Virgin![^197]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*

*Glory, in Tone 4:*
Having preserved unharmed that which is according to the image, establishing the mind as master over *(Fol. 23r)*

destructive passions by asceticism, thou didst attain, in so far as it is possible, unto that which is according to the likeness; for manfully forcing nature, thou didst strive to subject the worse unto the better, and to enslave the flesh unto the spirit. Therefore thou wast revealed as the summit of monks, a desert-dweller, a trainer of those running well, a most sure rule of virtues! And now in the heavens, the mirrors having been dissolved,[^198] O our father Joannicius, thou purely beholdest the Holy Trinity, praying directly for those who honor thee in faith and love![^199]

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Having laid all aside" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*[^200]
"A sword, even as Simeon said, pierced thy heart, O most pure Sovereign Lady, when thou beheldest Him Who shone forth from thee by an ineffable word, lifted up upon the Cross by the lawless as one condemned, given vinegar and gall to drink, His side pierced, and His hands and feet nailed; and weeping thou didst exclaim, crying aloud with a mother's voice: What is this new mystery, O my most sweet Child?"[^201]

*On the same month, the 5th day: The Holy Martyrs Galaction and Episteme.*[^209]

*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera of the martyrs, in Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*[^210]
Nourished with the milk of faith, for the sake of many torments and sorrows, O Galaction, thou didst attain unto the stature of Christ; having become an acceptable sacrifice and a perfect slaughter through voluntary impulse, O all-wealthy one, of thy firm and sure faith, *(Fol. 23v)*

of faith, whereby thou didst obtain God, being now most perfectly deified![^211]

*Sticheron 2, Podoben the same:*
Skilfully didst thou seek the Fountain of good things, the utmost of desirable things, O Episteme; with His brightnesses thou didst illumine both thy soul and thought, O divinely blessed one, and by steadfast resistances didst bring low the wily and ancient tormentor, O divine adornment of monastics, much-suffering martyr!

*Sticheron 3, Podoben the same:*
Two all-radiant luminaries of the noetic Orient shine forth by grace, and piously enlighten the whole creation with surpassing splendors of sufferings and divine ignitions of healings. Celebrating their all-radiant feast, let us glorify Christ Who sanctifies all for their sake!

*Glory, Both now, Theotokion, Podoben the same:*
Rejoice, enlightenment of souls, forgiveness of sinners, correction of the negligent! Rejoice, comfort and joy, helper of the afflicted! Rejoice, O good one, healing of infirm souls! Rejoice, reconciliation unto God and intercessor, as thou art holier than all the Seraphim, O pure one!

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding Thee nailed upon the Cross, O Jesus, and voluntarily accepting passions, the Virgin and Thy Mother, O Master, cried aloud: "Woe is me, O my sweet Child! How dost Thou endure unjust wounds, O Physician Who healedst human infirmity and deliveredst all from corruption by Thy tender mercy?"[^212]

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they brought down the tormentors, and crushed the feeble audacity of demons. By their supplications, save our souls![^213]

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos; and the canon of the saints on 4.*
*Whose Acrostic is:*
*It is meet to praise the non-joined pair of sufferers.*[^214]

*Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Unto Him Who shook off the tyranny of Pharaoh in the sea, and led Israel dryshod through the deep, let us sing unto Christ, for He has been glorified unto the ages![^215]

*Troparion:*
Joyfully standing before the Life-creating Trinity, O all-blessed one, and enlightened by radiant lightnings, ask enlightenment for those who celebrate thy holy memory!

*Troparion:*
Having inflamed thy soul with the Holy Spirit, thou didst burn up the fleshly passions by fasting, and didst quench the fire of godlessness with streams of blood, *(Fol. 24r)*

with streams of blood.[^216]

*Troparion:*
Having left lineage, wealth, and power for the sake of Christ, and taken up the cross, O venerable one, thou didst live as a monk in a God-loving manner, together with blessed Episteme, thy spouse!

*Theotokion:*
Protectress of the afflicted, salvation and hope of the despairing, O all-praised Theotokos: fervently pray that we may be delivered from tribulations!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thou Who by the Word didst establish the heavens, and founded the earth upon many waters: establish me unto the singing of Thy glorification, O Lord![^217]

*Troparion:*
She that gave thee birth brought thee forth, O martyr, as a day-star from barren loins,[^218] dispelling the night of godlessness!

*Troparion:*
Held fast by purity of love, thou didst teach thy spouse to preserve virginity; with whom having lawfully suffered, O martyr Galaction, thou wast glorified!

*Troparion:*
Oh, the marvel of the woman, who was instructed beforehand concerning all the trials of martyrdom that would betide her through a divine revelation, and brought down the tormentor![^219]

*Theotokion:*
Slain by harmful passions, make me alive, O thou who gavest birth unto the Life Who destroyed all the power of death, O Maiden!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предвари́):*[^220]
Having adorned the seeing faculty of thy soul with fasting, thou enlightenest the faithful with rays of suffering, O blessed Galaction! Therefore celebrating thy holy and light-bearing day in faith, we piously cry unto thee: as thou hast boldness toward God, pray that we may be saved!

*Glory, Both now, Theotokion:*
By thy divine childbirth, O pure one, thou hast renewed the mortal nature of earthborn men that was corrupted in passions, and raised all from death unto the life of incorruption. Therefore as is meet we all call thee blessed, O all-glorified Virgin, even as thou didst foretell![^221]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
O all-immaculate Virgin, Mother of Christ God, a sword pierced thy most holy soul when thou beheldest Thy Son and God voluntarily crucified; Whom, O blessed one, cease not to entreat to grant us remission of transgressions!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
The Prophet, discerning in divine vision that Thou, O Word, wast to become incarnate of the shadowed mountain, the only Theotokos, with fear glorified Thy power![^222]

*Troparion:*
You appeared as noetic lambs, manifestly following the Shepherd and Universal King, *(Fol. 24v)*

and as crown-bearers you settled with the martyrs in the heavenly fold.[^223]

*Troparion:*
You appeared as a chosen pair, dividing the furrow of honorable and good witness; and you produced an ear of grain preserved in the heavenly granaries!

*Troparion:*
Cut down for Christ's sake, O valiant ones, in your feet, and heads, and nails, and hands, you uprooted the deception of impiety, and were revealed as victorious![^224]

*Theotokion:*
The tongue of earthborn mortals cannot worthily hymn thee, the Birthgiver of God, who wast revealed as the refuge of Christians, O all-immaculate, most pure one!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Rising early out of the night we cry unto Thee, O Lord: Save us! For Thou art our God, and we know none other beside Thee![^225]

*Troparion:*
Having been nourished as with milk by asceticism, O Galaction, thou didst attain unto the perfect fulfillment of the sufferings of Christ!

*Troparion:*
With a cleansed mind thou didst behold, O Episteme, the resting place of the saints taken up exceedingly high!

*Troparion:*
You obtained co-dwelling with the martyrs in the highest; immortal glory did you find, O venerable martyrs!

*Theotokion:*
In time thou gavest birth unto the Timeless One, O most pure one, Who became man that He might save man!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Grant me a robe of light, Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, O greatly merciful Christ our God![^226]

*Troparion:*
Through the laver of divine enlightenment you drew near unto the unblemished; and afterward being most perfectly baptized with blood, O sufferers![^227]

*Troparion:*
Having enlightened thy soul with much austerity through fasting, O Galaction, thou didst show it beautiful with the light of suffering!

*Troparion:*
Having mounted upon the chariot of your blood, O martyrs, you reached the heavenly path in which you rest!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst give birth unto the Son of equal honor with the Father, O thou who knewest not wedlock, and beyond understanding didst nourish with milk the Nourisher of all!

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*[^228]
You were numbered among the hosts of Christ's martyrs who valiantly contended, having radiantly struggled, O glorious Galaction, together with thy venerable spouse and fellow-sufferer Episteme: unceasingly pray unto the only God for us all!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^229]

*(Fol. 25r)*

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^230]
O Thou Who didst save the youths from the fire by an angel, and turned the roaring furnace into dew: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having betrothed thyself unto the Divine Word, O Episteme, thou didst blind the infidels who were striving to strip thee naked; and when they repented, thou didst show them to be children of light.[^231]

*Troparion:*
Utterly refusing to sacrifice unto lifeless gods, you offered yourselves, O martyrs, as an honorable sacrifice unto our true God and the Master of souls.

*Troparion:*
Brought unto the fire of torment, O Galaction, by streams of blood thou didst quench the flame of godlessness, O martyr, wisely crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
With all the highest heavenly ranks, with a loud voice we all, saved through thee, call thee blessed, O Maiden, Birthgiver of God!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^232]
Sing, ye priests, and let the people supremely exalt unto all ages: the Beginningless King of glory, before Whom the heavenly hosts tremble!

*Troparion:*
Equal in honor through purity, and being equal in fasting and suffering, you received equal gifts from God, O valiant sufferers!

*Troparion:*
You preserved your union in incorruption, having longed for the angelic life, with whom joyfully you worthily dance, O passion-bearers of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Manfully standing before the tribunal, O martyr, thou didst proclaim the One True God and Lord, and didst destroy the insolence of polytheism.

*Theotokion:*
Let us hymn, O ye people, the one Mother and Virgin after childbirth, as the honorable and highest throne of the Most High God!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^233]
The birthgiving of the Ever-Virgin revealed unto the Lawgiver upon the mountain in the fire and the burning bush, unto the salvation of us the faithful, we magnify with unceasing hymns!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast shown to be a heavenly pillar, O divinely wise Galaction, a foundation of the Church, a pillar of piety, a confirmation of martyrs and fasters, and a divine adornment!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst blossom forth in virginal flowers like a rose, and in the valleys of martyrdom thou sheddest sweet fragrance like a lily, O Episteme, virgin martyr of the Lord; therefore with one accord we call thee blessed!

*Troparion:*
Illumined by the brightness of the Tri-sunned Light, unto Him you have now passed over, having appeared as sons of light; pray that en- *(Fol. 25v)*

-lightenment may be granted, O martyrs, unto those who praise you in faith![^234]

*Theotokion:*
Thou art our weapon and wall, O Theotokos; thou art the protection of those who flee unto thee. Thee do we now stir up unto prayer, that we may be delivered from our enemies![^235]

*(Woodcut headpiece: Decorative baroque banner with floral scrollwork and central medallion)*

*On the same month, the 6th day: Our Father among the Saints, Paul the Confessor, Archbishop of Constantinople.*[^236]

*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera on 6, in Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*[^237]
The God-proclaiming Paul ordains thee as an imitator, called by the same name and adorned with his ways, O all-blessed one, inflamed with piety, and courage of soul, and endurance of afflictions, and zeal, O champion of Orthodoxy; with whom thou art also now glorified together in the heavenly mansions.[^238]

*Sticheron 2, Podoben the same:*
With the firm cords of thy dogmas, O father, hieromartyr, thou didst choke godless Arius and malignant Macedonius; and by the upright word of teaching thou didst confirm the multitudes of the Orthodox. Therefore, accepting thy most radiant confession, the Lover of mankind showed thee to be a partaker of the Kingdom.[^239]

*Sticheron 3, Podoben the same:*
When thou hadst finished the course and kept the faith, O blessed hierarch, Christ crowned thee with a radiant crown of righteousness, and adorned thy confession, O marvelous one. Therefore, having received the heavenly inheritance, pray unto the Savior for those who sing of thee![^240]

*Sticheron 4, Podoben the same:*
O all-blessed Paul, namesake of confession, having become a fervent defender of those who praise thee well: from every tribulation, from every sin, and the storm of passions, and torment do thou deliver them, as an unconquerable martyr and an acceptable hierarch; for thou hast acquired boldness before Christ our God!

*Glory, in Tone 4, by Germanus:*[^241]
Clad in the hierarch's vestment, O venerable father, thou didst emulate thy namesake Paul; having endured persecutions and tribulations, in thine own con- *(Fol. 26r)*

-tinual afflictions thou didst put to shame the harmful opinions of Arius; for having suffered for the Beginningless and Consubstantial Trinity, thou didst bring low malignant Macedonius, who fought against the Spirit; and having clarified the Orthodox faith unto all, thou art lodged with the incorporeal angels: with whom also now pray that our souls may be saved![^242]

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "O all-praised martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*[^243]
Beholding Thy unjust slaughter, O Christ, the Virgin wept and cried aloud unto Thee: "O Child most sweet, how dost Thou die without justice? How dost Thou hang upon the Tree, Thou Who didst hang the whole earth upon the waters? Leave me not alone, O greatly merciful Benefactor, Thy mother and handmaid, I pray Thee!"

*At the Aposticha, in the Octoechos.*

*Then the verse: Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice.*[^244]

*Sticheron, in Tone 1:*
O venerable father Paul, clothed in virtue from Christ God, thou didst valiantly conquer every host, demonic and barbarian, being strengthened by faith. Upon the rock thou didst establish thy flock unharmed by any heresy. Therefore, dancing with the angels, pray unto the Savior that our souls may be preserved in peace!

*Glory, in Tone 2, by Byzantios:*[^245]
Having crossed the sea of fasting with the wind of temperance, thou didst escape the storm of passions, O venerable one; therefore, being named as namesake unto the divine Paul, thou didst endure persecutions and tribulations, being afflicted by the tongue-inflicted pains of heretics. Therefore thou didst bring low the opinions of Arius, and having overcome the heresies of Nestorius,[^246] thou wast shown to be a zealot of Christ's Church. Pray unto Him, O blessed hierarch, that our souls may be saved!

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дрѣ́ва):*[^247]
When the undefiled Ewe-lamb beheld her Lamb voluntarily drawn unto slaughter as a man, weeping she said: "Dost Thou hasten now to make me childless, O Christ, who gave Thee birth? What is this that Thou hast done, O Deliverer of all? Yet I hymn and glorify Thine extreme goodness that passes understanding and speech, O Lover of mankind!"

*Troparion, in Tone 3:*[^248]
By the confession of divine faith, the Church revealed thee unto the priests as another Paul, a zealot; together with thee Abel cries aloud unto the Lord, and the blood of Zechariah *(Fol. 26v)*

-righteous blood! O venerable father, entreat Christ God that great mercy may be granted unto us![^249]

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos, and the canon of the saint on 6; whose acrostic is: Wisely do I hymn Paul the mystagogue. By Theophanes.*[^250]

*Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^251]
I shall open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I shall pour forth a word unto the Queen Mother; and I shall appear radiantly celebrating, and I shall sing with joy her marvels!

*Troparion:*
The confirmation of the faith, teacher of the Church, and unshakable pillar of confession, most radiant luminary of grace, and fire-breathing mouth, do we proclaim thee, O Paul!

*Troparion:*
Paul the greatest, the sun of the universe, O thrice-blessed one, puts thee forward as a second Paul, like a fire strongly consuming heresies, and an axe cutting down godlessness!

*Troparion:*
Lawfully didst thou contend, standing in the forefront, O God-proclaiming one, for the divine proclamation, as a faithful hierarch; and by the cords of thy dogmas thou didst choke, like a wild beast, vainglorious Arius!

*Theotokion:*
Come, let us all hymn the most pure Mother, who alone adorned humanity, and gave birth unto God incarnate, yet remained an unblemished Virgin!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^252]
Establish thy singers, O Theotokos, living and inexhaustible Fountain, who have gathered as a spiritual choir; and in thy divine glory vouchsafe them crowns of glory!

*Troparion:*
By adoption through divine grace, following the dogmas of God-bearing Paul, thou didst not reduce the only-begotten Son by nature unto a creature, O Paul, Who is co-beginningless with the Father!

*Troparion:*
With mouth, heart, and tongue, thou didst proclaim Christ, O God-wise and venerable Paul, as the Wisdom and Power of God, the Hypostatic Word, having refuted malignant Arius!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst proclaim by righteous judgment, O all-wise one, the Holy Spirit of God of super-essential authority, whereby we are deified, to be God by nature, both all-working and all-powerful!

*Theotokion:*
The Word of the Beginningless Father, being above every beginning, now took a beginning incarnate of thee, O pure one, and came under time, He Who is higher than all times!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 3:*[^253]
Holding fast to the divine dogma, thou didst escape the godless speech, O God-wise Paul, putting Arius to shame; for thou didst proclaim unto the faithful the Son consubstantial with the Father, *(Fol. 27r)*

having confirmed them. O venerable father, entreat Christ God that great mercy may be granted unto us![^254]

*Glory, in Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^255]
As namesake, O father, and imitator of the chosen vessel, thou didst endure tribulations and persecutions for the sake of the faith; and even as he came unto Rome, O venerable one, everywhere proclaiming the equal honor of the Trinity, so also having finished thy course in Armenia, thou didst worthily receive the crown from the Lord, having put to shame Macedonius and godless Arius. Therefore entreat Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love![^256]

*Both now, Theotokion:*
As a virgin and only one among women, who without seed gavest birth in the flesh unto God, all generations of men call thee blessed; for the fire of the Godhead dwelt in thee, and as an infant thou didst nurse the Creator and Lord. Therefore we, the angelic and human race, worthily glorify thy most holy childbirth, and with one accord cry aloud unto thee: Entreat Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who venerate thy most holy childbirth in faith!

*Stavrotheotokion:*[^257]
Beholding the Lamb, and Shepherd, and Deliverer upon the Cross, the Ewe-lamb exclaimed, weeping and bitterly wailing, crying aloud: "The world indeed rejoices, receiving deliverance through Thee; but my bowels burn, beholding Thy crucifixion which Thou endurest out of tender mercy of compassion, O long-suffering Lord, Abyss of mercy and Inexhaustible Fountain! Have mercy, and grant remission of sins unto those who hymn Thy divine passions in faith!"

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^258]
Discerning the unsearchable divine counsel of Thine incarnation from the Virgin, O Thou Most High, the Prophet Habakkuk cried: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
The Creator placed upon thy head, with His life-bearing right hand, a priceless honor, the crown of confession, as unto a victor, O divinely blessed and glorious Paul!

*Troparion:*
Even as thou didst contend beforehand for the sake of pious dogmas, O all-wise one, thou hast received recompense, having now obtained the Tree of Life, O blessed, divinely blessed, marvelous Paul!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast vouchsafed to dance upon the heavenly earth, where the feet of the meek dance, as a radiant ascetic, having been a champion of truth, O all-honorable Paul!

*Theotokion:*
O Savior, seen as Son consubstantial with the Father, of the Virgin Thou didst become incarnate consubstantial with us, *(Fol. 27v)*

having willed to save mankind![^259]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^260]
All things were amazed at thy divine glory; for thou, O Virgin who knewest not wedlock, didst hold in thy womb God over all, and gavest birth unto the Timeless Son, granting peace unto all who hymn thee!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst stop the creeping course and rottenness of heresy, O God-wise one, by applying as an exquisite cure, O father, thy confession, and the brightness of thy dogmas, and the purest mind, and divine zeal!

*Troparion:*
Richly was the grace of the Holy Spirit poured out upon thy lips, O all-blessed one, having found thee an exquisite and truly strong champion of Orthodoxy among the faithful. Therefore thou didst enlighten the divine councils!

*Troparion:*
The godless weaving of Arius, and the harmful speech of Macedonius, O Paul, thou didst sling down with thy divinely inspired dogmas and teachings, as David did the Philistine of old, having choked them and firmly cast them down![^261]

*Theotokion:*
The Pre-eternal Son now came under time, having taken ensouled and intelligent flesh, the Beginningless Word, from thee, O pure one who knewest not wedlock, granting peace unto all who sing of thee!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^262]
I have come into the depths of the sea, and the storm of many sins has drowned me; but as God, lead my life up from the abyss, O Greatly Merciful One!

*Troparion:*
Arius, who spoke harmful blasphemy against the height and brought down the Son and Word of God into a creature, was condemned by thee, O wretched one, O God-wise father!

*Troparion:*
Senseless, foolish, and godless Macedonius, who rejected the Divine Spirit, O father, was cast down by thy steadfast resistance, O divinely blessed one!

*Troparion:*
The creeping serpent, who assembled a host of heresies, is slain by thy life-giving words, O all-blessed hierarch of God, most sacred God-proclaimer!

*Theotokion:*
We hymn, O Virgin Mother of God, thy childbirth beyond nature and thine undefiled purity; for in thee virginity and incorrupt childbirth marvelously met together!

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*[^263]
Having shone upon the earth like an unsetting star, thou now enlightenest the Catholic Church, for which thou didst also suffer, having laid down thy soul, O Paul; and even as the blood of Zechariah and Abel, clearly cries *(Fol. 28r)*

thy blood unto the Lord![^264]

*Ikos:*[^265]
From above thou didst have thy calling, O Paul, but thy birth was below from the earth, being full like a beautiful garden. For as from paradise thou didst blossom forth by fasting, exhaling sweet fragrance from the odor of thy many labors, struggles, sweats, exile, hunger, thirst, and every affliction; through which thou didst pass with good hope, and adorned with the crown of victory: for thy blood cries unto the Lord!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^266]
The God-wise youths did not serve the creature rather than the Creator; but manfully trampling upon the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst come unto the heavenly tabernacles, O God-wise Paul, and drawing near unto God, thou wast deified by divine communion, singing, O venerable one: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Instructed by thy teachings, O all-praised Paul, we are taught to venerate in three suns the undivided, unconfused Godhead, unto Whom we also sing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
As a most sacred, divine, and God-pleasing confession, like gold in a furnace, thou didst offer thyself unto God as an acceptable sacrifice, rejoicing, O venerable one, in the imitation of the passions of our Savior!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast revealed as the only intercessor of divine deliverance for all men, having given birth unto the Deliverer of all, O all-immaculate one; unto Whom we all sing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^267]
The childbirth of the Mother of God saved the pious youths in the furnace: then indeed prefigured, but now in reality, it stirs up the whole universe to sing unto Thee: Hymn the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
The fountains of thy dogmas flow and water the whole Church, and with thine honorable blood, O father, thou hast sanctified all those who have followed thee in Orthodox faith, crying: Hymn the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Thou hast now anchored in the quiet haven, having shaken off the billows of life; for thou hadst the Lord as the Pilot directing thy whole life, O all-praised Paul, Who by His nod creates all things, Whom we supremely exalt unto all ages!

*(Fol. 28v)*

*Troparion:*
The tri-radiant light of the Super-divine Trinity, dwelling in thee, showed thee to be a second light, enlightening the assembly of the Orthodox, but darkening the heretical host, O father, as they cry: Hymn the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^268]

*Theotokion:*
Following the prophetic voices, O Virgin, we proclaim thee as the Birthgiver of God; for thou gavest birth unto the Child more ancient than all, Who is called Emmanuel; unto Whom we now cry: Hymn the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^269]
Let every earthborn mortal leap for joy, enlightened by the Spirit; and let the nature of the bodiless minds celebrate, honoring the sacred solemnity of the Mother of God, and let it cry aloud: Rejoice, O all-blessed Theotokos, pure Ever-Virgin!

*Troparion:*
I bring my whole self, O God-inspired head, unto thy divine protection; as a hieromartyr having received authority from Christ to loose transgressions, tear apart the bonds of my sins, save me by thy prayers, and enlighten me with divine light!

*Troparion:*
A new Paul hast thou appeared, inflamed with zeal, O most excellent one, who now in paradise hast heard ineffable words, O father! For as a partaker of his ways, thou art also a sharer of his name, and hast received the most comely crown of Christ's Kingdom![^270]

*Troparion:*
As a valiant accuser of every heresy wast thou revealed, and a divine champion of Orthodoxy, O hieromartyr; being enlightened with rays of grace, and shining with the light of the Uncreated Trinity, O all-glorious Paul!

*Theotokion:*
The Word was clothed in flesh from thee, O all-immaculate one, and having become God-man He lived in the world as the Compassionate One, remaining no less bodiless than before; and him that afflicted all of old He brought down by divine power!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во ст҃и́лищи):*[^271]
Inflamed with zeal from a warm heart, thou wast revealed as a spiritual champion of grace, cutting through the heretical assembly with the sword of thy words, O hierarch; and having finished the course, thou wast an equal contender with the multitude of martyrs!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast the all-immaculate Bride of the ineffable bearing in the womb, and as the most honorable temple, O Theotokos; for the Pre-eternal Light dwelt in thee, and thou gavest birth *(Fol. 29r)*

unto God the Word. Hymning thy childbirth we worthily magnify thee, O all-immaculate Maiden![^272]

*At the Aposticha, in the Octoechos.*

*Glory, in Tone 7:*[^273]
Thou didst penetrate into the depths of the Spirit, and having lived upon earth as one bodiless, from thence thou didst draw the wealth of divine knowledge. With Orthodoxy thou didst enrich mankind by thy teachings, O venerable father!

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion:*[^274]
Beholding the Lamb stretched upon the Tree, the Ewe-lamb and Virgin in the midst of two robbers, cried aloud: "Woe is me, O sweet Child! What is this strange and most glorious mystery? How has the lawless assembly nailed Thee upon the Cross, and given gall to drink unto Thee Who didst nourish mankind with manna?"

*At the Liturgy:*[^275]
*The Beatitudes of the Octoechos on 4; and from the canon of the saint, Ode 3 on 4.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7: The venerable ones shall boast in glory. Verse: Sing unto the Lord a new song.*
