*On the same month, the 7th day: The Holy Thirty-Three Martyrs of Melitene; and our Venerable Father and Wonderworker Lazarus, who fasted on Mount Galesion.*[^276]

*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera, in Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ въ мꙋ́ченицѣхъ):*[^277]
A divinely chosen army, a sacred host, a divine assembly, a holy people, a God-inspired company of martyrs, a fair gathering, an unbreakable fellowship, truly were you shown to be, O praiseworthy ones, and worthy citizens of the heavenly metropolis: therefore as is meet you are called blessed!

*Sticheron 2, Podoben the same:*[^278]
With Nicander let us honor Hesychius, Athanasius, Mamas, divine Barachius and Callinicus, Diogenes and Nicon, Longinus and Theodore, Valerius together with Xanthias, Theodulus and Callimachus, and Eugenius *(Fol. 29v)*

and Eugenius; having all assembled, together with divine Diodochus and Ostrychius let us honor them![^279]

*Sticheron 3, Podoben the same:*
The good Hieron, glorious Epiphanius, Maximian together with Ducitius, Claudian and Theophilus, and divine Gigantius, and Dorotheus faithfully, and Theodotus let us sing, and Castricius and Anicletus together with Themelius, and Eutychius with one accord, witnesses of the truth!

*Other Stichera of the Venerable One, in Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid all aside" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*[^280]
Having laid aside all the irrationality of passions, and subjected the flesh unto the spirit, thou wast a rule of virtue, a confirmation of monastics, an image of fasters, an adornment of the venerable. And now thou beholdest the ineffable beauty of thy Creator, ever feeding upon the good things that are in heaven: assembled together in spirit, in the songs of sweet melodies we celebrate thy honorable and all-festal memory!

*Sticheron 2, Podoben the same:*
Having shaken off all the heavy burden of earth, and having calmed the turbulent surges of the flesh, O wise one, by thy breathings, thou didst remain unmoved by passions: as a pillar strengthened with spiritual armor by a valiant mind. And now thou hast truly obtained divine vision and brightness, and unto Him Whom thou didst desire hast thou passed over, delighting in His unending light, deified by adoption![^281]

*Sticheron 3, Podoben the same:*
Emulating Elijah, and John the Luminary, having loved the light, to keep silence in the mountains and deserts; ever learning divine walking with God, and advancing on the path of virtues: therefore thou didst reach the utmost desire, O all-wise one, and rejoicing thou standest before the tri-radiant light of the Trinity. From Whom directly receiving the divine ray, with boldness pray for our souls!

*Glory, in Tone 6:*[^282]
O venerable father, thou gavest not sleep unto thine eyes, nor slumber unto thine eyelids, until thou hadst freed soul and body from passions, and prepared thyself as a dwelling place of the Spirit. For Christ, having come with the Father, made an abode in thee; and having become a servant of the Consubstantial Trinity, O great proclaimer Lazarus, our father: pray for our souls!

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*[^283]
Beholding of old her Lamb drawn unto slaughter *(Fol. 30r)*

...earnestly followed Him, crying aloud these things unto Him: "Whither goest Thou, my sweetest Child, O Christ? For what cause dost Thou run this swift course so diligently, O Long-suffering One? O Jesus most desired, sinless, greatly merciful Lord, give a word unto Thy handmaid, O my dearly beloved Son; pass not by in silence, O Bountiful One, her who strangely gave Thee birth, O all-bountiful God Who grantest great mercy unto the world!"

*At the Aposticha, in the Octoechos.*

*Glory, in Tone 6:*
O venerable father, into all the earth went forth the report of thy correct deeds; therefore in the heavens hast thou found the reward of thy labors. Thou didst destroy the hosts of demons, and attained unto the ranks of angels, whose life thou didst blamelessly emulate. Having boldness toward Christ God, ask peace for our souls!

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*[^284]
Beholding the most lawless people unrighteously nailing Thee upon the Tree, O Savior, Thy Virgin and pure Mother, as Simeon foretold, was wounded in her bowels.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the tormentors, and crushed the powerless insolence of the demons. By their prayers save our souls!

*Glory, of the Venerable One, in Tone 8:*
By watchful prayers and tearful streams thou didst moisten the pillar, and by sighs from the depth didst bear fruit an hundredfold in thy labors; and thou wast a shepherd, granting forgiveness unto all, O our venerable father Lazarus: pray unto Christ God that our souls may be saved!

*At Matins, one canon of the Octoechos, and two of the saints.*

*Canon of the Martyrs.*

*Whose acrostic is:*
Unto the wise martyrs I offer this praise.

*Tone 8.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^285]
Having traversed the water as upon dry land, and having escaped from the Egyptian evil, the Israelite cried aloud: Let us sing unto our Deliverer and God!

*Troparion:*
Having become rich in divine heavenly powers, ask purification for all who praise your light-bearing memory, O good-victorious martyrs![^286]

*(Fol. 30v)*

Desiring to travel the path of martyrdom brightly, you endured with steadfastness all the tempest of torture, being strengthened by the Holy Spirit.

*Troparion:*
Luminaries did you appear upon earth, destroying the darkness of polytheism, O divine passion-bearers; therefore you receive the unsetting light.

*Theotokion:*
He Who by His nod makes all things is incarnate of thee beyond word, O pure Mother, Who crowned the passion-bearers that victoriously trampled the enemy.

*Another Canon of the Venerable One.*

*Whose acrostic is:*
A second prayer I sing unto thee, O thrice-blessed one.

*Tone 2.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^287]
Come, ye peoples, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He led forth from the bondage of Egypt, for He is glorified!

*Troparion:*
Come, ye faithful, faithfully rejoicing in the Divine Spirit, let us praise divine Lazarus, crying unto him: O blessed one, by thy prayers deliver us from tribulations!

*Troparion:*
God made Thee return again unto Thy fatherland, even though thou wouldst not; therefore, save me by Thy prayers who continually draw near unto passions!

*Troparion:*
Luminous God-given love, having richly shone upon thee, caused thee, O God-bearer, earnestly to lay down thy soul for thy neighbor.

*Theotokion:*
Save us, O all-immaculate Birthgiver of God, from all wrath and affliction, who bow before thy holy icon and confess thee in faith as the Mother of God!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^288]
O Lord, Chief Craftsman of the heavenly circle and Builder of the Church: do Thou establish me in Thy love, O Summit of desires, Confirmation of the faithful, O only Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
By thy sacred commands, O glorious Hieron, thou didst guide the sacred martyrs unto divine suffering, and didst cause them most gloriously to disregard tortures, O divinely blessed one!

*Troparion:*
By the crushing upon the tree, O holy ones, you imaged the saving mortal passion of the all-good Master, and you crushed the ruinous deceivers of darkness by the grace of the Almighty.

*Troparion:*
Having placed your hope upon the Lord of all, O God-beholding martyrs, you were entirely unmoved from the greater station, but lawfully completed the divine course by uprightness of character.

*Theotokion:*
O Maiden of many names, rejoice, O pure Lady, *(Fol. 31r)*

...who gavest birth unto the Uncircumscribed Word circumscribed in flesh, Whom the company of martyrs, confessing as God, suffered most steadfastly!

*Another, Heirmos:*[^289]
Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put sin to death, and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who sing of Thee!

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by divine power, O wise one, thou wast delivered from ferocious beasts; therefore pray unto Christ to deliver from spiritual beasts those who sing of thee!

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by the power of Christ, O venerable one, Thou didst valiantly endure thirst, and wilderness hardship, and scarcity, in the hope of ineffable sweetness.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst escape the hostile assaults of the descendants of the Hagarenes, O all-blessed one, being sheltered by divine grace, and being preserved for the benefit of many.

*Theotokion:*
O pure Virgin, beyond word thou didst ineffably give birth unto the Master of all: entreat Him, O all-hymned one, to change the dominion of passions for those who sing of thee!

*Kontakion of the Venerable One, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ):*[^290]
As a great luminary the Church of Christ glorifies Thee with rejoicing in psalmody; therefore cease not to pray unto Christ to grant forgiveness of transgressions unto all!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆диви́ся):*[^291]
Having shown steadfast courage, O wise ones, you blunted the all-malicious wiles of the enemy, having preached Christ in the judgment hall. Therefore beheaded with swords, you were crowned by the divine right hand, thirty-three blessed ones, citizens of Melitene: remember us who honor you in faith, O honorable martyrs!

*Glory, of the Venerable One, in Tone 3, Podoben: "Of the divine faith" (Бж҃твенныя вѣ́ры):*[^292]
Having a divine mind in thy heart, O venerable one, thou didst exchange earthly things for divine and lasting things, and thou dancest together with the angels, enjoying the unsetting light and rejoicing unceasingly: therefore, O venerable one, pray unto Christ God to grant great mercy unto us!

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Thou wast the divine tabernacle of the Word, O only all-immaculate Virgin Mother, who in purity didst surpass the angels. Cleanse me, who have become clay above all others and am defiled by carnal transgressions, by the divine waters of thy prayers, granting great mercy, O pure one!

*(Fol. 31v)*

...great mercy.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding hanging upon the Cross the One Who sprouted from her without pain, the undefiled Ewe-lamb of the Word, the incorrupt Virgin Mother, weeping maternally, cried aloud: "Woe is me, my Child! How art Thou suffering willingly, wishing to deliver man from the passions of dishonor?"

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^293]
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power; Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who hast not left the bosom of the Father, and hast visited our poverty. Therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
With the rays of divine struggles, O all-rich ones, you most gloriously enlighten all the ends of the universe, and drive away the darkness of invisible enemies; therefore in pious wisdom we celebrate your light-bearing and divine solemnity.

*Troparion:*
Having all equally completed the struggle, O wise ones, you were equally accounted worthy of honors, having given your blood for the One Who suffered and willingly shed His divine blood upon the Tree for our salvation; therefore we call you blessed.

*Troparion:*
Now let us praise the wise martyrs: Diogenes, and Mamas, Hieron, Claudian, Nicon together with Nicander, Longinus, and Hesychius, and Barachius, Callinicus the great, and divine Xanthias, Theophilus, and Valerius.

*Troparion:*
Having sevenfold rushed unto the struggles, O all-glorious ones, you found the divine grace of the Deliverer working all things; and you endured all tortures with valiant mind, gratefully singing unto Christ: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:*
The shadows of the Law and the riddles of the prophets preannounced thee of old as having become the Mother of the Deliverer. Beholding now their fulfillment, O all-immaculate one, with one accord we hymn thee, O glory of passion-bearers and strength of the holy martyrs!

*Another. Heirmos:*[^294]
I hymn Thee, O Lord, for I have heard report of Thee and was afraid; for Thou comest unto me, seeking me who am astray. Therefore I glorify Thy great condescension toward me, O Greatly Merciful One!

*Troparion:*
Having fled from attachment and love of all temporal things, O venerable one, thou didst ever possess all thy hope in God; and that which thou didst acquire, the hands of the poor received.

*Troparion:*
Repelling the malice of demons like the assaults *(Fol. 32r)*

...of wild beasts, O venerable one, thou didst remain completely untouched by it, O blessed one, being sheltered by divine grace, which ever protects thee in all things.

*Troparion:*
The all-wicked one sought to weaken thy strength, O venerable one, beholding thy love and thanksgiving toward God; therefore He stirred up dogs against thee, but in vain was his cunning exposed.

*Theotokion:*
I hymn thee, O Mother of God and Lady, and I cry aloud unto thee: Sanctify and preserve me by thy prayer, and guide unto salvation him who falls into many sins and is shaken by demonic assaults!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^295]
Why hast Thou cast me away from Thy countenance, O Unsetting Light, and an alien darkness has covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and direct my paths toward the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee!

*Troparion:*
Honoring the wise passion-bearers, Maximian, and divine Eugenius, with Diodorus, Ducitius, Callimachus, together with Diodolus and Dorotheus, let us praise them who manfully completed the struggle!

*Troparion:*
The valiant soldiers, willingly put to death and crushed, inherited eternal immortality, and now dance in the expanse of paradise, having received the blessed hope.

*Troparion:*
Having cast off the slumber of negligence, O all-praised ones, at the time of the struggles you ran together with divine vigilance the course of martyrdom of divine faith, and have now arrived at the heavenly haven.

*Theotokion:*
Bound with the cords of transgressions, O all-hymned Lady, who didst loose the bonds of Hades by thy divine childbirth, loose me, I pray thee; and make haste to tread the paths that lead unto life!

*Another. Heirmos:*[^296]
O Giver of light and Creator of the ages, O Lord, guide us in the light of Thy commandments, for we know no other God save Thee!

*Troparion:*
The evil one, hoping to cast down the firmness of thy soul and the steadfastness of thy mind, O venerable one, having transformed himself into a dog, thus came to bite thee.

*Troparion:*
In great scarcity and perplexity, the enemy was put to retreat, seeing thee, O blessed one, not at all troubled, but rather bearing scarcity with thanksgiving.

*Troparion:*
Having ever in thy hands as a weapon the Cross of evil-destroying power, O venerable one, thou didst crush all the working of the enemy's wiles like dust.

*Theotokion:*
O Hope of the hopeless *(Fol. 32v)*

...and Protectress of the faithful, save me, O Mother of God, from all violence of enemies, invisible and visible, O all-hymned one!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^297]
Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are my transgressions, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray; for unto Thee have I cried, and do Thou hear me, O God of my salvation!

*Troparion:*
In hymns let us duly call blessed the sufferer Theodotus, Hilarion, wise Gigantius, and Athanasius, and divine Eutychius with Epiphanius.

*Troparion:*
Let Hieron and Diodotus, wise Castricius, and divine Ostrychius, great Themelius, with Ammonitus, be faithfully blessed, the valiant martyrs of Christ!

*Troparion:*
Having drowned the invisible Pharaoh with all his host in the stream of your blood, O good-victorious martyrs, you reached the heavens and adorned the Church of the firstborn.

*Theotokion:*
The weapons of the enemy have failed, O Birthgiver of God, since Christ Whom thou gavest birth was pierced with a spear, rebuilding with blood and water the men who had grown old.

*Another. Heirmos:*[^298]
Unto the Lord from the sea-monster Jonah cried aloud: Lead me up from the depth of Hades, I pray, that as unto a Deliverer, with the voice of praise and in the spirit of truth, I may sacrifice unto Thee!

*Troparion:*
Desiring to show thy heart as a temple unto God, O venerable one, thou didst visit the churches of the saints, from whom thou didst receive the grace of the Holy Spirit abundantly, for the confirmation of many men.

*Troparion:*
Thy fatherland received thee back as a costly treasure, O God-wise one, by divine judgment. Therefore, O sacred venerable one, make me who am an alien a fellow-heir of the heavenly fatherland.

*Troparion:*
The church of the Virgin Martyr Marina first received thee as an inhabitant, in which like an unsetting star thou didst shine forth, O venerable one, illuminating those who were asleep in the darkness of ignorance.

*Theotokion:*
Entreat Thy Son and Lord, O Virgin, for thy servants who in faith ever bow before the honorable icon of thy likeness, O all-immaculate one, for thou art able!

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "As first-fruits of nature" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ нача́тки):*[^299]
A light-bearing company of martyrs, having assembled unto us in spiritual understanding, has enlightened the Church today with marvelous rays. Therefore, celebrating their honorable memory, we ask *(Fol. 33r)*

...of Thee, O our Savior: by their prayers deliver us from tribulations, that we may sing unto Thee: Alleluia!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^300]
The youths who arrived from Judea in Babylon of old trampled down the flame of the furnace by faith in the Trinity, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Beholding thy venerable hand severed for the truth, O glorious Hieron, singing songs of thanksgiving unto the All-seeing One, thou didst cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
With elevated understanding thou wast a prototype for thy fellow sufferers, O glorious Hieron, and with them thou didst receive the lot of the Kingdom on high, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having appeared as valiant soldiers of the Eternal King, with the sword of your courage you destroyed the hosts of the deceiver, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth unto the Physician, O pure Virgin, heal the passions of my heart, and deliver me from eternal torture as in hymns I cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Another. Heirmos:*[^301]
The children appeared as most wise philosophers of old, for from a God-receiving soul, theologizing with their lips, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers and our God, the Super-divine!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst prepare an abundant table, full of the good things of thy divine virtues, wherewith feeding all, thou didst teach them to sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
The people, following the voice of thy most wise teachings, truly and earnestly set aside love of all temporal things, and chose dwelling with thee as a good thing, O all-blessed one.

*Troparion:*
Having acquired the pattern of the life of marvelous Simeon, like an adamant stone thou didst stand upon a pillar without a roof, crying aloud with joy: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers and our God, the Super-divine!

*Theotokion:*
Save me from the snares of enemies by thine intercession, O pure one, and bind me unto the utmost love of thy good Son, me who am ever estranged from Him by improper pleasures!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^302]
Having become victors over the tormentor and the flame by Thy grace, cleaving earnestly unto Thy commandments, the youths cried aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*(Fol. 33v)*

Having died unto the world, you inherit the life to come, and pour forth the grace of healings unto those who sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
As luminous luminaries you appeared through the splendors of sufferings, illuminating the world, O passion-bearing martyrs, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Cast into prison, O truly divine guardians of the truth, and having your flesh unmercifully wounded with ox-sinews, O blessed ones, you turned aside in no wise from the upright way; therefore you received crowns of victory.

*Troparion:*
Enlightened through faith by sacred words, we confess God the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Undivided Trinity: one Kingdom, one Lordship, and one Dominion, unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
As one holier than the angels, O pure one, thou didst receive the God of all Who rests in the saints; therefore all we the faithful hymn thee and glorify thee unto all ages!

*Another. Heirmos:*[^303]
Unto God Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew youths, and changed the flame into dew: sing, ye works, as unto the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Diligently having learned the ascetical struggles and contests from the fathers who attained perfection before thee, O father, thou didst take care not to seem second; and thus it not only appeared, but indeed even surpassed them.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst fulfill the prayer wherewith thou didst pray unto God of old, O thrice-blessed one, saying: "Thy bread I offer unto all, and Thine own of Thine own we offer unto Thee, O Lord of glory, unto all ages!"

*Troparion:*
By word and deed, O father, guiding those who were with thee unto the divine path, and thyself being guided unto it far more than they, whereby thou didst work wonders; for God, through thy prayers, multiplied the threshing floor.

*Theotokion:*
Let heaven rejoice, and let the earth be glad with mankind, for the Virgin Mary ineffably gave birth unto the Creator of all; unto Whom we sing: We supremely exalt Thee, O Christ, unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^304]
Heaven was terrified at this, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God appeared bodily unto men, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens. Therefore the hierarchies of angels and men magnify thee as the Mother of God!

*(Fol. 34r)*

Thou wast able, being strengthened by divine power, O most marvelous Hieron, to vanquish the treacherous one by fortitude of mind; and thou didst bring unto Christ an assembly of passion-bearers by thy teachings, with whom in faith we ever call thee blessed.

*Troparion:*
You appeared as an honorable host gathered in Christ, O renowned ones, and resisted the powers of the ruler of this world; and having conquered them with the weapon of divine faith, you received crowns from the Life-originating hand, rejoicing.

*Troparion:*
Leap for joy, O Melitene, having brought unto the Almighty a numerous assembly of honorable martyrs, whom the former metropolis possesses, who have completed the sacred course; and with all cities faithfully call them blessed evermore!

*Troparion:*
O Unsetting Sun, Christ, by the prayers of Thy glorious martyrs, enlighten and sanctify with bright rays those who celebrate their light-bearing and divine suffering, and as God make them partakers of the Kingdom there!

*Theotokion:*
I tremble at Thy judgment to come, O only King, and am afraid lest I be cast into passion and torment; but cleanse me from all defilement of sin, by the prayers of Thy most pure Mother, as Lover of mankind!

*Another. Heirmos:*[^305]
God the Word of God, Who by ineffable wisdom came to renew Adam, who through eating had grievously fallen into corruption, and Who for our sake was ineffably incarnate of the Holy Virgin: with one accord we the faithful magnify in hymns!

*Troparion:*
Woe is me! In slothfulness have I finished all my life, and I fear the Dread Judgment; but O Lord, Lover of mankind, through the prayers of Lazarus send unto me streams of tears, that thereby I may wash away the defilement of my transgressions!

*Troparion:*
Having a calm soul, thou didst have a gentle appearance in beauty, O father, and didst show thyself courteous unto all, watering souls with the streams of thy words, O wise one: entreat Christ to grant that tranquility unto us also!

*Troparion:*
God, wishing to make known unto all thy virtue after the divine manner, caused thee, O venerable one, to ascend the rugged mountain, from whence, O father, sending forth more abundantly the rays of thy life, thou didst enlighten the universe.

*Theotokion:*
Show Thy Son, Whom thou gavest birth without seed, to be merciful unto me then as Judge, at the time when He shall sit, as it is written, *(Fol. 34v)*

...upon the holy throne, O Maiden, to judge all earthborn mortals concerning the improper things they did in life!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены̀ оу҆слы́шите):*[^306]
Protected by the weapon of Thy precious Cross, Thy passion-bearers, O Word, strongly conquered the opposing powers, and put the tormentor to shame; they suffered for Thy sake, and reign together with Thee, O my Christ, King of all!

*And of the Venerable One, Podoben: "Thou Who didst adorn heaven with stars" (Нб҃о ѕвѣзда́ми):*[^307]
All we praise in hymns the God-bearer and imitator of the Master, ever-memorable Lazarus, who destroyed the fierce cruelty of demons by divine power!

*Theotokion:*
Daniel prefigured thee as the unhewn mountain, from which the precious stone was cut without hands, crushing the idol temples, O Birthgiver of God, Mary!

*On the same month, the 8th day: The Synaxis of the Holy Archangel Michael, and the Other Bodiless Powers.*[^309]

*If it be the temple of the Synaxis of the Holy Archangel Michael, or if the superior wish to celebrate a vigil:*
*At Small Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried," stichera on 4, in Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*[^310]
O bodiless angels, standing before the throne of God, and illuminated by the splendors thence, ever shining with outpourings of light, and becoming secondary lights: pray unto Christ that He grant peace and great mercy unto our souls! *Twice.*

*(Fol. 35r)*

Immortal angels, having truly received from the First Life an imperishable life, O all-blessed ones: ye have become holy beholders of the wisdom of everlasting glory,[^311] being filled with light, and fittingly revealed as radiating beacons!

Archangels, angels, principalities, thrones, dominions, and six-winged seraphim, and many-eyed divine cherubim, instruments of wisdom; most divine powers and authorities: pray unto Christ that He grant peace and great mercy unto our souls!

*Glory, in Tone 4:*
O leader of the ranks of angels, who standest in the heavens before the throne of the Three-Sun Divinity, and art richly illumined by divine splendors unceasingly issuing from thence: deliver from the gloom of passions and irradiate with enlightenment us who are consecrated upon earth, joyfully singing the Thrice-Holy hymn, O Archistrategos Michael, intercessor for our souls!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*At the Aposticha, stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*[^312]
The archangelic powers, O Christ, standing before Thy throne, pray for the human race: by their supplications, therefore, cast down the audacity of the nations, and grant peace unto all the faithful!

*Verse: Who makes His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire.*[^313]
Circling about the throne of the King of all, ever dancing in choir, O ranks of angels: preserve us who call upon you in faith, and deliver all from torment![^314]

*Verse: Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His hosts.*[^315]
God the Father Who is over all, together with the Only-Begotten Word and the Spirit, brought forth the powers of heavenly minds, formless and immaterial, as chanters of His Three-Sun glory!

*Glory, and now, Theotokion, the same Podoben:*
Rejoice, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, in unison with Gabriel we cry aloud unto thee: for having received from above the most-divine joy, do thou fill all of us with joy!

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Leaders of the heavenly hosts, we the unworthy ever beseech you, that by your prayers you may shelter us beneath the roof of the wings of your immaterial glory, preserving us who fall down diligently and cry aloud: Deliver us from afflictions, as commanders of the higher powers!

*(Fol. 35v)*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion: The same [Tone 4].*[^316]

*At Great Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried," stichera on 8, in Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́бля):*[^317]
Appearing as the brightest champion of the Three-Sun Godhead, O Archistrategos Michael, with the heavenly hosts thou dost cry rejoicing: Holy art Thou, O Father; holy art Thou, O co-unoriginate Word; holy art Thou, O Holy Spirit: one glory, one kingdom and essence, one Godhead and power!

Fiery is thine appearance, and marvelous is thy beauty, O Michael, first among angels! For with immaterial nature thou dost traverse the ends of the earth, fulfilling the commands of the Creator of all; known to be mighty in thy strength, and making thy temple, revered by thy holy name, a fount of healings.

Thou Who makest Thine angels spirits, as it is written, and Thy ministers a flame of fire: Thou hast revealed, O Lord, Michael the Archistrategos holding primacy amidst the ranks of Thine archangels, obeying Thy nod, O Word, and proclaiming with fear the Thrice-Holy hymn unto Thy glory!

*Other Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*[^318]
The Pre-eternal Mind established thee, Gabriel, as a second light, illuminating the whole universe by divine partakings, and revealing unto us the truly divine and great mystery hidden from the ages: that He Who is bodiless is incarnate in a virginal womb, and become man, in order to save man!

Standing before the throne of the Three-Sun Godhead, and richly illuminated by divine splendors unceasingly issuing from thence: deliver from the gloom of passions and irradiate with enlightenment us who are consecrated, joyfully keeping festival on earth and praising thee, O Archistrategos Gabriel, intercessor for our souls!

Tame the rages of the Hagarenes that frequently assail thy flock; put an end to divisions in the Church; calm the tempest of boundless temptations; deliver from perils and tribulations those who honor thee with love and flee beneath thy protection, O Archistrategos Gabriel, intercessor for our souls!

*Glory, in Tone 6, by Byzantios:*[^319]
Rejoice together with us, all ye angelic ranks of leaders: for your prime leader and our protector, the great Archistrategos, appearing today in his precious temple, marvelously sanctifies it.

*(Fol. 36r)*

Therefore, chanting hymns as is fitting, let us cry aloud unto him: Shelter us beneath the cover of thy wings, O most great Archangel Michael!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Rejoice together with us, all ye choirs of virgins: for our protectress, mediatress, shelter, and great refuge, on this present day, in her precious and divine temple, consoles the sorrowful. Therefore, chanting hymns unto her as is fitting, let us cry aloud: Shelter us by thy divine intercession, O most pure Sovereign Lady Birthgiver of God!

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day.*

*The Reading from Joshua the Son of Nun (Chapter 5):*[^320]
It came to pass, when Joshua was by Jericho, that he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, there stood a man before him with his sword drawn in his hand. And Joshua went unto him, and said unto him: Art thou for us, or for our adversaries? And he said unto him: I am the Archistrategos of the host of the Lord; now am I come hither. And Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and said unto him: Sovereign Lord, what commandest thou unto thy servant? And the Archistrategos of the Lord said unto Joshua: Loose thy sandal from off thy feet; for the place whereon thou standest is holy. And Joshua did so.

*The Reading from the Judges of Israel (Chapter 6):*[^321]
In those days, Midian prevailed against the children of Israel, and they cried aloud unto the Lord God. And behold, an angel of the Lord came, and sat under the oak which was in Ophrah, in the land of Joash, the father of Abiezer; and Gideon his son was threshing wheat in the winepress, that he might flee with it from the face of Midian. And the angel of the Lord appeared unto him, and said unto him: The Lord is with thee, mighty in strength! And Gideon said unto him: In me, my lord? And if the Lord be with us, why then have all these evils found us? And where are all His marvelous deeds which our fathers told us of, saying: Did not the Lord bring us up out of Egypt? But now the Lord hath cast us off, and delivered us into the hand of Midian. And the angel of the Lord looked upon him, and said unto him: Go in this thy strength, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of Midian; behold, I have sent thee. And Gideon said unto him: In me, my lord? Wherewith shall I save Israel? Behold, my thousand is the poorest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house. And the angel of the Lord said unto him: I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite Midian as one man. And Gideon said unto him: If now I have found grace before thee, *(Fol. 36v)*

before thine eyes, and that thou wilt show me today a sign that thou talkest with me: depart not hence, until I come unto Thee, and bring forth my sacrifice, and offer it before Thee. And the angel of the Lord said unto Him: I am; and I will tarry until thou return. And Gideon went in, and prepared a kid of the goats, and an ephah of unleavened cakes of flour; and the flesh he put in a basket, and he poured the broth into a pot, and brought it out unto Him under the oak, and bowed down. And the angel of the Lord said unto Him: Take the flesh and the unleavened cakes, and lay them upon that rock, and pour out the broth. And he did so. And the angel of the Lord put forth the end of the staff that was in his hand, and touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and fire rose up out of the rock, and consumed the flesh and the unleavened cakes. And the angel of the Lord departed out of his sight. And Gideon saw that he was an angel of the Lord. And Gideon said: Alas for me, O Lord, O Lord! for I have seen the angel of the Lord face to face. And the Lord said unto Him: Peace be unto Thee; fear not, thou shalt not die. And Gideon built an altar there unto the Lord, and called it: The Peace of the Lord, unto this day.

*The Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 14):*[^322]
Thus says the Lord: Let all the earth cry aloud with gladness, and let the trees of Lebanon rejoice over thee. And the cedars of Lebanon shall say: Since thou art fallen asleep, no feller hath come up against us. Hades beneath was embittered meeting thee; coming upon thee, it stirred up against thee all the giants that ruled over the earth. All the kings of the nations have arisen from their thrones, all shall answer and say unto thee: And thou also art taken captive even as we, and art numbered among us! For thy glory hath gone down to Hades, and thy great joy; rottenness shall be spread under thee, and worms shall be thy covering. How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! He who sent unto all the nations is crushed to the ground. For thou saidst in thine heart:[^323] I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of heaven; I will sit upon a lofty mount, upon the lofty mountains toward the north; I will ascend above the clouds, I will be like unto the Most High. But now thou shalt go down to Hades, unto the foundations of the earth! And they that see thee shall wonder at thee, and shall say concerning thee: Is this the man that troubled the earth, that shook kings, that made the whole world a wilderness, and destroyed its cities, and loosed not those who were in captivity unto their homes? All the kings of the nations have slept in honor, *(Fol. 37r)*

every man in his own house. But thou shalt be cast out upon the mountains as an abominable corpse, with many dead that are thrust through with the sword, that go down to Hades. In what manner a garment defiled with blood shall not be clean, so neither shalt thou be clean; for thou hast wickedly destroyed My land, and slain My people: thou shalt not abide unto ages of ages![^324]

*At the Litiya, stichera, Tone 1, by Cyprian:*[^325]
Commanders of the noetic powers, who unceasingly stand before the Master's throne: pray unto the Lord that He grant peace unto the world, and great mercy unto our souls!

*By Arsenios:*[^326]
Michael, the leader of the hosts on high, the first-standing of the divine ranks, who ever walks with us, preserving all from every assault of the devil: hath summoned us today to festival! Come therefore, ye lovers of festivals and lovers of Christ, gathering the flowers of virtues with pure thoughts and an upright conscience, let us honor the assembly of the archangels: for standing unceasingly before God, and chanting the Thrice-Holy hymn, he prays that our souls may be saved!

*Tone 2, by the Studite:*[^327]
Leading the immaterial essence of the noetic hosts, and giving light to the universe by the splendors of the Three-Sun glory, O Archistrategoi: with unceasing voice ye sing the Thrice-Holy hymn. Pray ye, therefore, that our souls may be saved!

*The same Tone, by Arsenios:*
Surrounding the immaterial throne, O noetic essences, divine and bodiless ones, with fiery lips ye sing the Thrice-Holy hymn unto God the Ruler: Holy God, Father unoriginate; Holy Mighty, Son co-unoriginate; Holy Immortal, consubstantial Spirit, glorified together with the Father and the Son!

*By Anatolios:*[^328]
With bodiless lips and noetic mouths the angelic ranks offer unceasing hymnody unto Thy unapproachable Godhead, O Lord; and pure minds and ministers of Thy glory praise Thee, O Lord, together with whom the bodiless Michael and the most comely Gabriel, the first-standing of the celestial hosts, the archistrategoi of the angels, are become our hosts today: commanding us to sing the song of songs unto Thine unapproachable glory, O Lover of mankind, Whom they unceasingly beseech for our souls!

*(Fol. 37v)*

*Glory, in Tone 4:*
With fiery lips the cherubim hymn Thee, O Christ God, and with bodiless mouths the choir of archangels unceasingly glorifies Thee; and Michael, the Archistrategos of the hosts on high, unceasingly offers the triumphal hymn unto Thy glory. For he hath illumined us today unto bright festival: to raise aloft fittingly, according to the Psalms, the Thrice-Holy praise with earthen lips, for all things are filled with Thy praise; and thereby Thou dost grant great mercy unto the world!

*Now and ever, in the same Tone, by George of Nicomedia:*[^329]
Today the Virgin, the temple that is to contain God, is led into the temple of the Lord, and Zechariah receives her; today the Holy of Holies rejoices, and the angelic choir mystically keeps festival. With them let us also keep festival today, and with Gabriel let us cry aloud: Rejoice, thou who art full of grace, the Lord is with thee, Who hath great mercy!

*At the Aposticha, stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*[^330]
Keeping festival like angels in the world, let us cry aloud a hymn unto God Who sits upon the throne of glory: Holy art Thou, O heavenly Father; holy art Thou, O co-everlasting Word; holy art Thou, O all-holy Spirit!

*Verse: Who makes His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire.*[^331]
Holding primacy among the celestial ones with great boldness, and standing before the throne fearful in glory, O eyewitness of ineffable things: save us, O Archistrategos Michael, who are in the distress of afflictions and perils, by thy prayers, we beseech thee!

*Verse: Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His hosts.*[^332]
Thou art the first of the bodiless angels, and minister of that divine illumination, an eyewitness and initiate of mysteries: save us, O Archistrategos Michael, who year by year piously honor thee and faithfully hymn the Trinity!

*Glory, and now, Tone 8, by John the Monk:*[^333]
As commander and champion and prince of angels, O Archistrategos, deliver from every distress and sorrow, from diseases and cruel sins, those who faithfully praise and entreat thee, O glorious one! As one clearly beholding the Immaterial One, and illuminated by the unapproachable light of the Master's glory: for out of love for mankind He received flesh for our sake from the Virgin, desiring to save mankind!

*Troparion, Tone 4: Leaders of the heavenly hosts*[^334] *(Fol. 38r)*

*Leaders of the heavenly hosts... Twice.*
*Or if: At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion: Leaders of the heavenly hosts... Twice.*
*Glory, and now, Theotokion: The mystery hidden from the ages...*[^335]

*After the 1st Stikhologia, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*[^336]
Standing ever before the fearful throne, and illuminated by the bright rays of the Three-Sun Godhead, enlighten us who brightly celebrate your assembly, driving away the gloom of sins; and diligently pray, O most radiant intercessors, that we may be delivered from afflictions!

*Glory, in the same Tone, Podoben: "The choir of angels" (Ли́къ а҆́гглскїй):*[^337]
Having the divine Michael as archistrategos, the angelic choir together with him offers hymnody unto the Holy Trinity: for the Creator of all things brought forth from non-being the armies of fiery-visaged ranks by His word!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O all-holy Virgin, hope of Christians, whom thou didst bear as God beyond mind and word: unceasingly beseech Him, together with the heavenly hosts, to grant remission of all our sins and amendment of life unto us who ever glorify thee in faith and love!

*After the 2nd Stikhologia, Sessional Hymn, Tone 2, Podoben: "When Thou didst descend" (Е҆гда̀ снизше́лъ є҆сѝ):*[^338]
Thou hast been revealed as the eldest amidst the angelic regiments, O Archistrategos Michael! Unceasingly beseech the King on high to cast down the pride of earthly oppressors; and as thou hast boldness before the fiery-visaged throne, unceasingly pray for us thy servants!

*Glory, in Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*[^339]
The many-eyed cherubim and seraphim, the armies of archangelic ministers, with authorities, thrones, dominions, angels, powers, and principalities: entreat Thee, our Creator, God, and Master, that Thou despise not the supplications of a people that hath sinned, O most merciful God!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O all-immaculate Virgin, who didst bear the transcendent God: unceasingly beseech Him, together with the bodiless hosts, to grant remission of transgressions and amendment of life before the end unto us who hymn thee as is fitting in faith and love, O only all-praised one!

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^340]
Having worthily become the guide of the heavenly ranks and the minister of divine glory by the command of thy Creator, thou art the intercessor for Christians, *(Fol. 38v)*

savingly overseeing earthly things by thine immaterial glory. Therefore we all praise thee as is fitting, hymning today thy divine solemnity, O Archistrategos Michael! Pray thou unto Christ God that He grant remission of sins unto those who keep thy holy solemnity with love!

*Glory, in Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*[^341]
The angelic ranks stand with fear before Thy throne, O Master, Christ God; and ever illuminated by the rays from thence, they unceasingly chant the triumphal hymn unto Thee. By their sacred prayers grant peace unto the world, and great mercy unto our souls!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O pure, all-immaculate, and unwedded Virgin Mother, who alone in time didst bear the timeless Son and Word of God: beseech Him, together with the honored, bodiless heavenly hosts, to grant us cleansing of sins and great mercy!

*Then the Gradual Hymns, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4.*
*Prokeimenon: Who makes His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire.*[^342]
*Verse: Bless the Lord, O my soul!*[^343]
*Let every breath.*
*Gospel: Matthew, pericope 52.*[^344]
*Glory: Through the prayers of the Archangels...*
*Now and ever: Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God...*
*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 6:*
Thine angels, O Christ, standing before the throne of majesty in fear, and ever illuminated by Thy light-outpourings, are Thy chanters on high and ministers of Thy counsel; being sent forth from Thee, they impart enlightenment unto our souls!

*Canon of the Birthgiver of God with the Heirmos on 6, Tone 8, the Heirmos twice: Let us sing unto the Lord, Who led His people... Written in the Oktoechos in the Eighth Tone, on Sunday at Matins, the third canon. And two canons of the Bodiless Hosts, on 8.*[^345]
*The First Canon, the composition of John the Monk, of which the acrostic is: Let all us the God-wise celebrate the assembly of the bodiless.*[^346]
*Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^347]
Let us the peoples send up a hymn unto our marvelous God, Who freed Israel from bondage, chanting a song of victory and crying aloud: We sing unto Thee, the only Master!

*Troparia:*
Let all us the faithful hymn the uncreated Trinity, which directs all the immaterial principalities of the celestial choirs, crying aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God Almighty!

Thou hast laid down the beginning of creatures, an immaterial essence, O Creator *(Fol. 39r)*

of angels, surrounding Thy most pure throne, to cry unto Thee: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God Almighty!

Rejoice, Gabriel, beholder of mysteries of the incarnation of God; and Michael, first-standing of the immaterial ranks: unceasingly crying, Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God Almighty!

*Theotokion:*
I tremble at the mystery of Thy condescension, O Christ: that being God by nature, Thou didst accept to be born of a Virgin as a man, that Thou mightest save the world from the bondage of the adversary!

*Second Canon, the composition of the same John the Monk, in the same Tone.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^348]
The marvel-working rod of Moses, striking the sea crosswise and dividing it, drowned Pharaoh the chariot-driver of old; and it saved Israel the fugitive, who traversed on foot, chanting a hymn unto God!

*Troparia:*
Joining our chorus, come let us praise in hymns the ranks of noetic bodiless hosts as divine ministers, who unceasingly pray for our salvation, and rejoice together over our repentance!

The princes of the angels, the pre-chosen and radiant commanders, arouse the bodiless minds today unto the completion of the festival of their radiant memory; together with them men rejoice, offering hymnody unto the Trinity!

Let us men rejoice spiritually today with the angels in joy: for Gabriel again now proclaims the union of churches and the overthrow of every contrary heresy, at the memorial of the Archistrategoi!

*Theotokion:*
Thou dost bring forth, O most pure one, Him Who is above nature, the Father's Word Who dwelt in thee through the Holy Spirit: existing in two natures and wills, yet immutable in one Hypostasis, Whose form we also venerate!

*Katavasia: I shall open my mouth...*[^349]
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^350]
Plant Thy fear, O Lord, in the hearts of Thy servants, and be Thou our establishment, who in truth call upon Thee!

*Troparia:*
By Thy power, O Immortal One, Thou hast established the mighty ones, who fulfill Thine all-holy will, ever standing before Thee on high!

As initiates of mysteries of Thine incarnation and honorable resurrection, O Christ, accept the angelic commanders *(Fol. 39v)*

who pray for us, O Christ!

As Thou art compassionate, Thou hast appointed angels as guardians unto men, and hast revealed them, O Christ, as ministers of the salvation of Thy pleasing ones!

*Theotokion:*
Ineffably didst thou conceive the Lord and Savior, O Bride of God, Who delivers from cruel afflictions us who call upon thee in truth!

*Second Canon. Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^351]
Thou art the establishment of those who flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit hymns Thee!

*Troparia:*
Thou hast appeared unto us as the foremost of angels, and a second light of the Trinity, O Prince Michael, who faithfully praise thee!

With the ray of divine grace Gabriel faithfully filled the whole earth, proclaiming the coming of God in the flesh!

O ever-hymned pair and radiant, immaterial twain: reveal as lights of God those who faithfully celebrate your memory!

*Theotokion:*
I hymn thy childbearing which is beyond mind, O pure one; I also sing, that I may obtain cleansing thereof!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded" (Повелѣ́нное та́йнѡ):*[^352]
Rulers of the heavenly hosts, and first-standing of the high-throned and fearful divine glory: Michael and Gabriel, archistrategoi, commanders of the angels, together with all the bodiless ones, with the celestial ministers: unceasingly praying for the world, entreat that remission of our transgressions be granted, and that we may find mercy and grace in the day of judgment! *Twice.*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
O graced, pure, and blessed one: for the sake of the compassions of mercy of Him Who was born of thee, unceasingly entreat Him, together with the celestial hosts, the archangels, and all the bodiless ones, to grant us merciful forgiveness of sins and amendment of life before the end, that we may find mercy!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^353]
Thou didst mount horses, Thine apostles, O Lord, and didst take their reins into Thy hands; and Thy riding became salvation unto those who faithfully chant: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparia:*
Thou didst mount angels as horses, O Lover of mankind, and didst take their reins into Thy hand; and Thy riding became salvation unto those who unceasingly cry aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

Thy virtue covers the angels, O Lover of mankind, and fills the ends of the earth with Thy glorious, unoriginate, divine *(Fol. 40r)*

divine praise, crying aloud unto Thee with them: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

Thou didst go forth, O Compassionate One, for the salvation of Thy people, O Christ; Thou dost summon Thy hosts as friends, and Thy coming became gladness unto those who faithfully cry aloud unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Theotokion:*
A virgin and mother hast thou supernaturally appeared, O all-pure one, having given birth unto the same Christ, both God and man, unto Whom the angelic ranks cry aloud with fear: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Second Canon. Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^354]
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art my power; Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who hast not left the Father's bosom, yet hast visited our poverty. Therefore, with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparia:*
At Jericho the Archistrategos of the host of the Lord appeared unto Joshua, son of Nun, who waged war of old; giving victory and fighting as champion was great Michael, being leader of the bodiless hosts; having received power from him, the servant of the Lord captured the adversaries, having taken them with the spear.

The leader of the bodiless hosts, Gabriel the great and truly divine archangel, appeared of old unto Zacharias the priest with the glad tidings of new wonders; therefore, John having been born as the voice of the Word, restored unto his father the voice of speech.

All the ends of the earth rejoice today with joy, celebrating the precious memory of Thine archangels, O God: divine Michael and godly-wise Gabriel; and all the angelic rank rejoices together, as the world is preserved by their protection.

*Theotokion:*
Thou alone hast remained pure even after childbirth; thou alone unwedded hast appeared nourishing with milk the true Word of the Father, Who through the Holy Spirit took the form of a servant for our sake, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, Whose divine likeness of form we honor and venerate![^355]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^356]
From the night of ignorance, wandering ever upon the soul-destroying path: guide me by the light of Thy knowledge, O Lord, directing me beforehand upon the pathway of Thy commandments!

*Troparia:*
Ever borne aloft by irreversible longing toward Thee on high, O Christ, the utmost of all desires: the angelic powers unceasingly glorify Thee!

Thou hast appointed Thine angels, spiritual in essence and incorruptible by Thy grace, O Christ, as singers of Thy majesty, having made them according to Thine image, *(Fol. 40v)*

O Incomprehensible One!

By drawing near unto Thee, O Christ, Thou hast preserved Thy servants uninclined toward what is worse; for Thou art the fountain of goodness, doing good unto those who worthily serve Thee.

*Theotokion:*
O all-immaculate one, who hast given birth unto the Guardian of life: revive my soul, slain by loathsome passions, and guide it unto the pathway of everlasting and blessed life!

*Second Canon. Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^357]
Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy presence, O Never-setting Light, and an alien darkness has covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and direct my ways unto the light of Thy commandments, I pray!

*Troparia:*
When Balaam the sorcerer did not submit of old unto the ineffable and divine wonders of God, an angel, appearing unto the ass at the crossroads, dreadfully rebuked him; and by revealing the beast endowed with speech, he transformed the knowledge of nature.

When Peter was seized and kept in prison, an angel of God appeared, delivering him from the hands of Herod, and from bonds and death. Therefore, come, all ye people, let us honor the wise archangels as divine guardians of our souls!

O angels and archangels, divine hosts of God: dispel the tumults of wars, church heresies, and all offenses by your continual supplications unto God, and preserve us in peace!

*Theotokion:*
In two essences we know Thee, the one God of creation: in both operations and wills being unconfused, the Son of God, Who didst take flesh from a woman; Whose image we venerate upon panels![^358]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^359]
Thou didst settle Jonah alone in the whale, O Lord; do Thou also save me, who am bound by the nets of the enemy, even as Thou didst save him from corruption!

*Troparia:*
By Thy Word Thou hast brought into being the essences of the heavenly, immortal hosts, having made them radiant with light.

Ye have become precious initiates of the divine praise, O bodiless ones, heavenly citizens and truly divine tabernacles, worthily serving the Creator.

The spiritual ranks of the bodiless ones unceasingly praise and glorify Thee, O Son of God, Who art supremely without beginning, as Maker and Creator of all things.

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast deemed worthy, O all-pure one, to cradle in thine arms God of the highest, Who sits unoriginately with the Father;

*(Fol. 41r)*

make Him propitious unto us, thy servants, O pure one!

*Second Canon. Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^360]
Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are my iniquities, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray; for unto Thee have I cried, and give ear unto me, O God of my salvation!

*Troparia:*
Since the bodiless ones are as fire, and flame, and light: having soared with our mind above material corruption, let us with clay lips honor the immaterial ones with hymns in fear!

Put to death the tempests of passions, O archangels, and together with them calm all disturbances against the faith, being fiery-radiant archistrategoi of the Holy Trinity!

Archangels of God, leaders of the bodiless hosts: by your intercession preserve us from every heresy, O leader Michael and Gabriel, archistrategoi!

*Theotokion:*
Of Thine own will Thou didst appear from the womb, being incarnate from the unwedded one; being bodiless as God, O Christ, yet Thou didst become a bearer of flesh as man, the form of Whose likeness we the faithful venerate!

*Kontakion, Tone 2:*[^361]
Archistrategoi of God, ministers of divine glory, leaders of the angels and guides of men: ask that which is profitable for us, and great mercy, as archistrategoi of the bodiless hosts!

*Ikos:*[^362]
Thou hast said, O Lover of mankind, in Thy Scriptures, that there is joy among the multitude of angels in heaven over one man who repents, O Immortal One; therefore we who are in iniquities, O sinless, only Knower of hearts, ever dare to entreat Thee, as Thou art compassionate, to have pity, and to send down contrition upon us the unworthy, O Master, granting us forgiveness: for on behalf of us all, the archistrategoi of the bodiless hosts pray unto Thee!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^363]
The Hebrew children in the furnace boldly trampled upon the flame, and transformed the fire into dew, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Troparia:*
Thou hast revealed Thine angels as lights, O Compassionate One, their immaterial essence being filled unceasingly with ineffable light, as they cry: Blessed art Thou, O God, unto the ages!

Unto Whom myriads of angels stand before unceasingly serving, yet endure not to gaze upon the vision of Thy face, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*(Fol. 41v)*

By Thy hypostatic Word Thou didst create the nature of the angels; and having sanctified them by the Holy Spirit, Thou didst teach them to bless the Trinity: O God, unto the ages!

*Triadicon:*
Contemplating indeed three Hypostases, we glorify the uncircumscribed essence: the Father, the Word, together with the Spirit, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God, unto the ages!

*Second Canon. Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^364]
The children who came from Judea of old into Babylon, by faith in the Trinity trampled upon the flame of the furnace, chanting: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparia:*
Together with the choirs of the bodiless ones, let the human race also come, let us worship on this illustrious day, celebrating the memory of the wise archangels of Christ, singing: Holy, holy, holy art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Being hospitable of old, Abraham who saw God and glorious Lot entertained the angels, and found communion with the angels, crying: Holy, holy, holy art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Unto valiant Manoah and all-wise Tobit the angels appeared, bestowing the rewards of life according to worthiness; and an angel quenched the flame for the children of old when they were in the fiery furnace.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst take upon Thyself all that is ours according to essence from the Virgin, without change, O Jesus; dual in natures, yet one in Hypostasis, we paternally proclaim Thee, Whose visible likeness we also faithfully venerate when depicting it!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^365]
Him Who was glorified upon the holy mountain, and by fire in the bush revealed unto Moses the mystery of the Ever-Virgin: praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
Emulating the life of the angels, and burning in thought toward the heights, let us together with them immaterially sing of the Lord, praising and supremely exalting Him unto all ages!

Dancers in choirs immaterial, standing around the throne of glory, circling ever about God, the angels sing and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Unto the Trinity, Who makes a flame of immaterial fire those who unceasingly serve on high, and reveals angels as spirits, let us bow down and glorify unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
He Whom myriads of angels and archangels stand before in heaven with trembling: Him hast thou been deemed worthy to carry in thine arms, O Birthgiver of God; pray that they who glorify Him unto all ages may be saved!

*Second Canon. Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*(Fol. 42r)*

Sevenfold did the Chaldean tyrant madly kindle the furnace for the godly ones; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried aloud unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^366]

*Troparia:*
Michael the Archangel was leader of the angels; but glorified brightly with him is Gabriel, the initiate of grace and honored betrother of the Virgin, worthily commander of the bodiless ones, fore-announcing joy unto those who cry aloud: Ye people, supremely exalt Christ unto all ages!

Having seen the angelic ranks in diverse forms, Ezekiel foretold and proclaimed them: among whom the six-winged seraphim stood before, and the many-eyed cherubim encircled; and with them he beheld the radiant archangels, glorifying Christ unto all ages.

Making plain how fearful is the coming of Thy second throne of judgment, Daniel foretold: that thrones were placed, and the Ancient of Days sat down, and brought in myriads of angels who stood before Him in fear, crying with unceasing voices unto the Trinity unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*
The Word, consubstantial with the Father and the Spirit, willingly appeared also unto us, conformed in image from the Virgin without confusion of one with the other in that fearful union; for He is shown forth one and the same in both, in two natures and one Hypostasis, the image of Whose likeness we now worship![^367]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^368]
Thou hast passed beyond the bounds of nature, having conceived the Creator and Lord, and hast become the door of salvation unto the world; therefore, O Birthgiver of God, we unceasingly magnify thee!

*Troparia:*
Thee Who hast ineffably united earthly things unto heavenly, O Christ, and hast made one Church of angels and men, we unceasingly magnify!

Angels and archangels, thrones, authorities, and dominions, principalities and powers, cherubim and seraphim: pray with the Birthgiver of God for the world!

Shown forth as protectors of all, Michael together with Gabriel: visit those who lovingly honor your all-festive memory, and save from every affliction those who faithfully hymn you!

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, holy Bride of God! Rejoice, thou who hast given birth unto the Light of the world for the faithful! Rejoice, rampart and protection of us all: unceasingly pray unto God as Benefactor on our behalf!

*(Fol. 42v)*

*Second Canon. Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^369]
Truly we confess thee to be the Birthgiver of God, we who are saved through thee, O pure Virgin, magnifying thee together with the bodiless choirs!

*Troparia:*
Of the sick, and of seafarers, and of those in distress, ye have appeared as champions unto salvation, O foremost among the bodiless ones, Michael and Gabriel!

Sharing dignity with the divine powers and thrones, as commander of the angels and initiate of God: pray unto the Savior for us, O Gabriel!

As guardians of the world and the Church, and commanders of the hosts on high: beseech the Savior for us!

*Theotokion:*
In unison we glorify thee, O Birthgiver of God, for thou dost save us from passions and perils, and fulfillest our supplications in good things!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "In the spirit in the sanctuary" (Дх҃омъ во ст҃или́щи):*[^370]
O Archistrategos of fiery ministers, Michael: thou hast received the primacy from the Father of lights; therefore thou hast the radiant brilliance of His glory, standing around the all-pure throne as the first of the immaterial ranks!

*Glory, Podoben: "With the disciples" (Со оу҆чени́ки):*[^371]
Continual intercessor before God for the immaterial powers, the archangels and angels, dominions, thrones, and principalities, O divine Archistrategos, most glorious Michael, standing before the unendurable throne: shelter, preserve, protect, and save all who faithfully honor thee, the protector of the world!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
More sacred art thou than the glorious cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious, O all-hymned one, than the awesome seraphim, and holier than all the holy angels, O all-pure one; for thou didst ineffably give birth in the flesh unto the Maker of all, O Birthgiver of God; pray Him to grant remission of transgressions unto thy servants!

*At the Praises, stichera on 4, in Tone 4, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*[^372]
As leader of the heavenly ranks, and a mighty intercessor for men upon earth, a guardian and deliverer: we faithfully sing of thee, O Archistrategos Michael, praying that we be delivered from every corrupting affliction!

Being commander of the divine hosts on high, today he summons the human choirs to form one radiant feast together with the angels for their divine synaxis, and in unison to sing the Thrice-Holy hymn unto God!

Beneath the shelter of thy divine wings, fleeing *(Fol. 43r)*

unto thee in faith, O Michael, divine mind: protect and shelter us throughout our whole life; and in the fearful hour of death, O archangel, stand forth as our most propitious helper!

*In Tone 5, by Ephrem of Caria:*[^373]
Illumined with the divine light of the Three-Sun rays, O archistrategoi, ye enlighten the commanders of the immaterial hosts; appearing as light in dazzling brightness on high, ye flash forth the fire of unapproachable Godhead in the world. Therefore, with fiery lips ye unceasingly sing the Thrice-Holy hymn: Holy, holy, holy art Thou, O our God, glory to Thee!

*Glory, in Tone 5:*[^374]
Wherever thy grace overshadows, O archangel, from thence the power of the devil is driven away; for the fallen Lucifer cannot endure to see thy light. Therefore we entreat thee: quench his fiery darts directed against us by thine intercession, delivering us from his offenses, O praiseworthy Archistrategos Michael!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
We bless thee, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, and we the faithful glorify thee as is due: the unshakable city, the impregnable rampart, the firm protectress, and refuge of our souls!

*Great Doxology and Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the first canon, Ode 3; and from the second, Ode 6. Prokeimenon, in Tone 4: Who makes His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire.*[^375] *Verse: Bless the Lord, O my soul.* *Epistle to the Hebrews, pericope 305.*[^376] *Alleluia, in Tone 2: Praise the Lord, all His angels.* *Gospel according to Luke, pericope 101.*[^377] *Communion hymn: Who makes His angels spirits.*

*On the 9th Day of the Same Month:*

Commemoration of the Holy Martyrs Onesiphorus and Porphyrius; and our Venerable Mother Matrona; and Venerable Theoktiste of Lesbos.[^378]

*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera of the martyrs, in Tone 8, Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*[^379]
O suffering martyr, blessed Onesiphorus: thou didst confess Christ God, suffering most valiantly before the tribunal of the lawless, enduring the wounds of scourging and the burning of thy whole body; therefore thou hast been crowned with the crown of victory by the life-originating right hand, O all-praised one!

O suffering martyr Porphyrius, by the dye of thy blood thou didst anoint for thyself a purple robe, through the grace and power of the Spirit, wherewith being clothed thou hast appeared most radiant, reigning together with Him Who reigns, the only God of ours unto the ages, O glorious one; Whom ever diligently entreat that all of us be saved!

O glorious martyrs, being sacredly put to death for the Life of all: ye rejoicing stretched yourselves upon the fiery gridiron, and tied to horses were dragged along, and received a blessed end; therefore ye are glorified and called blessed, ever praying for us, O ever-blessed ones!

*Other Stichera of the Venerable Women, in Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^380]
By ascetic struggles thou didst chastely subject the leapings of the flesh unto the soul, and didst follow Christ; and thou didst dwell in the midst of ascetics, O divinely blessed Matrona, quenching the lustful burnings with divine streams of tears, and kindling an ardent desire toward the Creator!

A sacred dwelling-place for the profit of many hast thou raised up unto God, having become a temple of the Spirit through purity of soul, O all-wise one; and thou hast been a guide of souls unto profitable ascetic struggles, and hast brought them, O holy one, as a dowry of the saved with Matrona unto the Master, together with whom we faithfully honor thee!

The maidens, having loved the Bridegroom and Lord, submitting unto thy teaching, and having despised the weakness of the flesh in youth, by their zeal have piously *(Fol. 44r)*[^381]

mastered the passions, and were led in with thee, O Matrona, into the heavenly and divine bridal chamber, and now ever make merry!

*Glory, and now, Theotokion, the same Podoben:*
O thou who didst contain in thy womb the uncontainable God, Who out of love for mankind became man, and took from thee our mortal compound, and manifestly deified it: despise me not, O all-pure one, who am now in sorrow; but swiftly have compassion, and deliver me from diverse enmities and from the harm of the evil one!

*Stavrotheotokion, the same Podoben:*
When Thine ewe-lamb and Mother beheld Thee nailed upon the Cross, O Lord, she marveled and cried aloud: What is this sight, O most beloved Son? Is this what the faithless, most lawless assembly renders unto Thee, having enjoyed Thy many wonders? But glory to Thine ineffable condescension, O Master!

*Troparion of the Martyrs, Tone 4:*[^382]
Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received imperishable crowns from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the tyrants and shattered the powerless audacity of demons: by their supplications save our souls!

*Glory, of the Venerable Women, Tone 8:*[^383]
In thee, O mother, that which is according to the image was preserved with certainty; for having taken up the cross, thou didst follow Christ, and by thine actions didst teach us to despise the flesh, for it passes away, but to care for the soul, a thing immortal: therefore, O venerable Matrona, thy spirit rejoices together with the angels!

*Now and ever, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion.*

*The office of the Venerable Theoktiste is chanted at Compline.*[^384]

*Canon of the Venerable Theoktiste, in Tone 6.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^385]
Traversing the deep on foot as if upon dry land, when Israel beheld the pursuer Pharaoh drowned, he cried aloud: Let us sing a song of victory unto God!

*Troparia:*
How marvelous was thy life and conversation, touching upon the immaterial angels by a new and unusual character, through the supernatural narrowness of thy way of life, O Theoktiste!

From infancy thou didst utterly hate worldly food and carnal pleasure, having loved fasting, whereby thou didst bridle all bodily impulses.

The Sower of good things, having found the good ground of thy soul, as of youth in guilelessness, sowed the seed of life and gathered *(Fol. 44v)*

a hundredfold fruit!

*Theotokion:*
Having loved thee from the soul from childhood, O all-pure Maiden and strong defense of the faithful, Theoktiste became a receptacle of all virtues beyond nature.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^386]
There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and hast established us upon the rock of Thy confession!

*Troparia:*
Living in a godly manner, thou didst not remain hidden from the evil one; on this account he contrives evils upon thy shoulders, and brings upon thee a multitude of lacerating wounds for thy purification.[^387]

The enemy of the righteous sought to deliver thee into captivity by enemies; but near was the Deliverer, Who straightway preserved thee pure for Himself from their loathsome hands!

Having escaped the hands of enemies on the island of Paros, thou didst choose to live as a solitary, like a bird thereon, ever remaining as a handmaid in the temple of the Ever-Virgin Mother of God located there.

*Theotokion:*
Having placed all her hope in thee, O Virgin Mother and Maiden, Theoktiste acquired thee as protection, food, drink, and strong intercession in tribulations!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^388]
Christ is my power, my God and Lord, the venerable Church godly-fittingly sings, crying aloud from a pure mind, keeping festival in the Lord!

*Troparia:*
Having secretly departed into the inner and rugged parts of the island, thou didst escape visible enemies; but a fierce battle of invisible foes was joined against thee![^389]

Who can utterly express thy struggles, O venerable one, which thou didst wage against the rulers of darkness, whose fiery darts and elusive words thou didst suffer?

O conscience of the divine grace that preserved thee! How, being both alone and young, in female nature didst thou vanquish and put to shame the host of noetic Ethiopians!

*Theotokion:*
Having lived with perfect understanding from the bodily youth, O God, Theoktiste established all her hope in Thy Mother, and attained unto a good old age.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^390]
With Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine in love the souls of those who rise early unto Thee, I pray: that they may know Thee, O Word of God, the true God, Who callest them from the gloom of sin!

*Troparia:*
Having lifted up thy mind unto God, Thou didst pass beyond all desirable *(Fol. 45r)*

falls and bodily necessities; therefore neither hunger, nor thirst, O glorious one, nor frost, nor nakedness, nor burning heat conquered thee.

Beholding thy strange life, the enemy, raging with envy, troubled thee and tempted thee with all kinds of wiles; but he was not able to trip thy steps, O blameless one.

Having accounted as the arrows of infants all the assaults of the evil one,[^391] thou didst unswervingly accomplish the new course of thy fasting, and didst put to shame his vain arrogance.

*Theotokion:*
As blessed among women, the all-blessed Theoktiste set thee, O Birthgiver of God, as her noetic defense; having wrought strength through thee, she brought to naught those who afflicted her.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^392]
Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, fleeing unto Thy calm haven I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Greatly Merciful One!

*Troparia:*
She surpassed the laws of nature, living without necessities; therefore, as one touching them, she remained immaterial in the flesh, desiring invisible things.

Thou didst foretell by the Holy Spirit that Thy decease had drawn near; therefore also thou wast seen by the hunter, God having been well pleased that Thy marvelous life should not remain hidden.

When the hunter beheld thee in the church, O venerable one, having an earthly appearance without flesh and blood, he marveled, thinking he saw a phantom, so greatly wast thou wasted away: O marvel!

*Theotokion:*
O all-pure Sovereign Lady, cast me not away who am full of grievous uncleanness; but be merciful unto me and a refuge; accept him who brings the supplication of thy Theoktiste in prayers.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*[^393]
Having been dedicated unto God from infancy, O Theoktiste, as a good creation and resembling the Creator, having zealously taken up His good yoke from youth, thou didst not taste of worldly turmoil, guarding all thy senses; therefore as one bodiless thou didst live marvelously upon earth.

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
O unwedded, pure Virgin Birthgiver of God, sole intercessor and protection of the faithful: deliver from afflictions, sorrows, and cruel circumstances all who place their hope in thee, O Maiden, and save our souls by thy divine prayers!

*Or Stavrotheotokion:*

*(Fol. 45v)*

The undefiled Ewe-lamb, beholding the Lamb and Shepherd hanging dead upon the Tree, weeping said, crying aloud with a mother's voice: How shall I endure Thy descent beyond words, O my Son, and Thy voluntary passions, O all-good God?

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^394]
The angel made the furnace drop dew for the venerable youths, while the command of God, consuming the Chaldeans, persuaded the tyrant to cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*
Swiftly didst thou dispel the fear of him who was terrified at the sight of thee, revealing what had befallen thee according to divine providence, O pure one, for which things thou didst also render glory thankfully unto God before him.

Having fasted for six and thirty years, having no means to partake of the saving Body and Blood, thou didst ask of him who met thee to bring reverently unto thee a single portion thereof.

He came bearing that which was desired, and placed it reverently into thy hand; and having received it, rejoicing thou didst say unto God: Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace, according to Thy word![^395]

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast received thy handmaid who lived well-pleasing unto thee, O all-hymned one, and hast counted her worthy of ineffable divine good things; by her prayers make us also partakers of incorruptible food, O pure one!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^396]
Out of the flame Thou didst pour forth dew for the venerable ones, and didst consume with water the sacrifice of the righteous one; for Thou dost accomplish all things, O Christ, simply by willing them: Thee do we exalt above all unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
Having faithfully partaken of the fearful Mysteries as thou didst desire, O venerable mother, thou didst leave dust unto dust, while the angels honorably bore thy precious spirit unto the Lord!

The faithful hunter, having approached thee again, going to receive a blessing from thee, found thee lying dead according to the law of nature, and marveled what it was fitting for him to do.

By a thought, as he imagined who had not learned good, taking thy precious hand audaciously yet intending godly reverence, he promised to receive it in honor of thy holy memory, O blessed one, and to preserve thy manner of life.

*Theotokion:*
I venerate the virtues of the saints, O Birthgiver of God, yet I have not acquired the practice of virtue at all;

*(Fol. 46r)*

acquired; but as thou art merciful, have compassion on my senses, and deliver me from the all-evil habit!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^397]
It is not possible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-pure one, the Word incarnate became visible unto men: Whom magnifying with the heavenly hosts, we call thee blessed!

*Troparia:*
Thou didst restrain him who had stolen and taken thy hand, together with the ship, cargo, and sailors, to remain at the island of Paros until, having understood, he brought and laid it with supplication beside the rest of thy precious body.

Those in the burial and custody, having come into certainty of the power residing in thee, ran together unto thy relics to venerate and embrace them properly, yet they found nothing; for thou hadst become invisible in a manner known unto God.

Having received from Christ a recompense for great afflictions greater still, O venerable one, and having great boldness to pray unto Him: remember those who honor thy divine memory, and ask for us purification from sins and amendment of life.

*Theotokion:*
The Lord, desiring to save all, having chosen thee as His Mother, established thee as the cause of every good for the faithful; having embittered Him by lawlessness, through thee we hope to find mercy, O merciful Birthgiver of God!

*Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*[^398]
Desiring to obtain eternal good things, thou didst account all evil voluptuousness of corruptible things as a drop, and food as the kindling of passions; therefore from childhood thou didst join the choir of monastics, O pure one.

Not ignorant of all the wiles of unclean spirits, thou didst resist valiantly, tearing up the growths of passion by the root, and holding the infants of malice in Davidic manner, and dashing them against the rock of Christ![^399]

Having escaped the hands of the enemy by the nod of God, Thou didst settle in the wilderness seeking Christ; with discernment Thou didst traverse the worldly sea of the passions of life; and in the haven of calm that came to be, Thou beholdest Christ Whom Thou didst desire.

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
