Rejoice, fertile mountain! Rejoice, seat of God! Rejoice, divine dominion! Rejoice, unburnt bush! Rejoice, Birthgiver of God! Rejoice, bridal chamber! Rejoice, heavenly ladder! Rejoice, temple![^400]

*(Fol. 46v)*

rejoice, jar! Rejoice, tabernacle! Rejoice, unceasing joy of the world!

*Stavrotheotokion:*
When the ewe-lamb, the blameless Virgin, beheld Thee lifted up upon the Cross, weeping she cried aloud: O my sweet Child, what is this new and marvelous sight? How art Thou Who holdest all creation in Thy fist nailed in the flesh unto the Tree?

*One canon of both martyrs, and two of the venerable woman.*[^401]

*Canon of the Martyrs, having the acrostic: "Thou bearest profit unto those who praise thee, O blessed one. Joseph." Tone 4.*[^402]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^403]
I will sing unto Thee, O Lord my God, for Thou hast led forth the people from the bondage of Egypt, and hast covered the chariots and power of Pharaoh!

*Troparia:*
Bringing divine profit unto those who praise thee with faith, thy precious memory has arrived, wherein we entreat thee, O blessed one: remember us all!

Having thy valiant mind filled with boldness, thou didst disregard the irrational command, O divinely inspired one, and rejoicing, O blessed one, thou didst suffer!

Strengthened by heavenly power, O Onesiphorus, thou didst rush unto grievous torments, and didst vanquish all the might of the warring adversary.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst bring to a stop the tyranny of death, having given birth unto the immortal Life, the Creator Christ our Deliverer, O Virgin unwedded!

*Another Canon of the Venerable Woman, having the acrostic: "I worthily sing the glory of Matrona. Joseph." Tone 8.*[^404]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^405]
Let us sing unto the Lord, all ye peoples, Who drowned Pharaoh in the Red Sea, singing a song of victory, for He has been glorified!

*Troparia:*
Being ever with the heavenly ranks, and deified by divine communion: save by thy prayers those who honor thee!

Kindled thyself with divine desire, thou didst extinguish the burnings of soul-corrupting pleasures with the showers of abstinence.

Thou wast shown forth as an honorable vessel unto the Master, having cleansed thy heart, O mother, from bodily passions by fasting.

*Theotokion:*
O full of grace, entreat Him Who was well pleased beyond nature to be born of thee, to pacify and save all creation!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^406]
The bow of the mighty has grown weak, and the infirm have girded themselves with strength; therefore my heart is established in the Lord!

*(Fol. 47r)*

*Troparia:*
Equally with the Father and the Spirit confessing the Word in the stadium, the martyrs valiantly repelled the surge of torments.

Having set thy feet firmly upon the rock of confession and faith, O martyr Onesiphorus, thou wast not shaken by the winds of wounds.

Having departed with thy whole mind unto Christ the Desired One, O blessed martyr, thou didst not feel the pains of thy wounds, O all-blessed one!

*Theotokion:*
Look down, O all-pure one, to save me; for by divine nod thou didst incarnate God the Word Who orders all things, beyond word and thought!

*Another Canon. Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^407]
Thou art the establishment of those who flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit hymns Thee!

*Troparia:*
With the divine rod of faith thou didst divide the sea of passions, divinely opening for souls a direct passage.

Thou wast manifestly shown forth as the adornment of solitaries, O all-honored one, having acquired the pure and blameless life of monastics.

Thou didst put off the deadness of corrupting passions, O glorious one, and didst strip the enemy naked by thy godly life.

*Theotokion:*
For the Creator was united unto flesh in thy womb, O all-pure one, remaining that which He was, that He might grant well-being unto men.

*Kontakion of the Venerable Woman, Tone 2, Podoben: "Having received grace" (Благода́ть прїи́мше):*[^408]
For the sake of the love of the Lord, O venerable Matrona, thou didst hate the desire for rest, having illumined thy spirit with fasting; but by thy prayers destroy also the arrogance of adversaries: for mightily didst thou vanquish the wild beasts!

*Ikos:*
Grant me a stream of words, O my God, and make my mind a fountain of good order, and bless my tongue, that I may hymn Thine ewe-lamb whom Thou hast crowned with Thy goodness; for if Thou Thyself grant me not a worthy word, how shall I, being poor, bring a gift unto her who is rich in words and deeds? Therefore grant me strength to tell of her struggles: for mightily has she vanquished the wild beasts!

*Sessional Hymn of the Martyrs, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*[^409]
Kindled with the fire of divine desire, ye were not burned at all by the touch of sensible fire, O blessed ones, but burned up delusion; and dragged unmercifully, O ever-memorable passion-bearers, ye received *(Fol. 47v)*

your end, and obtained glory.

*Glory, of the Venerable Woman, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded" (Повелѣ́нное):*[^410]
Forechosen by God, O mother, guided unto the haven of life, thou didst traverse the tempest of life without pain, singing with the angels unto the Deliverer, and unceasingly praying for us, that Christ may grant us grace and mercy, preserving the flock which thou didst gather by thy labors.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O thou who didst give birth unto the Immutable God: by thy maternal prayers, O good one, establish my heart, which is ever altered by sin and sloth through the assaults of the deceiver; that I also may thankfully glorify thee, O Mary, parent of God: have mercy on thy flock which thou hast acquired, O all-blameless one!

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Ever protected by the Cross of thy Son and God, O Virgin, we vanquish the demonic assaults and wiles, truly hymning thee as the real Birthgiver of God; and with love all generations call thee blessed, O all-pure one, as thou didst foretell; therefore grant remission of our transgressions by thy prayers!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^411]
For the sake of the love of Thine image, O Merciful One, Thou didst stand upon Thy Cross, and the nations melted away; for Thou, O Lover of mankind, art my strength and praise!

*Troparia:*
The flashing brilliance of thy sufferings, O martyr Onesiphorus, drew blessed Porphyrius with love, O blessed one, to suffer together with thee.

Having placed them upon a fiery gridiron, the tyrants stretched out together Christ's pair of steeds, who rejoiced and were fervent in spirit.

As a perfect slaughter, O passion-bearers, and pure sacrifices, ye were rejoicing brought unto the Master of all; therefore ye are called blessed.

The deceptive discourses were not able to deceive thee at all, who hadst noetically offered thyself unto the Master, O divinely wise Porphyrius, all-wise and all-rich!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst give birth unto God the Word becoming incarnate, Who was well pleased through tender mercy to be made like unto all, O Maiden, all-blameless Sovereign Lady!

*Another Canon. Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^412]
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Godhead!

*Troparion:*
Having watered thy heart with the drops of thy tears, O Matrona, thou didst richly produce a hundredfold ear of virtues by divine grace!

*(Fol. 48r)*

*Troparia:*
Having raised up the steps of her contemplation unto Christ, she remained unbent by the assaults of evil demons, O richly praised one!

With valiant wisdom, having forsaken thy spouse and the turmoil of life, thou didst love the yoke of Christ, and didst follow after Him.

*Theotokion:*
Not leaving heavenly things, O all-pure one, God emptied Himself in thy womb, and the Measureless One is measured, having loosed the boundless transgressions of the world.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^413]
Thou, my Lord, hast come into the world as light, a holy light turning those who hymn Thee in faith from gloomy ignorance!

*Troparia:*
Unshakable pillars of the Church of Christ, ye were shown forth unbent by the shakings of torments through the strength of the Spirit.

Ye crushed the idols of defiled gods, and were shown forth as examples of piety and courage, O honorable great martyrs!

Girded with the true warfare from God, having forsaken temporal power in faith, ye suffered rejoicing.

*Theotokion:*
The Uncontainable dwelt in thee and was contained, and showed thee forth wider than the heavens, O Virgin; therefore we call thee blessed!

*Another Canon. Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^414]
Rising early we cry unto Thee, O Lord: Save us! For Thou art our God, and we know none other beside Thee!

*Troparia:*
Having clothed thyself in monastic garb, O Matrona,[^415] thou didst clothe the evildoing enemy with shame.

Thou didst exchange transient things for future things, and an earthly spouse for the immortal Bridegroom, the guide of our souls.

Offering all-night praise unto the Master, O Matrona, thou didst lull the bodily pleasures to sleep.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst give birth unto the Master of the living and the dead; slay the passions of my heart, O all-blameless one!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^416]
I came into the depths of the sea, and the tempest of many sins has submerged me; but as God, lead up my life from the depth, O Greatly Merciful One!

*Troparia:*
Thou didst endure the pains of wounds, O martyr Onesiphorus; having finished the course of witness and become a victor, thou didst receive heavenly honors.

Holding fast one unto another in faith, bound together and dragged along, ye received dissolution of the body as valiant sufferers, being joined unto the Lord.

*(Fol. 48v)*

*Troparia:*
Bound unto horses and dragged along by force through the most cruel disposition of the judge, O well-praised martyrs of the Lord, ye were counted worthy of a divine end!

*Theotokion:*
Apart from the laws of nature, O Virgin, thou givest birth unto the Lawgiver Who renews our crushed nature; pray Him to save me who am crushed by sins!

*Another Canon. Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^417]
I will pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and unto Him will I declare my sorrows; for my soul is filled with evils, and my life has drawn near unto Hades; and I pray like Jonah: Lead me up from corruption, O God!

*Troparia:*
Like a sweet-singing bird melodiously chanting in the forest of asceticism, thou didst attract like noetic sparrows the assembly of most sacred women, having escaped the nets of the enemy in spirit, O Matrona!

Governing the flesh with philosophy and bridling the passions, O venerable one, and radiantly adorning the fairest beauty of the soul for Christ, thou wast known as fair and comely in spirit, O Matrona!

Thou didst love an angelic conversation upon earth, unceasingly hymning Him Who for our sake became incarnate of the Holy Virgin through the multitude of His goodness, and Who strengthened female nature against the evil enemy.

*Theotokion:*
Human nature was enslaved unto sin; but thou didst deliver it from the evil bondage, O Birthgiver of God, having given birth unto the Benefactor of all, Who showed unto us the entrances of life, O all-blameless one!

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*[^418]
The pair of martyrs, having suffered valiantly, cast down the pride of the enemy unto the earth, illumined by the grace of the Uncreated Trinity, O glorious Onesiphorus and Porphyrius: pray ye unceasingly for us all!

*Ikos:*
Christ's soldiers were able through divine strength, being firmly established, to cast down the counsels and wiles of the enemy; bound together unto wild horses and suffering lawfully, they ask of God for us forgiveness of debts, deliverance from impending temptations, and rescue from cruel evils; therefore we ever praise them as true pleasing servants unto God, who pray unceasingly for us all!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^419]
Of old in Babylon the Abrahamite youths trampled upon the flame of the furnace, crying aloud in hymns:

*(Fol. 49r)*

O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparia:*
Displaying the noble dispositions of thy most noble soul, O martyr Onesiphorus, thou didst confess the incarnate God before the tyrants.

Loving eternal divine freedom, thou didst suffer together with thy master like an obedient servant, and dancest with him in chorus, O all-blessed Porphyrius!

Having extinguished the fiery flame of godlessness with your divine blood, ye cry aloud, O all-praised ones: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

That ye might be counted worthy of blessed and immortal glory, ye suffered a blessed death, O divinely radiant stars of the noetic Sun!

*Theotokion:*
Thou givest birth unto the Word incarnate of thy blood, Who was well pleased to deify earthly beings, O Virgin, as they hymn: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Another Canon. Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^420]
The Hebrew youths in the furnace boldly trampled upon the flame, and turned the fire into dew, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Troparia:*
Like a most comely turtledove, thou didst preserve for God the sweet fragrance of chastity, by barrenness of passions truly enriching those saved through thee, O blessed one!

Having forsaken the world, O honorable one, and the things in the world in divine hope, thou hast now inherited a transcendent heritage, being truly the beauty of solitaries, O Matrona!

*Theotokion:*
Having loosed Eve's curse, He dwelt in the all-blameless Maiden, pouring forth a fountain of blessing for those who cry aloud: Blessed is the fruit of thy womb, O all-pure one!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^421]
Him Who was nailed in the flesh upon the Cross, and showed unto us a weapon for salvation: ye children, exalt Christ our God above all unto the ages!

*Troparia:*
Yielding your members to be torn,[^422] ye tore asunder the senseless heart of the enemy, remaining unshaken in mind, O renowned crown-bearers!

With your blood ye extinguished the fire of ignorance, O sufferers, and watered the hearts and souls of all the faithful with the growth of the knowledge of God.

Ye passed through the waves of cruel torments by the pilotage of Christ, and reached the haven of the divine heavenly Kingdom in incorruption.

*(Fol. 49v)*

*Troparia:*
Ye were shown forth as coals kindled manifestly by the fire of the Comforter, O martyrs, and burned up the deception of the enemy, and illumined the universe.

*Theotokion:*
Having found thee, O Maiden, as a chosen flower in the valleys of life, God the Word desired thy beauty, and became incarnate to deify the universe.

*Another Canon. Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^423]
Having become victors over the tyrant and the flame by Thy grace, cleaving earnestly unto Thy commandments, the youths cried aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparia:*
Having adorned thy soul with the dispositions of piety, O Matrona, by the Divine Spirit thou didst bring unto God a choir of virgins, O pure one, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

The showers of thy sweats by divine grace dry up the turbid clouds of passions, O Matrona, and ever water the hearts of those who come in faith; therefore we honor thee unto all ages.

Having armed thyself with the weapons of the faith of abstinence, thou wast not wounded by the arrow of pleasure, dwelling in the midst of men; and him who of old wounded Eve, thou didst wound with the spear of chastity, O blessed Matrona!

*Theotokion:*
Behold, the Virgin, as Isaiah said in the Spirit,[^424] conceived in her womb Him Who delivered us from the belly of Hades, as we piously cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^425]
Eve, through the sickness of disobedience, brought in the curse; but thou, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, through the bud of thy pregnancy didst blossom forth blessing unto the world: therefore we all magnify thee!

*Troparia:*
By the power of Christ the divine ones were able to vanquish the bodiless foes with the body, being valiant diamonds and pillars of faith; and now in heaven they make merry with those who have suffered from the beginning of the ages.

Having become a sacred chariot of the Word, ye were bound unto irrational beasts, O divine martyrs; and ye reached the heavenly haven rejoicing, and received the honors of victory; therefore ye are worthily called blessed.

The glorious city of the Pangaioi[^426] now possesses your bodies, O divine martyrs, enriched with you as protectors and physicians healing the infirmities of bodies and souls of those who ever come in faith.

O divine and radiant pair, O passion-bearer Porphyrius *(Fol. 50r)*

ever-glorious, and valiantly wise Onesiphorus: pray ye unto the Most-holy Trinity to grant peace and deliverance from cruel evils unto our souls!

*Theotokion:*
Having been formed by good will, the Master comes forth from thy divine loins, O all-blameless one, as a bridegroom; and He Who by His nod nourishes all creation is nourished with milk, O blessed Ever-virgin!

*Another Canon. Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^427]
Every hearing was terrified at the ineffable condescension of God, that the Most High voluntarily descended even unto the flesh, having become man from the virgin womb; therefore we the faithful magnify the all-pure Birthgiver of God!

*Troparia:*
Like a divine dove with gilded wings of virtues, O glorious Matrona, thou didst swiftly fly up, and now thou restest where the choirs of the venerable and ranks of the righteous are, and eternal rejoicing, and ineffable joy.

Loving the Unwaning Sun Who shone forth from a woman through tender compassions of mercy, the pure one easily traversed the burning and impassable path of fasting, burning up demons and withering bodily passions.

Thy divine memory has shone upon us brighter than the sun, illumining our hearts and thoughts; wherein remember us who celebrate it with faith, O glorious Matrona, as thou truly hast boldness unto God!

*Theotokion:*
Bearing in thine arms, O Maiden, Him Who bears all things by His nod, deliver me from the hands of the stranger by thy mediation; and illumine my thought with thy light, and alienate me from passions which war against me unceasingly!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Женꙑ̀ оу҆слꙑ́шите):*[^428]
Let us honor the martyrs who shone forth in sufferings and illumined the world with the splendors of martyrdom, the glorious Onesiphorus, and with him Porphyrius; for they pray for us who with love celebrate their memory.

*Glory, of the Venerable Woman:*
In the midst of men didst thou dwell, O ever-memorable Matrona, having assumed their appearance. O strange wonder, O venerable one! How didst thou hide thyself from the tormentor who is ever bitterly enraged? By fasting, prayers, and unceasing vigils, thou didst crush his head!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, palace of God! Rejoice, overshadowing mountain! Rejoice, *(Fol. 50v)*

unburnt bush! Rejoice, throne of glory! Rejoice, divine table! Rejoice, all-golden jar! Rejoice, all-radiant lampstand! Rejoice, light cloud, O Virgin Mother Mary!

*In the same month, on the 10th day: The Holy Apostles Erastus, Olympas, Rodion, and those with them.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*
Passing most radiantly through the fullness of the world like winged eagles, O sacred preachers, ye drew those caught by error unto the blameless faith; therefore pray ye to grant peace and great mercy unto our souls!

With sacred voices let us honor Tertius and Sosipater, and Olympas and Rodion, and with them Erastus the sacred initiate, and divine Quartus, who glorify Christ our God and pray Him to grant peace and great mercy unto our souls!

Unto Christ God ye brought the nations, O blessed ones, redeemed by the Blood of Him Who was well pleased to be born on earth, and endured the Cross and death voluntarily, O all-wise ones: pray Him now to grant peace and great mercy unto our souls!

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
O all-hymned Sovereign Lady, hope and establishment of the faithful, refuge and help: we pray thee, preserve from every calamity thy servants who bow down in faith before thy childbearing; pray Him to grant peace and great mercy unto our souls!

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding the Lamb of God upon the Cross, having neither form nor comeliness,[^429] the Ewe-lamb and blameless Sovereign Lady, weeping, said with lamentation: Woe is me! Whither has Thy comeliness set, O sweetest One? Where is Thy majesty? Where is the radiant grace of Thine image, O my most beloved Son?

*Troparion, Tone 3:*
Holy apostles, entreat the Merciful God, that He grant *(Fol. 51r)*

remission of transgressions unto our souls!

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos, and of the Saints for 4.*

*Canon of the Apostles, having the acrostic: "I hymn the divinely-speaking disciples intensely. Joseph." Tone 1.*[^430]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^431]
Thy victorious right hand was divinely glorified in power; for that hand, O Immortal One, as all-powerful, shattered adversaries, making anew for the Israelites a path through the deep!

*Troparia:*
Being divine disciples of our God Who became incarnate through tender mercy: entreat Him to grant forgiveness of sins unto those who celebrate your memory, O blessed ones!

Ye are accounted radiant divine mirrors receptive of His gifts, O blessed ones, graciously giving saving rays unto all the faithful, O divinely beholding apostles!

Erastus and Tertius, and Olympas, and Rodion, and Sosipater together with Quartus, having drawn from the fountain of splendors, shone forth illumination unto all: whom let us piously call blessed!

*Theotokion:*
By thy childbearing, O Virgin, thou didst renew the human race; for thou didst give birth unto the Father's Word, Who clothed Himself in mortal flesh and showed unto us the paths of immortality.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^432]
Thou Who alone knowest the weakness of human nature, and didst compassionately take form therein: gird me with power from on high, that I may cry unto Thee: Holy is the living temple of Thine ineffable glory, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparia:*
Carrying the Word as an intelligible lamp, O apostles, in godly obedience ye traversed all creation, driving away the gloom of darkness, and by grace showing those who were in bondage unto the night of ignorance to be sons of light.

The saving utterance of your words went forth prophetically into all the universe,[^433] and the radiant demonstration of deeds encompassed all the earth, illumining souls, O divinely-speaking apostles of the Lord!

The All-holy Spirit, taking up His abode in your souls, O wise ones, made you altogether God-seers; going about everywhere throughout the world, by grace ye tore down the idol temples, and erected churches unto God.

*Theotokion:*
Knowing the Only-begotten Son of the Father to be motherless before, and born of thee without a father: we confess thee to be the Mother of God, who didst give birth impassibly and remain a virgin beyond word, O Mary, Bride of God!

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ дне́сь):*[^434]

*(Fol. 51v)*

The honorable festivity of the apostles has appeared today, manifestly granting remission of transgressions unto all who celebrate their memory!

*Then the Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*[^435]
Let us honor in unison the memory of Erastus and Olympas, Sosipater, and Tertius, together with Rodion and Quartus, singing unto them: O divine preachers and servants of the Word, deliver our souls from eternal torment by your prayers!

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
O unwedded, pure Virgin Birthgiver of God, sole intercessor and protection of the faithful: deliver all from perils, afflictions, and cruel circumstances who place their hope in thee, O Maiden, and save our souls by thy divine prayers!

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The undefiled Ewe-lamb, beholding the Lamb and Shepherd hanging dead upon the Tree, weeping said, crying aloud with a mother's voice: How shall I endure Thy descent beyond words, O my Son, and Thy voluntary passions, O all-good God?

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^436]
Having perceived thee with prophetic eyes as the mountain overshadowed by divine grace, Habakkuk proclaimed that the Holy One of Israel should come forth from thee, for our salvation and renewal!

*Troparia:*
Having become an establishment for those of old unestablished, by your God-given teachings ye dug up the diverse strongholds of the enemy, and gave them over to desolation, O divinely beholding apostles of the Savior!

Greatly proclaiming the majesties of Christ while utterly humbling yourselves, O great proclaimers, ye greatly illumined earthly beings radiantly, being perfected by the greatness of grace, O divine apostles!

Let divine Olympas be praised in hymns, and with him let Rodion be piously magnified; having finished the course of martyrdom, beheaded in Rome together with Peter the proclaimer of God![^437]

*Theotokion:*
A wonder greater than all wonders, O all-blameless one, was manifestly shown forth wrought anew in thee; for thou didst give birth bodily unto God, Who was united unto earthly beings through tender mercy in an unconfused union, O Bride of God!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^438]
Thou Who didst enlighten with the brilliance of Thy coming, O Christ, and illumine the ends of the world with Thy Cross: enlighten with the light of Thy divine knowledge the hearts of those who orthodoxly hymn Thee!

The Father's Wisdom, Who conversed with all, *(Fol. 52r)*

sent you forth into the world, O glorious ones, making all wise in the wisdom of the Spirit and the manifestation of truth.

*Troparia:*
Casting the hook of the word, O all-wise ones, by grace ye drew up from the depth of ignorance those who were more voiceless than fish, and brought them believing unto the Lord!

Let us praise Olympas, and the great Rodion, and Tertius, and Sosipater, together with Erastus, and divine Quartus: victors in Christ, and defenders of all the pious!

*Theotokion:*
By a word thou didst conceive the Word, O all-blameless one, and beyond mind and word didst give birth unto Him Who became man, O Birthgiver of God, unwedded of God; therefore with divinely-inspired words we ever call thee blessed!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^439]
The lowest abyss has surrounded us, there is none to deliver, we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter; save Thy people, O our God, for Thou art the strength of the weak and restoration!

*Troparia:*
Most honorable ones, like stones rolling upon the earth ye drew unto piety those who by evil disposition served unfeeling stones, O divinely beholding, most blessed initiates of the Word!

Proclaiming the Monad in three persons, undivided and unconfused, ye destroyed polytheistic deception from the earth, O honorable apostles of Christ, and guided those cruelly deceived unto the light of the knowledge of God.

By comely understandings, O all-wise apostles, ye destroyed the foolishness of the unwise, and established them to believe in the One Essential God, Who adorns all creation with divine effusions of light.

*Theotokion:*
As another heaven shown forth higher than the first, O Sovereign Lady, we glorify thee from whom the Sun of righteousness shone forth upon us, driving away the deep darkness of ignorance!

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*[^440]
Illumining your mind with divine light, ye wisely destroyed the rhetoricians' webs; and having caught all the nations, O glorious apostles, ye brought them unto the Master, teaching them to glorify the Divine Trinity!

*Ikos:*
As disciples of the Master of all, O God-seers, by the net of your prayers draw up from the depth of transgressions my humble soul, caught in the snares of demonic wiles; that having well passed the remaining time of my life, I may hymn you with love, and glorify your blameless life which ye accomplished on earth, having illumined those who were cruelly darkened, teaching them to glorify the Divine Trinity!

*(Fol. 52v)*

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^441]
We the faithful perceive thee, O Birthgiver of God, as a noetic furnace; for just as the Exalted One saved the three youths, the praised and most-glorified God of our fathers wholly renewed the world in thy womb!

*Troparia:*
Paul the apostle writing proclaimed thee, O Erastus, as a sacred steward of the Church of Christ which is in Jerusalem,[^442] with whom we honor thee, singing unto Christ: Blessed art Thou, O praised God of our fathers!

Tried by endurance of temptations and tribulations and persecutions, and adorned with the wounds of Christ, O most rich Erastus, with a loud voice thou didst cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O praised God of our fathers!

Thou wast shown forth as a proclaimer of the New Law, O Quartus, leading those of alien wisdom away from ancient iniquity, and bringing unto renewal of life those who cry: Blessed art Thou, O praised God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst incarnate the Father's Co-eternal Word Who appeared unto earthly beings, and bodily, O Maiden, didst give birth unto Him Who became man that He might save man: the praised and most-glorified God of our fathers!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^443]
In the furnace the children of Israel, as in a furnace by the beauty of piety, shone purer than gold, saying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; hymn the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
Ye were shown forth as unbreakable pillars of Christ's Church; ye tore down all the walls of impiety, and edified the faithful like stones upon the rock of faith, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Ye were shown forth as divine lawgivers, O all-blessed ones, having written the law of the Spirit in the hearts of the faithful; illumined by which they cried aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Thou wast adorned, O blessed Olympas; on the day whereon great Peter received his end, thus didst thou also finish thy course together with Rodion by the sword, by command of Nero the lawless emperor; and ye were joined unto the heavenly choirs![^444]

*Theotokion:*
The jar of old containing the manna prefigured thee, O pure one; for thou didst bear in thy womb our Sweetness, Christ, and didst give birth unto Him in the flesh, Who delivers from every bitterness of unbounded transgressions those who exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*(Fol. 53r)*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^445]
The burning bush shown unconsumed revealed the image of thy pure childbearing; and now we pray thee to extinguish the furnace of temptations raging against us, that we may unceasingly magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God!

*Troparia:*
Having accomplished an equal course, equally enriched by the Master Word, ye were counted worthy of equal gifts of the Spirit and received equal honors, O apostles of the Lord, illuminators of our hearts!

Like heavenly stars ye illumined all the earth with divine signs, driving away the deep darkness of ignorance, and showing those who of old were enslaved by the wiles of the enemy to be sons of the day.

Ye destroyed the army of evil-minded ones who of old cast into the depth the nations of men; and ye brought unto God a multitude of those being saved, being joined unto the ranks of the immaterial hosts.

The all-chosen apostles of Christ, having departed unto the transcendent realms: great Olympas and Sosipater, Tertius together with Rodion, and Quartus, and most sacred Erastus, now pray the Deliverer for the world!

*Theotokion:*
Spare Thy people, O Lord, delivering us from barbarian invasion, and from sins, and misfortunes, and eternal torment, by the prayers of the all-holy Virgin who gave birth unto Thee, and of Thy glorious apostles!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Having adorned heaven with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*[^446]
Let us all faithfully glorify in hymns the apostles: radiant receptacles of the Holy Spirit, most brilliant rays of the day that knows no evening, light-giving lightnings!

*Theotokion:*
We sinners all have thee as our protectress, O most-holy Virgin; make thy Son propitious unto us by thy maternal supplications!

*(Fol. 53v)*

*In the same month, on the 11th day: The Holy Martyrs Menas, Victor, and Vincent; and the Holy Martyr Stephanyda; and our Venerable Father and Confessor Theodore the Studite.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Martyrs, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^447]
Pierced with sharp points, beaten with ox tendons, and thy body scraped with fire, thou didst not deny the saving name of Christ; thou wast not conquered in thought, nor didst thou sacrifice unto idols, but wast a voluntary slaughter, and a pure and perfect sacrifice unto thy Master, O martyr Menas!

Having thine eyes pierced, and hanging upon the tree, and burned on every side with torches, and thy tendons cut by the cruelty of the judge, and beheaded with the sword, thou didst rejoice, O glorious Victor, sufferer of the Savior, having conquered the enemy's array by the operation of the Holy Spirit!

The Lord crowned Thee with a crown of graces, O much-suffering Stephanyda; for with spiritual courage thou didst surrender thy bodily frame unto torments. Bound unto two palm trees, thou wast torn asunder by the palms,[^448] and didst fly up unto God like a sparrow, leaving the flesh in the hands of the hunters, O praiseworthy martyr!

*Other Stichera of the Venerable One, Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*[^449]
O Father Theodore, truly named for God's gifts,[^450] having received gifts surpassing mind, thou didst piously impart them unto those who love thee; and having multiplied the talent, O blessed one, thou didst hear the divine voice calling thee within the bridal chamber, where now thou dwellest at the throne of the King of all, O wonderfully-honored one!

O father of fathers Theodore, thou didst bring unto Christ multitudes of monastics, having become a Godlike cause of salvation, illuminated by teachings and adorned by protection of souls, shown forth prophetically as the mouth of the Lord, O all-wise one; standing now before Whom, remember us!

Abundant grace of the Spirit was poured forth *(Fol. 54r)*

upon thy lips, and a fountain of teachings welled up, O Theodore, showing thee forth as a champion of piety and a mighty advocate of truth, a pillar and foundation of the faith for the Orthodox, a most sure rule of monastic life, O all-wise one!

*Glory, of the Martyrs, Tone 6, by Byzantios:*[^451]
Again the yearly memory of the world's luminaries has shone forth upon us: of Menas, Victor, and Vincent, illumining the hearts of the faithful with their struggles for Christ and His Cross. Therefore in hymns let us honor Christ our God Who crowned them with glory and honor!

*Now and ever, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Тридне́венъ):*[^452]
Beholding the most lawless people unrighteously nailing Thee unto the Tree, the pure Virgin and Thy Mother was wounded in her maternal heart, O Savior, as Simeon foretold![^453]

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos; then the Sticheron of the Martyrs, Tone 2:*
*Verse: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and the Lord will deliver them out of them all.*[^454]

Come, ye lovers of the sufferers, let us honor the threefold choir of martyrs: Menas, Victor, and Vincent; for they gave their blood, and bought eternal life; therefore also they patiently spoke against the inventor of evils: We prefer not corruptible things to incorruptible; we fight not for an earthly mortal king, but fight for the Living King Who ever cries unto the faithful: He that believes in Me, though he die, yet shall he live![^455]

*Glory, Tone 2:*
O venerable father, into all the earth went forth the proclamation of thy righteous deeds; therefore in the heavens hast thou found the reward of thy labors. Thou didst destroy the demonic hosts, and attain unto the angelic ranks whose blameless life thou didst emulate; having boldness unto the Lord, ask peace for our souls!

*Now and ever, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 2, Podoben: "On the third day" (Тридне́венъ):*[^456]
Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, she that gave birth unto Thee cried aloud: What is this strange mystery that I behold, O my Son? How diest Thou in the flesh, hanging upon the Tree, O Giver of life?

*Troparion of the Martyrs, Tone 4:*
Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the tormentors, and crushed the powerless insolence of demons: by their prayers save our souls!

*(Fol. 54v)*

*Glory, Troparion of the Venerable One, Tone 8:*
Instructor of Orthodoxy, teacher of piety and purity, luminary of the universe, divinely-inspired adornment of monastics, O all-wise Theodore: by thy teachings thou hast illumined all, O spiritual lyre! Entreat Christ God, that our souls may be saved!

*Now and ever, Theotokion.*

*At Matins, one canon of the Octoechos, and two of the Saints, for 8.*

*Canon of the Martyrs, by John the Monk, Tone 4.*[^457]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^458]
The choirs of Israel, having traversed the Red Sea with dryshod feet and driven through the watery depth, beholding the enemy captains buried therein, sang with rejoicing: Let us sing unto our God, for He has been glorified!

*Troparia:*
Ye sacred people, with glorious Moses and with Miriam the wise woman and prophetess, traversing not the Red depth, but now the sea of struggles of the sufferer Menas gloriously, let us sing unto our God, for He has been glorified!

When the fierce destroyer and lawless tormentor was breathing with the fury of threatening and zeal of wrath, thou didst choose to stand forth as a soldier of Christ, O Menas, champion of piety, and wast shown forth as a luminary unto Him, crying aloud: Let us sing unto our God, for He has been glorified!

When I am lifted up, I will draw earthly beings unto Myself,[^459] Thou didst foretell, O Christ, and in deed hast Thou accomplished it, having called the ranks of martyrs and peoples from the ends of the earth, who sing in rejoicing: Let us sing unto our God, for He has been glorified!

*Theotokion:*
The budded rod of Aaron prefigured that thou, O Virgin, shouldst sprout from the root of Jesse, who didst blossom forth unto the world the Incorruptible Flower: God incarnate; Whom entreat for us, O Birthgiver of God, who ever flee unto thee!

*Another Canon of the Venerable One, having the acrostic: "I honor the glorious Theodore in hymns. By Theophanes." Tone 8.*[^460]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^461]
Striking crosswise and dividing the sea, the wonder-working rod of Moses of old plunged Pharaoh the charioteer into the deep, and saved Israel the fugitive traveling on foot, as he sang a song unto God!

*Troparia:*
Illumined with the light-bearing splendors of the Holy Spirit, thou wast an all-radiant pillar, O father, guiding toward the land of promise those who strive with divine wisdom, O divinely-speaking Theodore, initiate of ineffable things!

*(Fol. 55r)*

Ascending unto God all-joyfully with unslackening aspirations,[^462] before the end thou wast shown forth clothed in life-bearing mortification, O venerable one, and now hast worthily received life that ages not, O God-bearing Father Theodore!

Having overcome the wanton stirrings of passions and the onrushes of tormentors with youthful vigor, O blessed one, thou didst rebuke all things, having shown forth courage, teaching how to venerate the image of Christ and the depictions of the saints, O God-receiver!

With purified mind, O all-wise one, obeying[^463] the divinely-inspired Scriptures, thou didst gather the wealth of virtues and the dogmas of piety; by vigilance and the radiance of life thou wast enriched, having shone forth in both, O venerable one!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst give birth unto the incarnate Word of God, Who before was bodiless, Who lived in the world divinely and humanly beyond nature, O all-immaculate one, who art still a Virgin; therefore we all honor thee as our protectress after God!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^464]
Not in wisdom, nor in power, nor in wealth do we boast, but in Thee, the hypostatic Wisdom of the Father, O Christ; for there is none holy save Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparia:*
Confounded by thy most wise words, the tormentor unsparingly wounds thee with raw ox tendons, thinking by these to bend thee, O unconquerable martyr!

Gazing with noetic eyes unto the Lord, thou didst endure the hard-to-bear bodily burdens of torments with a most valiant disposition, O laudable one!

Not fearing the exceedingly painful torments, breathing with divine zeal, thou didst betake thyself unto the struggles, crying aloud: Unsummoned, of mine own accord have I come!

*Theotokion:*
Having become incarnate of thee, He Who accepted voluntary death raised me up from the gates of hades, slain of old by the evil taste of the tree, O all-immaculate one!

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*[^465]
Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens with understanding, and didst found the earth upon the waters: establish me, O Christ, upon the rock of Thy commandments; for there is none holy save Thee, O only Lover of mankind!

*Troparia:*
Panoplied with desire for Christ, O all-blessed one, thou didst endure the pains of wounds, being cruelly beaten and shut up in prison, so that thou becamest a partaker of His sufferings and Kingdom!

Kindled with zeal, thou didst destroy the foul teachings of the lawless by thy teachings, O all-wise one;

*(Fol. 55v)*

for thou wast worthily enriched with grace from God, O father!

Active in contemplation, a theologian in action wast thou unto us, O divinely speaking one: an instructive faster, a glorious hieromartyr, a pillar of Orthodoxy, a confirmation of the Church!

*Theotokion:*
God the Word, co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit, wishing to renew the forefather, took him hypostatically from thee, O pure one, having found thee holier than all, O Mother of God!

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*[^466]
Thou didst make thy fasting and angel-like life radiant by thy suffering struggles, and wast shown forth a fellow-inhabitant with the angels, O divinely-blessed Theodore; with them cease not praying unto Christ God for us all!

*Ikos:*
Let us now praise Theodore, the radiant beauty of fasters, the confirmation of the Church of Christ; for he was shown forth as a new pillar of fire, burning up the heads of heretics, and enlightening the souls of the faithful toward the right faith, leading them like another Elijah into the heavenly divine city. Unto him let us cry aloud with one voice: O all-blessed father, forget not to pray unceasingly unto Christ for us all!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^467]
Egypt, which of old was held in the grievous darkness of ignorance, O divinely-wise martyr Menas, caused thee to shine forth as a universal luminary, mightily driving away the night of godlessness by the rays of thy divine struggles, O blessed one. Therefore, celebrating thy light-bearing and honorable day brightly, we diligently cry unto thee: O adornment of sufferers, entreat Christ God, that He grant remission of sins unto those who honor thy holy memory with love!

*Glory, of the Venerable One, in Tone 3, Podoben: "Of the divine faith" (Бж҃твенныя вѣ́ры):*[^468]
Enriched with divine dogmas, thou didst keep the faith of Orthodoxy, having braved dangers for its sake, O Theodore, suffering in exiles and beatings, enduring afflictions in prisons, O venerable father. Entreat Christ God, that He grant us great mercy!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast the divine tabernacle of the Word, O only most-pure Virgin Mother, who in purity didst surpass the angels; cleanse me, who beyond all others have become dust and am defiled by bodily transgressions, by the divine waters of thy prayers, granting great mercy, O pure one!

*(Fol. 56r)*

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The undefiled ewe-lamb of the Word, the incorrupt Virgin Mother, beholding Him Who sprouted from her without pain hanging upon the Cross, weeping as becomes a mother, cried aloud: Woe is me, my Child! How sufferest Thou willingly, wishing to deliver man from shameful passions?

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^469]
Sitting in glory upon the throne of Godhead, on a light cloud came Jesus the most divine, with incorrupt palm, and saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

*Troparia:*
By the sprinkling of thy blood the coals of polytheism were quenched, and the demonic host was drowned; but the Church of Christ was watered, praising thee, O all-blessed passion-bearer Menas!

By hanging upon the tree, thou didst typify the Passion of Him Who by the Cross put the bitter serpent to death, O martyr; and thou didst endure scrapings which procure for thee enjoyment in the heavens, O most valiant one!

Beyond nature didst thou receive the trial of painful wounds, O sufferer; and divine love, taking hold of thy nature, caused thee to forget them, moving thee to stretch forth unto wounds, O all-blessed one!

*Theotokion:*
Ineffably didst thou give birth unto God incarnate, Who built for Himself a house from thy blood, Who in two natures and wills is divinely known, O unwedded one!

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*[^470]
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power; Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing; Who didst not leave the Father's bosom, yet visitedst our poverty. Therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparia:*
True to thy name, thou wast given unto the world as a gift of God, radiant with rich gifts, truly having a fountain of sacred illuminations, O blessed Theodore; therefore thou wast accounted worthy to be joined unto the multitude of teachers, fasters, and witnesses!

By thy firm and steadfast resistance wherewith thou didst trample the cruelty of the tormentors, for whose sake thou didst manifestly attain unto the ultimate beatitude of the transcendent Goodness, O divinely-wise one, singing with the bodiless hosts: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

The Spirit of God most manifestly made His abode in thee, O all-wise Theodore, and wells forth streams of dogmas abundantly; enjoying which now, *(Fol. 56v)*

we thy disciples, O divinely-inspired one, gratefully cry aloud with unceasing voices: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:*
He Who departed not from the Father's bosom and was well-pleased to dwell in thy womb wholly renews man in thee, wholly united unto the whole of man, O all-pure one, having voluntarily become poor through the wealth of tender mercy, and enriched the world with His divinity!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^471]
The ungodly shall not behold Thy glory, O Christ, but waking early out of the night we hymn Thee, O Only-begotten, the radiance of the Father's glory of the Godhead, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparia:*
Having flashed forth with the bright rays of the witnesses, having darkened murky godlessness, O all-wise one, thou didst enlighten the fullness of the faithful who hymn thee, O all-lauded one!

Every device of the enemies vanished through thy steadfast endurance; for neither hunger, nor wounds, nor burning, nor the affliction of the trident[^472] darkened thy zeal!

Fenced about by faith as the sun with rays, thou didst dwell in the wilderness, and didst enlighten all cities, proclaiming Christ the Son of God Who came in the flesh,

*Theotokion:*
The Deliverer born of thee beyond nature makes me new who had fallen into corruption, setting me free from the ancient curse, O pure Mother of God; entreat Him to save me!

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*[^473]
Why hast Thou cast me away from Thy presence, O Light never-setting, and an alien darkness has covered me, the wretched one? But turn me, and direct my paths unto the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee!

*Troparia:*
Having purified mind, and soul, and body by the word, thou becamest an all-honorable temple of the God of all, living and animate, offering thy whole self unto Christ as a sweet-smelling sacrifice, O father, having become both priest and victim!

Illumined with the radiance of the Spirit, O blessed one, with theological tongue thou didst shine forth unto all the most pure Trinitarian Light, and the ineffable mystery of the incarnation of God the Word beyond mind, O father!

Now dwelling noetically with the angels, entreat Christ to deliver from passions and tribulations those who call blessed and honor the all-honorable and divine memory of thy sufferings, O God-bearing Theodore!

*Theotokion:*
In an ineffable manner, O Virgin, the Son of God dwelt in thee and *(Fol. 57r)*

became man; He Who shone forth from the Father before the ages delivers man from corruption, and led him unto life and incorruption, as He alone is tenderly compassionate!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^474]
I am come into the depths of the sea, and the tempest of my many sins has overwhelmed me; but as God lead up my life from the depth, O greatly Merciful One!

*Troparia:*
Thou didst remain without pain when consumed by fire and having thy wounds rubbed with haircloth rags; for divine grace visiting thee strengthened thee, O Menas!

Thou didst stand before the judging tribunals of the tormentors, rebuking deception, O ever-memorable Menas, offering thyself as a pillar of piety unto the faithful!

By the sweat of thy struggles thou didst dry up the idolatrous deception, and didst fashion thyself as a temple of the honorable Trinity, O wonder-worthy passion-bearer Menas!

*Theotokion:*
Heal the incurable passions of my soul, O all-immaculate one, by the essence of thy goodness, who didst give birth unto the good Savior Christ for those who are in the world!

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*[^475]
Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are my iniquities, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray Thee; for unto Thee have I cried, and do Thou hear me, O God of my salvation!

*Troparia:*
Chastely didst thou finish thy life, O sacred speaker; and adorned with righteousness, courage, and wisdom, thou didst yoke for thyself the most comely chariot of virtues, O all-blessed and venerable one!

The divine words of thy dogmas breathe forth fragrance with divine beauty, and from the depth of wicked heresies they lead all men up to the highest summit of Orthodoxy, O all-wise one!

Light has dawned for thee, and its yoke-fellow, bright gladness, is now manifest, O father; for like a palm tree thou hast blossomed forth, O all-blessed Theodore, and like a cedar hast thou been multiplied, O laudable one![^476]

*Theotokion:*
May we be delivered from grievous transgressions by thy supplications, O pure Birthgiver of God, and may we obtain the divine illumination of the Son of God, ineffably incarnate of thee, O all-holy one!

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ):*[^477]
Christ our God, Who is the incorruptible crown of the martyrs, snatched thee away from temporal soldiering, and showed thee forth as a partaker of the incorruptible heavenly kingdom, O passion-bearer Menas!

*Ikos:*
The memory of the martyrs is unto us an advocate of great gladness, showing forth *(Fol. 57v)*

courage against passions and victory over enemies, in the bright and joyful confession of grace. Come therefore, all ye feast-lovers, and let us rejoice in it, the best and enduring time of our gladness, celebrating the memory of the sufferer Menas, and receiving the gift of release from passions; the giver whereof is Christ God, the incorruptible crown of the martyrs!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^478]
Thou Who didst save Thy children of Abraham in the fire, and didst slay the Chaldeans whom justice justly overtook: O all-hymned Lord, God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparia:*
By wounds thou didst strip off the coats of skin of sin, and wast clothed in a garment that no longer suffers corruption, O blessed one, which grace wove when it appeared!

By the kindling of thine honorable and steadfast struggles, O martyr, thorny and evil godlessness is turned to ashes; and by the streams of blood the towering flame of ignorance is quenched, O all-blessed one!

Having abundant gifts, thou pourest forth miracles unto those who celebrate thine honorable festival, O laudable Menas, and helpest those who sing: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Theotokion:*
Blessed is the fruit of thy blessed womb, Whom the heavenly powers and the assemblies of earthly beings bless, Who has delivered us from the ancient curse, O blessed one!

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*[^479]
The fire was ashamed of God's condescension in Babylon of old; therefore the youths in the furnace, dancing with joyful step as in a meadow of flowers, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*
Foreseeing in thy depths the purity of thy mind, he sets thee forth, O father, as a shepherd of rational sheep; unto Whom now, O all-blessed Theodore, thou criest aloud rejoicing: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Continually venerating the divine likeness of the icon of Christ's incarnation, thou didst resist the fighters against God even unto blood, singing, O Theodore: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Thy word was shown forth seasoned with salt,[^480] O most rich one, and thy life, O father, was enlightened by the radiance of the Spirit, gleaming with which thou now criest aloud rejoicing: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Lo, now is fulfilled the divine prophecy of divine David: truly the rich among the people *(Fol. 58r)*

pray unto thy countenance, O pure Birthgiver of God, possessing the wealth of grace now, blessing the God of our fathers![^481]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^482]
O almighty Redeemer of all, having descended into the midst of the flame, Thou didst bedew those who acted piously, and taught them to sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works; hymn the Lord!

*Troparia:*
Thou wast shown forth as a crowned victor, O Menas; having cast down the enemies of the Cross of thy Lord, thou didst put them to shame, and criedst aloud, O all-blessed one: Hymn the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

God works marvelous wonders in thy memory, welling forth unto us through thy relics healings of soul and body, as we cry aloud: Hymn the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Thou didst offer thy ministry unto God; and having bowed thy head unto the earth, thou didst receive beheading by the sword, O martyr, crying: Hymn the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

As with purple and fine linen, the Church is adorned this day with your blood, O Menas, Victor, and Vincent, crying aloud: Hymn the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
Thy womb remained virginal even after giving birth unto the Son, Whom without seed thou didst conceive of the Holy Spirit: the uncircumscribed God robed in flesh, the Word co-beginningless with the Father; Whom all works hymn as the Lord, and exalt above all unto the ages!

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*[^483]
Sevenfold the Chaldean tormentor furiously kindled the furnace for the pious; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
Thou didst show the inventors of wicked heresies to be put to flight, O God-bearing Theodore, teaching all to venerate the most pure icon of Christ and to honor it reverently with divine wisdom, and to sing unto the Master: Ye priests, bless; ye people, exalt Him above all unto the ages!

In all thy life, O divinely-speaking Theodore, thou wast a guide of Orthodoxy,[^484] a most bright luminary, a God-beholding teacher, a pattern of monastics, and an unerring lawgiver, teaching all to sing: Ye priests, bless Christ the Master, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

On earth thou didst strive as a champion of piety, and wast shown forth an unlying rebuker of *(Fol. 58v)*

unrighteousness, O all-blessed one, as a gift of God; and in the heavens thou hast been crowned with the crowns of righteousness; thou hast finished thy course, and hast kept the faith,[^485] exalting Christ above all unto the ages!

With prudence thou didst adorn the mind, with temperance desire, and with courage didst gird the irascible part, O all-wise Theodore, having hierarchically directed the powers of thy soul by righteousness; harmoniously singing: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
O blessed, most pure Maiden, cleanse the arrows and the wounds of sin of my soul; for thou didst give birth unto God Who is over all from a virginal, unwedded womb, O pure Maiden; Whom all creation blesses, and exalts above all unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^486]
A cornerstone was cut out without hands from thee, the unhewn mountain, O Virgin: Christ, Who joined together the sundered natures; therefore rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God!

*Troparia:*
Thou didst love even more, not less, than thou wast loved, O passion-bearer, offering thy beloved soul unto Christ thy Lover, Who with Himself glorified thy witness, O ever-memorable one!

Kindled by the thrice-radiant Light as a lampstand, the threefold unity of martyrs was shown forth: Menas, Victor, and Vincent, enlightening the faithful and driving away the demonic darkness!

Accept praise as a debt proceeding from our zeal; for I know, O Menas, that thou surpassest our words; and grant in return boundless gifts from thy treasuries!

*Theotokion:*
Worthily did all the prophets of old praise thee as the Mother of the King and Master; and now the apostles and martyrs together with us glorifying thee magnify thee as the Birthgiver of God!

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*[^487]
Heaven was dismayed thereat, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God appeared unto men bodily, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens; therefore the hierarchies of angels and men magnify thee as the Birthgiver of God!

*Troparia:*
Illumined by the streams of thy tears as a faster, and by the fountains of thy blood as a witness of Christ, thou shinest brightly in both, clothed with righteousness as a priest, O venerable one; thou dwellest in the divine choirs, being now illumined in the untrodden realms, O thrice-blessed one!

Having passed thy life purely, thou now dwellest in the holy tabernacles of the *(Fol. 59r)*

saints, having received the crown of goodliness, and the royal, magnificent, and sacred vesture; wherein being now illumined, thou standest before the bridal chamber, enjoying deification!

Thou wast accounted worthy to behold the Fountain of good things, O God-bearing Theodore, having truly passed a most divine life, having freed thy mind from worldly attachments by a pure life, for thou wast a witness and a victorious soldier, O sacred one!

The utterance of thy words was made audible unto all as a divine gift unto us, O all-lauded one, like thunder unto the ends of the universe, and the writings of thy teachings flow forth like rivers; therefore we worthily name thee a theologian and a speaker of God!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast revealed, O Virgin, Mother of God, having beyond nature given birth bodily unto the good Word, Whom the Father as good poured forth from His heart before all ages;[^488] Whom we now perceive to be transcendent even over bodies, even though He was clothed in a body!

*Exapostilarion of the Octoechos, and of the Martyrs, Podoben: "Having adorned heaven with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*[^489]
Brightly do stars adorn heaven; and Menas, Victor, Vincent, and Stephanyda adorn the Church: for whose sake grant victories over enemies unto our King![^490]

*Glory, of the Venerable One:*
As an animate pillar of the dogmas of Orthodoxy thou wast shown forth in piety, having exposed the deception of the iconoclasts; therefore also, having accomplished thy confession by suffering, O Theodore, thou hast been glorified!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
All the faithful now set thee forth, O all-pure one, as an advocate unto Him Who was born of thee; and we still more, who are crucified together with Him. Therefore, O Virgin, cease not praying for us!

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos; then the Sticheron of the Martyrs, Tone 2:*
*Verse: The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them.*[^491]

Come, ye faithful, let us honor Christ's passion-bearer, glorious Menas, valiant in battles, who strove well for piety, and cast down the power of emperors and tormentors; therefore, having boldness unto Christ God, he unceasingly prays that our souls may be saved!

*Glory, of the Venerable One, Tone 8:*
We honor thee, O our Father Theodore, as an instructor of the multitudes of monastics; for by thy path we have learned truly to walk uprightly. Blessed art thou, having labored for *(Fol. 59v)*

Christ, and having exposed the enemy's power: converser with angels, companion of the venerable and righteous; with them pray unto the Lord that our souls may be saved!

*Now and ever, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "O Lord, though Thou didst stand before the tribunal" (Гдⷭ҇и а҆́ще и҆ на сꙋди́щи):*[^492]
O Lord, when the sun beheld Thee, the Sun of righteousness, hanging upon the Tree, it hid its rays, and the moon changed its light into darkness; and Thine all-immaculate Mother was wounded in her maternal womb!

*At the Liturgy, Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
*As for the saints that are in His earth, the Lord has made all His wonders marvelous among them.*[^493] *Verse: I foresaw the Lord always before my face.*[^494]

*Epistle to the Ephesians, section 233 [Eph. 6:10–17]; and of the Venerable One, Epistle to the Hebrews, section 335 [Heb. 13:7–16].*

*Alleluia, Tone 4: The righteous cried.*[^495] *Verse: Blessed is the man that fears the Lord.*[^496]

*Gospel according to Matthew, section 38 [Mt. 10:32–33, 37–38; 19:27–30]; and of the Venerable One, Gospel according to Matthew, section 10 [Mt. 4:25–5:12].*

*Communion Verse: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.*[^497]

*In the same month, on the 12th day: Our Father among the Saints John, Patriarch of Alexandria, the Merciful; and our Venerable Father Nilus.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*[^498]
Having dispersed, thou gavest thy bread unto the needy,[^499] O marvelous John, emulating in mercy the most merciful Master, O venerable one; therefore in truth thy memory abides unto all ages, O holy one. Those who celebrate it with faith save by thy prayers from temptations and tribulations, O most rich hierarch!

He Who sees hidden secrets, foreseeing thy purity, the uprightness of thy mind, and thy divine disposition, raised thee unto the greatest throne, having anointed thee with chrism, O wise one, and perfected thee, manifestly entrusting unto thee the helm of the flock, which thou didst steer unto the haven of divine will, O divinely speaking John!

*(Fol. 60r)*

All the petitions of thy heart the Lord granted thee, O marvelously worthy one; for thou didst keep all the saving ordinances. For thou didst love God with all thy heart, and thy neighbor as thyself, O divinely blessed one, and didst satisfy those in need; therefore this day we honor thee, O John!

*Other Stichera of the Venerable One, Tone 8, Podoben: "What shall we call you, O holy ones" (Что́ вы нарече́мъ):*[^500]
What shall we now call thee, O holy one? A river issuing forth from noetic Eden; a torrent of gifts granted by God; a flood of the teachings of grace; a cup of wisdom and knowledge; a most fervent intercessor; a most efficacious teacher! Pray that our souls may be saved!

What shall we name thee, O venerable one? A husbandman of immortal gardens, O blessed one; a planter of the rational paradise of the faithful; most skilled in the God-given laws; a knower of God-inspired dogmas; a most pious expounder and most sufficient instructor! Pray that our souls may be saved!

What shall I now call thee, O marvelous one? A lawgiver of marriage, a director of chastity, an instructor of monastics, and a guide of virginity, measuring rightly for both, as having passed through both by experience! Many are thy deeds, and from God is thy fasting. Pray that our souls may be saved!

*Glory, Tone 2, by Anatolius:*
John, imitator of Christ, great shepherd of the Alexandrians and luminary, multiplies the fountain of mercy and the compassionate compassions for the needy. Come, let us be filled, ye poor in spirit, imitating his gentleness; having entertained with a loving and tender-hearted disposition Christ Who wandered in the guise of the poor, even as Abraham of old, he was accounted worthy of beatitude, and with boldness he prays that our souls may be saved!

*Now and ever, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
Beholding Thee nailed unto the wood of the Cross, O Jesus, the unwedded Maiden weeping said: O sweet Child, why hast Thou left me alone who gave birth unto Thee, O unapproachable Light of the pre-beginningless Father? Make haste and be glorified, that they who glorify Thy divine passions may receive divine glory!

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*

*Glory, of the Venerable One, Tone 8:*

*(Fol. 60v)*

We honor thee, O our Father Nilus, as an instructor of the multitudes of monastics; for by thy path we have learned truly to walk uprightly. Blessed art thou, having labored for Christ, and having exposed the enemy's power: converser with angels, companion of the venerable and righteous; with them pray unto the Lord that our souls may be saved!

*Now and ever, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "Thy martyrs, O Lord" (Мꙋ́ченицы твоѝ):*
Beholding Thee nailed upon the Cross, O Jesus, and voluntarily accepting passions, the Virgin and Thy Mother, O Master, cried out: Woe is me, O sweet Child! How dost Thou endure wounds unrighteously, O Physician Who didst heal human infirmity, and by Thy compassion delivered all from corruption?

*Troparion, Tone 8:*
In thy patience thou didst acquire thy reward, O venerable father, persevering unceasingly in prayers, having loved the poor and satisfied them; but pray unto Christ God, O John the Merciful, blessed one, that our souls may be saved!

*Glory, Tone the same:*
By the streams of thy tears thou didst cultivate the barren desert, and by sighings from the depths thou didst bear fruit a hundredfold in labors; and thou wast a luminary unto the universe, shining with miracles, O Nilus our father: pray unto Christ God that our souls may be saved!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*At Matins, one Canon of the Octoechos, and two of the Saints.*

*Canon of the Hierarch, the composition of Joseph, Tone 8.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^501]
That which was cut cleaved the uncut water, and the sun beheld the earth which it had not seen; the water drowned the fierce enemy, and Israel passed through the impassable path. And a song was sung: Let us sing unto the Lord, for gloriously has He been glorified!

*Troparia:*
Enlightened in mind by compassion, and illumined by the love of Christ, O father, shining with the radiances of almsgiving, thou wast a most honorable receptacle of the one merciful God, O John; therefore we call thee blessed!

Looking unto that which abides unto the ages, with wise understanding, O most sacred father, thou didst brightly exchange corruptible things for incorruptible; and now thou dwellest in the heavens, crying aloud with the bodiless choirs: Let us sing unto the Lord, for gloriously has He been glorified!

The Giver of mercy, having endowed thy merciful disposition, O venerable one, showed mercy unto many through thy divine intercession;

*(Fol. 61r)*

for thou wast the consolation of souls and the providence of the poor, O all-wise John, divinely blessed and most sacred!

*Theotokion:*
O blessed, pure, and all-praised one, who alone gavest birth unto God incarnate, an ever-flowing fountain pouring forth healings unto the faithful who hope in thee: pray unto Him Whom thou didst bear, to grant great mercy unto the world!

*Another Canon of the Venerable One, whose acrostic is: "Nilus waters me with rational all-fruitfulness," the composition of Theophanes, Tone 8.*[^502]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^503]
Having passed through the water as upon dry land, and having escaped Egyptian malice, the Israelite cried aloud: Let us sing unto our Redeemer and God!

*Troparia:*
By thy mystical waterings, O blessed one, richly watering my sprouted thought, account me worthy by thy prayers to offer unto thee an ear of grain of song!

The streams of thy words, clearly issuing forth as from Eden, O most rich Nilus, ever water the entire face of the Church like an ever-flowing stream!

The river of thy dogmas and words, O speaker of God, inundating, waters the hearts of the pious, and drowns the assemblies of the impious!

*Theotokion:*
The destroyer and enemy spewed soul-destroying venom into the ears of Eve; but having given birth unto Christ, O Mother of God, thou didst heal his harm!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^504]
O Lord, Builder of the vault of heaven and Founder of the Church: do Thou establish me in Thy love, O summit of desires, confirmation of the faithful, O only Lover of mankind!

*Troparia:*
Goodly as a maiden, wearing a crown of olives, the compassionate grace of the Merciful One appeared unto thee, O marvelously worthy one, drawing thee unto divine mercy![^505]

Upon the sacred throne, by the judgment of God, thou didst sit, O glorious Father John; as an angel thou didst live, in peace offering sacred sacrifices unto the All-Bountiful!

Imitating the abundant mercy of the merciful Lord, O father, Who in His mercy became poor in the flesh, thou didst satisfy the poor, protecting strangers and the shelterless, having become a fulfiller of divine commandments!

*Theotokion:*
Having taken up abode bodily in the Virgin, O Lord, Thou didst appear unto men, as it was fitting to behold Thee;

*(Fol. 61v)*

and whom Thou didst show forth as the true Birthgiver of God, help of the faithful, O only Lover of mankind!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*[^506]
Thou art the confirmation of those who flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the Light of the darkened, and my spirit hymns Thee!

*Troparia:*
Thy thought bears the gifts of the Spirit, O father, driving away evil thoughts!

Having lived by active contemplation, O sacred minister, thou didst breathe forth unto us thy prayers like most fragrant myrrh!

Thou didst pour forth mystical teachings, O all-wise one, as from a fountain, and didst enrich the nurslings of the Church!

*Theotokion:*
Put to death the wisdom of our flesh, O all-pure one, who didst pour forth the Fountain of immortality unto men!

*Kontakion of the Venerable One, Tone 8, Podoben: "To thee, the champion leader" (Взбра́нной):*[^507]
The thorny uprisings of the passions that proceed from the body, O blessed Nilus, thou didst keenly cut down in thy vigilant prayer; but as one having boldness unto the Lord, deliver me from all perils, that I may cry unto thee: Rejoice, O universal father!

*Ikos:*
Who among the earthborn is able to recount, O Nilus, the sufferings of thy ascetic life, and the immeasurable labors of thy life, and thy many zealous endeavors which thou didst accomplish on earth as one bodiless? Nevertheless I cry aloud: Rejoice, river of divine graces! Rejoice, reed-pipe of Christ's teachings! Rejoice, cup of wisdom and knowledge! Rejoice, cultivation of immortal plantings! Rejoice, most efficacious dogma of God-inspired words! Rejoice, most skilled interpreter of the God-given law! Rejoice, planter of the noetic paradise! Rejoice, great treasury of virginity! Rejoice, beautiful psaltery of the Spirit! Rejoice, root-severing sword against passion's darts! Rejoice, height of venerable men! Rejoice, protector of the faithful earthborn! Rejoice, O universal father!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^508]
Having acquired a merciful disposition, thou wast shown forth tender-hearted, and a giver unto the poor and needy, O God-inspired John; therefore, fitting thy deed unto thy name, Christ, the Giver of good things, greatly enriched thee beyond all saints, O blessed one: unto Whom pray, O divinely wise and most rich hierarch, to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love!

*(Fol. 62r)*

*Glory, of the Venerable One, Tone the same, Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́иннѡ):*[^509]
Having adorned thy mind with contemplations, thou didst pour forth rivers of theology, watering the hearts, O God-bearing Nilus, of those who draw with faith the limpid and pure drink of thy teachings, and who honor thy radiant and honorable memory, O adornment of the venerable and boast of the fathers!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O thou who gavest birth unto the immutable God: my heart, ever mutable through sin and slothfulness by the assaults of the deceiver, do thou establish, O good one, by thy maternal prayers, that I also may thankfully glorify thee, O Mother of God Mary: have mercy upon thy flock which thou hast acquired, O all-immaculate one!

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding Him Who was incarnate of thy pure blood and born of thee beyond comprehension, O pure one, hanging upon the Tree in the midst of evildoers, thou wast pained in thy womb, and weeping maternally didst cry aloud: Woe is me, my Child! What is this Thy divine and ineffable dispensation, whereby Thou hast given life unto Thy creation? I hymn Thy tender-hearted compassion!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^510]
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I understood Thy works, and glorified Thy divinity!

*Troparia:*
Thou wast shown forth as a pure dwelling of the Holy Trinity, O venerable one, and a treasure of the divine temple, and the firstfruit of hierarchs!

Accepting thine abundant mercy, the tender-hearted Lord sanctified thy soul, O John, most sacred father!

Thou wast an unashamed doer of the commandments of the All-Bountiful, and wast filled with His good things, dwelling in the habitations of the saints!

*Theotokion:*
Grant cleansing of our ignorances, as Thou art sinless, and give peace unto Thy world, O God, through the prayers of her who gave birth unto Thee!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos the same:*[^511]
Lead me up, O all-wise one, from the captivity of the passions, offering thy prayers unto God as a ransom and price!

*Troparia:*
To elucidate sacredly the dogmas of wisdom concerning Christ, being skilled, thou didst pre-purify thyself by fasting, O all-blessed one!

Every proud uprising of thoughts, O father, thou didst humble, destroying the memory of them by the multitude of thy wisdom!

*Theotokion:*
Co-ever-existing with the Father, and as God the Word Who was bodiless before, in the last times He became incarnate of thy pure blood, *(Fol. 62v)*

O all-praised one!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^512]
Ever wandering from the night of ignorance along a soul-destroying path: guide me, O Lord, by the light of Thy knowledge, and direct me unto the path of Thy commandments!

*Troparia:*
Imitating by voluntary mortification Him Who was put to death out of mercy, O wise father, thou wast crucified unto the world and the passions, and wast accounted worthy of otherworldly life, O worthy of glory!

Thou wast accounted worthy of beatitude, having been meek, most compassionate, and peaceful, an inexhaustible bread for the hungry, a giver unto the poor, and clothing for the naked!

Adorned with divine communions, O father, as an angel thou didst minister sacredly and blamelessly unto God, enlightening the faithful with the radiances of thy teachings!

*Theotokion:*
We hymn the all-pure Birthgiver of God, who bore the God of all without seed in her womb and gave birth unto Him clothed in flesh for us, as the salvation of our souls!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*[^513]
Rising early from the night we cry unto Thee, O Lord: Save us, for Thou art our God, and we know no other besides Thee!

*Troparia:*
Chastely desiring divine purity, O all-wise one, thou didst forsake all attachment unto this life!

Being taught by divine union, O divinely blessed one, thou didst noetically attain unto noetic things that surpass knowledge!

We know thee, O God-bearer, as a cloud with showers of knowledge, drowning all foolishness!

*Theotokion:*
Having found thee among women as a lily shining in the midst of thorns, the Bridegroom loved thee, O Virgin Mother![^514]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^515]
I will pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and unto Him will I declare my sorrows, for my soul is filled with evils, and my life has drawn near unto Hades; and like Jonah I pray: Lead me up from corruption, O God!

*Troparia:*
Exercising thyself in prayers and fasting, and vigilantly entreating God, thou wast accounted worthy of divine revelations and visions, O divinely wise and most rich one, being taught things surpassing mind and thought through purity, O wise one!

As an angel in the flesh thou didst live on earth, O father, offering peaceful and bloodless sacrifices with faith, a contrite heart, and spirit unto the Creator, O blessed John, with joy!

Thy life, shining forth brighter than the sun, emitted rays of compassion unto the needy, *(Fol. 63r)*

driving away the dark cloud of poverty, O most rich one, and warming those held fast by the frost of bitter afflictions, O God-inspired one!

*Theotokion:*
Cease not praying for us, O all-holy Virgin Birthgiver of God, for thou art the confirmation of the faithful; and by hope in thee are we strengthened, and in love we unceasingly glorify thee and Him Who was incarnate of thee!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos the same:*[^516]
*Troparia:*
Adorned with the gift of wisdom, and beautified by the brightness of thy life, thou wast a divine sacred minister, interceding with the Creator for His creation; and thou wast a most bright and blameless teacher, O father!

Drawing near unto the mountain of virtues, and covered by the divine darkness, O father, thou didst receive from God the God-inscribed tablets of dogmas, O most rich one, and wast shown forth unto us as a second Moses, a lawgiver of grace!

Having sanctified thyself by mystical will, as a voluntary sacrifice by thy standing before the Creator, O Nilus, and adorned with contemplation and action: remember us who faithfully celebrate thy memory!

*Theotokion:*
Beholding the depth of thy fearful mysteries in figurative manifestations, that God was to take up abode in thy womb, the divinely speaking prophets proclaimed beforehand, O all-immaculate one; and we now, beholding the fulfillment, glorify it!

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*[^517]
Thou didst disperse thy wealth unto the poor, and now hast received heavenly wealth, O all-wise John; therefore we all honor thee, celebrating thy memory, O namesake of mercy![^518]

*Ikos:*
Having hoped in the mercy of God, O John, thou wast enriched with compassions and gifts from Him; whence thou also wast shown forth merciful, as He bestowed bounty upon all. Therefore, having compassion on my poverty, grant me the wealth of thy prayer, and fill my hungering heart with divine words, O divinely wise one, even as of old thou didst feed the hungry, O namesake of mercy!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^519]
The Hebrew children in the furnace boldly trampled upon the flame, and turned the fire into dew, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Troparia:*
Thou didst weave words with deeds, making them sure, and didst join the choir of the blessed, having been merciful and pure in spirit, O God-bearing John!

*(Fol. 63v)*
