Unto the sweetest taste of honey was refined gold converted for thee; for the Creator, looking upon thy rich good pleasure, gave thee rich recompense!

Illumined by the never-setting Light of the Trinity, O pleasing servant of the Trinity, thou now enlightenest those who honor thee and sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
Thee, the joy of the apostles and the glory of the passion-bearers, O Birthgiver of God, we faithfully entreat: account us worthy of eternal joy, who unceasingly hymn thee!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*[^520]
The youths who had come from Judea in Babylon of old trampled upon the flame of the furnace by their faith in the Trinity, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*
Watered with heavenly showers, O father, thou wast shown forth multi-fruitful, offering the fairest fruits unto the Master, for those who cry aloud in faith: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Opening the depths of dogmas, O all-blessed one, thy tongue powerfully drowns heretical deception, and teaches the faithful to sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

An angelic life in the flesh thou didst live on earth, O father; and enjoying the divine visions of heavenly spectacles, thou singest: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Incarnate from a virginal womb, Thou didst appear for our salvation; therefore, knowing thee as Mother and Birthgiver of God, thankfully we cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^521]
Having become victors over the tormentor and the flame by Thy grace, and holding fast unto Thy commandments, the children cried aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparia:*
Christ, having placed thee as a radiant star upon the height of the Church, O father, through thee enlightens those who sing in faith: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Thou wast shown forth merciful, meek, most compassionate, and guileless, O father: wealth of the poor, ornament and clothing of the naked, singing in faith: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Thou didst sacredly adorn the throne of Mark with divine works preeminently, O father; and by almsgiving and mercy thou wast named Merciful beyond all the saints who have shone forth in compassion![^522]

*(Fol. 64r)*

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast revealed as a daughter of fallen Adam, O Virgin, but Mother of God Who renewed my essence; Whom all works hymn as the Lord, and exalt above all unto all ages!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*[^523]
When the musical instruments sounded together, and countless peoples worshiped the image in Dura, three youths not submitting hymned and glorified the Lord unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
Having acquired perfect virtue, having loved the first of good things, and now illumined by the radiances of Him, thou criest aloud: Hymn the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Enriched with contemplative skill, thou didst attain active good renown, sending forth the rays of grace unto those who cry aloud: Hymn the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Having fled worldly tumults, thou didst reach the haven of silence, and didst mortify the assaults of the passions, crying aloud: Hymn the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
Knowing surely, O Virgin, that God the Word was born of thee, we hymn thee most piously, chanting in faith: Hymn the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^524]
Truly we confess thee to be the Birthgiver of God, being saved through thee, O pure Virgin, magnifying thee with the bodiless choirs!

*Troparia:*
Lo, after thy decease a pair of holy fathers receives thee in their midst, granting most sacred honor unto thee in the tomb, O father![^525]

As the morning, as the day, O Father John, thy radiant falling asleep shone forth, enlightening those who in faith call thee blessed!

Thou hast joined the choirs of hierarchs, prophets, apostles, and martyrs; with them remember, O father, those who praise thee!

The shrine wherein lie thy sacred and holy relics, O Father John, is a fountain of miracles unto those who come unto thee!

*Theotokion:*
O goodly Virgin, endow with goodness my soul afflicted by sin, who didst give birth unto the good God and Lord!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*[^526]
Heaven was dismayed thereat, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God appeared unto men bodily, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens; therefore the hierarchies of angels and men magnify thee as the Birthgiver of God!

*(Fol. 64v)*

*Troparia:*
Beholding thee, O father, having rent asunder the bonds of worldly attachment and drawing near unto God, the destroyer raised up barbarian tempests against thee, thinking to weaken thy strength; but by divine providence thou didst wound his craftiness, O all-blessed one![^527]

Shining with the rich radiances of manifold teachings, thou didst enlighten the souls of those who in the faith of piety come unto thee; for having touched thy lips unto the purest cup of wisdom, O all-wise Nilus, thou didst draw abundantly, and didst impart it unto those who love thee!

Thou didst zealously sanctify thyself mystically, O father, as an immaculate offering unto the Creator, having sincerely loved Him; before Whose throne thou now standest, O all-blessed Nilus, diligently pray that those who celebrate thy memory in faith may obtain thy brightness!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst set right the fall of womankind, O Virgin, having given birth unto the Word Who raises up the fallen, as good and mighty in power, Who out of surpassing loving-kindness became incarnate of thee, and saved the world by His passion-slaying passions!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены̀ ꙋ҆слы́шите):*[^528]
Imitating the mercy of the all-bountiful God, thou didst disperse wealth unto the needy, O John; therefore thou also didst receive inexhaustible wealth in the heavens. Therefore we now pray: pray unceasingly for those who praise thee!

*Glory, of the Venerable One, Podoben: "Having adorned heaven with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*[^529]
Desiring the angelic life, thou didst withdraw thyself into the wilderness; and having subjugated the carnal passions, thou wast shown forth an equal of angels, O our God-bearing father!

*Theotokion:*
Of the good things given by God unto the world, thou art the cause, O Birthgiver of God; but even now make the benevolent God merciful for our common salvation!

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*

*Glory, Tone 6:*
O venerable father, into all the earth has the sound of thy virtuous deeds gone forth; therefore in the heavens thou hast found the reward of thy labors: thou didst destroy the hosts of demons, and reached the ranks of angels, whose life thou didst blamelessly emulate. Having boldness unto Christ God, entreat peace for our souls!

*Now and ever, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*[^530]
Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, she who gave birth unto Thee cried aloud: What strange mystery is this which I behold *(Fol. 65r)*

...O my Son? How diest Thou in the flesh, hanged upon the tree, O Giver of life?

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Octoechos, on 4; and of the Saint, Ode 3, on 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 7: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones. Verse: What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He has rendered unto me?*

*Epistle: To the Hebrews, pericope 334.*

*Alleluia, Tone 2: The mouth of the righteous shall meditate on wisdom. Verse: The law of his God is in his heart.*

*Gospel: According to Luke, pericope 24.*

*Communion Verse: In everlasting remembrance shall the righteous be; [he shall not be afraid of evil tidings].*

*In the same month, on the 13th day: Our Father among the Saints, John Chrysostom, Archbishop of Constantinople.*

*At Small Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," stichera on 4, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*[^531]

Thou didst well emulate thy namesake the Baptist in self-control, O father, and Elijah the Great in fasting and purity; wounded by the zeal of both, O Chrysostom, thou didst speak boldly against the royal majesty, as a shepherd of the Church of Christ. *(Twice)*

By the divine inspiration of the Word, the sound of thy dogmas, according to that which is written, has gone forth into all the earth, O father, and enlightened the world; thou hast opened unto us the entrance of repentance by caring for the poor, proclaiming the Gospel of Christ.

The pure and undefiled light of thy soul leaves behind the rays of the sun, [enlightening] the world with the dogmas of piety, O wise father John Chrysostom; it drives away the darkness, and enlightens the universe unto piety.

*Glory, Tone 1:*
Thou wast a God-inspired instrument, O Chrysostom, through which the Holy Spirit proclaimed unto us; for with a most renowned voice the utterance of thy teachings went forth unto the ends [of the earth]; and having become an emulator of the Apostles, O venerable one, thou didst attain unto that choir *(Fol. 65v)*

...which thou didst desire. Pray unto the Lord, O all-blessed one, that He grant peace unto the world, and save our souls.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Deliver us from our necessities, O Mother of Christ God, who gavest birth unto the Creator of all, that we all may cry unto thee: Rejoice, the only protection of our souls!

*At the Aposticha, stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*[^532]

As a golden-hued trumpet brightly proclaiming the great works of God, thou hast been shown forth, O John, unto the ends of the world.

*Verse: My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be understanding.*

Even as Moses, thou didst receive the Law from the Lord, O Chrysostom, making wise and enlightening the world with thy divine teachings.

*Verse: Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice.*

Thou wast truly a herald of the divine kingdom, O golden-worded one, crying aloud: Repent, drowning all despair.

*Glory, in the same Tone and Podoben:*
Thou hast taught us to believe in the precious Trinity in one sovereignty: Father, Word, and Spirit, O Chrysostom our father.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O Virgin Birthgiver of God, together with golden-worded John, pray unto God the Word Who was born of thee, that He save our souls.

*Then: "Lord, now lettest Thou Thy servant depart"; the Trisagion; after the "Our Father":*

*Troparion, Tone 8:*
The grace that shone forth from thy mouth like a beam of fire enlightened the universe; it gained for the world the treasures of freedom from avarice, and showed unto us the height of humility. But as thou dost instruct us by thy words, O father John Chrysostom, pray unto Christ God the Word, that our souls may be saved.

*Glory, both now and ever, Theotokion:*
*"Who for our sake":*[^533]

*At Great Vespers, we chant the Kathisma, "Blessed is the man," the first antiphon. On "Lord, I have cried," stichera on 8, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^534]

The golden-forged trumpet, the God-inspired instrument, the inexhaustible deep of dogmas, the support of the Church, the heavenly mind, the abyss of wisdom, the all-golden chalice pouring forth rivers of honey-flowing teachings and watering creation, let us praise in song! *(Thrice)*

The unsetting star, enlightening all that is under the sun with the rays of teachings; the herald of repentance; the sponge *(Fol. 66r)*

...all-golden, that removes the bitter dampness of ignorance and bedews hearts wasted away by sins: let us worthily honor the golden-worded John! *(Thrice)*

The earthly angel and heavenly man, the sweet-speaking and many-voiced swallow, the treasure-house of virtues, the unyielding rock, the divine image of the faithful, the peer of martyrs, of equal rank with the holy angels, of one manner with the Apostles: let Chrysostom be magnified in hymns! *(Twice)*

*Glory, Tone 6:*
O venerable, thrice-blessed, most holy father, good shepherd and disciple of Christ the Chief Shepherd, who didst lay down thy life for the sheep: do thou thyself even now, O all-praised John Chrysostom, ask by thy prayers that great mercy be granted unto us!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
*"Who will not call thee blessed":*[^535]

*Entrance; Prokeimenon of the day; and the readings.*

*A Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 10):*[^536]
The memory of the righteous is with praises, and the blessing of the Lord is upon his head. Blessed is the man that has found wisdom, and the mortal that knows understanding. For to buy her is better than the treasures of gold and silver. And she is more precious than costly stones; no precious thing is worthy to be compared unto her. For length of days and years of life are in her right hand, and in her left hand are riches and glory. Out of her mouth proceeds righteousness, and law and mercy she carries upon her tongue. Give ear therefore unto me, O children, for I will speak noble things; and blessed is the man that keeps my ways. For my outgoings are the outgoings of life, and favor is prepared from the Lord. Therefore I pray you, and utter my voice unto the sons of men. For I, wisdom, have builded counsel, and understanding and knowledge have I called upon. Mine is counsel and safety, mine is understanding, and strength is mine. I love them that love me, and those that seek me shall find grace. Understand craftiness, therefore, ye simple ones, and ye uninstructed, lay it to your heart. Give ear unto me yet again, for I will speak noble things; and I will open from my lips right things. For my palate shall meditate truth, and false lips are an abomination before me. All the words of my mouth are with righteousness; there is nothing crooked or perverse in them. They are all right to those that understand, and plain to them that find knowledge.

*(Fol. 66v)*

"For I teach you the truth, that your hope may be in the Lord, and that ye may be filled with the Spirit."

*A Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 10):*[^537]
The mouth of the righteous distills wisdom, but the lips of wise men know grace. The mouth of the wise meditates on wisdom, and righteousness delivers them from death. When a righteous man dies, hope does not perish; for a righteous son is born unto life, and in his good things he shall reap the fruit of righteousness. Light is ever with the righteous, and from the Lord they shall find grace and glory. The tongue of the wise knows good things, and in their heart wisdom rests. The Lord loves holy hearts, and all that are undefiled in the way are acceptable unto Him. The wisdom of the Lord enlightens the face of the prudent. For she anticipates them that desire her, before they know her; and she is easily seen by them that love her. He that rises early to seek her shall have no toil, and he that watches for her sake shall quickly be free from care. For she goes about seeking such as are worthy of her, and shows herself favorably unto them in the paths. Wickedness can never prevail against wisdom; for this cause I became a lover of her beauty, and I loved her and sought her from my youth, and desired to take her unto myself as a bride, for the Master of all loved her. For she is an initiate of the knowledge of God, and a chooser of His works. Her labors are virtues: for she teaches temperance and prudence, righteousness and fortitude, which are such things as men can have nothing more profitable in their life. And if any man desire much experience, she knows things of old, and conjectures what is to come; she knows the subtleties of speeches and the solutions of dark riddles; she foresees signs and wonders, and the events of seasons and years; and unto all she is a good counselor, for immortality is in her, and good repute in communion with her words. Therefore I spoke unto the Lord, and prayed unto Him, and said from my whole heart: O God of our fathers, and Lord of mercy, Who hast made all things with Thy word, and ordained man through Thy wisdom, that he should have dominion over the creatures which Thou hast made, and order the world in holiness and righteousness: Give me wisdom that sits by Thy thrones, and reject me not from among Thy servants, for I am Thy servant and the son of Thine handmaid. Send her out of Thy holy heavens, and from the throne of Thy glory, that being present she may labor with me and teach me what is well-pleasing *(Fol. 67r)*

"...is well-pleasing before Thee; and she shall guide me in understanding, and preserve me in her glory. For the thoughts of mortals are all timorous, and their devices are fallible."

*A Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 4):*[^538]
When the righteous man is praised, the people shall rejoice; for his memory is immortality, because it is known with God and with men, and his soul was pleasing unto the Lord. Love wisdom therefore, O men, and ye shall live. Desire her, and ye shall be instructed; for the beginning of her is love, and the keeping of laws. Honor wisdom, that ye may reign for ever. I will tell you, and will not hide from you the mysteries of God; for He is the guide of wisdom and the director of the wise; and in His hand is all prudence and knowledge of workmanship. And wisdom teaches all understanding; for in her is an understanding spirit, holy, the radiance of the everlasting light, and the unspotted mirror of the goodness of God. She prepares friends of God and prophets. She is more beautiful than the sun, and above all the order of stars; being compared with light, she is found prior. She delivered them that waited upon her from distress, and guided them into right paths. She gave them knowledge of holy things, and preserved them from them that lay in wait, and gave them a mighty conflict, that all might know that piety is stronger than all. And wickedness can never overcome wisdom, neither shall judgment pass by the wicked in their conviction. For they said within themselves, reasoning unrighteously: Let us oppress the righteous man, let us not spare his holiness, neither reverence the gray hairs of the ancient in years. Let our strength be the law; let us lie in wait for the righteous, because he is displeasing unto us, and is contrary to our works, and upbraids us with our transgressions of the law, and objects to our infamy the transgressions of our education. He professes to have the knowledge of God, and calls himself the child of the Lord. He was made to reprove our thoughts; he is grievous unto us even to behold, for his life is not like other men's, and his ways are of another fashion. We are esteemed of him as a counterfeiting; he abstains from our ways as from filthiness, and pronounces the end of the just to be blessed. Let us see then if his words be true, and let us test what shall happen in the end of him. Let us examine him with spitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his guilelessness. Let us condemn him with a shameful death, for there shall be a visitation according to his words. Such things they did imagine, and were deceived; for their own malice blinded *(Fol. 67v)*

...them; and they knew not the mysteries of God, neither did they judge that Thou art God alone, Who hast the power of life and death, and savest in the time of tribulation, and deliverest from every evil; Who art bountiful and merciful, and givest grace unto Thy venerable ones, and with Thine arm opposest the proud.

*At the Litiya, the sticheron of the temple; and the idiomela of the Saint.*

*Tone 1. By Anatolius:*[^539]
O luminary John, golden-shining mouth, adornment of divinely wrought virtues, dwelling-place of mystical Scriptures: thou wast the most pure, incorruptible treasury of the All-Holy Spirit; whence thou didst gladden the whole Church by thy saving word. Having therefore found boldness toward God in the enjoyment of the heavenly heritage, pray for us, O most holy father!

Grace was poured out upon thy lips, O venerable father John Chrysostom; therefore God anointed thee hierarch of His people, to shepherd His flock in holiness and righteousness. Therefore, girded with the armor of the Mighty One, thou didst cut down the tongue-harming heresies; and even now cease not to pray, that He grant peace unto the world, and save our souls.

*Tone 2. By the Studite:*[^540]
Thee, the great hierarch and shepherd, guileless and venerable, herald of repentance, golden-worded mouth of grace, we praise with love and pray: Grant us thy prayers, O father, unto the salvation of our souls!

*By George of Nicomedia:*[^541]
Having adorned herself with thy golden words as with golden ornaments, O John Chrysostom, the Church, rejoicing as a bride, cries out unto thee: I am filled from thy gold-streaming waters! Adorned with gold-woven and honey-golden drinks, for by thy gentle teachings thou leadest up from action unto contemplation; and having united herself with Christ, the spiritual Bridegroom, she reigns with Him. Therefore we also, having assembled on thy memory, cry out: Cease not to pray for us unto the Lord, that He save our souls!

Thou didst receive the higher philosophy, O hierarch, and wast outside the world, living above visible things; and thou wast divinely shown forth an unspotted mirror of God; and as a son ever united with light, thou didst receive light, and obtained a most radiant, blessed end. Pray, O Chrysostom, for our souls!

*(Fol. 68r)*

*Tone 4:*
With most golden-radiant voices thou didst visibly water the earth, having a gold-streaming soul and body, O all-blessed one, gilding all things with thy words, O fashioner in gold of thy dogmas; and having written gold-inscribed books, thou didst take flight unto the heavens. Therefore we cry unto thee: O gold-streaming Chrysostom, pray unto Christ God, that He save our souls!

*Glory, in the same Tone. By Germanus:*[^542]
It was fitting for the imperial city of cities to have John as hierarch, as a certain adornment of the Church and a golden-forged trumpet, making all the ends [of the earth] resound with saving dogmas, and stirring up all to the zeal of divinely-befitting songs. Unto whom let us cry aloud: O golden-worded Chrysostom, pray unto Christ God, that He save our souls!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Thee have we gained as a wall, O most pure Birthgiver of God, a calm haven and confirmation; therefore we pray, who are storm-tossed in this life: guide and save us!

*At the Aposticha, stichera, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, life-bearing Cross" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*[^543]

Rejoice, golden-radiant and fair, God-inspired instrument of the Church; tongue that in love for mankind depicts for us manifold images of repentance; golden-minded intellect; golden-feathered swallow; dove, in the words of the Psalm, shining with gold between her shoulders upon the pasture of virtues; most golden stream pouring forth waters; divine mouth, pledge of divine love for mankind: pray unto Christ, that He send down upon our souls great mercy!

*Verse: My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be understanding.*

Rejoice, father of orphans, swift help of the wronged, supply of the needy, food of the hungry, correction of sinners, most acceptable and honorable physician of souls; lofty assurance of theology; exposition of spiritual Scriptures; most efficacious law, most upright rule; supreme wisdom of contemplation and action: pray unto Christ, that He send down upon our souls great mercy!

*Verse: The mouth of the righteous shall meditate on wisdom, and his tongue shall speak of judgment.*

Rejoice, the Church cries out unto thee, her bridegroom, O Chrysostom, who didst shine forth throughout the whole world, more than the rays of the sun, by virtues and pearl-like words, most wise above the wise, most exalted among rhetors, champion of true dogmas, refuter of falsehood, teacher of repentance!

*(Fol. 68v)*

...Rejoice, most tranquil abyss of knowledge, who, following the great Paul, didst inherit the mouth and mind of Christ: Whom beseech, that He grant great mercy unto our souls!

*Glory, Tone 6:*
Thou hast been shown forth as a golden-voiced trumpet, O golden-speaking Chrysostom, gilding the hearts of the faithful with thy gold-wrought teachings; for prophetic-like the utterance of thy righteous deeds has gone forth, O venerable father, and enlightened the ends of the whole world.

*Now and ever:*
*"My Maker and Redeemer":*[^544]

*At the blessing of the loaves: The troparion of the Saint, twice; and "O Birthgiver of God and Virgin, rejoice," once. But where an all-night vigil is not celebrated: after the troparion, Glory, both now and ever, Theotokion; and the dismissal.*

*At Matins, on "God is the Lord," the troparion twice; Glory, both now and ever, the Sunday Theotokion.*

*After the first stichology, the Sessional hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "The angelic choir" (Ли́къ а҆́гг҃лскїй):*[^545]
As a star of golden aspect thou didst brightly shine forth unto earthly men, O Chrysostom, all-blessed John, enlightening the ends [of the earth] with the beams of thy words. Therefore, celebrating this day thy most holy memory, we ask forgiveness of all our sins. *(Twice)*

*Glory, both now and ever, Theotokion:*
O unwedded, pure Virgin Birthgiver of God, sole protectress and shelter of the faithful: deliver from afflictions, tribulations, and cruel circumstances all who place their hope in thee, O Maiden, and save our souls by thy divine prayers!

*After the second stichology, the Sessional hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-beginningless" (Собезначя́лное сло́во):*[^546]
The flower-garden of sayings of the God-inspired Scriptures, who guides us unto repentance and endured many temptations: having learned from him, ye faithful, let us honor Chrysostom as is due; for he prays unto the Lord, that our souls may be saved. *(Twice)*

*Glory, both now and ever, Theotokion:*
The terrible wonder of thy conception and the ineffable manner of thy giving birth have been made known in thee, O pure Ever-Virgin; it astounds my mind and amazes my understanding. Thy glory, O Birthgiver of God, is spread abroad unto all, for the salvation of our souls.

*After the Polyeleos, the Sessional hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^547]
A spiritual treasure hast thou appeared, by thy divine words, as truly, O Chrysostom, having shone forth unto the ends of the world *(Fol. 69r)*

...ends of the world: saving riches hast thou granted unto all, guiding the people unto repentance, O blessed one. Therefore, having finished the course of this life, thou standest before the throne of the Most High, O all-blessed John Chrysostom; pray unto Christ God, that He grant forgiveness of sins unto those who in love celebrate thy holy memory! *(Twice)*

*Glory, both now and ever, Theotokion:*
The heavenly gate and ark, the most holy mountain, the radiant cloud let us hymn, the unburnt bush, the rational paradise, the recall of Eve, the great treasure of all the universe: for in her was wrought the salvation of the world and the remission of ancient sins. Therefore we cry unto her: Pray unto thy Son, that He grant remission of transgressions unto those who piously worship thy most holy childbearing!

*The Graduals: The first antiphon of Tone 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4: My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be understanding. Verse: Hear these things, all ye nations.*

*"Let every breath..."*

*Gospel: According to John, pericope 35 from the midpoint.*

*After Psalm 50, idiomelic sticheron, Tone 6:*
Grace was poured out upon thy lips, O venerable father; and thou wast a shepherd of Christ's Church, teaching the rational sheep to believe in the consubstantial Trinity, in one Godhead.

*Canon of the Most Holy Birthgiver of God, with the Heirmos on 6, Tone 8.*[^548]

*Ode 1, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^549]
Having traversed the water as dry land, and escaped the evil of Egypt, the Israelite cried aloud: Let us sing unto our Redeemer and God!

*Troparion:*
Held fast by many temptations, unto thee do I flee, seeking salvation: O Mother of the Word and Virgin, save me from hardships and afflictions!

*Troparion:*
Assaults of the passions trouble me, filling my soul with much despondency: calm them, O Maiden, with the tranquility of thy Son and God, O all-immaculate one!

*Troparion:*
Thee, who didst give birth unto the Savior and God, I entreat, O Virgin, that I may be delivered from tribulations; for fleeing now unto thee, I stretch forth both soul and understanding.

*Troparion:*
Ailing in body and soul, vouchsafe me divine visitation and providence from thee, O sole Mother of God, as good, and parent of the Good!

*Canon of the Saint on 8, whose acrostic is:*[^550]

*(Fol. 69v)*

"By the Spirit, I sing of thee, O golden mouth." By Theophanes, Tone 8.[^551]

*Ode 1, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^552]
The wonderworking staff of Moses, striking the sea crosswise and dividing it, once overwhelmed the charioteer Pharaoh; but it saved the fleeing people of Israel as they journeyed on foot, singing a hymn unto God.

*Troparion:*
Having been a most fervent preacher of repentance, O Chrysostom: pray unto God, O father, that I may repent with all my heart, and entreat Him by thy intercession to heal the wounds of my ancient transgressions!

*Troparion:*
Having received the whole radiance of the Holy Spirit, O father, thou wast shown forth an all-bright pillar guiding the Church, O venerable one, and a radiant cloud overshadowing the assemblies of the Orthodox, O all-blessed one!

*Troparion:*
Ordained by Christ as a teacher, O father, thou didst richly pour forth divine teachings with a golden-hued tongue and a divinely-wise mind; for thou wast shown forth as God's river, filled with the waters of the Spirit, O divinely-blessed Chrysostom!

*Theotokion:*
Adorned with the variety of grace, O thou who art full of divine joy, beyond mind and word thou, O blessed one, didst give birth unto the Father's Word Who became flesh through His manifold compassion, whilst remaining an undefiled Virgin.

*Katavasia: "I will open my mouth":*[^553]

*Ode 3, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^554]
O Lord, Creator of the vault of heaven and Builder of the Church, do Thou establish me in Thy love, O summit of desires, confirmation of the faithful, O only Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
The protection and shelter of my life do I place in thee, O Virgin Birthgiver of God: do thou pilot me unto thy haven, who art the cause of good things, the confirmation of the faithful, O only all-lauded one!

*Troparion:*
I entreat thee, O Virgin, to disperse the tempest of my grief and the turmoil of my soul; for thou, O Bride of God, hast given birth unto Christ the Prince of peace, O only most pure one!

*Troparion:*
Having given birth unto the Benefactor, the Cause of good things, pour forth the riches of benevolence unto all; for thou canst do all things, as having given birth unto Christ Who is mighty in strength, O divinely blessed one!

*Troparion:*
Unto me who am afflicted by cruel diseases and painful passions, O Virgin, do thou help; for I know thee to be an inexhaustible, unfailing treasury of healings, O all-immaculate one!

*Another Heirmos:*[^555]
Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens with understanding, and the earth upon the waters and established the earth upon the waters: do Thou establish me, O Christ, upon the rock of Thy commandments; for there is none holy save Thee, O only Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Enriched with the mind of Christ through thy pure life, thou wast a fellow-worker, narrator, and minister of the salvation of men, O Chrysostom, pouring forth the saving teachings of divine inspiration, O divinely-inspired one!

*Troparion:*
Enriched with the immaterial treasures of the Spirit, thou didst draw from the springs of salvation an ever-flowing fountain of teachings, and didst fill the face of the whole Church, O venerable father!

*Troparion:*
Having cleared the overgrown fields of the soul with the wise husbandry of thy words, O Chrysostom, thou, O wise one, didst show them forth to be fruitful, watering them divinely acceptably with heavenly showers!

*Theotokion:*
There is no blemish nor defilement in thee at all, O Virgin, but rather thou wast shown forth as the dwelling-place of heavenly goodness; for in thee dwelt all the holiness of virtues, O all-immaculate one.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премудрости):*[^556]
Divinely drawing forth the wealth of understanding of ineffable wisdom, thou didst treasure up for all the waters of Orthodoxy, which divinely gladden the hearts of the faithful, and deservedly submerge the opinions of the unbelieving. Therefore, by the sweat of piety on both sides, thou wast shown forth an undefeated champion of the Trinity, O John Chrysostom: entreat Christ God to grant the remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love!

*Glory... Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премудрости):*[^557]
Having known the wisdom that is from above, and the grace of words from God, Thou didst shine forth unto all like gold in a furnace; and Thou didst preach the Holy Trinity, the Unity. Thou didst pierce the deceit of avarice with thy words. Therefore, also having rebuked the Empress with zeal, Thou didst crush the foreign arrogance of Arius, O John Chrysostom: entreat Christ God to grant the remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love!

*Now and ever... Theotokion, Tone 8:*[^558]
Reflecting upon the fiery flame of Gehenna, and the burning, the weeping therein and the wailing, the most wretched parting, and the hotter separation from the inheritance and joyful assembly of the saints, tremble, O my soul, and groan; and make haste to blot out the record of thy myriad debts by tears of compunction having as an unashamed advocate the pure Mother of God; for on her account remission of transgressions is granted unto those who orthodoxly glorify her as Birthgiver of God.

*Ode 4, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^559]
I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation, I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Divinity.

*Troparion:*
Having given birth unto the Lord and Pilot, do thou, O Bride of God, quell the turmoil of my passions and the tempest of my transgressions!

*Troparion:*
Do thou, who didst give birth unto the Compassionate One and Savior of all that hymn Thee, grant unto me who call upon the abyss of thy loving-kindness!

*Troparion:*
Enjoying thy gifts, O most pure one, we sing a thanksgiving song, knowing thee to be the Mother of God.

*Troparion:*
Unto me who lie upon the bed of my sickness and infirmity, do thou, O Birthgiver of God, help as a lover of good, O only Ever-Virgin!

*Troparion:*
Having thee as hope and confirmation, and an immovable wall of salvation, O all-lauded one, we are delivered from every distress!

*Another Heirmos:*[^560]
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art my power, Thou art my God, Thou art my joy, Who, without leaving the bosom of the Father, hast visited our poverty. Therefore, with the Prophet Habakkuk, I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Christ, Who as the Good One provids for all by His providence, gave thee unto us as another one of one mind with the Apostles: an initiate mystagogue, a preacher, and a divine expositor of heavenly mysteries, O all-blessed John Chrysostom!

*Troparion:*
Let us honor the golden-radiant and golden-worded John Chrysostom, who hath gilded all things with the golden-hued radiances of his teaching, and enlightened the world with a tongue brighter than gold and fuller of light, pouring forth divine grace!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast entirely a dwelling-place of God, Thou wast entirely shown forth an instrument of the Spirit, sounding forth a divinely inspired hymn of every virtue, and manifesting the cause of salvation and the beauty of the Heavenly Kingdom, O all-blessed John Chrysostom!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst preach the loving-kindness of God, setting forth patterns of repentance, and most excellently teaching of the avoidance of evils, O most blessed and all-perfect one, pouring forth discourses on excellent works, O all-honored father Chrysostom!

*Theotokion:*
After God we have acquired thee as an advocate, for thou, O all-immaculate one, wast the Mother of God the Creator and Maker, Who took our form, and saved it from corruption and death, and glorified it with divine glory.

*Ode 5, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^561]
Enlighten us by Thy commandments, O Lord, and by Thy high arm grant Thy peace unto us, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Fill my heart with gladness, O pure one, giving thine incorruptible joy, who didst give birth unto the Cause of gladness!

*Troparion:*
Deliver us from distress, O pure Birthgiver of God, who didst give birth unto eternal redemption, and the peace that surpasses all understanding!

*Troparion:*
Disperse the gloom of my transgressions, O Bride of God, by the illumination of thy radiance, who didst give birth unto the divine and pre-eternal Light!

*Troparion:*
Heal the infirmity of my soul, O pure one, having vouchsafed it thy visitation, and grant me health by thy prayers!

*Another Heirmos:*[^562]
Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy face, O unwaning Light, and an alien darkness hath covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and guide my paths unto the light of Thy commandments, I pray!

*Troparion:*
All of us know thee as the most radiant and soul-saving luminary of the Church, snatching souls from the deadly throat and guiding them unto eternal life, O ever-hymned father!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst destroy the ranks of the heretics, O thrice-blessed one, having armed thyself with the weapons of piety and the courage of the soul, O most sacred one; and rejoicing, thou didst gather together the all-bright choirs of the Orthodox in the bond of the Spirit!

*Troparion:*
Thy cheeks are filled like bowls of divine aromatics, and gladden the universe with spiritual fragrances through the myrrh-scented mystagogy of understandings and the beauty of thy words, O all-wise one!

*Theotokion:*
Having conceived God the Creator, Maker, and Lord, all human generations call thee blessed, O pure one, and the intelligent hierarchies of the bodiless hosts glorify thee as the Mother of God!

*Ode 6, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^563]
I will pour out my supplication unto the Lord, and unto Him will I proclaim my griefs; for my soul is filled with evils, and my life hath drawn near unto Hades; and I pray like Jonah: Raise me up from corruption, O God!

*Troparion:*
As He hath saved from death and corruption, having surrendered Himself unto death my nature which was held captive by corruption and death; do thou, O Virgin, pray unto the Lord and thy Son, to deliver me from the malice of enemies!

*Troparion:*
I know thee to be the advocate of my life, and a firm guardian, O Virgin, dispersing the tumult of temptations, and driving away the assaults of demons; and I pray ever to be delivered from the corruption of my passions.

*Troparion:*
We have acquired thee as a wall of refuge, and the all-perfect salvation of souls, and spaciousness in sorrows, O Maiden, and in thy light we ever rejoice; O Lady, do thou even now save us from passions and distress!

*Troparion:*
I lie now infirm upon my bed, and there is no healing for my flesh; but having given birth unto God and the Savior of the world, and the Deliverer from infirmities, I pray unto thee who art good: Raise me up from the corruption of sicknesses!

*Another Heirmos:*[^564]
Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray; for unto Thee have I cried, and do Thou give ear unto me, O God of my salvation!

*Troparion:*
With spiritual wisdom thou didst enrich the whole world, having become a rich dispenser of the Word; for rich grace was poured forth from on high upon thy lips, O hierarch!

*Troparion:*
Into all the earth went forth thy sound like lightning, and the power of thy words, O Chrysostom, like a loud-sounding trumpet, resounded throughout all the ends of the universe!

*Troparion:*
From on high thou wast clothed in the incorruptible vesture of virtues, O all-blessed one, and robed in the beauty of words, thou wast shown forth a glorious confirmation of the truth!

*Theotokion:*
Bearing all things by His almighty power, the Lover of mankind clothed Himself from thee in weak flesh, O all-immaculate Virgin, for the benefaction of men.

*Kontakion, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having fulfilled the dispensation for us" (Еже о насъ исполнивъ):*[^565]
From the heavens thou didst receive divine grace, and with thy lips thou teachest all to worship the One God in Trinity, O John Chrysostom, all-blessed venerable one! Worthily do we praise thee, for thou art a guide, revealing divine things!

*Ikos:*[^566]
Unto the Creator of all I bow the knee, unto the Pre-Eternal Word I stretch forth my hands, seeking the gift of speech, that I may hymn the venerable one whom He Himself magnified; for He Who lives unto the ages says unto the Prophet: "With faith I glorify them that glorify Me." He Who of old exalted Samuel hath now glorified the hierarch; for the talent that was entrusted unto him trading well with that which was entrusted unto him, he brought it unto the King. Therefore also the Pre-Essential One highly exalted him. Of his grace do I, the unworthy one, ask, worthily to hymn his discourse; for he is a guide unto the ends of the earth, revealing divine things.

*Ode 7, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^567]
The Children that came down from Judea in Babylon of old trod down the flame of the furnace by their faith in the Trinity, singing: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
When Thou wast pleased to order our salvation, O Savior, Thou didst dwell in the womb of the Virgin, whom Thou didst show forth unto the world as an advocate: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
Do thou, O pure Mother, entreat the Lover of mercy Whom thou hast borne, that they may be delivered from transgressions and spiritual defilements who cry in faith: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
A treasury of salvation and fountain of incorruption hast Thou shown forth her that bare Thee, and a tower of strength and door of repentance unto them that cry: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
Vouchsafe to heal bodily weaknesses and spiritual infirmities, O Birthgiver of God, in those who approach thy shelter with love, O Virgin, who didst give birth unto Christ our Savior!

*Another Heirmos:*[^568]
The fire was abashed at God's condescension in Babylon of old; therefore the Children in the furnace, dancing with joyful foot as in a meadow of flowers, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having learned the abyss of the goodness and loving-kindness of God, thou wast shown forth a surety of salvation unto them that repent fervently and with all their soul cry unto the Lord: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
By thy teachings thou dost guide every mind, O Chrysostom, and dost heal the infirmities of the soul as one most compassionate, rejoicing in divinely flowing words: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast exalted, having been chosen, venerable, guileless, a priest of the Most High, brightly clothed with righteousness, and crying in gladness, O all-wealthy one: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst conceive, O most pure one, God and the Lord Who is over all, Who was pleased to save mankind from corruption and death, Whom worthily hymning, we cry: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Ode 8, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^569]
The King of heaven, Whom the angelic hosts hymn: praise and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Despise not them that require help of thee, O Virgin, who hymn and supremely exalt thee unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Thou healest the infirmity of my soul and bodily sicknesses, O Virgin, that I may glorify thee, O pure one, unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Thou pourest forth the wealth of healings unto them that faithfully hymn thee, O Virgin, and supremely exalt thine ineffable birthgiving!

*Troparion:*
Thou drivest away the assaults of temptations and the onslaughts of passions, O Virgin; therefore we hymn thee unto all ages!

*Another Heirmos:*[^570]
Sevenfold did the Chaldean tormentor furiously kindle the furnace for the godly; but seeing them saved by a greater power, he cried unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye Children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
We who converse intelligently with thy words, O Chrysostom, are taught honored theology, and bring forth the useful fruit of good things, and flee the harm of malice; for thou wast the common steward of salvation, crying: Supremely exalt Christ unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Pray unto the Master for us, O Chrysostom, having most compassionate boldness and by thy merciful and philanthropic love, O father; for thee do we, the faithful, set before the Savior as mediator, advocate, and most fervent intercessor, O divinely wise hierarch, all-blessed John!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst rebuke the youthful resistance and unbending pride of the rulers' injustice, warmly interceding for the wronged, O venerable one; and thou wast a father to orphans, widows, and the poor with loving purpose, crying: Supremely exalt Christ unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
By bodily types, and various enigmas, and symbolic and significant prefigurations, the divinely-speaking prophets proclaimed beforehand thy supernatural and marvelous birthgiving, O Virgin; therefore, rejoicing, we piously hymn thee, supremely exalting Christ unto all ages!

*Ode 9, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^571]
Truly we confess thee to be the Birthgiver of God, who through thee are saved, O pure Virgin, magnifying thee with the bodiless choirs!

*Troparion:*
Turn not away from the stream of my tears, O Virgin, who didst give birth unto Christ Who wipes away every tear from every face!

*Troparion:*
Fill my heart with joy, O Virgin, who didst receive the fullness of joy, consuming the sorrow of sin!

*Troparion:*
Enlighten with the rays of thy light, O Virgin, driving away the darkness of ignorance from them that piously confess thee to be the Birthgiver of God!

*Troparion:*
Heal him that is brought low in the place of affliction and infirmity, O Virgin, turning him from ill-health unto health!

*Another Heirmos:*[^572]
Heaven was stricken with awe at this, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God hath appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens. Therefore the hierarchies of angels and men magnify thee as the Birthgiver of God!

*Troparion:*
Truly enjoying life, O father, for which thou didst strive as much as was possible, thou didst excel on earth with an angelic life, and didst acquire the tongue of Christ and gentle lips: pray, O divinely-speaking one, for the salvation of them that exquisitely bless thee with faith!

*Troparion:*
Thy words, O thrice-blessed one, are words of life, mediating unending life; for Christ showed thee forth as a flowing fountain and a river pouring forth streams of divine teachings: truly a torrent of sweetness, a stream of remission, and a radiant preacher of repentance!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast shown forth a most radiant mediator between God and men, O hierarch; for thou wast shown forth a divinely-radiant luminary of piety, of divine knowledge, and a corrector of mothers: therefore with heartfelt love do we now worthily magnify thee, O golden-worded one!

*Theotokion:*
O pure, all-glorious Mother of God, save them that hymn thee with love, mercifully quelling the tumult of temptations; for having given birth unto God, thou accomplishest whatsoever thou wilt, succeeding unhindered, and art able to do all things, O Virgin: therefore do we all magnify thee!

*Exapostilarion, Tone 2, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Духомъ во святилищи):*[^573]
With thy golden-radiant words the Church of Christ is brightly illumined, O father Chrysostom! And the souls of the faithful rejoice, honoring thine all-holy memory; for unto all thou wast shown forth a guide of repentance and a leader of salvation!

*Glory... Another Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены услышите):*[^574]
Let us all praise the all-wise John, the most loud-voiced preacher of repentance, the treasury of the poor, the golden and divinely speaking lips of the Church, the manifestation of the Scriptures: that having been confirmed by him confirmed.

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*
O all-immaculate Virgin, my Lady and Sovereign Lady, entreat thy Son together with the glorious Chrysostom, that they who hymn thee may be delivered from all temptations, and obtain eternal blessings, O all-holy one; for thou canst do whatsoever thou wilt!

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4. Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Далъ еси знаменiе):*[^575]
A most honored vessel of the Divine Spirit wast thou, and a most sacred shepherd, an angel on earth, a pillar of the Church, and a foundation of dogmas, a surety of sinners, the divine consolation of the repentant, a provider for the poor, and the comfort of orphans, O John Chrysostom, intercessor for our souls!

*Sticheron:*
An all-radiant sun illuminating the universe with thy words, thou wast a most radiant star, a lamp shining with dawn-like rays, drawing unto the haven of tranquility those who are ever tempest-tossed upon the sea of the world, by the grace of salvation, O golden-worded Chrysostom, intercessor for our souls!

*Sticheron:*
An earthly angel and heavenly man, a sweet-singing nightingale, a river filled with the waters of words, a cloud dropping spiritual waters, pouring down richly unto us all, a teacher of salvation and a helper of repentance, O John Chrysostom, thou truly wast!

*Sticheron:*
Unjustly driven from thy flock, O venerable father, thou didst partake in tribulations and bitter exile, wherein thou wast vouchsafed a blessed end like a valiant sufferer, having conquered the manifold-wiled adversary; and with a diadem of victory Christ crowned thee, O John Chrysostom, intercessor for our souls!

*Glory... Tone 8, by Anatolius:*[^576]
Having adorned the Church of God with golden words and divinely-uttered teachings, thou didst lay up spiritual wealth in her: thy divinely-transmitted words. Therefore, having woven a crown of incorruptible flowers with hymns, she offers it unto thy most sacred memory, O John, all-golden in soul and tongue, divinely wise! But as thou hast boldness, O venerable one, pray for our souls!

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*
O Sovereign Lady, accept the prayer of thy servants, and deliver us from all distress and sorrow!

*The Great Doxology. And the Dismissal.*
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes from the Canon, Ode 3 and Ode 6.*[^577]
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.[^578]
*Verse:* Hear this, all ye nations; give ear, all ye that inhabit the world.
*Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 318 [Heb. 7:26–8:2].*[^579]
*Alleluia, Tone 2:* The mouth of the righteous shall meditate on wisdom.
*Gospel according to John, Pericope 36 [Jn. 10:9–16].*[^580]
*Communion Verse:* The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance.
*At the trapeza there is great consolation for the brethren.*

*In the same month, on the 14th day: The Holy and All-Lauded Apostle Philip.*

*At Vespers, we chant "Blessed is the man", the first antiphon.*[^581]
*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Apostle on 6, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having set aside all" (Все отложше):*[^582]
Having posited action as the ascent unto true contemplation, O blessed one, and contemplation as the end of godly action: thou didst entreat Christ to show unto thee the ineffable glory of the Father; for every rational nature, O glorious one, desires God Who brought it into being.[^583] And thou didst obtain that which was desired, immediately receiving the Son, His seal: Whom do thou with boldness entreat for our souls! *(Thrice)*

*Sticheron:*
Ever instructed by divine ascents, like Moses of old thou didst desire to see God: and spiritually thou didst see His image, having received it unto likeness; for the Son is the swift persuasion and demonstration of the Father: the Son and the Begetter are known as one essence, and in all things honorably extolled in identity of Kingdom, power, glory, and worship! *(Thrice)*

*Sticheron:*
Thou wast an instrument sounded by divine inspirations and expositions of the Holy Spirit. And singing a celestial song, thou didst proclaim the Gospel of salvation in the world with thy fiery tongue; for thou didst consume all deceit like readily combustible matter and as grass of the earth that withers; and thou didst preach unto the universe Christ, the Master and Lord Who is over all, O Philip, beholder of God! *(Twice)*

*Glory... Tone 6, by Byzantios:*[^584]
Kindled with the splendors of the Great Light, O Philip, thou didst shine forth as a universal luminary; and seeking the Father of lights in the Son, thou didst find Him: for in Light is Light found. For He is a seal of equal form, revealing the Archetype: Whom entreat, O Apostle, that they who have been sealed with His divine Blood may be saved!

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*
Who will not call thee blessed?...[^585]

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day, and three readings. Seek them on the 4th day of this month.*[^586]
*At the Litiya, Sticheron of the Temple, and of the Apostle, Tone 1, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Яко добля):*[^587]
By the simplicity of grace, O thou who art worthy of all wonder, obeying the summons of the Teacher, thou didst draw men from the depth of vanity, O Philip, for He enlightened thy understanding in all things, and showed thee forth, O all-blessed one, an apostle and honorable, divinely-speaking herald of His unsearchable Divinity!

*Sticheron:*
The radiance of the Spirit came down upon thee as in the appearance of fire, and made thee, O blessed one, a divine vessel: swiftly driving away the gloom of godlessness, and enlightening the world with the radiance of thy most wise words, O mystical speaker, adornment of the Apostles, blessed eyewitness of Christ!

*Sticheron:*
With the lightnings of thy preaching, O glorious one, having enlightened those sitting in the darkness of ignorance, thou didst show them forth as sons of God through faith; for thou wast zealous for His passions and death, and becamest an heir of glory, as one wise and divinely speaking, as a disciple of the truth!

*Glory... Tone 2:*[^588]
Having left earthly things, thou didst follow Christ, and having been sent by Him into the lost nations through the inspiration of signs of the Holy Spirit to turn men unto the light of His knowledge, O Apostle Philip: and having finished the contests of thy divine suffering and various torments, thou didst commit thy soul unto Christ: Him do thou entreat, O all-blessed one, to grant us great mercy!

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*[^589]
All my hope do I place in thee, O Mother of God: keep me under thy shelter!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Небныхъ чиновъ):*[^590]
The utterances of thy heavenly preachings resounded upon the earth, O all-blessed one, and filled it with dogmas, wherewith having mystically theologized the Son as consubstantial with the Father and the Spirit, O Apostle, we glorify Him!

*Verse:*[^591]

*Verse: Their proclamation hath gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the universe.*[^592]
Having thee now as a light-bearer of the Apostles of Christ, and as an all-radiant luminary of the honorable Church, O thrice-blessed Philip, we are enlightened in soul, and delivered from cruel perils by thy prayers, O all-praised one!

*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands.*[^593]
Having finished the contest of suffering by thy blood, thou hast worthily arrayed thyself in crowns of victory, O Philip; entering with them into the heavenly realms, thou standest together before Christ, O Apostle, and prayest that we may be saved!

*Glory... Tone 2:*[^594]
Thy cups of aromatics, poured forth in the world, have appeared, O wise Apostle Philip, as a life-creating drink unto the faithful who draw therefrom. For having the ascent of action into contemplation, thou wast a follower and welcomer of Christ; thou didst adorn the barren and childless church of the nations with teachings, that she may bear good children in Him: whom also now entreat to be delivered from necessities and distresses, for thou art able, drawing near unto God in abundance!

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*[^595]
O new wonder!...

*Troparion, Tone 3:*[^596]
O holy Apostle Philip, entreat the merciful God, that He may grant unto our souls the remission of transgressions!

*Or this, Tone the same:*[^597]
The universe is adorned, Ethiopia dances, as though beautified by a crown through thee; having been enlightened, she radiantly celebrates thy memory, O divinely-speaking Philip! For thou didst teach all to believe in Christ, and didst finish the course worthily of the Gospel. Therefore boldly reaches the Ethiopian hand unto God: Whom do thou entreat to grant us great mercy!

*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion:*
Thee, who didst mediate...[^598]

*At Matins, on "God is the Lord", the Troparion of the Apostle twice.*
*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion:*
*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb" (Гробъ твой):*[^599]
O Apostle of Christ, eyewitness and martyr, most wise Philip, blessed friend of God: deliver from besetments of transgressions those who celebrate with faith thy honorable memory, through thy prayers, and vouchsafe them to obtain the heavenly inheritance! *(Twice)*

*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion:*
The bush which Moses saw unconsumed, the mountain of God, the holy cloud, the undefiled tabernacle, the table received of God the table received of God, the palace of the Most High King, the all-radiant and impassable door, we hymn thee!

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "Co-beginningless Word" (Собезначалное слово):*[^600]
A disciple of the Word and preacher of truth, thou wast sent forth as an arrow, enlightening those who were in cruel darkness, O holy Apostle; and driving away the gloom of godlessness from the earth, thou didst show forth all the faithful to be sons of day, O eyewitness of Christ, holy Philip! *(Twice)*

*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion:*
Having unwavering hope in thee, O most pure Virgin, who art our shelter, deliver us from diverse misfortunes, distresses, and cruel perils, entreating thy Son together with His Apostles, and save all who hymn thee!

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премудрости):*[^601]
Thou didst cast down the deception of idols, having desired the passions of the Savior, O glorious Philip! Thou didst appear unto the world, pouring forth marvelous healings for all, and becoming an Apostle of the nations, O all-blessed one. Therefore we worthily honor thy memory, chanting praises: O Apostle of the Lord, pray to Christ God that He may grant the remission of sins unto those who celebrate with love thy holy memory! *(Twice)*

*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion:*
Having fallen into multifaceted perils from enemies visible and invisible, held fast by the tempest of mine unnumbered transgressions, and running unto the harbor of thy goodness, O pure one, as unto my fervent intercession and shelter: therefore, O most pure one, entreat Him Who was seedlessly incarnate of thee, fervently for all thy servants, who unceasingly pray unto thee, O most pure Mother of God, entreating Him ever, to grant the remission of sins unto those who worthily hymn thy glory!

*Anavathmoi, 1st Antiphon of Tone 4.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4: Their proclamation hath gone out into all the earth... Verse: The heavens declare...*[^602]
*Let every breath praise the Lord. Gospel from John, pericope 67.*[^603]
*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 7, Idiomelon:*[^604]
O most wise hunter, holy disciple, laborer of the Savior, and teller of His passions, who hast traversed creation in faith, and gathered the deceived nations, and brought them unto God: as a sweet-smelling incense was He taken up into the heavens. Therefore standing before the Judge, pray that we may be delivered from our iniquities, and in the day of judgment be saved from torment!

*Canon of the Theotokos with the Heirmos to 6, and of the Apostle to 8. Whose acrostic is: "I sing glorious Philip becomingly. Theophanes." Tone 6.*[^605]
*Ode 1, Tone 6. Heirmos:*[^606]
*Traversing the deep on foot as on dry land, Israel, seeing Pharaoh the pursuer drowned, cried aloud: Let us sing unto God a song of victory!*

*Troparion:*
Clearly delighting in the most radiant beams of Christ's divine splendor, O divinely-proclaiming Philip, enlighten us with thy rays by participation!

*Troparion:*
Teaching glory unto thee, having shown forth in Himself, O Philip, Christ appointed thee unto the choir of disciples, foreknowing thy virtue, O divinely-blessed one!

*Troparion:*
Now not in enigmas dost thou behold, nor in shadows, nor in mirrors, O most wise one, Christ the source of good things and the summit of desires, but face to face clearly dost thou behold Him!

*Theotokion:*
When the rulers from the tribe of Judah had failed, O most pure one, thy Son and God, coming as the Leader unto the ends of the earth, truly was made King now!

*Katavasia: I will open my mouth...*[^607]
*Ode 3, Tone 6. Heirmos:*[^608]
*There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established us upon the rock of Thy confession.*

*Troparion:*
Full of the light of active contemplation, when the Great Light was with us, thou wast vouchsafed to minister unto Christ, O divinely-speaking Philip!

*Troparion:*
The ladder of pious dogmas did thy mystagogy piously reveal; for through it we have known the Son to be of one essence and united with the Father!

*Troparion:*
A golden candlestick wast thou, shining unto men the ever-existing Light, and clearly enlightening the universe with knowledge through Him, O most excellent Philip!

*Theotokion:*
Having hoped in thee, O most holy and pure one, let me not fall away from thy expectation; but as the merciful Mother of the God Who loves mankind, deliver me from the snares of the enemy!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премудрости):*[^609]
A spiritual, teaching-bearing cloud hast thou truly appeared unto those upon the earth, watering our hearts mystically as a field; running through with the word, thou waterest the ends, and pourest forth a rain of myrrh from thy shrine. Therefore, having breathed into faithless hearts the fragrance of the Spirit, in which thou didst treasure up grace, O Apostle Philip: pray to Christ God that He may grant the remission of sins unto those who celebrate unto those who celebrate with love thy holy memory!

*Glory... Podoben the same:*[^610]
Thou didst cast down the deception of idols, having desired the passions of the Savior, O glorious Philip! Thou didst appear unto the world, pouring forth marvelous healings for all, and becoming an Apostle of the nations, O all-blessed one. Therefore we worthily honor thy memory, chanting praises: O Apostle of the Lord, pray to Christ God that He may grant the remission of sins unto those who celebrate with love thy holy memory!

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*[^611]
Having fallen into multifaceted perils from enemies visible and invisible, held fast by the tempest of mine unnumbered transgressions, and running unto the harbor of thy goodness, O pure one, as unto my fervent intercession and shelter: therefore, O most pure one, entreat Him Who was seedlessly incarnate of thee, fervently for all thy servants, who unceasingly pray unto thee, O most pure Mother of God, entreating Him ever, to grant the remission of sins unto those who worthily hymn thy glory!

*Ode 4, Tone 6. Heirmos:*[^612]
*Christ is my power, God and Lord, the honorable Church divinely sings, crying aloud from a pure mind, keeping festival in the Lord.*

*Troparion:*
An abode of the Sun, Christ the existing Light, and a temple capacious of His splendor hast thou appeared, O heaven that declarest the glory of God unto men!

*Troparion:*
Humanity having withered with passions, thou, O blessed one, divine salt from Christ, didst dry up its grievous rottenness, O praiseworthy proclaimer of God!

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by the power of Christ, O Philip, thou didst appear mightier than the demonic host and the evil-believing, crying aloud unto those upon earth the good tidings of divine life!

*Theotokion:*
A calm harbor art thou unto Christians who with faith and love proclaim thee to be the true, all-immaculate Mother of God from a pure conscience!

*Ode 5, Tone 6. Heirmos:*[^613]
*With Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine, I pray Thee, the souls of those who dawn early unto Thee with love, to know Thee, O Word of God, the true God, Who callest them from the gloom of sins.*

*Troparion:*
Having dried up the poison of the soul-destroying enemy by thy healing hands, O divinely-speaking one, thou didst deliver from cruel disease those held fast by the death-bearing abyss!

*Troparion:*
Wholly fire-breathing didst thou appear by the descent of the Paraclete and by grace, O Philip, and those who had been consumed by the winter of godlessness, thou didst quicken by the warmth of faith!

*Troparion:*
A bath wast thou of Christ, unceasingly receiving the beams granted unto thee, enlightening those who run unto thee, and leading them unto thy Creator!

*Theotokion:*
Working all things by His Word, and guiding by wise providence alone as He wills, the Lord is formed from thee for His tender mercy's sake, and ineffably becomes flesh, O most pure one!

*Ode 6, Tone 6. Heirmos:*[^614]
*Jonah was swallowed, yet was not held fast in the whale's belly; for bearing the figure of Thee, Who didst suffer and wast given over to burial, he came forth from the monster as from a bridal chamber, and called unto the watch: Ye that observe vain and false things have forsaken your own mercy!*

*Troparion:*
Beholding the deception of the enemy holding fast and destroying the human race, Thou didst bend Thy sharpened arrows, the Apostles, and didst fill them; and Thou didst cleave open the clay mouth of the serpent, O Savior, healing all from his harm and corruption!

*Troparion:*
Shining with the radiance that came to be, thou didst appear as lightning enlightening the universe, and as a mountain dripping sweetness, as divine dew falling from heaven, as a chosen apostle completing the twelve-numbered company of the disciples of Christ, O all-blessed one!

*Troparion:*
Having been taught the depth of Thy mysteries, the divine disciple proclaimed Thee with loud voice as a river of peace flooding the stream of delight, as drowning the sick glory of the nations, and proclaimed the good tidings of Thy glorious emptying for our sake, O Good One!

*Theotokion:*
All men being put to death and rotting through death, thou, having given birth unto Christ, incorruptible immortality, hast called them unto eternal life, and hast enlightened the darkened, and delivered them, having loosed the bonds of our delusion, O all-immaculate one!

*Kontakion, Tone 8, Podoben: "As first-fruits" (Яко начатки):*[^615]
Thy disciple and friend, and imitator of Thy passion, the divinely-speaking Philip, proclaimed Thee as God unto the universe: by his prayers, from most lawless enemies preserve Thy Church and every city of Thine through the Mother of God, O greatly merciful One!

*Ikos:*[^616]
Grant me a stream of speech, O Lord, Who didst make the watery nature Who didst establish the earth by Thy word, strengthen my heart, O Compassionate One! And enlighten my contemplation, O Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment: that I may speak and chant what is fitting, and worthily praise Thine attendant, O greatly merciful One!

*Ode 7, Tone 6. Heirmos:*[^617]
*The Children in Babylon feared not the flame of the furnace, but cast into the midst of the flame, being bedewed, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!*

*Troparion:*
As light wast thou sent forth, after the likeness of an arrow, O Apostle, enlightening with beaming splendors those who cry aloud in faith: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Shining brightly with the rich effusions of light of divine preaching, O blessed one, thou didst enlighten those in darkness to chant: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having conquered the babbling of Athens and all the fierceness of worldly words with the mighty word of faith, thou didst sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers![^618]

*Theotokion:*
In two natures, superessentially united without confusion, didst thou, O pure one, give birth unto Christ; unto Whom we cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!

*Ode 8, Tone 6. Heirmos:*[^619]
*Braving danger for the ancestral laws, the blessed youths in Babylon spat upon the God-defying decree of the king; and joined together by the fire wherein they were not burned, they sang a worthy song unto the Ruler of all: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!*

*Troparion:*
The Father's Light, the hypostatic Word, Who chose thee as an apostle from the world, O thrice-blessed one, made thee the light of the world; and having armed thee with His divine power, He sent thee forth as an unconquerable warrior, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by divine power, O Apostle, thou didst vanquish the opposing ranks, destroying their beast-like array; for having received peace as an unpayable portion, thou didst plant peaceful order in the world, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
With all love didst thou cleave unto the incarnate Word of God, O Apostle, having become His disciple, and God's servant and mystic speaker; whence, sent by Him unto the nations, thou didst proclaim His coming: Bless the Lord, all ye works praise Him, crying aloud, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
The All-divine One was wholly united beyond comprehension, immutably with all humanity in thy womb, O all-holy Virgin! Therefore is Christ known in two natures, being one and the other; unto Whom we chant, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Ode 9, Tone 6. Heirmos:*[^620]
*It is impossible for men to see God, upon Whom the angelic ranks dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-immaculate one, the incarnate Word appeared unto men: Whom magnifying, together with the heavenly hosts, we call thee blessed!*

*Troparion:*
Now having been vouchsafed ineffable glory and unwaning light, where is unspoken merriment, where is unceasing joy in the church of the firstborn, where are the dwellings of the righteous: pray for all Christians, O all-wise Philip!

*Troparion:*
Adorned with the beauty of noetic comeliness, and encircled with the crown of the Kingdom, O divinely-wise one, and enlightened with rich effusions of light, O Philip, by the beams of superessential light, rejoicing, thou standest before the throne of thy Master, O blessed one!

*Troparion:*
Together with all the honorable apostles, and the prophets and passion-bearers, O Philip, with the venerable, the hierarchs, and the righteous, pray with the Mother of God, that release from many sins and cleansing of transgressions be given unto those who celebrate with faith thy light-bearing and divine memory!

*Theotokion:*
The Word incarnate, Who formerly was incorporeal, hast thou brought forth, O Virgin Mother! Therefore as the Lady and Mother of God do we all piously glorify thee, offering unto thee the most true title, O pure one: for thou remainest the root of salvation of the faithful!

*Exapostilarion, Tone 2, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Духомъ во святилищи):*[^621]
Directing the course of thy fair feet toward the heavenly journey, O Philip, thou didst ascend rejoicing; and standing before the Trinity, in the Father thou beholdest the Son and the divine Spirit! Therefore with faith we celebrate thy all-sacred and divine memory! *(Twice)*

*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion:*
I remember the hour of the fearful examination, for the multitude of my deeds terrifies and frightens me; but have compassion, O most pure one, through thy fervent prayer, and grant me salvation! For as much as thou wilt, thou canst also do, as having given birth unto God, O blessed Mary!

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ преславнагѡ чудесе):*[^622]
O most marvelous wonder! The apostle who once caught fish became a fisher of men, produced by God; with the net of words he caught the nations, with the hook of the Cross he drew up the world! O what a catch did the divine laborer bring unto God, whose memory we now celebrate!

*Sticheron:*
O most marvelous wonder! Sent by God into the midst of wolves, as a sheep the Apostle Philip walked without fear, and showed the beasts to be lambs through faith, divinely bringing peace unto the world. O deeds of faith! O most excellent powers! By his prayers, O Christ, save our souls, as Thou alone art compassionate!

*Sticheron:*
O most marvelous wonder! A well pouring forth life with wise drawing did the Apostle Philip become unto those in the world; from him streams of dogmas proceed, from them we drink the torrents of wonders! O how many awesome wonders did the divine laborer perform, whose memory we glorify with faith!

*Sticheron, Tone 2, Idiomelon:*[^623]
A heavenly cup of wisdom hast thou appeared, for thou wast shown to be a fair abode of the Spirit, and didst utter the truth of virtues, catching earthly men with the noetic hook of the wisdom of God! Therefore we entreat thee, O Apostle Philip: pray for our souls!

*Glory... Tone 2:*[^624]
Turning the catching of fish into the catching of men, having drawn forth those in the depth of deception with a mystical net, O Apostle Philip, thou didst catch the whole world, and didst bring it unto Christ thy Teacher! Therefore we entreat thee: pray unto Him unceasingly, that He may save our souls who faithfully celebrate thy most honorable memory!

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*[^625]
O Mother of God, mediatress of all who pray unto thee: in thee do we take courage, and in thee do we boast, and in thee is all our hope! Entreat Him Who was born of thee, for thine unprofitable servants!

*Of the Holy Martyrs and Confessors Gurias, Samonas, and Abibus. Alleluia.*[^633]
*Be it known that if the beginning of this Fast fall on a Saturday: on Friday evening, at "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the saints on 6.*[^634] *If on a Sunday, Stichera first of the Octoechos, and of the saints, 3; Glory of the saints; Now and ever, Theotokion. At the Aposticha of the Octoechos, Glory of the saints; Now and ever, Theotokion. Evening, and at Matins, on "God is the Lord", Troparion of the saints; Glory... now and ever... Theotokion. On the other days, from Monday to Friday, we chant Alleluia, to honor the beginning of the holy Fast.*[^635]
*At "Lord, I have cried", we chant Stichera first of the Theotokos, 3, and of the saints, 3; Glory... now and ever... Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion. Instead of the Prokeimenon, we chant Alleluia in Tone 6.*[^636] *At the Aposticha of the Octoechos, Glory... now and ever... Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion. At Matins, instead of "God is the Lord", we chant Alleluia and the Trinity Hymns; and after Ode 6, the Kontakion of the saints.*
*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Далъ еси знаменiе):*[^637]
Abibus the all-wise, and Samonas the marvelous, and Gurias the glorious, having gathered a common choir for the faithful, now dance together with us in joy, O passion-bearers, and are glad! For unto the souls of the martyrs was this granted by God, clearly to behold what takes place here!

*Sticheron:*
Having endured the pains of intolerable torments, and having valiantly suffered, O ye who are equal in number to the Trinity, Samonas and Abibus, and Gurias divinely wise: ye are now filled with eternal and fair delight, Christ measuring out unto you the recompense of your labors; Whom do ye fervently entreat, that our souls may be saved!

*Sticheron:*
Having put in at the untempestuous harbor, and at the immaterial life and calm haven, O passion-bearing martyrs, having fled unto the abode of dispassion, ye have now exchanged the earthly things, worthily receiving from God the rewards of labors and the honors of sufferings, O blessed ones!

*Other Stichera of the Mother of God, Tone and Podoben the same.*
*If Alleluia, we chant these* Stichera first:*[^638]
Rain down upon me, O Mother of God, the abyss of thy mercy, and water my heart which is scorched by the heat of passions, as thou art merciful, O Maiden; and grant, I pray thee, that I may unceasingly pour forth drops of compunction, whereby I may be vouchsafed comfort, O pure one, which they who have genuinely wept shall obtain!

*Sticheron:*
Shaken by demonic assaults and dragged into the pit of perdition, have compassion, O Mother of God, and establish me upon the rock of virtues; and having broken the counsels of enemies, vouchsafe me to do the commandments of thy Son and our God, that I may obtain remission in the day of judgment!

*Sticheron:*
Wash away the filth of my wretched heart, O all-hymned Mother of God, and cleanse, O pure one, all the wounds and putrefactions which are from sin, and quiet the instability of my mind: that I, thy passionate and unprofitable servant, may magnify thy power and great defense!

*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion:*
Turn the weakness and despondency to work of my soul into health and strength, O all-immaculate one, that with fear and love I may do and work the statutes of Christ: that I may escape the intolerable fire, and ever obtain through thee the heavenly portion and the unending life!

*If on Wednesday or Friday, Stavrotheotokion, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Яко добля):*[^639]
Beholding Christ, the Lover of mankind, being crucified, and His ribs pierced with a spear, the most pure one, weeping, cried aloud: What is this, O my Son? What have the ungrateful people rendered unto Thee for the good things which Thou hast done unto them? And Thou makest haste to leave me childless, O most dearly beloved! I marvel, O Compassionate One, at Thy voluntary crucifixion!

*If "God is the Lord", Glory... Tone 2, Idiomelon:*[^640]
Today she is glad, as having been enriched with the shrine of radiant Gurias, Samonas, and Abibus; and summoning the Christ-loving flock, she cries aloud: Come, ye lovers of the martyrs, be enlightened in the radiant memory! Come then, ye lovers of the feast, rejoice! Come and see the luminaries of heaven who lived upon earth! Come and hear what bitter death the valiant adamants gave themselves unto, for the sake of endless life! Therefore, being sureties of truth, they saved the maiden who was cast alive into the tomb, and delivered to destruction the all-defiled Parthian who had disregarded them, as a murderer and merciless one![^641]

...merciful: and they fervently pray unto the Holy Trinity to deliver from corruption and temptations and every kind of misfortune those who perform their memory with faith.
