*Now and ever... Theotokion.*

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos:*

*Glory... Tone 2, Idiomelon:*[^642]
Come, all ye lovers of the martyrs, let us honor with hymns the weapons of Christ, Gurias, and Abibus, and Samonas, for most gloriously do they work wonders! For they disregarded not the oath to present the maiden, but fulfilling the petition, they saved the virgin, having wrought vengeance upon the most lawless Goth.[^643] By their prayers, O Christ God, save us, as Thou art good and the Lover of mankind!

*Now and ever... Theotokion.*

*Troparion, Tone 5:*[^644]
O Christ God, Who hast granted unto us the wonders of Thy holy martyrs as an unconquerable wall: by their prayers break down the counsels of the heathen, and strengthen the scepters of the kingdom,[^645] as Thou alone art good and the Lover of mankind!

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos; and the canon of the saints on 4.*

*Whose acrostic is: "I praise most wisely the three who speak together. By Theophanes."*[^646]

*Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^647]
*Traversing the deep of the Red Sea with dryshod feet, ancient Israel of old, by the cross-shaped hands of Moses, conquered the power of Amalek in the wilderness.*

*Troparion:*
Honorably theologizing the single Principle of the Trinity, O holy ones, ye easily dispersed the unstable gloom of polyarchy,[^648] having shone forth as most radiant stars of the Orient!

*Troparion:*
The three confessors, visibly enlightened by the grace of the primordial Trinity, and patiently showing opposition, destroyed the deception of polytheism!

*Troparion:*
God, indeed, by His beneficent adoption, through love, the natural Son, now clearly gives Himself as an inheritance, and as compassionate hath shown them to be fellow-heirs and partakers of the Kingdom!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast the tabernacle of the most wise Wisdom, O all-immaculate one: for He was well pleased to fashion His temple from thy most pure blood, O pure one, unto the salvation of our souls!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^649]
*Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge and establishment!*

*Troparion:*
Voluntarily did the confessors and servants of Christ deliver their bodies unto torments and cruel wounds implore, O holy ones, that those who celebrate your memory with faith may be delivered from cruel, sinful thoughts!

*Troparion:*
Patiently suspended upon the tree, the honorable witnesses piously preserved their confession unharmed!

*Theotokion:*
He Who entered into thy womb, O most pure Mother of God, showed thee to be a fountain of healings: do thou therefore heal my soul!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^650]
Armed with the Cross of Christ, through it ye manfully cast down all the might of the tormentors, as champions of the faith: ye rebuked all the godlessness of idols, and fervently proclaimed the Holy Trinity! Therefore did ye worthily receive from Her the crowns of victory, as having lawfully suffered, O all-glorious passion-bearers: entreat Christ God, that He grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate with love your holy memory!

*Glory... Tone 8, Podoben the same:*[^651]
Having served Christ as martyrs, ye enslaved the deception of the tormentor, possessing an unenslaved soul and wisdom; for, wounded by faith in the Trinity, O all-praised ones, ye rebuked the inglorious glory of polytheism! Therefore as stars ye shine brightly in the world with the radiance of wonders, O blessed ones, all-lauded passion-bearers: entreat Christ God, that He grant remission of sins unto those who honor with love your holy memory!

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*[^652]
As a Virgin and the only one among women who without seed didst bring forth God in the flesh, all we generations of men call thee blessed: for the fire of the Godhead dwelt within thee, and as an infant thou didst nurse the Creator and Lord! Therefore the angelic and human race worthily glorifies thy most holy childbirth, and with one accord we cry aloud unto thee: Entreat Christ God, that He grant remission of sins unto those who worship in faith thy most holy childbirth!

*Stavrotheotokion:*[^653]
Beholding upon the Cross the Lamb and Shepherd and Deliverer, the Ewe-lamb cried aloud weeping, and bitterly lamenting, exclaimed: The world indeed rejoices, receiving redemption through Thee; but my womb burns, beholding Thy crucifixion, which Thou endurest for the tender mercy of Thy lovingkindness, O longsuffering Lord, abyss of mercy and inexhaustible fountain! Be compassionate, and grant remission of transgressions unto those who chant in faith of Thy divine passions!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^654]
*Beholding Thee, the Sun of Righteousness, lifted up upon the Cross, the Church stood in her place, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*

*Troparion:*
The crown-bearers, equal in number to the Trinity, with a thrice-radiant lamp enlighten those who perform their all-sacred memory, granting healings unto all!

*Troparion:*
With reverence let us run, O divinely-wise ones, unto the light-bearing and radiant shrine of the martyrs, for it pours forth remedies unto those who cry aloud in faith: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Confessing with theological tongues the divine dispensation and the mystery that surpasses the mind, the divine and all-wise confessors trampled underfoot all the godlessness of the tormentors!

*Theotokion:*
Beyond comprehension didst thou give birth, O Virgin, and after childbirth thou wast shown to be a maiden again: therefore with unceasing voices, Rejoice, do we cry unto thee, O Lady, with unwavering faith!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^655]
*Thou, my Lord, hast come into the world as a light, a holy light turning men from dark ignorance, who chant unto Thee in faith.*

*Troparion:*
Clearly shining with the brightness of their struggles, the champions of the faith put to shame the fierce disposition of the tormentors!

*Troparion:*
Unto all the ends of the universe the wonders of the martyrs have been manifestly proclaimed, and have established all things through faith!

*Troparion:*
As good ground receiving the seeds of grace, the blessed ones by their laborious life produced wealth!

*Theotokion:*
He Who alone is good, and Who by the abyss of His goodness holds all things, O Mother of God, was well pleased to be held in thine embrace!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^656]
*I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood which flowed from Thy ribs for mercy's sake!*

*Troparion:*
Lawfully, as good soldiers, O divinely-wise ones, having restrained all things and preserved great faith, ye received the crowns of divine righteousness!

*Troparion:*
Formerly indeed [surrendered] unto the devil by sovereign decree; yet through you, O divinely-speaking ones, the tormented maiden was returned unto her that reared her![^657]

*Troparion:*
The shrine of the martyrs shines with wonders, and pours forth rivers of healings unto all who draw near in faith and marvel at their endurance!

*Theotokion:*

Having found thee alone amidst the thorns as a most pure lily and a flower in the valleys, O Mother of God, the noetic Bridegroom dwelt within thee!

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*[^658]
Having received grace from on high, O wise ones, ye protect those who are in trials, O all-praised ones: therefore, O holy ones, ye delivered the maiden from bitter death; for truly ye are the glory of Edessa, and the joy of the world!

*Ikos:*[^659]
Deliver me from the enemy's slavery, O Savior, Giver of life, being entreated by the supplications of Thy sufferers: that having gained my soul and body unenslaved from passions, I may praise their most speedy help, how when she was shut up in the tomb by the cunning of a man, they speedily came beforehand and delivered her from death, as she cried aloud: The glory of Edessa and the joy of the world!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^660]
*In the Persian furnace the children of Abraham, burned rather by the love of piety than by the flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!*

*Troparion:*
Thou Who art, Who didst deliver the children of Abraham in the furnace, didst also deliver the stranger maiden from cruel distress, O Savior, now through the intercession of Thy holy attendants, as Thou art compassionate!

*Troparion:*
Suffering the punishment of bloody inhumanity, examined in a pit of all evils, the murderer bearing an evil name was judged by Thy righteous judgment, O Word of God, Wisdom and Power![^661]

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by hope toward you, O glorious ones, the maiden shut up in the tomb with the dead, not having buried her limbs, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
As a newly mingled and radiant mirror of the furnace of divine radiance, O Virgin, I behold that thou didst contain Him Who joined Himself unto thee! Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Lady!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^662]
*Stretching out his hands, Daniel shut the lions' mouths in the pit; and girded with virtue, the youths, lovers of piety, quenched the power of the fire, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*

*Troparion:*
A worldwide feast of the martyrs of Christ hath dawned upon us today, enlightening with the grace of wonders those who come in faith, and who cry aloud with spiritual joy and love: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Easily did the confessors of Thy Godhead abolish all godlessness, O Master, not fearing the threats of the evil-minded tormentors, being strengthened by faith, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
The all-wise confessors, standing before the divine command, conquering the ranks of the enemies, being slaughtered with the sword, manifestly showed forth a most glorious and transcendent victory: for falling, they conquered their adversaries!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst bring forth Christ visible in two natures, manifestly bearing one composite Hypostasis of Godhead and manhood, which came together according to true natural union! Therefore we bless thee, O Mary, Bride of God!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^663]
*A cornerstone was cut out without hands from thee, the unhewn mountain, O Virgin: even Christ, Who hath joined together the divided natures! Therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Mother of God!*

*Troparion:*
Following the divine and divinely-inspired words of Christ, O divinely-radiant confessors, ye gladly took the Cross upon your shoulders, following in the life-bearing footsteps, O most glorious ones!

*Troparion:*
Admitted with joy into all the light of the Trinity, the valiant confessors receive the honors of their struggles, having been vouchsafed to dwell together with the incorporeal ranks!

*Troparion:*
Today not in a mirror do ye behold the hopes of the blessed, O confessors of the Savior; but rather the beauty of truth do ye behold, O all-wise ones, all-honorable crown-bearers!

*Troparion:*
As the divinely-speaking confessors were manifestly shown to be equal in number unto the super-divine Trinity, ye are enlightened by Her beams; as having suffered for Her sake, they have now attained incorruptible life!

*Theotokion:*
The Word Who adorned all things, willing to come in the flesh, dwelt within thee, having found thee alone more honorable than all, and showed thee truly to be the Mother of God, O Virgin Mother!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Heavens with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣ́здами):*[^664]
O ye who delivered the maiden from the tomb of old, Gurias, and Samonas, and Abibus, martyrs of Christ: come beforehand, delivering us as from the tomb of transgressions!

*Theotokion:*[^665]
By thy mighty protection preserve us, thy servants, unharmed from the assaults of enemies, O pure one: for thee alone have we acquired as a refuge in afflictions!

*At the Liturgy, Prokeimenon* Tone 4: Unto the saints that are in His earth.[^666] Verse: I beheld the Lord ever before me.[^667] Epistle to the Ephesians, pericope 233.[^668] Alleluia, Tone 4: The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them.[^669] Verse: Many are the afflictions of the righteous.[^670] Gospel from Luke, pericope 64.[^671] Communion Hymn: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous![^672]

*On the same month, the 16th Day.*
*Of the Holy Apostle and Evangelist Matthew.*[^673]

*At Vespers, "Blessed is the man", 1st Antiphon.*[^674]

*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera on 8, Tone 4, Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*[^675]
He Who tries the hearts of men, when by His divine foreknowledge He beheld thy divine mind, O Apostle, drew thee forth from unrighteousness and from the world; then He made thee a worldwide light, commanding thee to enlighten and illumine the ends of the universe, Whose divine Gospel thou wast also vouchsafed manifestly to write: entreat Him, that He save and enlighten our souls! *(Twice)*

*Sticheron:*
Called from the tax office unto discipleship, when the beginningless Word summoned thee, commanding thee to follow, and promising fellowship in the Kingdom: then, O all-blessed one, having left all, and departed from turbulent commotion, thou didst firmly follow Him; and now, O beholder of God, art clearly filled with His ineffable vision: entreat Him, that He save and enlighten our souls! *(Twice)*

*Sticheron:*
A prophetic sharp-sightedness of mine beheld thee of old as a rolling stone appearing upon the earth and crushing the craftiness of deception; and the hypostatic Word, O all-wise one, made thee the light of the world and a preacher of righteousness and truth, brightened with the beams of the thrice-radiant Light, O all-honorable one: entreat Him, that He save and enlighten our souls! *(Twice)*

*Sticheron:*
O servant of super-divine Wisdom: when the unapproachable Light came in the flesh as He was well pleased was well pleased, destroying the gloom of ignorance: then, being summoned, thou didst follow His life-bearing commandments, and having become a divine guardian surpassing comprehension, thou wast a lamp of the Church, O Matthew, an abode of Christ! Entreat Him, that He save and enlighten our souls!

*Sticheron, Tone 4:*
With a fiery tongue, consuming deception, thou didst appear, O all-praised, all-wise Matthew, having received the advent of the Comforter, which essentially enlightened thee: whence thou didst astonish every thought of those who heard thy words proclaiming unto the people the majestic deeds of the Almighty; and now into all the earth hath thy proclamation gone forth, O divinely-inspired one: entreat Him, to have compassion upon all who chant unto thee!

*Glory... Tone 4, Idiomelon:*[^676]
When Christ called Thee unto His discipleship, O God-receiver, Thou didst eagerly follow: having cast away at once all the business of earthly care; for, having submissively received a mind worthy of the heavenly Kingdom, Thou didst withdraw from lowly living and vain glory: having become an evangelist from a tax-collector, Thou didst appear as a light unto those in darkness, and a guide unto salvation for the lost: and now Thou art a most fervent intercessor for the whole world, and a saving guardian, O Matthew, for those who honor Thee!

*Now and ever... Theotokion: "He Who for thy sake..."*[^677]

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day, and three readings: seek on the 14th day of this month.*[^678]

*If the superior will to chant the Litiya: see the 14th day of this month.*[^679]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менiе):*[^680]
With the trumpet of thy words thou didst gather men into the knowledge of God, O ever-hymned one; and having driven from the earth the assemblies of deception, thou didst direct the faithful into one single-mindedness: and thou prayest now, that those who ever perform with faith thy honorable memory may be delivered from corruption and misfortunes!

*Verse: Their proclamation hath gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the universe.*[^681]

*Sticheron:*
Having armed thee with the fiery tongue of the Holy Spirit, Christ our God showed thee to be a mighty champion against deception, O Apostle, whereby thou didst receive the bright honors of grace: entreat Him, that those who ever perform with faith thy honorable memory may be delivered from corruption and misfortunes!

*Verse: The heavens declare the glory* of God, and the firmament declares the work of His hands.[^682]

*Sticheron:*
Stooping down unto the depth of the Spirit, O Apostle, thou didst perceive inexhaustible wealth; and having drawn forth abundant grace therefrom, thou didst dispense this unto all of us in the Gospel: and thou prayest now, that those who ever perform with faith thy honorable memory may be delivered from corruption and misfortunes!

*Glory... Tone 6:*[^683]
From the lowest depth of malice unto the exceedingly highest height of virtue, as an eagle soaring on high, most gloriously didst thou ascend, O all-praised Matthew: for thou didst follow in the footsteps of Christ, Who covered the heavens with virtue and filled the whole earth with His understanding: an ardent imitator didst thou appear unto Him in all things, preaching the good tidings of peace, life, and salvation unto those who piously obey the divine commandments: wherein do thou also guide us, who are well-pleasing unto the Creator and call thee blessed!

*Now and ever... Theotokion: "My Maker and Deliverer..."*[^684]

*Troparion, Tone 3:*[^685]
O holy Apostle and Evangelist Matthew, entreat the merciful God, that He grant remission of transgressions unto our souls!

*Or this one, Tone the same:*[^686]
Eagerly following from the tax office Christ the Master Who called thee, Who appeared upon earth unto men for His goodness' sake, thou wast shown to be a chosen apostle and a loud-voiced herald of the Gospel unto the universe: therefore we honor thy venerable memory, O divinely-speaking Matthew: entreat the merciful God, that He grant remission of sins unto our souls!

*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion: "Thee, who didst mediate..."*[^687]

*At Matins, on "God is the Lord", Troparion twice; Glory... now and ever... Theotokion.*

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*[^688]
Having been the first to write the Gospel of Christ, and having enlightened all creation under the sun, O Matthew exceedingly all-wise and excellent initiate of Christ, being now honored with sacred hymns, he entreats remission of sins for all who honor him with love! *(Twice)*

*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion:*[^689]
All we who flee with love unto thy goodness know thee truly to be the Mother of God, and a Virgin who appeared as such even after childbirth: for we sinners have thee as an intercessor, and thee have we acquired as salvation in trials, O only all-immaculate one!

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Of divine faith" (Бж҃твенныя вѣ́ры):*[^690]
Having shone forth with the stars of right faith, thou didst quench all evil renown: having become an unconquerable victor, thou didst proclaim the Gospel unto all; thou didst richly adorn all the Churches, O Apostle Matthew: entreat Christ God, that He grant unto us great mercy! *(Twice)*

*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion:*[^691]
Without departing from the divine nature, He became flesh within thy womb, yet remained God incarnate; Who after childbirth preserved thee, His mother, a Virgin even as before childbirth, all-immaculate, the only Lord: Him do thou fervently entreat, that He grant unto us great mercy!

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom and the Word" (Премꙋ́дрости и҆ сло́ва):*[^692]
Unto all the ends of the earth hath the proclamation of thy wise words truly run, O all-praised Apostle of the Lord! Clearly didst thou preach the vision of God unto all, and didst bring the folly of the nations unto understanding: therefore, having driven away the darkness of idolatry, thou didst shine forth the light of knowledge unto those in darkness, O all-praised Matthew: entreat Christ God, that He grant remission of sins unto those who honor with love thy holy memory! *(Twice)*

*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion:*[^693]
As a Virgin and the only one among women who without seed didst bring forth God in the flesh, all we generations of men call thee blessed: for the fire of the Godhead dwelt within thee, and as an infant thou dost feed with milk the Creator and Lord! Therefore the angelic and human race worthily glorifies thy most holy childbirth, and with one accord we cry aloud unto thee: Entreat Christ God, that He grant remission of sins unto those who worship in faith thy most holy childbirth!

*Gradual Hymn, 1st Antiphon of Tone 4.*[^694] *Prokeimenon, Tone 4: Their proclamation hath gone out into all the earth... Verse: The heavens declare...*[^695] *Let every breath...*[^696] *Gospel from John, pericope 67.*[^697] *After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 6:*[^698]
Let us clap our hands in hymns today, ye faithful, in the memory of the venerable Apostle and Evangelist Matthew: for having cast down the yoke and gold of the tax office, he followed Christ, and became a preacher of the divine Gospel: whence prophetically his proclamation went out into the universe; and he prays that our souls may be saved!

*Canon of the Theotokos with the Heirmos on 6, and of the Apostle on 8. By Theophanes.*[^699]

*Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^700]
*I will open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit; and I will utter a word unto the Queen Mother; and I will appear radiantly keeping festival, and rejoicing I will chant her wonders!*

*Troparion:*
Richly grant me the grace that dwelt within thee, O all-glorious Matthew, and servant of Christ: that proclaiming with light, I may cry aloud, and rejoicing may sing thy wonders!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst leave all the turmoil of earthly things: for hearing the voice of the incarnate Word, thou wast shown to be a steward of grace, and an acceptable preacher, O divinely-blessed one!

*Troparion:*
Having become an eyewitness and servant of the Word Who shone forth from the pre-eternal Father, O Apostle, thou didst run, preaching His coming unto all the nations!

*Theotokion:*
The destruction of death, and the annulment of corruption, and the manifestation of life didst thou preach, O wise one: for the Virgin, having conceived the Incomprehensible in her womb, renewed the world!

*Katavasia: "I will open my mouth..."*[^701]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^702]
*Establish thy hymnographers, O Mother of God, living and inexhaustible fountain, who have spiritually assembled their company, and in thy divine glory vouchsafe them crowns of glory!*

*Troparion:*
Thou didst show forth Thine apostles as luminaries of life, O Word of God, driving away the gloom of godlessness, O Master, and enlightening the whole world with Thy divine glory!

*Troparion:*
Having armed most valiant Matthew with Thy new armor, O Savior, Thou didst make him stronger than the tormentors, O Master, and didst show him to be a destroyer of idol delusion, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
The utterance of thy fiery tongue burned up the temples of demons, O divinely-inspired Matthew, thou instrument of the Paraclete, through whom Christ, the hypostatic Life of all, is preached!

*Theotokion:*
The theological trumpet of divinely-wise Matthew, uttering mightily, enlightened the people with the radiance of the Trinity, and with the incarnation of the Word beyond comprehension from thee, O most pure one!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^703]
Unto all the ends of the earth hath the sound of thy wise words truly run, O all-praised Apostle of the Lord; clearly didst thou preach the vision of God unto all, and didst bring the folly of the nations unto understanding! Therefore, having driven away the darkness of idolatry, thou didst shine forth the light of knowledge unto those in darkness, O all-praised Matthew: entreat Christ God, that He grant remission of sins unto those who honor with love thy holy memory!

*Glory... Podoben the same:*

As a luminary of the Light and a disciple, as an eyewitness of the divine Word, we all praise thee, O Apostle of the Lord; for having spread thy nets of grace, thou dost catch rational fish by His command. Therefore the nations also were counted blessed, being guided by faith through the power of the Spirit, O all-praised initiate of heavenly mysteries: pray unto Christ God that He grant remission of sins unto those who honor with love thy holy memory![^704]

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*[^705]
As the all-immaculate bride of the Creator, as the unwedded Mother of the Deliverer, as the vessel of the Comforter, O all-hymned one: since I am a defiled habitation of iniquity and have consciously become a plaything of demons, hasten to deliver me from their wickedness, and make me a radiant dwelling of virtues, O light-bearing and incorrupt one! Drive away the cloud of passions, and vouchsafe me communion with the Highest and with the unwaning Light, through thy prayers!

*Ode 4, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^706]
*Perceiving the unsearchable divine counsel of Thine incarnation from the Virgin, O Highest One, the Prophet Habakkuk cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*

*Troparion:*
Having been taught by Thy hypostatic Word, O God, the disciple who beheld God destroyed worldly wisdom, crying aloud unto Thee with a great voice: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Unto thee who wast blessed by Christ, what hymn of blessing shall we bring, O divinely-speaking one? For man cannot express in words the grace blossoming upon thee, O worthy of wonder!

*Troparion:*
Beholding thy undefiled and pure mind, O divinely-manifest one, the Most High set thee forth before all as a lamp upon a lofty lampstand, shining upon those who sit in darkness!

*Theotokion:*
Thou, O blessed one, didst exalt deadened human nature, having borne the strength of the Most High beyond nature, O all-hymned Maiden, even as Matthew taught!

*Ode 5, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^707]
*All creation was amazed at thy divine glory; for thou, O unwedded Virgin, didst hold in thy womb the God Who is over all, and didst bear the timeless Son, granting peace unto all who praise thee!*

*Troparion:*
Having received the grace of the All-Holy Spirit, Thou wast shown to be a divine dwelling, having divinely taught the knowledge of God, being entrusted to set forth in writing the dogmas of Christ to the world as a divinely-chosen eyewitness!

*Troparion:*
Thy tongue became the pen of the Paraclete Who grants swift deliverance unto those who have known His beatitude, and Who breathes heavenly understanding into the souls of the wise, O all-honored Matthew!

*Troparion:*
Radiant with wonders and with the graces of healings, Christ sent thee unto the world, trampling down the power of demons and enlightening the souls of the faithful, who all praise thee as the herald of peace!

*Theotokion:*
A Virgin, thou didst bear the pre-eternal Son Who clothed Himself in human nature, even as the divinely-speaking one taught, saying: and Who saved it from corruption by His ultimate goodness; and thou didst remain a Virgin!

*Ode 6, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^708]
*I came into the deep of the sea, and the tempest of many sins hath overwhelmed me; but as God, lead up my life from the deep, O greatly Merciful One!*

*Troparion:*
Having departed from the tax office, as he followed Thee, O Almighty Creator, by Thy all-powerful might, most excellent Matthew was transformed into a divinely-speaking herald!

*Troparion:*
By the soul-nourishing words of thy Gospel, the multitude of the nations is guided, being lifted up unto the lofty summit of virtues, O all-blessed Matthew!

*Troparion:*
Through the divinely-woven nets of the disciple Matthew, the assemblies of the faithful are ever blessed, being guided unto the knowledge of Thee, O Benefactor!

*Theotokion:*
Praising the Virgin who bare Thee, most excellent Matthew preaches the good tidings of Thee Who didst make all things without seed and corruption, O all-immaculate one!

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*[^709]
Having cast off the yoke of the tax office, thou didst yoke thyself unto the yoke of righteousness, and wast shown to be a most excellent merchant, having brought the wealth of wisdom from on high. Therefore thou didst preach the word of truth, and didst raise up the souls of the despondent, having written of the hour of judgment!

*Ikos:*[^710]
The enemy's torment attacks me insatiably, and snatches away all the seed of my soul, O Matthew, friend of Christ. But do thou thyself, having given the seed of thy prayers, make it fruitful unto thy praise, and show me forth as the least singer of thy praise, and as a narrator of thy many and great accomplishments: and how, out of love for Christ, having immediately forsaken all things, thou didst follow Him Who called thee, having become the first evangelist in the world, having written of the hour of judgment!

*Ode 7, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^711]
*The godly-minded children did not serve the creature rather than the Creator; but manfully trampling upon the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers!*

*Troparion:*
Thou didst become a divine image of the primal radiance, being kindled by the splendors of that disciple, unto Whom thou didst answer in harmony: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
As a servant of the Word, O all-blessed one, thou didst make thy dwelling in the divine mansions where Christ dwells, even as He promised thee, the most divine Lord and only God of all our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Diseases are driven away, O Matthew, and a multitude of demons flees, through the gifts of the Holy Spirit dwelling in thee, in which thou didst sing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
With thy divine words thou didst describe the all-hymned Virgin, who bare the Creator of all, O Apostle, unto Whom we all sing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers!

*Ode 8, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^712]
*The pious children in the furnace the offspring of the Theotokos saved; then figured forth, but now active, it moves the whole inhabited earth to sing unto Thee: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*

*Troparion:*
By the ineffable nods of divine grace within thee, O most sacred Matthew, being deified by adoption while remaining in nature what thou wast, thou didst draw the inhabited earth, O Master, to sing unto Thee: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
As lightning unto the inhabited earth, the Word sent forth the divine theologian, driving away the gloom, and enlightening the nations with the dogmas of theology. Therefore he sang: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
With pure speech and mind God conversed with thee; for having fled from the mire, thou didst draw near unto Him and wast united with Him, O glorious one. Therefore thou dost sing: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
For the benefaction of mankind the Word was pleased to become incarnate, for the Lord passed through the gate of virginity and showed thee forth as the Theotokos. Therefore we cry aloud: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^713]
*Let every earthborn mortal leap for joy, enlightened by the Spirit; and let the nature of the bodiless minds celebrate, honoring the sacred festival of the Mother of God, and let them cry aloud: Rejoice, O all-blessed Theotokos, pure Ever-Virgin!*

*Troparion:*
Thou didst receive the divine diadem of spiritual beauties, O Apostle; and thou wast adorned with the most beauteous crown of the Kingdom by the right hand of the Almighty. And thou shinest, O wise one, standing before the throne of Christ the Master together with the angels, O all-blessed one!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst worthily attain the Tree of Life, O herald of the living God, having proclaimed to the world life, the divine visitation; for with the poison of carnal knowledge thou didst not corrupt thy mind, remaining an unshakable and unswerving step of the Church, O all-blessed one!

*Troparion:*
With thy Gospel, as with a diadem, thou didst divinely adorn the Church, the bride of Christ, O divinely-blessed one; and now she brightly celebrates thy divine memory. Pray, O Apostle Matthew, that she be delivered from every surrounding danger and cruel distress!

*Theotokion:*
Without leaving the bosom of the beginningless Father, the beginningless Word, as Matthew preaches in his writing, God became incarnate of thee, O pure and all-hymned Theotokos, entirely clothing Himself in human form in every way, and receiving its properties!

*Exapostilarion, Tone 3, Podoben: "He hath visited us" (Посѣти́лъ ны̀ є҆́сть):*[^714]
The glorious writer of the Gospel of Christ, divinely-acceptable Matthew, hath made known unto us divine benefactions; whom honoring with love, let us sing with harmonious praise!

*Glory... Podoben the same:*[^715]
Having wisely cast away the yoke of the tax office, thou didst follow Christ, O divinely-wise Matthew; and marvelously following in His footsteps, thou wast a partaker of His Kingdom, and a companion of His glory, and an initiate of ineffable mysteries!

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*[^716]
Thy all-holy hands, O Virgin Theotokos, with which thou didst bear the Creator, lift up in prayer for us unto Him, that He deliver us from all temptations of the devil, and vouchsafe us to obtain those good things to come, O all-hymned one!

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менiе):*[^717]
Thou didst shine forth, O Apostle, light-like as the sun, with the beams of the Spirit; and thou didst illumine the whole inhabited earth, O blessed one, with the knowledge of God, and didst drive away the gloom of polytheism O all-wise Matthew. Therefore today we celebrate thy most radiant and worthy-of-wonder festival, as a fountain of sanctification! *(Twice)*

*Sticheron:*
Sitting upon the height of the knowledge of God, O Apostle, thou didst receive the radiance of the Spirit that appeared unto thee in the form and fiery tongue, and didst burn up all the deceit of impiety, the material of polytheism. Therefore we honor thee as an apostle and divinely-speaking herald, celebrating today thy holy festival!

*Sticheron:*
O all-wise one, thou didst thunder forth sacred and saving teachings unto the inhabited earth, and didst cleanse all creation from idol-madness, O Matthew; and thou didst enlighten the people with the brightness of the Gospel, and having broken down idol temples by grace, thou didst build churches to the glory of God!

*Glory... Tone 2, by Byzantios:*[^718]
Forsaking the yoke of unrighteousness and casting away the gold of extortion, thou didst run unto the yoke of righteousness, gathering inexhaustible wealth; like a wise merchant, exchanging temporal things for eternal, and perishable things for enduring. For having acquired the divine and precious pearl, thou didst wisely render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's, leaving behind the things that drag downward; and following Christ the King of all with submissive obedience, thou didst enrich all creation with Gospel words spoken by God, O wise one. But entreat even now, O most excellent Matthew, salvation and great mercy for those who honor thee!

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*[^719]
Save thy servants from dangers, O Virgin Theotokos, for after God we all flee unto thee as an unbreakable wall and intercession!

*Then the Great Doxology, and Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Apostle from the Canon, Ode 3 and Ode 6.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 8: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.*[^720]
*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God.*[^721]
*Epistle to the Corinthians, pericope 131.*[^722]
*Alleluia, Tone 1: The heavens shall confess Thy wonders, O Lord.*[^723]
*Gospel from Matthew, pericope 30.*[^724]
*Communion Hymn: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.*

*On the same month, the 17th Day.*
*Our Father among the Saints Gregory, Bishop of Neocaesarea, the Wonderworker.*[^725]

*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera on 6, Tone 8, Podoben: "What shall we call you" (Что́ васъ нарече́мъ):*[^726]
What shall I call thee, O Gregory? A master, for thou didst subject the passions unto the mind! A laborer, for thou didst reap the fruit of wisdom, being vouchsafed divine vision, and being instructed by heavenly theology! A most sacred celebrant of sacred mysteries, and a most marvelous wonderworker! Entreat that our souls may be saved!

*Sticheron:*
What shall I now call thee, O Gregory? A mighty destroyer of godless impiety, an ordainer of piety, and a teacher of the catechumens! An invincible giver of peace, an unconquerable dispeller of warfare! Dwelling in the mountains and seeing that which was done in the cities! Entreat that our souls may be saved!

*Sticheron:*
What shall I now proclaim thee, O venerable one? An emulator of the apostles, as a firsthand worker of wonders! Rebuking rivers by the invocation of Christ, and drying up the fratricidal lake! Dissolving the God-opposing assembly, multiplying and enlightening Christian gatherings! Entreat that our souls may be saved!

*Sticheron:*
What shall I now proclaim thee, O venerable one? A guide of the lost, and a physician of the diseased! An abundant supplier of needs unto those who ask, a most mighty chaser-away of demons! A reporter of the martyrs' contest, prophetically shining with graces, O worthy of glory! Entreat that our souls may be saved!

*Glory... Tone 6:*[^727]
Having entered into the depth of divine vision, O all-wise hierarch of Christ, thou wast taught the divine revelation of the Trinity, unswervingly seeing in the Spirit Christ our God, Who pours forth unto us an abyss of wonders: having transformed the watery nature of the waters into the appearance of stone, and having changed the dark altars of delusion, thou didst persuade the persecutors to believe in the truth; and thou wast shown forth unto them as a pillar of the virtues of piety, and wast called a prophet through wonders. Therefore we entreat thee: cease not to pray unto the Savior for us, that our souls may be saved that our souls may be saved!

*Now and ever... Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*[^728]
Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, she who bare Thee cried aloud: What strange mystery is this which I behold, O my Son? How dost Thou die in the flesh, hanging upon the Tree, O Giver of life?

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*

*Glory... Tone 6:*[^729]
Divine wisdom was given unto thee, O wise one, as unto Daniel; for as a dream was revealed unto him, so was the mystery of the faith revealed unto thee. Therefore pray, O venerable father, that our souls may be saved!

*Now and ever... Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*[^730]
When the all-pure one beheld Thee hanging upon the Cross, weeping she cried aloud as a mother: O my Son and my God, my sweetest Child, how dost Thou endure this shameful passion?

*Troparion, Tone 8:*[^731]
Vigilant in prayers, enduring in the working of wonders, thou didst acquire achievements matching thy name: but pray unto Christ God, O father Gregory, to enlighten our souls, lest we ever sleep unto death!

*Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion.*

*At Matins, both Canons from the Octoechos, and of the Saint on 6, whose acrostic is: "To the wonderworker Gregory I weave praise." A composition of Theophanes. Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^732]
*The chariot-driver Pharaoh the wonderworking rod of Moses once submerged, striking crosswise and dividing the sea; but it saved Israel the fugitive, who marched on foot and sang a hymn unto God.*

*Troparion:*
Show brightly even now in me the divine working of thy wonders, O father Gregory, delivering me from the depth of transgressions, O blessed one, and enlightening me with thy brilliance, that I may worthily sing of thee!

*Troparion:*
As one circumspect, intelligent, and wise, O blessed one, thou didst prefer the nobility of the soul before carnal pleasures, industriously observing the dogmas of wisdom, wherewith the soul is nourished as it draws near unto God, O Gregory!

*Troparion:*
Having acquired chastity as a good helper, the fierce serpent, beholding thee, O Gregory, raised up envy against thee; which serpent thou didst put to shame, O father, by thy longsuffering, having healed the woman possessed by passion!

*Troparion:*
Dwelling in a foreign land, O venerable one, thou wast shown to be honored by all for thy virtue pious and God-loving; having received the gift of working wonders from God, whereby Thou wast known, O divinely-speaking one, shining in the world like the sun!

*Theotokion:*
From a royal root thou didst bud forth, O pure one, and didst bear the King, Christ the Word of God, incarnate beyond mind and thought from thy pure blood: Who is twofold in nature, and single in hypostasis!

*Ode 3, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^733]
*Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens with understanding, and didst found the earth upon the waters: establish me upon the rock of Thy commandments, O Christ, for none is holy save Thee, O only Lover of mankind!*

*Troparion:*
Having cleansed thy mind from the surge of passions, and being filled with philosophical vision, thou didst appear comely, a dwelling of wisdom, and wast enriched with the gift of prophecy, O Gregory!

*Troparion:*
Conversing with divinely-inspired Scripture, O all-blessed one, and having chosen for thyself the forms of diverse ways of life, thou didst establish within thyself one image of virtue, O divinely-wise Gregory!

*Troparion:*
Having divinely learned the mystery of theology through divine guidance: enlighten us to worship the consubstantial Trinity, co-natural, uncreated, and co-eternal!

*Troparion:*
Guided by God, for out of love thou didst seek Him, thou didst have the pure Virgin Mother of God and the Son of Thunder as teachers of mysteries, instructing thee, O divinely-speaking one, in the light of the Trinity!

*Theotokion:*
As the rod that budded forth Christ, the flower of incorruption, and as the golden censer, we all know thee, O pure Maiden, bearing in thine arms the coal of divine holiness, O divinely-blessed one!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Of divine faith" (Бж҃твенныя вѣ́ры):*[^734]
A new Moses wast thou in deeds, having received upon the mount the tablets of the faith of the mystical manifestation of God, a lawgiver unto the people of the mysteries of piety through thy labors, O Gregory. Therefore we all, the faithful, honor thy memory, asking great mercy through thee! *(Twice)*

*Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:*[^735]
Thou wast a divine tabernacle of the Word, O only all-pure Virgin Mother, surpassing the angels in purity! Cleanse me with the divine waters of thy prayers, who more than all have become dust and am defiled by carnal transgressions, granting great mercy, O pure one!

*Stavrotheotokion:*[^736]
The undefiled ewe-lamb of the Word, the incorrupt Virgin Mother, seeing Him hanging upon the Cross Who painless budded forth from her, lamenting like a mother, cried aloud: Woe is me, my Child, how dost Thou suffer willingly, wishing to deliver mankind from the passions of dishonor?

*Ode 4, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^737]
*Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art my power; Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who didst not leave the bosom of the Father, and didst visit our poverty. Therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!*

*Troparion:*
Having plowed the good earth, O divinely-wise father, and having received the seed of the Word, thou didst multiply it a hundredfold according to the Gospel; even now, O Gregory, bringing by thy teachings those who sing unto God: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Thy life, shining forth like lightning, O father, drove away demonic delusion; for the darkness of the demons could not touch the light of thy virtue. Therefore, unhurt by soul-destroying delusion, appearing like a rock, thou art radiant!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast vouchsafed to behold the darkness of the most divine Light; and having received the God-written law like Moses, O father, thou didst learn the sure doctrine of theology. Thence thou wast shown forth as a lawgiver of Christ's Church, O divinely-wise Gregory!

*Troparion:*
Turning away from rhetorical eloquence, and being enlightened by the word of grace, O father, thou didst truly receive apostolic power over demons; for the prince of darkness flees from thy shining beam, O Gregory!

*Theotokion:*
The Ark prefigured thee from afar, which received the God-written law, O all-immaculate one who didst ineffably conceive in thy womb the Life-originating Word, Who richly nourishes the souls of those who cry aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Ode 5, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^738]
*Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy face, O unwaning Light, and why hath alien darkness covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and direct my ways toward the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee!*

*Troparion:*
Smoothing down chilled hearts by the working of thy words, thou didst cast the divine seed into them, O hierarch, and didst bring forth unto the Deliverer the multifold fruit of the salvation of the faithful, O divinely-speaking one!

*Troparion:*
The divine prelate, kindled with zeal, anointed thee, O father, though absent, piously trusting in God Who knows all things, and relying upon thy honorable life relying upon thy honorable life, O divinely-speaking Gregory!

*Troparion:*
By the footsteps of thy commandments thou didst quench the ignitions of idols, and by thy teachings thou didst confirm the faithful, O all-wise one: having ascended the mountain like Samonas in visions, and having become like an oak in firmness!

*Troparion:*
Deliver me from cruel things by thy holy prayers, O divinely-wise one; tear up the handwriting of my transgressions, O father, as being a priest who hast received power from God to remit transgressions!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast adorned, O Virgin, with thy virginal, all-pure beauties, and didst cover the ill-favored shame of the first Eve, having given birth unto Christ Who grants the garment of immortality unto those who honor thee!

*Ode 6, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^739]
*Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray; for unto Thee have I cried, and do Thou give ear unto me, O God of my salvation!*

*Troparion:*
Working wonders, thou didst dry up the fratricidal lake, and didst stay the torrent of the river, O all-wise one, having planted a staff which immediately took root and grew by divine nods, O Gregory!

*Troparion:*
Divine zeal consumed thee, O all-rich one, for thou couldst not endure to see God insulted; therefore by Thy prayers, O divinely-speaking one, thou didst destroy the vain-minded thoughts of Acacius!

*Troparion:*
The wretched, impious Hebrew who wished to mock thee as dead, showed thee to be an accomplisher of the dogmas of God Who glorifies thee, O divinely-wise Gregory!

*Theotokion:*
The all-creative Spirit came upon thee, O all-immaculate one, and the Word of God made His dwelling within thee, and became flesh ineffably, remaining unchanged!

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*[^740]
Having received the power of many wonders, with fearful signs thou didst terrify demons, and didst drive away human ailments, O all-wise Gregory; and thou art called a wonderworker, having received thy title from thy deeds!

*Ikos:*[^741]
Whence shall I, the wretched one, begin to weave praises, beholding many and most marvelous things? If I begin from the life of the venerable one, I shall not be able at all; for his divine life surpasses every mind. If from his wonders, in this too I shall be ashamed, for they are more numerous than the sand. Therefore he was called a wonderworker, having received his title from his deeds!

*Ode 7, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^742]
*Before the condescension of God, the fire was put to shame in Babylon of old; therefore the youths in the furnace, treading with joyful step as in a meadow of flowers, danced and sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*

*Troparion:*
The praise of the flock, the honor of teachers, a luminary of the Church, an unshakable pillar of piety wast thou shown to be, O Gregory, crying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having shone forth with wonders, thou didst enlighten the universe; therefore, having gathered together, O divinely-wise one, we call thee blessed, being nourished by thy words, O Gregory, and singing: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst pour forth healings unto all the infirm, O all-wise one; for an abundant, wonder-working grace was poured out upon thy lips, wherewith thou didst cry aloud: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Now all things are filled with divine light through thee, O all-immaculate one; for thou wast shown to be the gate through which God came into the world, enlightening those who cry in faith: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Ode 8, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^743]
*The Chaldean tyrant madly kindled the furnace sevenfold for the godly; but seeing them saved by a greater power, he cried aloud unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye youths, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*

*Troparion:*
Having been enriched through thee with the radiant light of the consubstantial and honorable Trinity, O Gregory, as we celebrate thy festival today, we ask to be illumined with wonder-working grace, crying unto the Benefactor: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Having received the radiances of the primordial Godhead as a newly-revealed mirror, O all-wealthy one, thou didst enlighten the world, sending forth rays of light unto those who hymn Orthodoxy in song: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Sheltered by God, as a cause of piety, thou wast preserved for the pious, O all-wise one, being concealed upon the mountain like another lawgiver Moses, teaching all to praise the Creator and Deliverer: Ye youths, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast the dwelling of the unwaning Light, O all-pure one, shining with the beauties of virginity and illuminating all who truly confess thee from their soul as Theotokos, and who cry: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^744]
*Heaven was filled with awe at this, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God hath appeared in the flesh unto men, and thy womb was made more spacious than the heavens. Therefore the ranks of angels and men magnify thee as the Theotokos!*

*Troparion:*
Shining with the light of the most excellent life, thou standest now before the Great Light with divine-working wonder-workings, crowned as a victor, O venerable one, O father, hierarch, and wonderworker, divinely-wise Gregory, luminary of the Church, adornment of the Orthodox!

*Troparion:*
Direct by thy prayers the priesthood of the Church now, chosen and sanctified, O wonderworker; and entreat that those who now faithfully celebrate thy memory may obtain the heavenly Kingdom and be vouchsafed divine gladness!

*Troparion:*
Having conquered the demonic assaults, and having subdued carnal mindsets, and having become a guiltless and venerable hierarch, clothed in the garment of righteousness, O wonderworker, thou standest with boldness before the throne of the King of all, O all-blessed one!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast revealed, O Virgin, Mother of God, having beyond nature given birth in the flesh unto the good Word, Whom the Father poured forth from His heart before all ages as Good; Whom we now understand to be also beyond bodily nature, even though He clothed Himself in a body!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены̀ ѹ҆слы́шите):*[^745]
Thou didst shine forth with wonders, O wonderworker Gregory; thou didst deliver the idolater from corruption and demonic delusion, moving a stone by thy command; and having dried up a lake, thou didst stay a river. Therefore we all praise thee with one accord, O thrice-blessed one!

*Theotokion, the same Podoben:*[^746]
Rejoice, praise of the faithful! Rejoice, confirmation of the venerable! Rejoice, glory of the righteous! Rejoice, light of those in darkness! Rejoice, all-holy temple! Rejoice, paradise of God! Rejoice, dissolution of the curse, O blessed Mary!

*At the Aposticha, stichera of the Octoechos, and of the saint, Tone 4:*
*Verse: Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice.*[^747]
Having received the choice of the priesthood from God, and having clothed thyself from on high with the divine robe, thou didst show forth those who formerly were sons of unbelief to be children of light and heirs. For the grace of God's wisdom was poured out upon thy lips, O Gregory, personal worker of the most glorious deeds of the Lord! Therefore now also, in thy memory, pray unto Christ God for our souls!

*Glory... Tone 8:*[^748]
Before the hierarch renowned in wonders, even soulless things were marvelously transformed in reverence: for the lake dried up that drove the brothers to folly, and the staff grew, bridling the river; the stone was moved by a word, bringing the unbelieving unto the knowledge of God. For his sake, grant unto our souls great mercy, O God!

*Now and ever... Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*[^749]
What is this visible sight * that is seen by mine eyes, * O Master? * Thou Who upholdest all creation, * lifted up upon the tree, * Thou diest, granting life unto all! * the Theotokos, weeping, said, * when she beheld Him lifted up upon the Cross, * Who shone forth from her ineffably, * God and Man!

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Octoechos, and of the saint, Ode 3.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*[^750] *Verse: What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me?*[^751] *Epistle to the Corinthians, composite section 151.*[^752] *Alleluia, Tone 2: Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice.*[^753] *Gospel according to Matthew, section 34 from the midpoint.*[^754] *Communion Hymn: In everlasting remembrance shall the righteous be.*[^755]

*In the same month, on the 18th day: The Holy Martyrs Plato and Romanus.*
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of Saint Plato, Tone 4, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*[^756]
Full of valiant wisdom, * thou didst endure with most courageous resolve * the severing of limbs, the slashing of thy body, * the unendurable fire, famine, and death; * awaiting the unending glory * that lay before thee eternally, * and foreseeing everlasting beatitude 

*Sticheron 2:*
Having surpassed all sensation, * and having directed thy mind unto the higher life * by divinely-wise contemplation * and with a magnanimous soul: * thou didst despise the baseness and lowliness of visible things. * Therefore, scraped with irons * and burned with fire for Christ, O martyr, * thou didst endure most valiantly!

*Sticheron 3:*
Every assault of the enemy * and the onslaughts of the persecutors * thou didst destroy by grace; * thou wast crowned with the crown of victory, O all-wealthy one, * being vouchsafed incorruptible gladness * and ineffable divine radiance; * where thou art now, * entreat remission of sins for those who praise thee!

*Other Stichera of Saint Romanus, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^757]
Kindled by fasting, * constrained by suffering, * and tormented by many tortures, * having become a two-edged sword, * thou didst cut down the demonic legions, O Romanus, * adornment of sufferers, * divine boast, * honorable beauty of the Church, * of those who ended their course by their own blood, O all-praised one!

*Sticheron 2:*
Stretched out and scraped, * enclosed in prison, * having thy tongue cut out, O glorious one, * and thy jaws shattered, * and receiving a blessed end by violent strangulation, O fellow-sufferer, * thou wast shown to be unshaken and unbending * through the cooperation of the Divine Spirit, O Romanus. * Therefore we faithfully praise thee!

*Sticheron 3:*
The child speaks truth, * he amazes the earthly-born, * and is adorned by honorable resistances, * and is enlightened by his end. * He is enriched with the glorious fame of the holy sufferers, * whose zeal he acquired, O worthily-blessed, * valiantly-wise Romanus. * With them entreat that remission of debts * be sent down unto us all!

*Glory... Tone 6. Idiomelon:*[^758]
Fearful and most glorious are the victories of Thy martyr, O Lord: for having emulated the boldness of the fishermen, and by net-woven theology, he tore to shreds the mythology of Plato and historical blasphemy in words and deeds! Having his skin flayed and his head severed, by the shedding of his blood he drowned the enemy. But as the adornment of martyrs, who didst boldly proclaim the great name of Christ, entreat, O wonderworker, all-blessed Plato, that great mercy be granted unto our souls!

*Now and ever... Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*[^759]
Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, * she who bare Thee cried aloud: * What strange mystery is this that I behold, O my Son? * How dost Thou die in the flesh, suspended upon the tree, * O Giver of life?

*Troparion, Tone 4:*[^760]
Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the tormentors and crushed the powerless audacities of the demons: through their prayers save our souls!

*Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion.*

*At Matins, one Canon of the Octoechos, and two of the saints.*

*Canon of Saint Plato, whereof the acrostic is: "I sing the breadth of thy praises, O Plato." By Theophanes.*[^761]

*Ode 1, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^762]
*The wonderworking rod of Moses of old, striking the sea in the form of a cross and dividing it, overwhelmed the charioteer Pharaoh, but saved Israel who fled on foot, as they chanted a song unto God!*

*Troparion:*
Traversing the most pure expanse of the spiritual Kingdom, O glorious one, save those who praise thee from all tribulation and the strait of afflictions, leading them without turning back into the heavenly path!

*Troparion:*
Warded by the armor of piety, thou wast shown to be an unshakable pillar, O Plato; thou didst endure the full fierceness of wounds, and didst submit to the straits of sufferings, reaching forth through divine grace!

*Troparion:*
Having displayed youthful resistance, through suffering thou didst cast off mortal and corruptible grossness, O all-wise one; and having clothed thyself in an incorruptible robe, thou standest rejoicing before the Master!

*Theotokion:*
Beyond understanding thou didst give birth, O blessed and all-immaculate Theotokos, unto the incarnate Only-begotten Word, co-unoriginate and co-eternal with the Father; therefore, with venerable wisdom, we proclaim and truly glorify thee!

*Another Canon, of Saint Romanus, whereof the acrostic is: "With crowns of suffering I praise thee, Romanus." Tone 4.*[^763]

*Ode 1, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^764]
*Having traversed the Red Sea's deep with unwetted feet, Israel of old, by the crosswise-stretched hands of Moses, vanquished the power of Amalek in the wilderness!*

*Troparion:*
Shining clearly with the unwaning rays of thy labors, and enlightened with the choirs of passion-bearers, send down enlightenment unto me, driving away passionate darkness by thy God-pleasing prayers, O Romanus!

*Troparion:*
Unshaken by the surging waves of the idol sea, as one established upon the Rock of Christ, through the calm of the Divine Spirit thou didst quell the surging tempest of much-troubled godlessness!

*Troparion:*
As a glorious and fruitful garden, thou didst preserve the Church of Christ, abounding in all good things, inaccessible to wolves, O Romanus, confirming her by thy teaching!

*Theotokion:*
Truly through thee, O all-immaculate one, human nature was shown mercy; for the Creator, having become incarnate from thee beyond word and intellect, was willingly led unto death, delivering us from hades!

*Ode 3, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^765]
*Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens with understanding, and didst found the earth upon the waters: establish me upon the rock of Thy commandments, O Christ, for there is none holy save Thee, Who alone art the Lover of mankind!*

*Troparion:*
Like an incorruptible spark, thou didst patiently enter into the fierce flame, O all-blessed one, plainly kindled with the zeal of piety, and illuminated by the divine fire of faith!

*Troparion:*
Having supernaturally overcome the demonic servants, and having endured the pains of severe tortures with patience, thou wast shown to be a fellow-citizen of angels and a crown-bearer, O divinely-wise and all-blessed Plato!

*Troparion:*
Having contested on earth for Christ, O all-blessed one, and having received heavenly gifts and ever-abiding crowns from Him, thou dost take up thine abode rejoicing in the honorable place!

*Theotokion:*
Gate of the Light, adorned with the radiant beams of the Spirit, O Mother of God: for through thee the Word descended unto us, enlightening with divine light all who praise thee!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^766]
*Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge and confirmation!*

*Troparion:*
Having slain the noetic beast with the sling of thy words, O Romanus, thou didst save the flock of Christ unharmed from idol hurt!

*Troparion:*
Having grown mighty by the weapon of the Cross, thou didst turn back the assaults of the enemy and didst expose their weakness, O wise and worthily-blessed Romanus!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst cast down the enemy, shattering his jaws, O glorious Romanus, having thy cheeks scraped for Christ, O ever-memorable blessed one!

*Theotokion:*
God, Who is one in essence, the Father's Word, co-essential with the Spirit, having clothed Himself in flesh from thee deified the earthly-born, O Mother of God!

*Sessional Hymn of Saint Plato, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^767]
Reaching forth in faith into the expanse of struggles, O all-glorious and wise martyr, having constricted the enemy's snares, thou didst destroy them; and having well finished the divine course, thou didst reach the expanse of paradise, rejoicing. Therefore the Church, radiant today in the vast expanse of piety, celebrates thy memory and cries unto thee, O blessed one: Entreat Christ God that He grant remission of transgressions unto those who honor with love thy holy memory!

*Glory... of Saint Romanus, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*[^768]
Having trampled the crafty one by asceticism and having been glorified through sufferings as a martyr of Christ, thou didst endure manfully with a perfect mind. Therefore thou hast been numbered among the choirs of martyrs, and hast obtained an everlasting Kingdom; dancing therein, remember us who celebrate thy memory with faith!

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*[^769]
Having fled under thy divine and sheltering protection, O humble Theotokos, falling down I pray: Have mercy, O all-immaculate one, for my sins have risen above my head; and being a prodigal, I fear the torments and tremble. Make supplication, O pure one, unto thy Son, that He may deliver me from them!

*Stavrotheotokion:*[^770]
She who bare Thee in the flesh at the end of times, Who wast begotten of the unoriginate Father, beholding Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ, cried aloud: Woe is me, most beloved Jesus! How art Thou, Who art glorified as God by angels, now willingly crucified by lawless men, O my Son? I praise Thee, O Long-suffering One!

*Ode 4, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^771]
*Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power; Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who hast not left the bosom of the Father, and hast visited our poverty. Therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!*

*Troparion:*
Mingled wholly with the love of thy Creator, thou didst not feel bodily pains; having stripped off the passionate, mortal, and leathern garments of the flesh, thou didst clothe thyself, O Plato, in the robe of chastity and salvation!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast shown to be a divine sacred-minister, O martyr, having offered thyself as a blameless, male, and perfect whole-burnt-offering unto Christ the Deliverer Who was slaughtered for all. For having kindled thy soul with good love, concerning the burning of thy very flesh, thou didst take no thought!

*Troparion:*
Emulating the three youths who were in Babylon, thou didst not fear the all-devouring fire, but manfully and youthfully didst endure its unendurable flame; therefore the Fellow-Creator worthily received thee with them into the bridal chamber of glory!

*Theotokion:*
Being from a royal root, thou didst bear for us the Word of God Who rules over all, Who became flesh and remained unchanged; therefore as the true and sovereign Theotokos, O all-holy Virgin, we glorify thee!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^772]
*Beholding Thee, the Sun of Righteousness, lifted up upon the Cross, the Church stood in her order, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*

*Troparion:*
Guided as by a ladder, thou didst ascend the tree, O blessed one, with ineffable beauty; and thou didst attain unto the abiding choir, O worthily-glorious martyr Romanus!

*Troparion:*
Having stripped off the mortal garments in tortures, O blessed one, brightly wast thou clothed, O all-glorious martyr Romanus, in the radiant robe of salvation!

*Troparion:*
The tongue of the child, made wise by the inspiration of the Comforter, proclaimed Thee, O Lover of mankind, the Lord of glory, the Creator of all, and God Who art able to save!

*Theotokion:*
Blessed, O Virgin, is the Fruit of thy womb, by Whom all nations were delivered from the mortal curse and cleansed; and blessed through thee, we hymn thee as the mediatress of life!

*Ode 5, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^773]
*Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy countenance, O unwaning Light, and an alien darkness hath covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and direct my ways toward the light of Thy commandments, I pray!*

*Troparion:*
Thou gavest no slumber unto thine eyelids, nor sleep unto thine eyes, O martyr, until thou didst fall asleep, O blessed one, with that blessed and fitting sleep beloved by those who love God, having had thy head severed by the sword!

*Troparion:*
Suffering, thou didst contest as though in an alien body, O all-blessed one; having become a spectator of others suffering, thou didst suffer thyself: for kindled by divine longing, thou didst not fear the impending tortures, O glorious one!

*Troparion:*
Thou hast found an unassailable wealth and an unfading glory, dancing with the angels in heavenly mansions, and having most excellently become a partaker of incorruptible immortality!

*Theotokion:*
The remission of sins grant unto Thy servants by thy prayers, O all-hymned Virgin Theotokos, delivering them from temptations, afflictions, sorrows, and the domination of blasphemous heretics!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^774]
*Thou, my Lord, hast come into the world as a Light, a holy Light turning from gloomy ignorance those who praise Thee in faith!*

*Troparion:*
With the suffering streams of thy blood thou didst drown the sea of godlessness, and thou didst pour forth rivers of healings, O Romanus!

*Troparion:*
As a chosen gift, as a blameless sacrifice, thou didst offer unto the Master, O Romanus, the theological child who was slaughtered!

*Troparion:*
The foolishness of the enemy thou didst strike by the wisdom of the Holy Spirit, wounding thy body with stripes, O all-praised Romanus!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst abolish the curse, having given birth unto Joy, and didst renew humanity by thy childbearing, O Virgin Mary unwedded!

*Ode 6, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^775]
*Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray; for unto Thee have I cried, and give ear unto me, O God of my salvation!*

*Troparion:*
Having become superior to passions and torments, thou didst endure the cuttings of the flesh, O glorious one; for thou didst have Christ as Helper, Creator, and Co-worker!

*Troparion:*
Beholding ever with spiritual understanding the splendor of the Creator, and contemplating ineffable beauty, thou didst disregard the baseness of visible things!

*Theotokion:*
As an animate ark thou didst contain the Lawgiver; as a holy temple thou didst receive the Holy One Who became man for the benefaction of mankind, O all-blessed one!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^776]
*I will sacrifice unto Thee with a voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, cleansed of the demonic blood by the blood which flowed for mercy's sake from Thy side!*

*Troparion:*
Having put off mortality and corruption through scraping, thou didst clothe thyself in the beauty of incorruptible life, O martyr, adorned, O Romanus, with unwaning spiritual splendors!

*Troparion:*
Like blood streams, thy severed tongue poured forth torrents of teachings, whereby thou didst inherit, O passion-bearer, imperishable beatitude, abiding for ever thirsting, thou didst drink the stream of wisdom, by the counsel of her who bare him, the lips of the child speaking of God, who by the sword departed unto endless life!

*Theotokion:*
Be a swift refuge unto me, O all-immaculate one, delivering me from violence, rescuing me from shameful passion, and directing me unto the divine path, O Mother of God!

*Kontakion, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*[^777]
Thy holy memory gladdens the universe, gathering all the faithful into thy most honorable temple, where now assembled with joy, we sing in hymns and brightness. Therefore, O Plato, we cry aloud unto thee: Deliver thy city from barbarian invasion, O holy one!

*Ikos:*[^778]
Having forsaken all Hellenic vanity, divinely-wise Plato greatly loved the soul-profiting teachings of Christ's disciples. Therefore was he shown to be honorable unto all, as an anchor of faith in his fatherland, whose name is clearly called Ancyra. For having well nurtured him, she ever finds in him an assured shelter against enemies and a fervent defender in battles, crying aloud: Deliver thy city from barbarian invasion, O holy one!

*Ode 7, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^779]
*Before the condescension of God, the fire was put to shame in Babylon of old; therefore the youths in the furnace, treading with joyful step as in a meadow of flowers, danced and sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*

*Troparion:*
Having lawfully suffered and having trampled down thine enemies, the Lawgiver crowned thee with the crown of victory, as thou didst cry aloud with a great voice, saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst depart rejoicing unto Him Whom thou didst desire from of old, emulating Whose all-pure passion that became the cause of salvation unto men, thou didst sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
All the heavenly powers were amazed at the endurance of thy suffering, and likewise the men who beheld it at that time: for supernaturally, while being severed, thou didst cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Being delivered, O all-immaculate one, through the divine childbearing of thy virginity from the bonds of death and the curse of the first-fashioned Adam, knowing thee in wisdom as Theotokos, we cry: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^780]
*The Abrahamite youths from the furnace of the Persians, through the love of piety* more than inflamed by the flame of piety, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
By thy strangling, O passion-bearer, having strangled the serpent, thou didst truly find life, O most glorious Romanus, crying aloud unto the Lord: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Illumined with the rays of the unwaning Light, thou didst extinguish the lofty flame, O Romanus; adorned with the prophetic gift and united with the choirs of martyrs, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
As from a garden of many flowers, nurtured by maternal teachings, the sweet-smelling rose of infancy, watered with martyr's blood, is incorruptibly offered unto Christ!

*Theotokion:*
Deliver us who have fallen into the depth of sins, O all-hymned one, who alone didst bear God without seed, as we sing unto thee: Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Lady!

*Ode 8, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^781]
*Sevenfold did the Chaldean tormentor furiously kindle the furnace for the godly; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried aloud unto the Creator and Redeemer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*

*Troparion:*
With radiant struggles didst thou contend, O all-laudable one, and most radiantly did Christ bestow upon thee abundant blessed glory that abides eternally, establishing thee in the heavenly mansions as thou fervently singest: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Christ unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
As a most faithful intercessor, as a most fervent advocate, we now offer thee unto the King of all and Creator of creation. Pray for us, interceding with thy martyr's boldness for those who praise thee, that we may faithfully sing: Ye people, supremely exalt Christ unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast vouchsafed to receive an unshakable kingdom through thine active faith, which God Who lies not promised to grant unto Thee; for Whose sake thou didst surrender thy body to fire and torments, crying aloud: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Christ unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst divinely give birth unto the unoriginate Word of God, understood together with the Father, Who by paternal counsel composed all things out of non-being, Who became flesh for the sake of us men. Therefore, confessing thee as Theotokos in Orthodox wisdom, we supremely exalt Christ unto the ages!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^782]
*Daniel, stretching forth his hands, shut the lions' gaping mouths in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of fire, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*

*Troparion:*
Thou wast an obedient hearer of the words of Christ, O glorious one, laying down thy soul for thy flock; fervently strangled, tortured, scraped, and wounded for His sake, thou didst cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Truly thy mouth and tongue were filled with joy and gladness, blessing God unceasingly; for being cut off and dripping with blood, it lays down for us the law of faith, O Romanus, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth unto the paternal Word by the Divine Spirit, thou didst remain a virgin, O unwedded Parent of God, having surpassed the laws of nature by thy childbearing. Therefore, rejoicing, we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Ode 9, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^783]
*Every ear trembled at the ineffable condescension of God: how the Most High of His own will came down even unto the flesh, becoming man from a virginal womb. Therefore, O faithful, we magnify the all-immaculate Theotokos!*

*Troparion:*
Come, then, ye who love the martyrs, let us hymn the divinely-crowned martyr, who extended piety from his birth; for having become a plant of the Vine of life, he brings forth fruit that ever pours out compunction unto us!

*Troparion:*
Precious in the sight of God is shown to be the death of the martyrs; for it becomes an advocate of everlasting, imperishable, true life, and grants an incorruptible portion, immortal glory, and rich recompense!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst surrender thy whole life unto Almighty God, O martyr, and rejoicing, didst offer thyself as an acceptable, living sacrifice; therefore wast thou vouchsafed beyond all mind the sweet streams of beatitude;[^784] but pray that those who hymn thee may be delivered from temptations!

*Theotokion:*
Save me, O Mother of God, who didst bear Christ my Savior, God and man, twofold in nature but not in hypostasis: only-begotten indeed of the Father, and born of thee the firstborn of all creation. Therefore do we all ever magnify thee!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^785]
*A cornerstone was cut out from thee, an uncut mountain, O Virgin, not cut by the hand of man: even Christ, Who joined together the sundered* natures! Therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Theotokos!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst extend all thy desire unto the Master, O martyr; and having endured manifold wounds, O glorious Romanus, thou didst attain unto ineffable glory and blessed delight!

*Troparion:*
Instead of suffering, the sweet stream was given unto thee, O martyr, as thou wearest a crown, O Romanus, and hast received a purple robe from thy blood; as a sweet-smelling and unfading rose, the infant was slain for the sake of Christ!

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast delivered earthly mortals from the ancestral curse, O Virgin, and hast opened unto us the life of Eden by thy supernatural childbearing. Therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Theotokos!

*Exapostilarion, Tone 3, Podoben: "In spirit in the sanctuary" (Дх҃омъ во ст҃и́лищи):*[^786]
Thou didst walk the rough path by the divine track, and didst ascend unto the breadth of the heavenly kingdom, O Plato, glory of martyrs, shining with the light of the incorruptible Trinity! Therefore, partaking of unending glory, remember those who honor thee!

*Theotokion:*
As an invincible protectress and a true rampart, I offer thy protection, O Virgin Theotokos, our mediatress before God: that I may piously be delivered from eternal torment, and through thee partake of the heavenly kingdom in incorruptible life!

*In the same month, on the 19th day: The Holy Prophet Obadiah; and the Holy Martyr Barlaam; and our Venerable Fathers, the Desert-Dwellers who shone forth in fasting, Barlaam and Joasaph the Prince, in the great land called India.*[^787]
*(Their service is written after this service).*
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Prophet, Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-laudable martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мч҃еницы):*[^788]
Having become a radiant receptacle of the Spirit, O Obadiah, and illumined by Him in most divinely-contemplative wise, thou wast enriched by the image of prophecy, by the foreknowledge of future things, and by the knowledge of the truth pray now that there be granted unto our souls peace and great mercy!

*Sticheron 2:*
