Those things whereby God is represented by His primary properties and essential indications: of these the glorious and honorable prophets partake secondarily according to grace and participation by gift; as the Lord illumines His pleasing servants with His own radiance!

*Sticheron 3:*
Filled with the unwaning Light and beholding glory beyond mind and reason, standing close unto the God of all as a glorious prophet and divine proclaimer of God: pray unto Him, that there be granted unto our souls peace and great mercy!

*Other Stichera of Saint Barlaam, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^789]
Thou wast a pillar firmer, stronger than bronze, and mightier than iron; for each of these melts when burned and is straightway destroyed by fire, overcome by its force; but thine unyielding right hand, held forth while coals burned upon it, most marvelously conquered, O all-wise one!

*Sticheron 2:*
Having become as a priest, standing before God, and drawing near unto Him, O blessed one: not with the blood of others, but rather with thine own, and with a martyr's hand, thou didst offer a censer of sweet fragrance; not unto smoky deceits, but unto Christ the Savior, good and ever-reigning!

*Sticheron 3:*
We joyfully name thee both together, O all-laudable one: the priest who offers and the lamb that is offered; as consecrating both, thou didst offer thyself unto God as an all-immaculate slaughter, whole-burnt by fiery martyrdom. Pray unto Him to save those who ever honor thy most glorious memory!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion, Tone 4:*
Bedew my mind with the showers of the All-Holy Spirit, O all-immaculate one, who didst bear the inestimable drop, Christ, Who washed away the measureless iniquities of men by His compassions; dry up the fountain of my passions, and vouchsafe me ever the stream of the sweetness of life, by thy prayers!

*Stavrotheotokion, Tone 4:*
When the Ewe that bare Thee beheld Thee, the Lamb and Shepherd, upon the tree, she wailed and with motherly lament said unto Thee: O beloved Son, how art Thou suspended upon the tree of the Cross, O longsuffering One? How were Thy hands and feet pierced with nails by the lawless, O Word, and Thou didst pour out Thy blood, O Master?

*Troparion of the Martyr, Tone 4:*
*Thy martyr* Thy martyr Barlaam, O Lord, in his suffering received an imperishable crown from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, he cast down the torturers and crushed the powerless audacities of the demons. By his prayers, save our souls![^790]

*At Matins: One canon of the Octoechos, and two of the saints.*
*Canon of the Prophet, the acrostic whereof is: "I sing the glory of the seer Obadiah. By Theophanes."*[^791] *Tone 5.*
*Ode 1, Tone 5. Heirmos:*[^792]
*Unto God the Savior, Who guided the people through the sea with dryshod feet, and drowned Pharaoh with all his host: unto Him alone let us sing, for He hath been glorified!*

*Troparion:*
Standing now prophetically before God the Savior, pray with boldness that He may enlighten with luminous rays those who in faith call thee blessed, O divinely-inspired one!

*Troparion:*
He Who clearly sees all things knowingly, beholding the undisturbed, pure, and light-bearing state of thy heart, O blessed one, appoints thee a God-pleasing prophet!

*Troparion:*
Having truly beheld visions delivered unto thee from God, thou didst proclaim the wickedness of brethren, their grievous destruction, and their righteous uprooting, O blessed one!

*Theotokion:*
Saved by thy seedless childbearing, O pure Parent of God, we pray thee: Deliver us from worldly assaults, as we harmoniously cry aloud a song of victory!

*Another Canon, of the Martyr, the acrostic whereof is: "I sing thy patient sufferings, O Barlaam. By Theophanes."*[^793] *Tone 4.*
*Ode 1, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^794]
*I will sing unto Thee, O Lord my God, for Thou hast led Thy people forth from Egyptian bondage, and Thou didst cover the chariots of Pharaoh and his power!*

*Troparion:*
Illumined with the splendors of thy suffering, preserve by thy prayers us who in faith honor thy memory, O Barlaam!

*Troparion:*
Having quenched the fire of impiety by the divinely-inspired fire of piety, let wonderful Barlaam be truly honored with canticles!

*Troparion:*
Having contended in piety, O crown-bearing Barlaam, thou hast now worthily been honored with the crown of glory by the right hand of the Almighty!

*Troparion:*
The Master granted thee strength against manifold wounds, O all-blessed martyr; therefore hast thou overcome the ferocity of the godless!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast shown to be the heavenly ladder, whereby the Word descended unto us, O Virgin, which thy forefather Jacob foresaw of old!

*Ode 3, Tone 5. Heirmos:*[^795]
*By the power of Thy Cross, O Christ, establish my mind, that I may hymn and glorify Thy saving Ascension!*

*Troparion:*
Thou wast a river of mystical waters, proceeding from the deep of the gifts of the Spirit, O proclaimer of God!

*Troparion:*
By the divine will and providence, thou wast set forth to foretell things to come, O praiseworthy one!

*Troparion:*
Illumined by divine and heavenly light, thou didst proclaim beforehand the coming salvation of the nations, O all-blessed one!

*Theotokion:*
The Word took up His abode in thee, O Virgin Mother, and saves by thine intercession those who acknowledge thee in wisdom as Theotokos, O all-immaculate one!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^796]
*The bow of the mighty is weakened, and the weak have girded themselves with strength; therefore my heart is established in the Lord!*

*Troparion:*
All the bond of the flesh and the joining of thy limbs were dissolved, yet the strength of thy soul was preserved unbroken. With divine power thou didst endure the onset of those scraping thy ribs, O all-blessed one, having stoutly displayed youthful endurance!

*Troparion:*
Who can worthily praise with laudations thy steadfast and strong resolve, and the unslumbering wisdom of thy mind, O all-blessed one?

*Theotokion:*
The corruption of death was stayed when the Hypostatic Life appeared in flesh unto men from thy womb, O all-immaculate Bride of God!

*Sessional Hymn of the Prophet, Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*[^797]
Having acquired a mind radiant with great splendors and bright to behold, he declares things to come, speaking by the Holy Spirit. Honoring Him today in godly wisdom, we celebrate his sacred memory, which illumines our hearts!

*Glory... Sessional Hymn of the Martyr, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*[^798]
Having quenched the flame of impiety and refreshed the hearts of the faithful with the dew of the knowledge of God, let glorious Barlaam now be faithfully honored with divine hymns; for he routed the deceit of idols, and having received the crown of victory, he asks for all the forgiveness of sins!

*Now and ever... Theotokion, Tone 4:*
He Who sits upon the cherubic throne and abides in the bosom of the Father: as upon a holy throne He sits in thy bosom, O Lady; for God, having truly become incarnate, hath reigned over all nations, and in understanding we now sing unto Him: pray thou unto Him, that thy servants may be saved!

*Stavrotheotokion, Tone 4:*
Beholding Thee, Who wast born of the unoriginate Father and at the last didst take flesh of her, hanging upon the Cross, O Christ, she that bare Thee wailed: Woe is me, O most beloved Jesus! How is it that Thou, Who art glorified as God by the angels, art now willingly crucified by lawless men, O Son? I hymn Thee, O longsuffering One!

*Ode 4, Tone 5. Heirmos:*[^799]
*I heard the report of the power of the Cross, that paradise hath been opened thereby, and I cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*

*Troparion:*
Having purified thy soul beforehand from the passions, and having received the grace of prophecy through the Holy Spirit, thou didst cry aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
O Prophet Obadiah, illumined with the radiance of light-giving lightnings, enlighten us to cry aloud unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast shown to be an adornment of the bridal chamber of the Church, O all-blessed one, having proclaimed that the Savior should come forth from Zion, unto Whom we cry: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst divinely give birth unto the Word of the Father, co-unoriginate and co-eternal, O pure one, unto Whom we cry: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^800]
*Proclaiming beforehand the coming of Thine appearance upon earth, O Christ God, the prophet cried aloud with joy: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*

*Troparion:*
Having received the Antiochian blessing and the apostolic teaching, O truly glorious one, thou wast a true witness![^801]

*Troparion:*
Having acquired a resolve stronger than fire, and having cast down the madness of the tormentors, thou criest aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Patiently enduring in Christ even unto death, thou didst resist the fire and the torments, singing with a great voice: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Held fast with most fervent zeal, O all-blessed one, thou didst trample down deceit in godly wisdom, singing: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Theotokion:*
The Bodiless One, incarnate of the Virgin, came upon earth unto men; therefore in faith we cry aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Ode 5, Tone 5. Heirmos:*[^802]
*Rising early at dawn, we cry aloud unto Thee, O Lord, save us: for Thou art our God* beside Thee we know none other!

*Troparion:*
Rising early unto the Lord, Thou didst receive from heaven the gift of the All-Holy Spirit, O all-laudable one!

*Troparion:*
Having acquired a divine life as thy companion, thou wast vouchsafed to behold Him Who is understood invisibly!

*Troparion:*
Light shone forth upon thee as a prophet, O all-blessed one, and its consort bestowed joy upon thee!

*Theotokion:*
He Who created all things by His will, the transcendent God, formed from thee that which belongs unto our nature, O all-immaculate one!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^803]
*Thou Who didst make light to dawn, Who didst illumine the morning and show forth the day: Glory to Thee, glory to Thee, O Jesus, Son of God!*

*Troparion:*
Thou hast shown forth unto us a witness of Thy sufferings, crying aloud: Glory to Thee, glory to Thee, O Jesus, Son of God!

*Troparion:*
For thy great endurance, a reward and a crown of victory have been woven for thee as thou criest: Glory to Thee, glory to Thee, O Jesus, Son of God!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst pierce the hearts of the enemy with the arrows of thy words, crying aloud: Glory to Thee, glory to Thee, O Jesus, Son of God!

*Theotokion:*
Acknowledging thee as the holy mountain and the tabernacle of the Most High, O Virgin, we cry aloud: Glory to thee, O Theotokos, our hope!

*Ode 6, Tone 5. Heirmos:*[^804]
*The abyss encompassed me, the sea-monster became my grave; but I cried aloud unto Thee, the Lover of mankind, and Thy right hand saved me, O Lord!*

*Troparion:*
By the power of the Divine Spirit thou didst behold things to come, O prophet, receiving the images of divine appearances as in a mirror by the brightness of thy soul!

*Troparion:*
Entreat the Lord by thy prayers, O all-blessed prophet, asking that forgiveness of transgressions be granted unto those who celebrate thy memory in faith!

*Troparion:*
Be compassionate unto Thy servants, and grant unto them forgiveness of transgressions, O Lover of mankind, having as intercessor Thy prophet who proclaimed Thee unto the world!

*Theotokion:*
He Who upholds all things by His word with divine power is borne in thine arms, O unwedded one. Pray now unto Him, that our souls may be saved!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^805]
*The Prophet Jonah prefigured the three-day burial, praying in the sea-monster: Deliver me from corruption, O Jesus, King of powers!*

*Troparion:*
Let the faces of demons be struck by the fiery right hand, and let the hearts of the faithful leap for joy and let the choirs of the bodiless joyfully make merry!

*Troparion:*
The victories and triumphs of thy noble struggles, and the chosen and light-bearing festival of the firstborn who behold the martyr's labors, are adorned!

*Troparion:*
O good painters, come now, adorn the image of the martyr with your fine arts, fittingly portraying the Master of the contest in him![^806]

*Theotokion:*
The ancestral mother rejoices in thee, O all-hymned Mother of God, having been delivered by thy childbearing from the ancient curse and bitter condemnation of death!

*Kontakion of the Martyr, Tone 2, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ):*[^807]
Thou wast shown to be marvelously strong, and didst offer thyself as a fitting and fragrant whole-burnt sacrifice unto Christ; and having received the crown of honor, O Barlaam, pray ever for us, O passion-bearer!

*Ode 7, Tone 5. Heirmos:*[^808]
*Thou Who didst save the children that hymned Thee in the fiery furnace: Blessed is the God of our fathers!*

*Troparion:*
Supernatural truly is the glory of Thy prophets, O blessed God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Vouchsafed to dwell with God, thou singest: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Thou manifestest Thy divine grace in Thy prophets, O blessed God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Delivered by thy childbearing, O all-immaculate Virgin, we sing: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^809]
*O God of our fathers, put us not to shame, but grant us with boldness to cry aloud unto Thee: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*

*Troparion:*
With the choirs of martyrs, as an unconquered martyr, thou wast vouchsafed to cry aloud unto Christ with a great voice: Blessed is the God of our fathers!`

*Troparion:*
With bright torches thou didst enter into the divine bridal chamber, crying unto Christ, O great martyr: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having acquired a right hand stronger than fire, standing as an advocate at the right hand of thy Master, thou criest: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Delivered by thy most pure childbearing, we the faithful unceasingly sing unto thee, crying: Blessed, O all-immaculate one, is the Fruit of thy womb!

*Ode 8, Tone 5. Heirmos:*[^810]
*From the Father* begotten of the Father before the ages, Son and God, and in these latter times incarnate of the Virgin Mother: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Illumined by God, the prophets proclaim the knowledge of future things, crying aloud in godly wisdom: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
As a morning star in the deep, thou didst shine forth upon those in darkness, illumined with divine rays, O proclaimer of God, crying aloud: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
Consubstantial with Thy Father according to the divine essence, Thou wast shown to be of one nature with us, taking flesh of an unwedded Mother. Therefore we sing unto Thee, O Christ, and bless Thee unto all ages!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^811]
*All ye works of God and all creation, bless the Lord: ye venerable and humble in heart, sing unto Him and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*

*Troparion:*
Thou didst overthrow all the armed assault of the enemy, O praiseworthy Barlaam, and didst burn up the deceit of idols, crying aloud: We supremely exalt Thee, O Christ, unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Splendidly adorned, thou didst stand before Christ, O ever-memorable passion-bearer, wearing a purple robe dyed crimson with martyr's blood, and singing unto the Master unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Kindled with the fire of piety, thou didst burn up all demonic illusions like thorns, crying aloud: We supremely exalt Thee, O Christ, unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
Those who bless thee in faith are blessed of the Lord, O all-immaculate one; for thou bearest the Master Who blesses creation, Whom we supremely exalt, O pure one, unto the ages!

*Ode 9, Tone 5. Heirmos:*[^812]
*Thee, the Mother of God beyond mind and word, who ineffably gavest birth in time unto the Timeless One: with one mind, we the faithful magnify!*

*Troparion:*
Adorned with divine word and deed, and borne aloft on wings by the Spirit, O wonderful prophet, thou wast vouchsafed to behold things to come!

*Troparion:*
Dwelling where the prophetic choirs and the splendors of the saints abide: pray unto the Lord to save those who in faith praise thee, O glorious one!

*Troparion:*
Wholly and fervently cleaving unto God, thou didst converse purely through divine visions, which thou now also enjoyest, O all-blessed one!

*Theotokion:*
Thee we hymn as the lamp of the Light, O pure one, thee also the table of grace, having received the incarnate Word knowing that thou didst receive the incarnate Word of God, we magnify Thee!

*Another Heirmos, Tone 4:*[^813]
*A cornerstone was cut out from thee, an uncut mountain, O Virgin, not cut by the hand of man: even Christ, Who joined together the sundered natures. Therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Theotokos!*

*Troparion:*
The law of praises is overcome by the greatness of thy struggles; Christ the Master alone knows how to glorify thee with divine splendor. Fervently entreat Him for those who sing of thee in faith!

*Troparion:*
Having offered thine entire self unto the Lord as a living sacrifice, Thou wast shown to be wholly an heir and partaker of His kingdom, and rejoicing with Him, Thou now reignest, O ever-memorable one!

*Troparion:*
For love of Thee, O Savior, even unto blood and unto death, against the sword, and fire, and torments, the divine martyr set himself in battle array; and having received immortality from Thee, O Lover of mankind, he delights therein!

*Theotokion:*
Rejoicing, I set thee forth, the protectress of the world and Virgin Mother of God, as the advocate and salvation of my whole life; for having given birth unto God, thou art able to save those who hymn thee!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "While the disciples looked on" (Оу҆ченикѡ́мъ зрѧ́щымъ):*[^814]
O Prophet Obadiah, dance and be glad, beholding the fulfillment of thy sayings! Therefore, as thou standest before the Trinity, remember those who celebrate thy light-bearing memory and honor thee, O all-blessed one!

*Theotokion:*
Beholding God the Word, Who ineffably came forth from thy most pure loins, crucified, O Virgin Mother, thou didst cry aloud: Glory to Thine ineffable dispensation, O my Savior, whereby Thou savest Thy world!

*Service of our Venerable Fathers, the Desert-Dwellers who shone forth in fasting, Barlaam and Joasaph, in the great land called India.*

*At Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having set aside all" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*[^815]

*Sticheron 1:*
From a royal root, a most fair branch grew up, a sweet-smelling lily: the blessed Prince Joasaph, who, through the instruction of the spiritual guide, desiring to see the priceless pearl, came to know God Who is glorified in the Trinity, and was shown to be an excellent doer of His commandments. And now, dancing in the heights, he prays for our souls!

*Sticheron 2:*
Barlaam, enlightened in soul, said unto Prince Joasaph: Thou hast known God the Creator of all; may He enlighten thine inward eyes and grant thee the spirit of wisdom and understanding, that thou mayest know what is the hope of His calling; for in the end, thou shalt be a guide unto salvation for thy father also. But I may not remain here, but depart on my way, having God as my guide, Who leads me unto salvation!

*Sticheron 3:*
When the noble Prince Joasaph heard the words concerning departure, weeping bitterly in soul and bathing his face with tears, he said: O spiritual teacher, mediator of all my good things, wilt thou leave me again in this world? Who shall bring to completion for me thy manner of teaching? Who shall be my guide unto salvation? Thou hast brought me unto God, and hast guided me into the rank of the adoption of a guide, and through thee I hope to receive great mercy from Christ!

*Glory... Tone 6:*
When Zardan learned with certainty of the teacher's diligent care for the youth and his conversion unto Christ, his soul was filled with many sorrows, and he took upon himself great affliction. In no wise able to hide it, he related everything in detail unto the king, and named the name of Barlaam, saying: He hath deceived thy son! And the king roared like a lion in fury, and all but tasted of death; but Joasaph prayed unceasingly, calling upon the Savior of our souls!

*Now and ever... Theotokion, Tone 6, Dogmatikon:*
*Who will not call thee blessed*[^816] *Entrance. The Prokeimenon of the day. And the Readings:*

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 3):*[^817]
The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to die, and their departure was accounted an affliction, and their going from us destruction; but they are in peace. For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastened, they shall be greatly rewarded; for God proved them, and found them worthy for Himself. As gold in the furnace hath He tried them, and received them as a whole burnt offering. And in the time of their visitation they shall shine forth, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble. They shall judge nations, and have dominion over peoples, and the Lord shall reign over them unto the ages. They that put their trust in Him shall understand the truth, and such as be faithful in love shall abide with Him; for grace and mercy are in His saints, and visitation in His elect.

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 5):*[^818]
The righteous live unto the ages, and their reward is in the Lord, and the care of them is with the Most High. Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of glory, and a crown of beauty from the hand of the Lord; for with His right hand shall He cover them, and with His arm shall He shield them. He shall take to Himself His zeal for complete armor, and make creation His weapon to avenge Him of His enemies. He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, and take true judgment instead of a helmet. He shall take holiness for an invincible shield; His severe wrath shall He sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with Him against the foolish. Then shall the right-aiming thunderbolts go abroad, and from the clouds, as from a well-drawn bow, shall they fly to the mark. And hailstones full of wrath shall be cast as out of a stone-bow, and the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the rivers shall harshly drown them. Yea, a mighty wind shall stand up against them, and like a whirlwind shall it winnow them away; thus iniquity shall lay waste the whole earth, and ill-doing shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty. Hear therefore, O kings, and understand; learn, ye judges of the ends of the earth! Give ear, ye that rule multitudes, and that boast yourselves in the throngs of nations! For dominion is given unto you from the Lord, and sovereignty from the Most High...

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 4):*[^819]
The righteous man, though he happen to die early, shall be in rest for honorable age is not that which stands in length of time, nor that is measured by number of years. But wisdom is the gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is old age. He pleased God, and was beloved of Him; and living among sinners, he was translated. He was taken away, lest wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul. For the fascination of wickedness darkens good things, and the roving of desire undermines the simple mind. Being made perfect in a short time, he fulfilled long years; for his soul was pleasing unto the Lord: therefore He hastened to take him away from the midst of wickedness. This the people saw, and understood it not, neither laid they up such a thing in their mind: that grace and mercy are in His saints, and visitation in His elect.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 8, Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѽ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*[^820]

*Sticheron 1:*
When King Abenner said unto his son: My beloved child, thou hast forsaken the honor of our gods, and hast chosen to serve a foreign God! Why, my child, hast thou done this? I nurtured thee with love, hoping that thou wouldest be the heir of my kingdom; but thou, my child, hast acted thus, having followed what was told thee!

*Verse: The venerable shall boast in glory, and they shall rejoice upon their beds.*[^821]

*Sticheron 2:*
I have rejected demonic darkness, and have run unto the light of the knowledge of God, having forsaken the deceit of idols and drawn near unto the truth, and I have chosen to serve Christ; for He hath abolished our ancient condemnation, and hath raised our nature unto the heavens, and promised the kingdom of heaven unto all that truly love Him!

*Verse: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and from them all shall the Lord deliver them.*[^822]

*Sticheron 3:*
When the king sought to terrify the holy youth with fury and threatening, he said: I shall surrender thee unto many torments, and put thee to death with an evil death, and no longer shall I call thee son, but as an enemy and an apostate! And thus threatening, he departed in anger; but Joasaph, entering into his chamber, prayed unceasingly unto God!

*Glory... Tone 8. Idiomelon:*
In his prayer Prince Joasaph said: O Lord my God, sweet hope, unfailing promise, firm refuge of those who hope in Thee: strengthen me in Thy good confession even unto my final breath; for my soul is kindled with great love for Thee love! Therefore grant me throughout my whole life to suffer all things for Thy name and for Thy confession, and to sacrifice my whole self unto Thee; for Thou alone art the invincible champion and merciful God!

*Now and ever... Theotokion:*
*O unwedded Virgin...*[^823]

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Taught by the spiritual guide to know God, O Prince Joasaph, and enlightened by baptism, thou didst turn the people unto the faith, and having become godfather unto thy father from the font, and having forsaken the kingdom, thou didst reach the wilderness, and didst laboriously contend therein. Pray unto Christ God with thy teacher Barlaam, that our souls may be saved![^824]

*Glory... Now and ever... Resurrectional Theotokion, Tone 4.*

*At Matins, after the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^825]
King Abenner, having received counsel from his friend Arachis, began to seduce Joasaph with flattering and gentle words, embracing and kissing him, saying: O my longed-for child, honor the gray hairs of thy father, and having listened unto my entreaty, offer sacrifice unto the gods; for thus shalt thou receive mercy from them, and length of days, and divine glory, and an unhindered kingdom, and thou shalt receive from them a portion of all good things! *(Twice)*

*Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:*
O all-pure Virgin, Mother of God, heal the grievous passions of my soul, I pray thee, and grant forgiveness of my transgressions, which I have foolishly committed, having defiled both soul and body, wretch that I am! Woe is me! What shall I do in that hour when angels shall separate my soul from my passionate body? Then be thou my helper and most fervent advocate; for I, thy servant, have thee as my hope!

*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Co-unoriginate Word" (Собезначáлное сло́во):*[^826]
Joasaph said unto his father: It is not right to honor the gray hairs of one's father and to dishonor the true God; nor is it fitting, having forsaken the Creator of all creation, to offer sacrifices unto idols; rather it is meet to honor the true God, and to offer sacrifice unto Him alone! *(Twice)*

*Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:*
Before the judgment I now weep for myself, pondering my wicked and grievous deeds, and the depth of transgressions that has held me fast from youth from youth, and which oppresses my mind; but by thy pure protection grant me remission, and vouchsafe me to attain unto undefiled salvation: entreat thy Son and God to grant peace unto the world, and salvation, and great and rich mercy!

*After "Praise ye the name of the Lord," Magnification:*[^827]
We call thee blessed, O venerable father Joasaph, and we honor thy sufferings and labors, wherewith thou didst labor in the confession of Christ!

*Selected Psalm:*
*Blessed is the man that fears the Lord...*[^828]

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3:*
Abenner ceased not to devise the deception of his son; having assembled the orators for a dispute, he said unto them: If ye establish our faith and overthrow the Christian faith, ye shall be glorified; but if ye be vanquished, ye shall be put to death. In like manner Joasaph also said unto Nachor, who pretended to be Barlaam: If thou overcomest the deceitful orators, thou shalt be glorified; but if thou art vanquished, I shall tear out thy heart and tongue with my hands and cast them with the rest of thy members to the dogs for food, so that seeing thee, all may be afraid to deceive the sons of kings! *(Twice)*

*Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion, Tone 3:*
Fervent protectress, firm hope, rampart and protection, and haven of those who flee unto thee, O pure Ever-Virgin...

*Then the Gradual Hymns, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree; and like a cedar in Lebanon shall he be multiplied.[^829]
*Verse: Planted in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God shall they flourish.*

*Let every breath... Verse: Praise God in His saints.*

*Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 40.*[^830]

*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 6:*
O venerable father, into all the earth hath gone forth the sound of thine achievements; therefore in the heavens hast thou found the reward of thy labors: thou didst destroy the hosts of demons and hast attained unto the angelic ranks, whose blameless life thou didst emulate. Having boldness before Christ God, entreat peace for our souls!

*Canon of the Theotokos, with the Heirmos, on 6; and of Saint Joasaph, on 8.*
*Tone 8.*
*Ode 1, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^831]
*Unto Him Who hath shattered wars by His arm, and led Israel through the Red Sea: let us sing unto Him as our Redeemer* and our God; for He hath been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Hearing the words of threatening, Nachor trembled greatly; for instead of subversion he uttered a blessing, refuting the Jews and the Greeks; and he proclaimed upon earth the coming of Christ, for He hath been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Nachor set forth the sayings concerning the law; and the orators and priests were put to shame and were found voiceless; while Prince Joasaph rejoiced in soul and glorified the true God, for He hath been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Prince Joasaph said unto Nachor: I confess gratitude unto thee, for truly thou hast been a champion; and if thou wilt love Christ, thou shalt inherit life: for unto those who turn unto Him, He opens the heavenly gates!

*Troparion:*
Though unworthily I have brought thee such an abundance of words, O divinely-wise Prince Joasaph, receive these with love, and offer supplication unto the Mother of God for me, that I may find mercy in the day of the dread examination!

*Troparion:*
Having instructed Nachor with gracious words, he with weeping and joy reached the wilderness, was converted unto the faith, and was enlightened by baptism; and instead of a wolf, he was found to be a sheep of Christ!

*Troparion:*
Theudas said unto King Abenner: Fear not, O king, the so-called wise men; for these shall quickly fall away, and shall not be able to stand before my face, nor to speak contrary words!

*Troparion:*
They brought adorned maidens to serve the king's son, that they might seduce the righteous youth; but though he felt carnal burning in his heart, by prayer and fasting he was delivered from that snare!

*Theotokion:*
Encompassed by many temptations, from the depth of my heart I cry unto thee: O Theotokos, deliver me, thy worthless servant, from cruel distresses, and grant stillness unto my heart!

*Katavasia: I shall open my mouth...*[^832]

*Ode 3, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^833]
*My heart is established in the Lord, my horn is exalted in my God; my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies, I rejoice in Thy salvation!*

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 3:*
The pure and blameless soul of the divine youth feared not the array of the enemy; manfully strengthening himself for the contest, asking deliverance from on high, that he might not defile the garment which he received from holy baptism, so that he might attain unto the beauty and glory of Christ! *(Twice)*

*Glory* Now and ever... Theotokion, Tone 3:*
Whithersoever one is being saved, thither does he rightly flee; and what other refuge is such as thee, O Theotokos, who shelterest our souls!

*Ode 4, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^834]
*The Prophet Habakkuk foresaw with noetic eyes Thy coming, O Lord; therefore he also cried aloud: God shall come from Theman! Glory to Thy power; glory to Thy condescension!*

*Troparion:*
When he had afflicted his body with fasting and prayer, he beheld in a dream a most fair pasture, and the inconceivable beauty of a city; and in one corner he desired to abide, and heard a voice: For those who contend are these things prepared!

*Troparion:*
Having passed by those bright places, he beheld a place full of darkness, and a furnace roaring with a dread flame, and a voice saying: This is the torment for sinners, who have defiled themselves by foul deeds!

*Troparion:*
Lying upon his bed, awakened from the vision, he poured forth tears like rivers; and being wholly seized with fear, he pondered within himself: How bright is the recompense for the righteous, and how dread the torment for sinners! And he cried aloud unto Christ: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Theotokion:*
Carrying in thine arms God Who holds all things in His hand, O all-blessed Virgin: having borne Him as a virgin, even after childbearing thou didst remain a virgin!

*Ode 5, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^835]
*O Lord our God, grant us peace; O Lord our God, possess us; O Lord, beside Thee we know none other, we call upon Thy name!*

*Troparion:*
Thy son is unwell, they told the king; and he quickly ran, and in tender compassion asked: What hath befallen thee, my beloved son, solace of my old age? Why art thou lying thus upon thy bed, conversing with no one?

*Troparion:*
Thou hast laid a snare for my feet; my soul would well-nigh have dwelt in hades, had not the Lord helped me and shown me the way unto salvation: and no longer wouldest thou have been able to see me alive, and to call me thy son!

*Troparion:*
Weaving weeping and sorrow with bitter lamentation, having an unquenchable turmoil, the king said within himself: Child, not only dost thou depart from the gods, but thou dost even renounce thy life!

*Theotokion:*
Having ineffably conceived God, and given birth unto Him beyond nature: entreat Him, O all-immaculate one, that He may have mercy on one corrupted by inappropriate deeds, according to His ineffable mercy!

*Ode 6, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^836]
*As the waters of the sea, O Lover of mankind, I am tossed by the waves of this life. Therefore like Jonah I cry unto Thee: Bring up my life from corruption, O compassionate Lord!*

*Troparion:*
To be delivered from standing on the left hand, and to desire to be vouchsafed the standing on the right hand: thus Joasaph spoke the truth, and to honor nothing more than the love of Christ; for this is true sweetness and joy, and an eternal abode!

*Troparion:*
The sorcerer Theudas said: Why hast thou departed from the gods and angered the king, thy father? For this reason thou art hated by all people: did not the gods, having heard the prayers of thy father, grant thee unto him?

*Troparion:*
Prince Joasaph cried aloud: O depth of delusion, Babylonian seed, grandchild of Babel's tower-building, wretched sorcerer elder! Why wilt thou steal away the saving proclamation of the coming of Christ, with Whose glory heaven and all the earth are filled?

*Theotokion:*
Help, O Theotokos, and give ear unto my word, O all-immaculate one, which from the depth of my soul I offer unto thee, and grant me remission of debts!

*Kontakion, Tone 8:*[^837]
Knowing thy good purpose from infancy, O Joasaph, God, the only Knower of hearts, Who brought thee from an earthly kingdom into the monastic habitation, vouchsafed thee to follow the great Barlaam. And now, having the all-radiant heavenly Jerusalem as thy fatherland with him, delightfully enjoying the desired beauty of the Holy Trinity: we pray thee, O adornment of churches, remember us who honor thee in faith!

*Ikos:*
A second physician and protector hast thou been shown to be, O father, for those seized with the affliction of disease, O marvelous Joasaph, healing all the faithful who run beneath thy divine protection. Therefore thou hearest from us: Rejoice, root of a good father! Rejoice, branch of a good mother! Rejoice, thou that didst cast aside their love! Rejoice, thou that didst receive the only God! Rejoice, for thou didst leave warfare upon earth! Rejoice, for thou didst cast down barbarian pride! Rejoice, thou that wast a rampart and guardian of kings! Rejoice, for thou wast shown to be a weapon and pillar of the world! Rejoice, thou that didst burn up paganism with fire! Rejoice, candlestick shining with wonders! Rejoice, unto the naked a manifold covering, rejoice, deliverer of the captive! Remember us who honor thee in faith!

*Ode 7, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^838]
*The Chaldean furnace, kindled with fire, was bedewed by the Spirit through the presence of God; the children sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*

*Troparion:*
Dividing the glory and the kingdom and all dominion in two: leaving one part to himself, he entrusted the other unto his son, appointing him king. Having assigned him many princes and generals, he graciously and honorably sent him forth unto his land!

*Troparion:*
Not simply did he go unto his kingdom, but they carried the precious Cross before him; and having entered into the city, he set up the sign of the Cross upon all pillars, and destroyed the pagan shrines. A most fair church of Christ the Master he erected, and commanded all to gather there; and he himself prayed fervently!

*Troparion:*
He taught all his subjects to believe in Christ; and the exiled fathers, bishops, priests, and monks, he joyfully welcomed; and with his own hands he washed their feet, and provided every care for them, and fervently cried aloud: O supremely glorified God, blessed art Thou!

*Theotokion:*
Of old Jacob prefigured thee; and Isaiah, purified by the coal of the Spirit, foreshadowed that God Emmanuel should be born of thy womb, unto Whom he cried aloud with a great voice: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Ode 8, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^839]
*Thou Who coverest Thy chambers with waters, Who settest the sand as a bound unto the sea, and Who upholdest all things: Thee the sun hymns, Thee the moon glorifies, unto Thee all creation brings a song, as unto the Creator of all unto the ages!*

*Troparion:*
The house of Joasaph was flourishing, while that of Abenner was diminishing; straightway the king by letter summoned his son. And he, quickly coming, converted his father unto the faith; and having become his godfather from the font, he cried aloud with joy: I glorify Thee, O Christ, unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
A most marvelous wonder occurred: a son became father unto his own father! The surrounding lands were enlightened, churches were built, bishops and priests offered sacrifice unto God, singing a hymn and glorifying Christ unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
By the grace of the Lord King Abenner rejoiced, and surrendered all royal power unto his son; and he himself remained in silence, placing himself in such a depth of humility, that even the ancients he surpas- sed in true piety; and he glorified Christ unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*
We have no other help save thee, O Lady; thou art our strength and confirmation; thou art the boast and rejoicing and guardian of the world: fleeing unto thee, we are all saved.

*Ode 9, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^840]
*Thee, the unwedded Mother of the Most High God, Thee, who beyond understanding hast by the Word given birth unto the true God, higher than the most pure powers, with unceasing doxologies we magnify.*

*Troparion:*
Some days after his baptism, King Abenner straightway fell into bodily infirmity; and when the end of his life began to draw near, in good confession, with warm tears, he surrendered his soul.

*Troparion:*
With joyful tears the son honored his father; he did not adorn him with royal robes, but covered his body with simple apparel. Standing over the grave, lifting up his hands, he sent up thanksgiving unto God, Who had received him in repentance.

*Troparion:*
Unto the people he said, as he sat upon the royal throne: My father King Abenner died as one of the poor; nothing followed him, neither riches nor royal glory. Choose therefore for yourselves whom ye wish, that he may reign over you!

*Theotokion:*
The ladder of Jacob, whereon of old he saw the angels descending; the overshadowed mountain, from which a stone was cut without hands; and the heavenly gate, through which the Lord alone passed, bearing the God of the living: thou alone art, O Most Pure!

*Exapostilarion:*
Forsaking the kingdom, thou didst hasten unto the wilderness; and dwelling in the hut of a poor man, stripping off thy royal robe, thou gavest it unto the poor, and showing forth uttermost almsgiving, thou didst follow Christ.

*Theotokion:*
Fleeing unto thy temple, we cry aloud unto thee, O Most Pure: Grant us help and deliverance from dire afflictions, that we may ever magnify thy childbearing.

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having set aside all" (Все отложше):*
*Written at Vespers.*

*Glory, Tone 6:*
Venerable fathers, into all the earth went forth the proclamation of your righteous deeds; therefore in the heavens ye found the reward of your labors: ye destroyed the demonic legions and attained unto the angelic ranks, whose life ye blamelessly emulated. Having boldness before Christ God, entreat peace for our souls our souls!

*Both now:*
*Theotokos, thou art the true vine...*

*The Great Doxology.*
*And the Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes, Odes 3 and 6.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* The righteous man shall be glad in the Lord, and shall hope in Him.[^841]
*Verse:* Hear, O God, my voice, when I make supplication unto Thee.[^842]
*Epistle to the Colossians, §258 [Col. 3:12–16].*
*Alleluia, Tone 5:* The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them.[^843]
*Verse:* Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and out of them all the Lord will deliver them.[^844]
*Gospel according to Matthew, §55 from the half [Matt. 11:27–30].*
*Communion Verse:* In everlasting remembrance shall the righteous be.[^845]

*In the same month, on the 20th day: The Forefeast of the Entry into the Temple of the Most Holy Theotokos; and our Venerable Father Gregory the Decapolite; and our Father among the Saints Proclus, Archbishop of Constantinople.*

*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Forefeast, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the ranks of heaven" (Небесныхъ чиновъ):*[^846]
The torch-bearing virgins, brightly escorting the Ever-Virgin, * truly prophesy in the Spirit that which is to come; * for being the temple of God, the Theotokos * is led into the temple with virginal glory, * being yet an infant.

The fruit of the holy promise and most glorious, * the Theotokos in truth was revealed unto the world * as higher than all; * who, being piously brought into the temple of God, * fulfills the vow of her parents, * being preserved by the Divine Spirit.

Nourished with heavenly bread, O Virgin, * faithfully in the temple of the Lord, * thou gavest birth unto the world's Bread of Life, the Word; * unto Whom, as an elect and all-immaculate temple, * thou wast mystically betrothed by the Spirit, * espoused unto God the Father.

*Stichera of the Venerable Father, Tone 1, Podoben: The same:*
Into the heavenly mansions with rejoicing thou didst make thy dwelling, * and standing with the angels, O father, * boldly before the throne of the Lord: * pray that forgiveness of sins and passions be granted * unto those who celebrate thy memory on earth!

With the sickle of prayer, O father Gregory, * cutting down the thorns of passions, * and having tilled the soil of thy soul with the plow of abstinence, * thou didst cast into it the seeds of piety, * wherewith thou makest the fruits of healing grow for us.

A vessel of virtues we call thee, O venerable one, * as a friend of silence, * a worker of vigilance, * and an example of temperance, * and an unshakable dwelling of prayer, * and a treasury of miracles, * and an intercessor for those who honor thee, O Gregory.

*Glory, Both now, Tone 4:*
Today the temple that contained God, * the Theotokos, is brought into the temple of the Lord, * and Zechariah receives her; * today the Holy of Holies rejoices, * and the angelic choir mystically keeps festival; * with them let us also celebrate today, * and with Gabriel let us cry aloud: * Rejoice, thou who art full of grace, the Lord is with thee, * Who hath great mercy!

*If on Friday evening: Glory, of the Forefeast; Both now, the Dogmatikon of the Tone.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of Saint Proclus, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Далъ еси знаменіе):*[^847]
With the splendor of dogmas * and the beauty of life * thou didst piously adorn the sacred hierarchy, O ever-memorable Proclus; * and thou wast truly revealed as a pillar of the Church, * enlightening all with thy words. * Therefore we call thee blessed, * and in psalms and hymns * celebrate thy holy and all-honorable memory.

*Verse:* Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*[^848]
Brightly didst thou teach, * and godly-mindedly didst thou preach the all-pure Maiden, the Theotokos, * who gave birth unto Him Who is before the ages, * the Creator and Master, * the Son and Word of the Father, * Who in the last times became man for our sake by His own will, * immutable in nature; * and thou didst put to shame Nestorius, * as impious and utterly foolish.

*Verse:* Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice.*[^849]
Thou didst draw forth the waters * of the wise proclaimer of God radiant with gold,[^850] O ever-memorable one, * whose successor in piety and on the throne thou wast shown to be, * strengthening the flock of Christ with the teachings of truth; * and his most honorable and divinely honored relics, * as the adornment of the church, thou didst restore unto the church.

*Glory, Both now, Tone 4. Idiomelon:*
Come, all ye faithful, let us praise the only immaculate one, * foretold by the prophets, * and into the temple brought into the temple, * who before the ages was fore-ordained to be the Mother, * and in the last years was revealed as the Theotokos. * O Lord, by her prayers grant us Thy peace * and great mercy!

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
O God of our fathers, Who dealest ever with us according to Thy meekness, take not away Thy mercy from us, but by their prayers direct our life in peace!

*Glory, Both now, of the Forefeast, the same Tone:*
Joy doth Anna pre-betroth unto all today, having brought forth the fruit contrary to sorrow, the only Ever-Virgin; whom she also brings, fulfilling her vows today, rejoicing into the temple of the Lord, as the true temple of God the Word and pure Mother.

*It should be known that if the Forefeast of the Entry of the Most Holy Theotokos falls on a Sunday:*
*On Saturday at Small Vespers, the Sunday stichera, and of the Theotokos, as usual.*
*At Great Vespers: After the usual Kathisma, on "Lord, I have cried", 3 Sunday stichera, 1 Anatolian, 3 of the Forefeast, and 3 of the Venerable Gregory. Glory, of the Forefeast; Both now, the 1st Theotokion of the Tone. At the Litya, as usual. At the Aposticha, the Sunday stichera. Glory, Both now, of the Forefeast. At the Blessing of the Loaves, the Troparion: "O Theotokos Virgin, rejoice", 3 times.*
*Note: If there is no Vigil, we say the Sunday Troparion; Glory, of Gregory, Tone 3:*
An example of temperance thou wast, having enlightened all with the Divine Spirit; thou didst finish the course of thy good struggle, by thy teaching thou didst enlighten the world, and didst rebuke the minds of the ill-believing, O venerable father Gregory: entreat Christ God to grant us great mercy!
*Both now, of the Forefeast.*

*At "God is the Lord", the Sunday Troparion twice; Glory, of Gregory; Both now, of the Forefeast. After the Kathismata, the Sunday Sessional Hymns and their Theotokia. Then the Polyeleos, and the Troparia "The Angelic Assembly"; Litany; Hypakoe of the Tone; Hymns of Ascent; the Sunday Prokeimenon and Gospel, and the rest up to the Canon. After Ode 3, the Kontakion of the Forefeast and the Ikos; and the Kontakion of Gregory; Glory, his Sessional Hymn; Both now, of the Forefeast. After Ode 6, the Sunday Kontakion and Ikos* and Ikos. *At Ode 9 we sing "More honorable". The Sunday Exapostilarion; Glory, of Gregory; Both now, of the Forefeast. At the Praises, 4 Sunday stichera; and 3 model stichera of the Forefeast, written at the Aposticha; and their Idiomelon with the refrains; Glory, the Gospel Sticheron; Both now, "Most blessed art thou"; the Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Sunday Troparion only; Litanies and dismissal; and the First Hour. At the First Hour, the Sunday Troparion; Glory, of the Forefeast; Both now, the Theotokion of the Hours.
