Then the Troparion of Gregory; the Sunday Kontakion, and of the temple; Glory, of Gregory; Both now, of the Forefeast. The Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Verse, first of Sunday, and then of the Saint. Service of a Venerable Monk.*

*The service of Saint Proclus is sung when the Ecclesiarch decides.*

*Troparion of Proclus, Tone 4:*
Established by the divine beginning of wisdom, the fear of the Lord, thence by sacred ascents thou didst ascend unto discipleship under Chrysostom; and having been made worthy of his archiepiscopal throne by the beauties of purity, having fashioned thyself according to the apostolic rule, living not for thyself, but for Christ and thy flock; therefore thou didst enter into incorruptible life in an apostolic manner, O Hierarch Proclus: entreat Christ God to save our souls!

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord", the Troparion of the Forefeast, twice; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, of the Forefeast.*

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph marveled" (Удивися Іосифъ):*[^851]
Before conception thou wast sanctified unto God, O pure one, and having been born upon earth, thou art now brought as a gift unto Him, fulfilling the parental promise. In the divine temple, as being the divine temple, from infancy purely given over with bright candles, thou wast revealed as the receptacle of the unapproachable and divine Light. Great in truth is thy procession, O only Bride of God and Ever-Virgin!
*Glory Both now, the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, and the Podoben the same:*
The temple of God, the most precious bridal chamber, goes forth with bright candles to dwell with rejoicing in the temple of God; and Zechariah rejoices over her, seeing the revelation of the sacred prophets clearly fulfilled, and he makes glad, and sings the forefestal song: Thy going forth proclaims joy, O Virgin Maiden!
*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*Canon of the Forefeast with its Heirmos on 6; and both Canons of the Saints on 8.*
*Canon of the Forefeast.*
*Whose acrostic is by the alphabet up to the Seventh Ode; likewise also the Eighth has its own verses; and the Ninth is by Joseph.*
*Ode 1, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^852]
*I will open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I will utter a word unto the Queen and Mother; and I will be seen radiantly keeping festival, and rejoicing I will hymn her wonders.*

*Troparion:*
Into the Holy of Holies the all-holy and immaculate one goes forth to dwell, that she may become the consecrated temple of the all-holy God; and virgins, young maidens, go before her.

*Troparion:*
The pre-eternal counsel of our pre-eternal God comes unto fulfillment, foreordaining thee to be reared in the Holy of Holies, as a dwelling for the Word, O all-immaculate Maiden.

*Troparion:*
The godly parents, seeing that thou art to become the Mother of God, bring thee to be reared in the Holy of Holies, fulfilling the vow of the prayer wherewith they prayed, O Most Pure!

*Theotokion:*
Strengthen, O Lady, the weakness of my heart, and establish that which is shaken by passions, that in faith and love I may bless thee, who art ever-blessed and all-immaculate.

*Another Canon, of the Venerable Gregory, Tone 8. The Work of Joseph.*
*Ode 1, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^853]
*The wonder-working staff of Moses, striking the sea crosswise and dividing it, once drowned the chariot-driving Pharaoh, while saving Israel, the fugitive traveler on foot, as he sang a hymn unto God.*

*Troparion:*
My humble soul, deadened by bodily pleasures, enliven by thy prayers, O blessed Gregory; for thou hast now received the life that grows not old, having put to death thy earthly members, O venerable one, by fasting labors.

*Troparion:*
Restraining bodily pleasures by the purity of thy mind, from young years, O father, thou wast an instrument of the Spirit, brightly receiving His operations, and being recognized as God-seeing.

*Troparion:*
With divine desire thou didst wither the desires of the flesh, and for thyself, O blessed one, thou didst betroth purity as thy spouse, from whom all the virtues were born unto thee, O ever-glorious one, making thee a child of God.

*Theotokion:*
The heavenly ladder reaching from earth unto the heavens, whereby God the Word descended unto those on earth, O blessed and all-pure one: an ineffable wonder, an incomprehensible sight, save those who flee unto thee!

*Another Canon of Saint Proclus, Tone 4. The Work of Theophanes.*
*Ode 1, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^854]
*Thy victorious right hand was divinely glorified in strength; for it, O Immortal One, as all-powerful, shattered the adversaries, fashioning a new path through the deep for the Israelites.*

*Troparion:*
In deed and truthful word, thou wast conformed unto the spiritual archangels, O God-receiver, and standing with them before the throne of the Honorable Trinity, Whom do thou entreat, O Proclus, to save us.

*Troparion:*
Clearly following in the footsteps of Chrysostom,[^855] O all-blessed and ever-memorable one, thou didst take up the divine vesture of his priesthood as a paternal inheritance, O worthy of glory!

*Troparion:*
That God came down to earth of old, unconfusedly in the Spirit, Nestorius with damaged mind proposes slander against His Incarnation; but he is synodally cast down by thee, O thrice-blessed one!

*Theotokion:*
With divinely-inspired words thou didst clarify the awesome Incarnation of God the Word from the Virgin, and didst proclaim her to be the Theotokos, following the all-wise dogmas of the apostles.

*Canon of the Forefeast.*
*Ode 3, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^856]
*O Theotokos, thou living and plentiful fountain, spiritually establish thy singers united in choir, and in thy divine glory vouchsafe them crowns of glory.*

*Troparion:*
Virgins, young maidens, leading the way, bearing candles brightly, prefigure that which is to come; for from her shall be born the illumination of knowledge, dissolving the darkness of deception.

*Troparion:*
Emulating of old with godly wisdom, Anna fulfills her prayer; and she brings thee unto the sanctuary, O all-immaculate one, who wast to have a most sacred conception and childbearing.

*Troparion:*
The sun stretched forth its rays, beholding the radiant cloud spread forth by divine bidding, into the Holy of Holies, from which she shall rain down forgiveness upon those held fast by passions.

*Theotokion:*
God, Who dwelt within thee in His tender compassion, O all-immaculate and pure one, deifies me who was of old stolen away by food through the deceit of the serpent, and in place of corruption He gives back the food of incorruption.

*Canon of the Venerable Gregory.*
*Ode 3, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^857]
*O Lord, Craftsman of the celestial vault and Builder of the Church: do Thou establish me in Thy love, O summit of desires, confirmation of the faithful, O only Lover of mankind.*

*Troparion:*
Having ascended the mountain of virtues, O venerable one, thou didst enter into the darkness of vision; and having perceived as much as thou couldst contain of Him Who is incomprehensible in nature, thou becamest filled with illumination, O father.

*Troparion:*
He Who was born in a cave for the salvation of earthly men, illuminated thee of old, O all-blessed one, when thou wast living in a cave, with heavenly light as Paul, showing thee to be radiant with light, O father Gregory!

*Troparion:*
The invisible door, the all-pure Mother of Christ, gave thee wings, O father, when thou wast surrounded by demonic assaults; and through the grace of the Spirit she made thee mighty in power against them.

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, thou who alone gavest birth unto the Lord of the blessed; rejoice, thou who hast mediated life for men; rejoice, overshadowed and uncut mountain, confirmation of the faithful; rejoice, O all-immaculate one!

*Canon of Saint Proclus.*
*Ode 3, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^858]
*O Thou Who alone knowest the weakness of human nature, and in Thy compassion hast taken form therein: gird me with power from on high, that I may cry aloud unto Thee, O Holy One: O living temple of Thine ineffable glory, O Lover of mankind!*

*Troparion:*
Receiving light from Light in godly manner, O all-blessed one, thou becamest the light of the Church; therefore also divine light shone upon thee spiritually, even as it is written; enlightened whereby, thou illuminest those who sing of thy memory.

*Troparion:*
With the thunderous sharpness of dogmas, as walls thou didst cast down all the bold assaults of the Jericho-like heresies, and didst establish the highest victory, clearly proclaiming the divine Incarnation from the Virgin.

*Troparion:*
Applying thy lips unto the fountain of wisdom, O God-receiver, thou didst draw forth the divine waters of spiritual wisdom, O Proclus, drowning the muddy torrents of Nestorius's godless opinions, O all-blessed one!

*Theotokion:*
He Who on high is the only-begotten Son, ineffably understood with the Father understood, the Only-begotten Son was born below of thee, O Most Pure, beyond cause and understanding, and He deifies man, O most pure Sovereign Theotokos: therefore we glorify thee.

*Kontakion of Gregory, Tone 3:*
The Church knows thee as a bright sun, enlightening all with the beauties of virtues and the rays of healings, O pleasing servant of Christ; therefore we celebrate thy venerable memory and honor thy struggles, O all-blessed and all-wise father Gregory!

*Kontakion of Proclus, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared" (Явился еси):*[^859]
Worthily today doth the most honorable of all cities truly keep festival at thy venerable translation, O father of fathers, wise Proclus!

*Sessional Hymn of Gregory, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou didst quickly anticipate" (Скоро предвари):*[^860]
Illuminated by divine splendor, thou didst banish the darkness of soul-corrupting passions, O all-wise Gregory, being taken up unto the purest height of dispassion; thou didst shine forth gloriously with the dawn of healings, having taken up thy dwelling in the unwaning light of Christ's Kingdom.

*Glory, of Proclus, Tone 3, Podoben: "Of the divine faith" (Божественныя веры):*[^861]
Having become a divine sacred preacher, thou didst enrich the Church with divine teachings, O all-praised mystagogue, and didst proclaim the all-pure Virgin to be the Theotokos, and didst put Nestorius to shame. Therefore we all faithfully honor thy memory, asking to receive great mercy.

*Both now, of the Forefeast, Tone 1, Podoben: "The stone having been sealed" (Камени запечатану):*[^862]
Praise, ye virgins! Keep the forefeast, ye mothers! Doxologize, ye peoples! Bless, ye priests, the all-pure Mother of God! For being yet an infant in the flesh, she was of old brought into the temple as the most holy temple of God. Therefore, celebrating a spiritual feast, let us sing unto her as the protectress of the human race.

*Canon of the Forefeast.*
*Ode 4, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^863]
*Perceiving the unfathomable divine counsel of Thine Incarnation from a Virgin, O Thou Most High, the Prophet Habakkuk cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*

*Troparion:*
Sacred tongues foreproclaimed thee, O pure one, to be the dwelling-place of the incomprehensible Nature; for this cause the virginal choirs escort thee, bearing candles into the Holy of Holies.

*Troparion:*
Joachim with Anna received glory, walking and bearing thee with rejoicing into the holy temple, O most holy temple of God, pure and all-immaculate Lady!

*Troparion:*
The prophetic utterance is fulfilled; for lo, the vine has budded vine, which bears for us the incorruptible cluster of grapes, pouring forth wine of rejoicing unto the ends of the earth.

*Theotokion:*
Having found thee alone all-immaculate, the Word and Creator dwelt within thy womb, working our salvation by grace, O Most Pure, according to His ineffable mercy.

*Canon of the Venerable Gregory.*
*Ode 4, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^864]
*Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power, Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who leaving not the bosom of the Father hast visited our poverty; therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry aloud unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!*

*Troparion:*
For the sake of those who are estranged by alien descent, O Gregory, thou becamest a stranger by goodness; for this cause He, seeing thee become a stranger from thy homeland, received thee and made thee a divine heir of His Kingdom, adorned with virtues.

*Troparion:*
For the sake of Christ Who became an infant for our sake and a child, O venerable one, thou didst give thyself over unto the school of children, having become an infant in malice, O godly-wise father; and by divine humility thou didst humble the malice of the enemy, O blessed Gregory!

*Troparion:*
With torrents of thy tears, O father Gregory, watered as by divine dew, thou didst rear every virtue and make every good fruit of righteousness bloom, like a fruitful tree planted by the streams of waters of perfect asceticism.

*Theotokion:*
O blessed and all-immaculate Mother of God, heal the wounds of my soul, calm carnal pleasures, enlighten my darkened heart, pacify my mind, and deliver me from all harm and from the assaults of the enemy.

*Canon of Saint Proclus.*
*Ode 4, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^865]
*Habakkuk, having perceived with prophetic eyes thee as the mountain overshadowed by the grace of God, foreproclaimed that from thee should go forth the Holy One of Israel, for our salvation and renewal.*

*Troparion:*
The sayings of angels and the melodious thunder of the dogmas of thy teachings wisely make glad the Church of God, driving away heretical ferocity, O divinely revealed Proclus, all-blessed one!

*Troparion:*
As gold in the fire, O most sacred one, having purified thy precious body through abstinence, O wise one, thou didst show it fair unto the Creator; therefore He granted unto thee the vesture of priesthood unto the ages.

*Troparion:*
Having learned divine knowledge, having become a consecrated hierarch, thou didst graciously impart illumination unto all others, and with divine of divine brightness, unto the salvation of souls, O thou who art worthy of praise.

*Theotokion:*
Having received the divine Coal within thy womb beyond understanding, O all-immaculate one, truly thou wast not burned; for from afar the bush prefigured thy childbearing in image, unto our salvation and renewal.

*Ode 5, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^866]
*All things were amazed at thy divine glory; for thou, O Virgin who knewest not wedlock, didst hold in thy womb the God Who is over all, and didst give birth to the timeless Son, granting peace unto all who hymn thee.*

*Troparion:*
Let the clouds drop down righteousness today; for as in heaven, the divine cloud extends into the temple of God, which drops sweetness, taking away all the bitterness of our souls.

*Troparion:*
Strange is thy conception, strange is thy childbearing, strange is thy proceeding, O Virgin, thy bringing into the inner sanctuary. Strange and all-glorious are thy things, surpassing word and thought, O most pure one!

*Troparion:*
The All-Holy Spirit sanctified thee wholly, as thou didst abide within the temple and wast nourished with heavenly food, O all-comely Bride of the Father; therefore thou didst also become the Birthgiver of the Word.

*Theotokion:*
Placing all my hope in thee, O Maiden, I flee unto thy compassions; show my fallen soul to be without share in demonic harm, weakened as it is by the deluges of pleasures.

*Canon of the Venerable Gregory.*
*Ode 5, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^867]
*Why hast Thou cast me away from Thy face, O Never-Setting Light, and a strange darkness hath covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and direct my ways unto the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee!*

*Troparion:*
By the practice of the word, thou wast shown to be a fruitful vine, O venerable father, bearing the ripe and greatest clusters of virtues, which pour forth the spiritual wine of salvation, O father, making glad the hearts of the faithful.

*Troparion:*
Glorious Rome, having received thee in faith from the East as an unsetting luminary, O father, was enlightened by thy precious gifts; for thou didst hold Christ in thy soul as light, illuminating those who behold thee, O father.

*Troparion:*
The crawling serpent that lay in wait for thy heel,[^868] walking in the paths of life with divine vigilance as God's well-pleasing servant, as a doer of Christ's commandments, thou didst put to death by the power of the Spirit.[^869]

*Theotokion:*
O protectress of the world, Mother and Ever-Virgin, guide me, and lead me along the right path, and direct my thought unto the paths of righteousness, guiding aright the goings of my soul.

*Canon of Saint Proclus.*
*Ode 5, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^870]
*O Christ, Who hast enlightened the ends of the world with the brightness of Thy coming, and hast illumined them with Thy Cross: enlighten the hearts of those who orthodoxly hymn Thee with the light of Thy divine knowledge.*

*Troparion:*
Having become light-bearing as a luminary, O all-blessed one, thou wast shown to be a champion of the divine Church; and thou didst make clear the divine, immutable birth from the all-holy Virgin, O glorious one.

*Troparion:*
Having placed the glorious divine incarnation from the Virgin into the sling of dogmas, as anciently divine David did,[^871] thou didst cast down the fierce disposition of Nestorius as another alien Goliath.

*Troparion:*
Being filled with Paul's teachings, and having seen his vision, O all-chosen one,[^872] thou didst appear as a second Elisha, anointed mystically with divine chrism unto the priesthood.

*Theotokion:*
God, coming forth in flesh from the Virgin's womb, suffered neither alteration nor confusion; but what He was, He remained: God and man, immutably revealed in His operations.

*Ode 6, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^873]
*Celebrating this divine and all-honorable feast of the Mother of God, O ye divinely wise, come, let us clap our hands, and glorify God Who was born of her!*

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by divine grace, the parents of the divine Virgin offer her in love as a spotless dove to be reared in the Holy of Holies.

*Troparion:*
As thou art about to receive the Light proceeding from Light, maidens kindle lamps and go before thee in purity with radiant appearance, keeping festival toward the divine temple.

*Troparion:*
The palace full of glory, the proclamation of the great prophets, the holy throne, is led inside the Holy of Holies, preparing herself for the King of all.

*Theotokion:*
I hymn thy conception, O Maiden, I hymn also thine ineffable childbearing, I hymn also thy protection, by which we are delivered from every harm, who flee unto thy calm haven.

*Canon of the Venerable Gregory.*
*Ode 6, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^874]
*Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray Thee; for unto Thee have I cried, and do Thou give ear unto me, O God of my salvation!*

*Troparion:*
Being deified by action toward God, O most sacred one, by divine operations and divine illuminations, as a divine prophet, as God's well-pleasing servant, thou wast counted worthy of the grace of God.

*Troparion:*
In silence thou didst accomplish thy life, O divinely inspired one; thou didst show thyself greater than worldly turmoils and passions, having become a stranger and a sojourner on all the earth.

*Troparion:*
Like a pure mirror, thou wast enriched with the divine dawn; as a sacred vessel, thou didst adorn the temple on high, O Gregory, and didst enlighten the Church of the firstborn.

*Theotokion:*
O Mary, pure palace, through thy prayers cleanse me who was previously an unclean den of thieves, and show me forth as a holy temple unto Him Who was born of thee.

*Canon of Saint Proclus.*
*Ode 6, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^875]
*The uttermost abyss hath surrounded us, there is none to deliver; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter. Save Thy people, O our God; for Thou art the strength of the weak and their restoration!*

*Troparion:*
Thou didst drive away the champions of heresies that surrounded Christ's flock like wild beasts, with the spiritual rod of thy teachings, O blessed Proclus, and didst direct the flock unto the pasture of Orthodoxy.

*Troparion:*
As another ark, unto the Church of Christ thou didst deliver the body of the all-blessed Golden-Spoken One[^876] through thine instructions, O Proclus, and didst make glad the choirs of the Orthodox by his coming.

*Troparion:*
Having ascended the great cathedra, O venerable one, thou didst adorn it in a manner befitting God with greatest righteous deeds; therefore, coming together, we praise thee, O hierarch, great-minded, glorious Proclus.

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast shown to surpass the Cherubim, O Virgin full of God's grace; for Him Who is borne upon their shoulders, O pure one, thou didst bear in thine embrace; therefore we all ever glorify thee as the Mother of God.

*Kontakion of the Forefeast.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Яви́лся есѝ дне́сь):*[^877]
All the universe is filled with joy today in the auspicious feast of the Mother of God, crying aloud: She is the heavenly tabernacle!

*Ikos:*
The Maker of all, Creator and Master, having inclined Himself through His ineffable tender compassion, solely through His love for mankind, seeing him whom He fashioned with His own hands fallen, took pity on him, and was well pleased to raise up this most divine creation; and by His emptying since He is God by nature and merciful; therefore He accepts Mary as Mediatress, and as a Virgin and the pure sanctuary of the mystery, from her He willed to bear our nature: She is the heavenly tabernacle!

*Ode 7, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^878]
*The divinely wise worshipped not the creature rather than the Creator, but valiantly trampling down the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of the fathers!*

*Troparion:*
The holy temple receives thee as the light-bearing sun shining the dawn of salvation within unto the ends of the earth, O pure one, who art to be the temple of the Son of God, O Virgin.

*Troparion:*
Let us all clap our hands, beholding the Virgin who knewest not wedlock bearing the types of redemption; for she is nourished by an angel's hand, as one who is ineffably to bring forth the Heavenly Bread for us.

*Troparion:*
All the souls of the righteous beneath the earth have proclaimed thee the good tidings, O golden dove, bringing rest, prefiguring the spiritual deluge, as thou devoutly keepest festival in the Holy of Holies.

*Theotokion:*
Fair as thou art, thou didst bring forth the Comely One Who restores our deformity unto the first image, O all-immaculate Maiden, unto Whom we also sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord and God of the fathers!

*Canon of the Venerable Gregory.*
*Ode 7, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^879]
*Before God's condescension the fire was ashamed in Babylon of old; therefore the children in the furnace, dancing with joyful step as in a meadow of flowers, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*

*Troparion:*
By outpourings of tears thou didst quench the fire of sin, and the water of dispassion and the pure drink of healings thou pourest forth unto those who hymn thee, O Gregory: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Borne upon the fiery chariot of precious love by perfection, thou didst ascend unto the heights, where thou didst obtain thy divinely wise life, crying aloud: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst put to sleep the surge of passions by vigilant standpoints; and having fallen asleep with a sleep resembling that of the righteous, thou didst pass unto the never-waning light, crying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Having become dead through sin and perishing, O pure Virgin who didst bear Life, quicken and save me, and snatch me from Gehenna, as I sing: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Canon of Saint Proclus.*
*Ode 7, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^880]
*Thee, the spiritual furnace, O Mother of God, do we the faithful contemplate; for just as the Highly Exalted One saved the three children* so He wholly renewed the world within thy womb: the praised and supremely glorified God of the fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having cleansed body, mind, and soul by the removal of passions, O hierarch, wise Proclus, from then on thou didst dogmatize that God, born of the Virgin without alteration, received body, soul, and mind in order to save us.

*Troparion:*
Having gained boldness before Christ, O holy one, pray that those on earth who praise thy glorious memory with hymns may be delivered from all assaults, singing unto the praised, all-glorious God.

*Troparion:*
Having kindled spiritual fire in thy thoughts, thou didst burn up the brushwood-like and rotten heresy of impious Nestorius; therefore we pray thee: through thy supplications unto God, burn up and cleanse our brushwood-like pleasures, O glorious one.

*Theotokion:*
Thou bearest God clothed in flesh upon thine arms, O pure one, as the Cherubic Throne, Him Who upholds all things by the word of His power; unto Whom we sing, rejoicing: O all-hymned and supremely glorified God of the fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Ode 8, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^881]
*Give ear, O Maiden, pure Virgin; let Gabriel speak the ancient, true counsel of the Most High: Be ready for God's reception; for through thee the Incomprehensible hath dwelt with men; therefore rejoicing I cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*

*Troparion:*
Give ear and understand, O prudent elder, Anna says unto Zechariah: By divine counsel, receive with a valiant soul the pure Maiden whom I have; for through her shall redemption come; and lead her into the holy temple, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Blessed is the Lord alone, cried aloud the priest: They now manifestly reveal unto us the entrances of life, the chamber capable of containing God, into which Christ, the King of divine things, is about to dwell; unto Whom all the earth cries: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Behold, O wisest elder, Anna said reverently: Receive radiantly the most virtuous Maiden whom God hath given me, and prophesy of her who alone in deed is about to fulfill the preachings; and with them crying aloud prophetically: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Now have I known most manifestly, O woman, wisely said the elder The Tree grows in the midst of the temple, which shall blossom with divine Fruit, bringing into Paradise those who through corruptible food were cast out, unto those who cry with joy: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Thy soul, O pure Maiden, shall manifestly become the teacher of ineffable words, the elder clearly said: Into this divine temple, O Virgin, shalt thou dwell; for nourished by an angel, thou shalt give birth to the Angel of Great Counsel, unto Whom we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
We joyfully sing unto thee, O pure Maiden, the greeting of Gabriel: Rejoice, the sole cause of the joy of all! Rejoice, cleansing of souls! For thou didst bear our redemption and the fashioning of those who hymn Him: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Canon of the Venerable Gregory.*
*Ode 8, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^882]
*Sevenfold did the Chaldean tyrant frantically kindle the furnace for the godly ones; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried unto the Creator and Redeemer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*

*Troparion:*
Patiently laboring in thy supplications unto God, O all-blessed one, thou didst receive what was asked in faith; for by night as thou wast asleep, an angel appeared unto thee, handing thee a fiery sword that cuts off the passions of the heart, cleansing thee with immaterial fire, and illuminating thee with glory ineffably.

*Troparion:*
Bright as the sun, spiritually thou didst shine forth radiantly with the light of virtues, O Gregory, illuminating the whole earth with the splendors of miracles, and enlightening those who devoutly hymn: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Christ unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Having heard the angelic hymnody while still walking in thy mortal body, O Gregory, by which thou didst manifestly delight thy spiritual senses, and wast known as godlike and radiant, crying aloud, O blessed one: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
Having brought forth the Judge and Lord beyond word, O all-holy one, entreat Him as thy Son: in the hour of judgment, to deliver from condemnation and fire, from unillumined darkness, and from the gnashing of teeth, those who in faith devoutly sing: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Canon of Saint Proclus.*
*Ode 8, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^883]
*The children having come forth from the furnace* shone brighter than gold in the crucible through the beauty of piety, saying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; hymn the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
As in a radiant crucible, O all-glorious one, having cleansed carnal passions through purity, thou didst shine forth unto all like gold, singing: Hymn the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Adorned by the utterance of the organ of thy precious tongue, O blessed one, the Church of God hymns the saving descent upon earth, crying clearly unto all and exclaiming: We supremely exalt Thee, O Christ, unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Truly thou wast shown to be a divine harp uttering proclamation unto those who receive in faith God's saving incarnation toward us, O father, blessed Proclus, crying aloud in faith: Hymn the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
Having preserved the signs of thy virginity unharmed, O Virgin, the Master, God, came forth from thee beyond understanding, in order to save those who cry aloud: Hymn the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^884]
*Let every earthborn mortal leap for joy, enlightened in spirit; and let the nature of immaterial bodiless minds celebrate, honoring the sacred festival of the Mother of God, and let them cry aloud: Rejoice, O all-blessed Mother of God, pure Ever-Virgin!*

*Troparion:*
Behold, the holy mountain of God,[^885] with radiant lamps, proceeds within the Holy of Holies; from her the Stone was cut without hands, which shall crush the altars and idols of demons, and shall make men themselves temples and precious dwelling places.

*Troparion:*
God swore, and now hath He fulfilled it, having given us from the tribe of Judah the Ever-Virgin, whose womb shall rear the Tree of Life that delivers from deadly food those who were guilty of the fall through eating and were defrauded through the serpent's deceit.

*Troparion:*
With radiant lips Anna cried aloud in the temple of God: Unto Thee do I offer the Maiden whom Thou hast given me, O Master; from whom, in Thine ineffable mercy, appearing as a bearer of flesh, Thou shalt save the world which Thou didst create, having magnified her as Thy Mother!

*Troparion:*
Behold, the day of salvation hath dawned for those in the night of fierce evils: The Heavenly Gate, opening the doors of the temple, enters with lamps within the Holy of Holies, to be nourished by holy powers, the holy habitation of God!

*Theotokion:*
Enlighten the eyes of my soul, O pure one who didst bear the Light, lest the deepest darkness of sin overtake me, nor the abyss of despair cover me; but do thou thyself save me and guide me unto the haven of divine desire.

*Canon of the Venerable Gregory.*
*Ode 9, Tone 8. Heirmos:*[^886]
*Every ear trembled at the ineffable condescension of God: how the Most High of His own will came down even unto the flesh, becoming man from the virginal womb; therefore, we the faithful magnify the all-pure Mother of God!*

*Troparion:*
By fasting sweats thou didst quench the coals of sin, and from heaven thou didst manifestly receive grace in the likeness of fire, not consuming, O wise one, but rather dewing, and showing thee strong with might against passions.

*Troparion:*
As a rose in the valleys of fasting didst thou blossom, O father Gregory, and as a fragrant lily; therefore thou pourest forth sweet-smelling myrrh, and thy bones abundantly breathe forth fragrance of life; for thy cheeks were shown to be full, as bowls of spices.[^887]

*Troparion:*
Today with us the assembly of ascetics and venerable ones rejoices, of patriarchs and prophets, in thy memory, O blessed one; the apostles and martyrs feast together with us; with them remember those who faithfully honor thee, O thou who art worthy of wonder!

*Troparion:*
The shrine wherein thy precious and much-suffering body lies pours forth for us the grace of miracles, O father Gregory, sanctifying our souls and bodies, who are enriched through thee and have thee as an advocate and fervent protector.

*Theotokion:*
We the faithful joyfully offer thee Gabriel's salutation: Rejoice, O paradise, who didst sprout forth the Tree of Life! Rejoice, release from the curse, crowning of the martyrs, praise of the venerable, and steadfast foundation of pious men!

*Canon of Saint Proclus.*
*Ode 9, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^888]
*The unburnt burning bush showed forth an image of thy pure childbearing. And now we pray thee to quench the furnace of assaults that rages against us, that we may unceasingly magnify thee, O Mother of God!*

*Troparion:*
Having bypassed types and shadows, and having truly known Christ, being reborn through the bath of baptism, thou wast anointed as a most sacred priest; therefore thou didst also proclaim the Mother of God who gave Him birth.

*Troparion:*
Winged by Chrysostom, O blessed one, and by his holy zeal of faith, thou didst pour forth the deep abyss of thy dogmas, drying up the torrents of heresies by grace.

*Troparion:*
By thy sacred prayers calm the confusion raised against us, and drive away the darkening of assaults and the mistreatment of evil men, since thou hast boldness before the Mother of God and our God.

*Theotokion:*
Surpassing the mind are thy miracles; for thou alone, O Virgin Mother, didst bring forth supernaturally God the Word made flesh, Who by divine will wisely upholds, governs, and preserves all things.

*Exapostilarion of the Venerable Gregory.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "As the disciples were beholding" (Оу҆ченикѡ́мъ зрѧ́щымъ):*[^889]
Thou wast a temple of holiness, O hierarch, and by divine communion thou art now a god and a citizen of Paradise; wherein, unhindered, thou art nourished with the tree of knowledge and incorruptible glory; make remembrance, O wise Gregory, of those who from love praise thee in faith, O sacred father!

*Glory, both now, of the Forefeast.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены̀ оу҆слы́шите):*[^890]
The forefeast day brings us into the temple today, through the all-honorable entrance of the Mother of God Mary, whom angels hymn and men call blessed; and virgins escort her, carrying lamps and rejoicing, into the temple of the Lord.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 1.*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Небе́сныхъ чино́въ):*[^891]
Come, ye faithful, having gathered together, * let us honor with hymns the one all-gloriously born of a barren mother, * the unwedded Mother of the Creator; * and with virgins and lamps let us precede her, * as she enters into the temple, into the Holy of Holies.

*Verse: Virgins shall be brought after her unto the King, her companions shall be brought unto Thee.*[^892]

*Troparion:*
Having gathered various flowers * from the spiritual meadows of the words of the Spirit, * let us joyfully weave a crown of praise for the Virgin, * and worthily offer unto her a forefeast gift!

*Verse: They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing, they shall be led into the King's temple.*[^893]

*Troparion:*
Let the doors of the temple of the Lord be prepared, * and let them be opened, * and let them receive with rejoicing the house of glory, * and the only one who is higher than the heavens, * who became such beyond understanding; * and let them hymn Christ the Savior!

*Glory, both now, Tone 1. By George of Nicomedia:*[^894]
Let heaven above rejoice today, and let the clouds drop down gladness at the exceedingly all-glorious majesties of our God! For lo, the gate that looks toward the east, having been born from a barren fruitlessness according to the promise, and having been dedicated unto God as a dwelling place, is brought today into the temple as an unblemished offering; let David rejoice, strumming on the harp: Virgins (he said) shall be brought after her unto the King, her companions shall be brought: inside the tabernacle of God, inside His mercy seat, to be reared as a dwelling place for Him Who was incorruptibly begotten of the Father before the ages, unto the salvation of our souls!

*In the same month, on the 21st day: The Entry into the Temple of our Most Holy Sovereign Lady, the Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary.*

*At Small Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 1.*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Небе́сныхъ чино́въ):*

Having received from the Lord the Fruit of promise, * Joachim and Anna today led the Mother of God, an acceptable sacrifice, * into the temple; * and Zechariah the great high priest, having blessed her, received her. *(Twice)*

The Holy of Holies * is worthily brought to dwell in the Holy of Holies * as an acceptable sacrifice unto God; * and the virgins, beautifully adorned with virtues, * carrying lamps, led her beforehand unto the Lord as a most sacred vessel.

Let the door of the temple that receives God be opened! * For today Joachim, having received the temple and throne of the King of all, * inside with glory, dedicates unto the Lord * her who was chosen by Him to be His Mother His Mother.

*Glory, and now: Tone 8.*
David proclaimed beforehand concerning thee, O most pure one, foreseeing the sanctification of thy entry into the temple, wherein today the ends [of the earth] celebrate and glorify thee, O all-hymned one; for she who was a virgin before childbearing, and remained incorrupt after childbearing, is the Mother of the Word of life. Today Zechariah rejoices in the temple, receiving thee, O Sovereign Lady; and the Holy of Holies rejoices, receiving thee, the fount of our life! Therefore we also cry aloud unto thee in psalms: Pray for us unto thy Son and our God, to grant us great mercy!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Ye heavenly doors, * receive the Virgin * into the Holy of Holies, * as the undefiled tabernacle * of God the Almighty.

*Verse: Virgins shall be brought after her unto the King, her companions shall be brought unto thee.*[^900]
Ye ranks of virgins, * receive the pure Virgin, * brightly bearing torches, * into the Holy of Holies, * as the Bride of God the King of all.

*Verse: They shall be brought in gladness and rejoicing, they shall be led into the temple of the King.*[^901]
The bridal chamber of God the Word, * dwelling in the Holy of Holies, * receives noetic bread * from the hand * of the divine angel.

*Glory, and now: Tone 2, Podoben: The same.*
The Three-sunned Light, * having embraced thee with fire, O Theotokos, * in the temple of glory, * sends thee heavenly food, * magnifying thee.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Today is the prelude of the good pleasure of God and the proclamation of the salvation of men: in the temple of God the Virgin clearly appears and beforehand foretells Christ unto all. Unto her let us also cry aloud: Rejoice, O thou fulfillment of the Creator's dispensation!

*At Great Vespers, we chant "Blessed is the man," the first antiphon.*[^902]
*On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, 8.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
Today, ye faithful, let us dance with joy, * chanting in psalms and hymns unto the Lord, * and honoring His consecrated tabernacle, * the living ark, * which contained the uncontainable Word; * for she is offered unto God, being an infant in the flesh beyond nature, * and the great high priest Zechariah receives her with joy * as the dwelling place of God. *(Twice)*

Today the living temple * of the holy glory * of Christ our God, * she who alone among women is blessed and pure, * is offered in the temple of the Law to live in the Holy of Holies; and Joachim and Anna rejoice with her in spirit, and the ranks of virgins sing unto the Lord, chanting in psalms and honoring His Mother.

Thou art the preaching of the prophets, and the glory of the apostles, and the praise of martyrs, and the renewal of all earthborn, O Virgin Mother of God; for through thee we have been reconciled unto God. Therefore we honor thy entry into the temple of the Lord, and with the angel we all cry aloud in song unto thee, O most pure one: Rejoice! being saved by thy prayers.

*Other Stichera, Tone 4.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
The Holy of Holies, the holy and immaculate one, * is led by the Holy Spirit * into the Holy of Holies, * and is nourished by a holy angel, * being the most sacred temple * of our Holy God, * Who sanctified all things by her entry, * and deified the fallen nature of the earthborn.

The maidens rejoicing, * and holding torches, * today go before the noetic torch * and lead her * into the Holy of Holies reverently, * showing forth the ray that is to shine forth * ineffably from her * and to enlighten through the Spirit * those who sit in the darkness of ignorance.

Rejoice and receive her, O Zechariah! * Anna the all-praised cried aloud, * her whom the prophets of God proclaimed through the Spirit; * and lead her into the holy temple * to be reverently reared, * that she may become the divine throne, * and palace, and couch, * and radiant dwelling place * of the Master of all!

*Glory, and now: Tone 8.*
After thy birth, O Bride of God and Sovereign Lady, thou didst come into the temple of the Lord to be reared in the Holy of Holies, as consecrated. Then also Gabriel was sent unto thee, the all-immaculate one, bringing thee food. All the heavenly hosts were astonished, beholding the Holy Spirit having taken up His abode in thee. Therefore, O most pure and undefiled one, who art glorified in heaven and on earth, Mother of God, save our race!

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day.*
*Readings, 3.*

*The Reading from Exodus (Chapter 40):*[^903]
The Lord spoke unto Moses, saying: On the first day of the first month thou shalt set up the tabernacle of testimony; and thou shalt put therein the ark, and shalt cover it with the veil. And thou shalt bring in the table and its lampstand; and thou shalt put the golden censer to burn incense before the ark of testimony. And thou shalt put the hanging of the veil over the doors of the tabernacle of testimony and thou shalt take the oil of anointing, and anoint the tabernacle, and all that is therein; and thou shalt sanctify it, and all its vessels, and it shall be holy. And thou shalt sanctify the altar, and the altar shall be the Holy of Holies. And Moses did all things, according to all that the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, commanded him. And the cloud covered the tabernacle of testimony, and the tabernacle was filled with the glory of the Lord. And Moses was not able to enter into the tabernacle of testimony, because the cloud overshadowed it, and the tabernacle was filled with the glory of the Lord.

*The Reading from the Third Book of Kings (Chapter 8):*[^904]
It came to pass, when Solomon finished building the house of the Lord, that he gathered all the elders of Israel in Zion, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion. And the priests took up the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the tabernacle of testimony, and all the holy vessels that were in the tabernacle of testimony; and the king and all Israel were before the ark. And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the Lord into its place: into the sanctuary of the temple, into the Holy of Holies, under the wings of the cherubim. For the cherubim were spreading forth their wings over the place of the ark; and the cherubim overshadowed the ark and its holy things from above. And there was nothing in the ark except the two tables of the covenant, which Moses put there in Horeb, which the Lord covenanted. And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house. And the priests could not stand to minister because of the presence of the cloud, for the house of the Lord God the Almighty was filled with glory.

*The Reading from the Prophecy of Ezekiel (Chapters 43 and 44):*[^905]
Thus says the Lord: It shall be from the eighth day and onward, that the priests shall offer upon the altar your whole burnt offerings, and your peace offerings; and I will accept you, says Adonai the Lord. And He brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, which looks toward the east; and it was shut. And the Lord said unto me: This gate shall be shut, and shall not be opened, and no man shall pass through it, because the Lord God of Israel shall enter through it, and it shall be shut. For the Prince, He shall sit in it to eat bread; He shall enter by the way of the porch of the gate, and shall go out by the way of the same. And He brought me by the way of the holy gate that is toward the north, in front of the house; and I looked, and, behold, the house of the Lord was full of glory.

*At the Litiya At the Litiya, Stichera, Tone 1. Idiomela. By George of Nicomedia:*[^906]
Let heaven above rejoice today, and let the clouds drop down gladness, at the exceedingly glorious great deeds of our God! For behold, the gate looking toward the east, born of a barren non-bearing one according to the promise, and consecrated unto God to be His dwelling place, is led today into the temple as an unblemished offering. Let David rejoice, strumming on the harp: Virgins (he said) shall be brought after her unto the King, her companions shall be brought:[^907] inside the tabernacle of God, inside His mercy seat, to be reared as a dwelling place for Him Who was incorruptibly begotten of the Father before the ages, unto the salvation of our souls!

*Tone 4:*
Today the temple that contains God, the Theotokos, is brought into the temple of the Lord, and Zechariah receives her; today the Holy of Holies rejoices, and the angelic choir mystically keeps festival; and celebrating with them today, let us cry aloud with Gabriel: Rejoice, O full of grace, the Lord is with thee, Who has great mercy!

Come, all ye faithful, let us praise the only immaculate one, who was foretold by the prophets, and brought into the temple, foreordained before the ages to be the Mother, and in the latter times revealed as the Mother of God! O Lord, by her prayers grant us Thy peace and great mercy!

*Glory, and now: Tone 6. By Leo the Master:*[^908]
A joyful day and an all-honorable feast has shone forth! For today she who was a virgin before childbearing, and remained a virgin after childbearing, is brought into the temple of the Lord; and the elder Zechariah, the father of the Forerunner, rejoices and cries aloud with joy: The protectress of the sorrowful has drawn near unto the holy temple, as holy, to be consecrated to be the dwelling place of the King of all! Let Joachim the forefather make merry, and let Anna rejoice, for they offered unto God, as a three-year-old heifer, the immaculate Sovereign Lady! Ye mothers, rejoice together; ye virgins, leap for joy; and ye barren ones, keep festival together, for the foreordained Queen of all has opened the heavenly kingdom unto us! Rejoice, ye peoples, and make merry!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 5.*
*Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*
Heaven and earth rejoice, beholding the noetic heaven coming to be reverently reared in the divine house, the only immaculate Virgin! Marvelling at her, Zechariah cried aloud: O gate of the Lord, I open unto thee the doors of the temple; rejoice and dance with joy therein! For I have known and believed that already the redemption of Israel will manifestly come, and from thee God the Word shall be born, Who grants great mercy unto the world!

*Verse: Virgins shall be brought after her unto the King, her companions shall be brought unto thee.*[^909]
Anna, being visibly divine grace, leads with joy into the temple of God the honorable Ever-Virgin given by grace, having called the maidens bearing torches to go before her, and saying: Go, child; be thou an offering and sweet-smelling incense unto Him Who gave thee! Enter into the inaccessible shrines and learn the mysteries; and prepare thyself to be the joyful and fair dwelling place of Jesus, Who grants great mercy unto the world!

*Verse: They shall be brought in gladness and rejoicing, they shall be led into the temple of the King.*[^910]
Inside into the temple of God, the all-holy Virgin, the temple that contains God, is dedicated; and the maidens bearing torches now go before her. The excellent couple of parents leaps for joy, and Joachim and Anna celebrate, for they gave birth to her who gave birth to the Creator; and she, dancing with joy in the divine tabernacles and nourished by an angel's hand, the all-immaculate one, is revealed as the Mother of Christ, Who grants great mercy unto the world.

*Glory, and now: Tone 6. By Sergius the Hagiopolite:*[^911]
Today the assemblies of the faithful having come together, let us spiritually keep festival, and piously praise the maiden of God, the Virgin and Theotokos, who is led into the temple of the Lord, chosen beforehand from all generations to be the dwelling place of Christ the King and God of all! Ye virgins bearing torches, go before, honoring the honorable going-forth of the Ever-Virgin! Ye mothers, putting aside all sorrow, joyfully follow after her who is becoming the Mother of God and mediatress of the joy of the world! Let us all therefore cry aloud with the angel unto her who is full of grace: Rejoice! as she ever prays for our souls.

*At the blessing of the loaves, the Troparion, Tone 4:*
Today is the prelude of the good pleasure of God... It is written at Small Vespers. But where there is no All-Night Vigil, look at Great Vespers: we say the Troparion once.

*It should be known that if the Feast of the Entry of the Theotokos occurs on a Sunday:*
*On Saturday evening, at Small Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," the Resurrection Stichera of the Tone, 4. Glory, and now: of the feast, which was on "Lord, I have cried" at Small Vespers. At the Aposticha, one Resurrection Sticheron; then the Aposticha of the feast from Great Vespers, with festal* verses. Glory, and now: of the feast. Troparion of the Resurrection. Glory, and now: of the feast. Then the Little Litany and the Dismissal.

*At Great Vespers:* On "Lord, I have cried," Resurrection Stichera, 3; and an Anatolian, 1; and of the feast, 6. Glory, and now: of the feast. Then the Entrance; the Prokeimenon of the day; and the readings of the feast, 3. At the Litiya, the Stichera; Glory, and now: of the feast, "A joyful day has shone forth." At the Aposticha, Resurrection Stichera; Glory, and now: of the feast. At the blessing of the loaves, the Troparion of the feast, thrice; and reading in the Epistles of the Apostles.

*At Matins:* At "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Resurrection, twice; Glory, and now: of the feast. After the customary Kathismata, Sessional Hymns of the Resurrection, with their Theotokia; and a reading in the Commentary Gospel. Then the Polyeleos ("O give thanks unto the Lord") and the Troparia: "The angelic counsel"; the Hypakoe of the Tone; and all the Sessional Hymns of the feast, once each. Glory, and now: of the feast, the Sessional Hymn after the Polyeleos; and a reading of the feast. The Anabathmoi of the Tone; the Prokeimenon and Gospel of the feast. Then "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"; Psalm 50; and the veneration of the Gospel according to custom. Then Glory: the Refrain of the feast; And now: the same; and the Sticheron of the feast. The Canon of the Resurrection with the Heirmos on 4; and to the Theotokos, 2; and of the feast, both canons on 8. Katavasia: "Christ is born," both choirs together. After Ode 3, Kontakion and Ikos of the Resurrection; and Sessional Hymns of the feast, 2; and reading of the feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the feast, and reading in the Prologue. At Ode 9 we do not sing the refrains, but the "More honorable than the cherubim." Exapostilarion of the Resurrection; Glory, and now: of the feast. At the Praises, Resurrection Stichera, 4; and of the feast, 4, with festal verses. Glory: of the feast; And now: "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos." Then the Great Doxology; after the Trisagion, only the Resurrection Troparion; the litanies and dismissal. Then the Gospel Sticheron, the Catechesis, the customary departure, and the First Hour in the narthex. At the Hours, the Troparion of the Resurrection; Glory: Troparion of the feast; And now: Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father," the Kontakion of the Resurrection. Likewise at all the Hours, saying the Kontakia alternately.

*At the Liturgy:* The Beatitudes of the Resurrection of the Tone on 6; and of the feast, Ode 3 on 4. After the Entrance, the Troparion of the Resurrection, and of the feast; Glory: Kontakion of the Resurrection; And now: of the feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn, first of the day, then of the feast.

*At Matins At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Troparion:*
*Today is the prelude of the good pleasure of God... (Thrice)*

*After the first Kathisma, the Sessional Hymn, Tone 4.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "The angelic choir" (Ли́къ а҆́гг҃лскїй):*
The fruit of the righteous Joachim and Anna is offered unto God in the holy sanctuary, being an infant in the flesh, the nourisher of our life, whom the holy Zechariah blessed. Let us all faithfully call her blessed as the Mother of God!
*Glory, and now: The same.*

*After the second Kathisma, the Sessional Hymn, Tone 4.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was astonished" (Оу҆диви́сѧ І҆ѡ́сифъ):*
Before conception, O pure one, thou wast consecrated unto God, and having been born upon earth, thou hast now offered thyself as a gift unto Him, fulfilling the promise of thy father. And in the divine temple, as being the divine temple, given up purely from infancy with bright torches, thou wast revealed as the receptacle of the unapproachable and divine Light. Great indeed is thy entry, O only Bride of God and Ever-Virgin!
*Glory, and now: The same.*

*After the Polyeleos, the Sessional Hymn, Tone 8.*
*Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was mystically commanded" (Повелѣ́нное та́йнѡ):*
Let David the hymnographer rejoice, and let Joachim dance with joy together with Anna, for the holy fruit came forth from them: Mary the light-bearing, the divine lamp; and she rejoices entering into the temple. Beholding her, the son of Barachiah blessed her, and rejoicing cried aloud: Rejoice, O universal marvel!
*Glory, and now: The same.*

*Then the Anabathmoi, the first antiphon of Tone 4.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear.*[^912]
*Verse: My heart has poured forth a good word.*
*Let every breath [praise the Lord].*
*The Gospel according to Luke, pericope 4.*[^913]

*After Psalm 50, instead of "Through the prayers of the Theotokos":*
*Glory, Tone 2:*
Today the living temple and [ark] of the great King enters into the temple to prepare herself to be His divine dwelling place. Ye peoples, make merry!
*And now: The same.*
*Then: Have mercy on me, O God [according to Thy great mercy].*[^914]

*Idiomelon Sticheron, Tone 4:*
Today the temple that contains God, the Theotokos, is brought into the temple of the Lord, and Zechariah receives her; today the Holy of Holies rejoices, and the angelic choir mystically keeps festival; and celebrating with them today, let us cry aloud with Gabriel: Rejoice, O full of grace, the Lord is with thee, Who has great mercy!

*Two Canons of the feast: the first with the Heirmos on 8:*
*Heirmos* twice, troparia on 6.*
*A composition of George.*[^915]
*Whose acrostic is: Thou, O Sovereign Lady, give grace unto my word.*[^916]
*Ode 1, Tone 4. Heirmos:*
I will open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I will pour forth a word unto the Queen and Mother; and I will be seen keeping radiant festival, and rejoicing I will sing her entry.

*Troparia:*
We know thee, O most pure one, to be a treasury of wisdom, welling forth grace, an ever-flowing fount of understanding; we pray thee, O Sovereign Lady, shower thy drops upon us, that we may ever sing of thee!

Having been made higher than the heavens, O most pure one, a temple and palace, thou hast dedicated thyself in the temple of God, to prepare thyself to be a divine dwelling place for His coming!

The Theotokos, having shone forth the light of grace, enlightened all; and she has gathered us to adorn her most radiant festival with songs. Come, let us hasten unto her!

The glorious gate, impenetrable to thoughts, having opened the doors of the temple of God, now commands us who have assembled to enjoy her divine wonders!

*Second Canon of the feast, likewise with the Heirmos on 8.*
*Heirmos twice, troparia on 6.*
*A composition of Basil, Tone 1.*[^917]
*Ode 1, Tone 1. Heirmos:*
Let us all sing a song of victory unto God, Who did marvelous wonders with a lofty arm, and saved Israel, for He is glorified!

*Troparia:*
Let us hasten today, honoring the Theotokos with hymns, and let us keep a spiritual festival; for she is offered as a gift unto God in the temple.

Let us sing with songs the glorious entry of the Theotokos; for today, as the temple of God, she is offered prophetically unto the temple as a priceless gift.

Anna the immaculate was rejoicing, as in a motherly manner she was offering unto God a priceless gift in the temple, and Joachim with her celebrates radiantly.

David thy forefather sang of thee of old, O Virgin Bride of God, calling thee the daughter of Christ the King, Whom thou also, having given birth in a motherly manner, didst nurse as an infant.

Being three years old in the flesh, the Theotokos is offered unto the Lord; and Zechariah the priest of God, having received her, with joy placed her in the temple.

Ye virgins, torch-bearers, dance with joy! Begin today, ye mothers also! Sing unto the Queen and Mother coming into the temple of Christ the King!

*Glory: Triadikon:*
Consubstantial Trinity, Father, and Word, and Holy Spirit, we faithfully glorify Thee as the Creator of all, and we piously cry aloud unto Thee: Save us, O God!

*And now: Theotokion:*
From the purple dye of thy blood having clothed Himself in a scarlet robe, O most pure one, having come forth, the King and God renewed the whole human race in His tender compassion.

*Katavasia, both choirs together:*
Christ is born, glorify Him! Christ from heaven, come to meet Him! Christ on earth, be ye lifted up! Sing unto the Lord, all the earth, and with gladness sing in praise, ye peoples, for He is glorified![^918]

*(From this day, this Katavasia is sung until the 1st day of January.)*

*Ode 3, [First Canon]. Heirmos:*
O Theotokos, living and plentiful fount, spiritually establish thy choir who have gathered together, and in thy honorable entry make them worthy of crowns of glory!

*Troparia:*
Today the fair temple and bridal chamber of the Virgin was revealed as a bridal adorner, having received the living bridal chamber of God, the pure, immaculate one, more radiant than all creation.

David, leading the chorus, plays and dances with joy with us, and calls thee an adorned queen, O most pure one, standing in the temple before the King and God, O all-pure one.

From her from whom transgression of old came forth unto the human race, from her correction and incorruption blossomed forth, as the Theotokos is led today into the house of God.

The angelic hosts dance with joy, and the multitude of all men; and today, O most pure one, torch-bearers run before thy face, proclaiming thy wonders in the house of God.

*Another [Canon], Heirmos:*
Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God, Who didst establish the second heaven above the waters, and didst found the earth upon the waters, O Almighty One!

*Troparia:*
Let us keep festival, ye feast-lovers, and let us rejoice together in spirit, feasting today on the holy feast of the King's Daughter and Mother of our God!

Rejoice today, O Joachim, and make merry in spirit, O Anna, as ye offer unto the Lord her who was born of you, being three years old, as a pure, all-immaculate heifer!

The habitation of God, the Theotokos Mariam, is led into the holy temple, being three years old in the flesh, and the virgins, running before, shine with torches for her The unblemished lamb of God and undefiled dove, the tabernacle that contains God, the sanctification of glory, chose to dwell in the holy tabernacle.

Being three years old in the body, and ancient in spirit, wider than the heavens, and higher than the hosts on high, let the Bride of God be praised with songs!

Celebrating the entry of the Theotokos into the shrines that are not to be entered, carrying torches noetically with gladness today, let us also draw near unto the temple with the virgins!

Ye priests of God, clothe yourselves in righteousness through grace, and meet her radiantly, granting entrance into the sanctuary unto the Daughter of the King and God!

*Glory: Triadikon:*
Light is the Father, Light is His Son, Light is the Spirit, the Comforter; for shining as from one sun, the Trinity divinely illumines and preserves our souls.

*And now: [Theotokion]:*
The prophets proclaimed thee, O pure one, to be the ark of holiness, the golden censer, and the lampstand, and the table; and we sing of thee as the tabernacle that contains God.

*Katavasia:*
Unto the Son Who was begotten incorruptibly of the Father before the ages, and in latter times was seedlessly incarnate of the Virgin, unto Christ God let us cry aloud: Thou Who hast lifted up our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord![^919]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was astonished" (Оу҆диви́сѧ І҆ѡ́сифъ):*
Cry aloud, O David: What is this present feast of her whom thou didst once sing in the book of the Psalms: Virgins shall be brought after her mystically unto the King, as His daughter, the Maiden of God and Virgin, and her companions shall be brought;[^920] and make it a marvelous and universal feast for those who cry: The Theotokos, the mediatress of salvation, has appeared unto us!

*Glory, and now: Tone and Podoben the same.*
The immaculate ewe-lamb and undefiled bridal chamber, the Theotokos Mariam, is most gloriously led with joy into the house of God, whom the angels of God faithfully attend, and all the faithful ever call blessed, and thankfully sing unto her unceasingly with a loud voice: Thou art our glory and salvation, O all-immaculate one!

*Ode 4, [First Canon]. Heirmos:*
Perceiving the unsearchable divine counsel of Thine incarnation from the Virgin, O Thou Most High, the Prophet Habakkuk cried: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^921]

*Troparia:*
Receiving today the impenetrable gate into the house [of the Lord], He made all legal worship to cease, as truly manifested, crying to the consecrated: Truth upon earth!

The overshadowing mountain which Habakkuk foresaw of old,[^922] he foretold as having been contained within the inaccessible places of the temple, blossoming with virtues, and covering the ends [of the earth].

All the earth, seeing most glorious things, both strange and marvelous: how the Virgin, receiving food from an angel, bears the tokens of the dispensation.

Having appeared as the animate temple and palace and heaven, O Bride of God the King, thou art led today into the temple of the Law, being preserved there, O all-pure one.

*Another [Canon], Heirmos:*
Having heard, O Prophet Habakkuk, foreseeing the incarnation of the Word, thou didst proclaim, crying: When the years draw near, Thou shalt be known; when the time is come, Thou shalt be shown forth. Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^923]

*Troparia:*
O Prophet Isaiah, prophesy unto us: Who is the Virgin that shall have in womb?[^924] She who budded from the root of Judah, and was born of King David, from holy seed, a blessed fruit.

Begin, ye virgins, and sing hymns: holding torches in your hands, praising the procession of the pure Theotokos, who now goes into the temple of God, feasting together with us.

Rejoice now, O Joachim and Anna, leading into the temple of the Lord the pure Mother of God, who is to be the Mother of Christ, the King of all, but was born of you as a three-year-old heifer!

Being the Holy of Holies, O pure one, thou didst love to dwell in the holy temple, and conversing with angels, O Virgin, thou abidest, most gloriously receiving bread from heaven, O nourisher of life.

Having begotten beyond hope the all-pure Virgin, they piously promised to offer her unto God; and Joachim and Anna fulfill it today in the house of God, giving as a sacrifice her who was born of them.

The rod of Aaron budded once of old, prefiguring, O pure one, the divine birthgiving; for thou shalt conceive seedlessly, and shalt remain incorrupt, and after childbearing appear as virgin, nursing the Infant, the God of all.[^925]

Ye virgins, assemble piously to honor with us the Virgin, and ye mothers, the Mother who was born, as an unblemished sacrifice and fruit-bearing child born unto God; let us all therefore brightly keep festival!

*Glory: Triadikon:*
In three Persons, in one form, let us piously glorify the true God, Whom the angelic and archangelic ranks sing ranks sing as Master of creation, and men faithfully worship ever.

*And now: [Theotokion]:*
Pray unceasingly, O most holy, pure one, unto Him Whom thou didst bear in the flesh, thy Son and God, to deliver all thy servants from the manifold snares of the devil, and from all temptations that assail.

*Katavasia:*
Rod from the stem of Jesse, and blossom from it, O Christ, Thou hast budded forth from the Virgin; from the mountain praised and densely shadowed, Thou hast come, incarnate from the unwedded, O immaterial God: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^926]

*Ode 5, [First Canon]. Heirmos:*
All creation was amazed at thy precious entry; for thou, O Virgin who hast not known wedlock, didst enter within into the temple of God as a most pure temple, granting peace unto all who praise thee.

*Troparia:*
A glorious consecration and sacred offering, today the all-pure Virgin, having offered herself in the temple of God unto God our King of all, is preserved to be the dwelling for Him alone, as He Himself knows.

Seeing of old the beauty of thy soul, O all-pure one, Zechariah cried aloud in faith: Thou art deliverance, thou art the joy of all, thou art our restoration, through whom the Incomprehensible appears to me contained!

Beyond mind are the marvels of thy wonders, O all-pure one! Strange is thy birthgiving, strange is the manner of thy rearing; strange and most glorious are all thine affairs, O Bride of God, and unutterable by men!

Being a radiant lampstand, O Bride of God, today thou hast shone forth in the house of the Lord, and dost illumine us with the precious gifts of thy wonders, O all-praised Theotokos.

*Another [Canon], Heirmos:*
Shine forth upon us Thy radiant, ever-existing Light, as we rise early unto the judgments of Thy commandments, O Master, Lover of mankind, Christ our God.[^927]

*Troparia:*
Let all the Orthodox run together bearing light, and glorifying the Mother of God, as she is led today unto the Lord as an acceptable sacrifice.

Let the forefathers rejoice today, O Lady, and let her who bore thee be glad together with thy father, as their fruit is offered unto the Lord.

Let us all praise the much-renowned and most glorious unblemished heifer, as having borne in the flesh the Divine Bullock, celebrating in faith.

The divine tokens of the espousal are depicted, beyond the mind of thy birthgiving, O pure Virgin, today by the Holy Spirit in the house of God.

Let the portals of the glory of our God be opened, and let them receive the unmarried Mother of God, as a three-year-old, undefiled heifer.

Let us praise the much-honored and overshadowed mountain, the Ever-Virgin who became the Mother of God; for she has shone forth light unto the ends of the earth.

*Glory: Triadikon:*
Praising in words the original and ever-existing single Godhead, let us worship the nature undivided in three Persons, and equal in honor in glory.

*And now: [Theotokion]:*
We have acquired thy prayer, O Mother of God, as a fair-weather haven and an invincible wall in tribulations, being ever delivered from misfortunes and afflictions.

*Katavasia:*
God, being the God of peace and Father of mercies, hast sent unto us the Angel of Thy Great Counsel, Who gives peace; therefore, guided unto the light of the knowledge of God, rising early from the night, we give glory to Thee, O Lover of mankind.[^928]

*Ode 6, [First Canon]. Heirmos:*
Celebrating this divine and all-honorable feast of the Mother of God, come, ye godly-minded, let us clap our hands and glorify God Who was born of her.

*Troparia:*
He Who upholds all things by His word gave ear to the prayer of the righteous; therefore He loosed the disease of barrenness, as He is tender-hearted, and granted them the cause of joy.

The Lord, willing to reveal His salvation unto the nations, has now received from among men the unwedded Maiden, as a sign and renewal of reconciliation.

As thou art the house of grace, in which the treasures of God's unutterable dispensation lie, O all-pure one, thou didst partake of incorruptible sweetness in the temple.

Receiving thee as a royal diadem, O Bride of God, the temple was illumined, and gave way to better things, seeing upon thee the fulfillment of the things foretold.

*Another [Canon], Heirmos:*
Imitating the Prophet Jonah, I cry: Deliver my life from corruption, O Good One, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: Glory to Thee![^929]

*Troparia:*
Let us, the faithful, celebrate a spiritual feast, singing piously unto the Mother of God; for she is holier than the heavenly minds.

With spiritual hymns, let us, the faithful, praise the Mother of Light, as today she has appeared unto us, going before into the temple of God.

The undefiled ewe-lamb and pure dove was led to dwell to dwell in the house of God, as the unblemished one foreordained to be the Mother of God.

The temple of God, the heavenly tabernacle, accomplishes her entrance into the temple of the Law, out of whom light has shone forth unto us who sit in darkness.

An infant in the flesh, but mature in soul, the holy ark enters into the house of God, to be nourished by divine grace.

From all temptations and tribulations of soul, deliver us who flee unto thee, O all-praised one, by thy supplications, O Mother of Christ God!

*Glory: Triadikon:*
O Father, and Son, and right Spirit, Trinity in three Persons and undivided Unity, have mercy on those who worship Thy divine dominion!

*And now: [Theotokion]:*
Contained within thy womb, O Mother of God, He Who cannot be contained by all went forth from thee, O all-pure one, dual in nature, God and Man.

*Katavasia:*
The sea monster cast forth Jonah as an infant from its belly, such as it had received him; and the Word, having dwelt in the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth, having preserved her incorrupt. For He suffered not decay Himself, and kept her who bore Him uninjured.[^930]

*Kontakion, Tone 4.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*
The most pure temple of the Savior, the most precious bridal chamber and Virgin, the sacred treasury of the glory of God, is led today into the house of the Lord, bringing in with herself the grace which is in the divine Spirit; whom the angels of God praise: This is the heavenly tabernacle![^931]

*Ikos:*
Beholding the grace of the unutterable and divine mysteries of God manifested and plainly fulfilled in the Virgin, I rejoice; and I am at a loss to comprehend the strange and unutterable manner: How has the chosen pure maiden alone appeared above all creation visible and intelligible? Therefore, wishing to praise her, I am greatly amazed in mind and word; yet daring, I proclaim and magnify: This is the heavenly tabernacle![^932]

*Ode 7, [First Canon]. Heirmos:*
The godly-minded served not the creature rather than the Creator; but courageously trampling down the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers![^933]

*Troparia:*
Behold, today a joyful spring has shone forth unto the ends of the earth, illumining our soul and thoughts and mind with grace, by the festival of the Theotokos today; let us feast mystically!

Let all creation bring gifts today unto the Queen and Mother of God: heaven and earth, and the ranks of angels, and the multitude of men; and let them cry aloud: Joy and deliverance is led into the temple!

The Scripture has passed away, and the Law has failed like a shadow, and the rays of grace have shone forth, as thou, O Virgin, pure Mother, blessed therein, hast entered into the temple of God.

Heaven and earth and the nether regions bowed down unto thy Child, O all-pure one, as unto the Creator and God; and every tongue of earthly beings confesses that the Lord has appeared, the Savior of our souls.

*Another [Canon], Heirmos:*
The furnace, O Savior, was bedewed, and the youths dancing rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^934]

*Troparia:*
Let us, the lovers of feasts, dance today and sing unto the pure Lady, worthily honoring Joachim and Anna!

Prophesy, O David, speaking unto us: Virgins shall be brought after thee, they shall be brought unto thee into the temple of the Queen and Mother.[^935]

The ranks of angels rejoiced, the spirits of the righteous were glad, as the Mother of God is led into the sanctuary.

Receiving heavenly food, she advanced in wisdom and grace, having become the Mother in the flesh of Christ God.

And rejoicing in body and spirit, the immaculate Mary abides in the temple of God as a most sacred vessel.

Thy chaste parents led thee into the innermost part of the temple, O all-pure one, to be reared in a strange manner as a dwelling for Christ God.

*Glory: Triadikon:*
Let us glorify the undivided Trinity; let us sing unto the one Godhead: the Word and the all-holy Spirit with the Father!

*And now: [Theotokion]:*
Pray unto Him Whom thou didst bear, the Lord, as He is tender-hearted by nature, O Mother of God, that He may save the souls of those who praise thee!

*Katavasia:*
The Children raised together in piety, disdaining the ungodly decree, feared not the threat of fire, but standing in the midst of the flame, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^936]

*Ode 8, [First Canon]. Heirmos:*
Give ear, O maiden, pure Virgin: let Gabriel tell the ancient and true counsel of the Most High; be thou ready for the reception of God, for through thee the Uncontained has dwelt among men; therefore rejoicing I cry: Bless[^937] all ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord!

Leading the most pure temple into the house of God of old, Anna, crying with faith, said to the priest: The child given to me by God, receive now and lead into the temple of thy Creator, and rejoicing sing unto Him: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

Seeing her of old, Zechariah in the Spirit said to Anna: Thou leadest the true Mother of Life, whom the prophets of God brightly proclaimed to be the Theotokos; and how shall the temple contain her? Therefore, marveling, I cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

I was a handmaid of God, Anna answered him, calling upon Him with faith and prayer to receive the fruit of my travail; and having received her, to lead the newborn child unto Him Who gave her. Therefore I cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

The priest said to her: It is truly a lawful work, but I perceive a thing wholly strange, seeing her led into the house of God who most gloriously surpasses the sanctuary by grace. Therefore rejoicing I cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

Anna said to him: Knowing what thou sayest, thou hast understood it; for by the Spirit of God thou dost clearly perceive what things thou hast proclaimed concerning the Virgin. Receive then the all-pure one into the temple of thy Creator, and rejoicing sing unto Him: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

The priest cried aloud: A light-bearing lamp has been kindled for us, shining with greatest joy in the temple! Let prophetic souls rejoice with me, seeing most glorious things accomplished in the house of God, and let them cry unceasingly: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Another [Canon], Heirmos:*
Him of Whom the angels and all the hosts are afraid, as Creator and Lord, praise, ye priests, glorify, ye youths, bless, ye peoples, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^938]

*Troparia:*
Joachim rejoices brightly today, and immaculate Anna offers a sacrifice unto the Lord God: the holy daughter given to her by promise.

The saints boast: David and Jesse; and Judah is honored; for from their root a fruit grew up: the pure Virgin, from whom the eternal God was born.

Mary, the all-pure one and animate tabernacle, is led today into the house of God; and Zechariah receives her with his hands as a consecrated treasury of the Lord.

As the saving gate, and noetic mountain, as the living ladder[^939] and the animate ladder, let us the faithful truly honor the Virgin and Mother of God, who was blessed by the hands of the priests!

Ye prophets, apostles, and martyrs of Christ, angelic ranks, and all earthborn, let us honor with songs the pure Virgin, as the blessed Mother of the Most High!

Those who divinely bore thee, O all-immaculate and pure one, brought thee into the temple as a pure offering; and thou dost take up thine abode in a marvelous manner in the places inaccessible unto God, to prepare thyself as a dwelling for the Word.

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord. Triadikon:*
Let the holy Trinity be praised: Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, undivided Unity, one Godhead, Who holds all creation in His palm unto all ages!

*And now: [Theotokion]:*
The unoriginate Word begins in the flesh; He was born as He was well pleased, both God and Man, of the Virgin Maiden, refashioning us who had fallen of old, for the sake of His extreme tender-heartedness.

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord, singing and exalting Him supreme unto all ages.*

*Katavasia:*
The furnace moist with dew prefigured the image of a marvel beyond nature; for it burned not the youths whom it had received, even as the fire of the Godhead burned not the Virgin's womb into which it entered. Therefore singing we praise: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^940]

*At Ode 9, we sing not "More honorable", but we sing the refrains of the feast:*
*Refrain:*
The angels, beholding the entrance of the Most Pure One, were amazed: how the Virgin has entered into the Holy of Holies!

*And after this, the Heirmos:*
*As to an animate ark of God:*
*Then the second choir sings the same refrain of the feast, and the Heirmos.*
*And at each troparion they sing the refrains of the feast, alternating between both choirs.*

*Ode 9, [First Canon]. Heirmos:*
