Let no hand of the profane touch the animate ark of God; but let the lips of the faithful, singing unceasingly the voice of the angel unto the Theotokos, cry aloud with joy: Truly thou art higher than all, O pure Virgin! *Twice.*

*Refrain:*
The angels, beholding the entrance of the All-Venerable One, were amazed: how she has entered with glory into the Holy of Holies!

*Troparia:*
Having the beauty of radiant purity of soul, O pure Mother of God, and being filled with the grace of God from heaven, thou dost ever illumine with the ever-existing Light those who cry aloud with gladness: Truly thou art higher than all thou art, O pure Virgin!

*Refrain:*
The angels, beholding the entrance of the Virgin, were amazed: how she has most gloriously entered into the Holy of Holies!

*Troparia:*
Thy marvel, O pure Theotokos, transcends the power of words; for I perceive in thee a body surpassing reason, unreceptive to the flow of sin. Therefore, with thanksgiving I cry unto thee: Truly thou art higher than all, O pure Virgin!

*Refrain:*
Ye angels and men, let us honor the entrance of the Virgin: for with glory she has entered into the Holy of Holies!

*Troparia:*
Most gloriously, O pure one, did the Law prefigure thee as the tabernacle and divine jar: a marvelous ark, and the veil, and the rod; the indestructible temple, and the door of God. Therefore they teach us to cry unto thee: Truly thou art higher than all, O pure Virgin!

*Refrain:*
The angels, beholding the entrance of the Virgin, were amazed: how she has in a manner well-pleasing unto God entered into the Holy of Holies!

*Troparia:*
David, chanting unto thee, proclaimed thee, calling thee the King's daughter, seeing thee adorned with the beauty of virtues, standing at the right hand of God.[^941] Therefore, prophesying, he cried aloud: Truly thou art higher than all, O pure Virgin!

*Refrain:*
Ye angels, leap for joy with the saints; ye virgins, join the chorus; for the Maiden of God has entered into the Holy of Holies!

*Troparia:*
Foreseeing thee to be acceptable unto God, Solomon proclaimed thee to be the couch of the King, the living well sealed,[^942] out of which clear water has come forth unto us who cry with faith: Truly thou art higher than all, O pure Virgin!

*Refrain:*
Ye angels and men, let us magnify the Virgin with hymns: for in a manner befitting God she has entered into the Holy of Holies!

*Troparia:*
Thou grantest the tranquility of thy gifts, O Mother of God, unto my soul: pouring forth life unto those who duly honor thee, thyself defending, and covering, and keeping them, that they may cry unto thee: Truly thou art higher than all, O pure Virgin!

*Then the first choir sings the refrain of the second canon for the feast:*
*Refrain:*
Magnify, O my soul, her who was led into the temple of the Lord, and blessed by the hands of the priests!

*And after this, the Heirmos:*
*The cloud bearing light:*
*And the second choir sings the same refrain of the feast, and the Heirmos.*
*And at the troparia we sing the same refrain of the feast.*

*Another [Canon], Heirmos:*
The cloud bearing light, in which the Master of all came down from heaven as rain upon the fleece,[^943] and was incarnate for our sake, becoming Man, the Unoriginate: all of us magnify as the pure Mother of our God! *Twice.*

*Refrains:*
Magnify, O my soul, her who was led into the temple of the Lord, and blessed by the hands of the priests!

From the righteous Joachim and Anna came forth the fruit of promise, the Maiden of God Mary; and as acceptable incense, being an infant in the flesh, she is led into the holy sanctuary, to dwell as holy in the Holy of Holies.

Being an infant by nature, yet appearing beyond nature as the Mother of God, let us praise her with hymns; for today she is led into the temple of the Law unto the Lord, as an odor of hymnographic sweetness, a spiritual fruit.

With the angel, let us the faithful appropriately cry aloud unto the Theotokos: Rejoice, O all-good Bride! Rejoice, O radiant cloud, from whom the Lord has shone forth unto us who sit in the darkness of ignorance! Rejoice, O hope of all!

O Holy of Holies, and Mother of God Mary, by thy prayers, O pure one, deliver us from the snares of the enemy, and from every heresy and affliction, who faithfully venerate the image of thy holy countenance!

With the Angel Gabriel, all creation lifts up a worthy song unto the Theotokos, crying aloud: Rejoice, O all-immaculate Mother of God, through whom we have been delivered from the first curse, having become partakers of incorruption!

Greater than the Cherubim, and higher than the Seraphim, and wider than the heavens hast thou appeared, O Virgin; for in thy womb thou didst contain our God, Whom none can contain, and didst bear Him ineffably: Whom pray thou earnestly for us!

*Triadikon. Refrain:*
Magnify, O my soul, the dominion of the Godhead in three Persons and undivided!

*Troparion:*
Let us glorify the undivided Trinity: nature in three Persons and unseparated glory, sung unceasingly in one Godhead in heaven and on earth, piously worshiping the Father with the Son, and the Spirit!

*Theotokion. [Refrain]:*
Magnify, O my soul, her who is more honorable and more glorious than the hosts on high, the most pure Virgin Theotokos!

*Troparion:*
Unto those who faithfully flee beneath thy tender-heartedness and piously worship thy Son, O Virgin Mother of God, as the God and Lord of the world: pray that He deliver them from corruption and dangers, and from all manner of temptations!

*Then both choirs, having assembled together, sing the refrain of the first canon:*
*Refrain:*
The angels, beholding the entrance of the Most Pure One...

*And after this, the Heirmos:*
A strange and most glorious mystery do I behold: heaven is the cave; the cherubic throne[^944] the Virgin is the throne; the manger is the receptacle, in which Christ God, Who cannot be contained, lay down: Whom singing we magnify!

*Exapostilarion.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жєны́, ᲂу҆слы́шите):*
She whom the prophetic choir foresaw of old: the jar, and the rod, and the tablet, and the unhewn mountain:[^945] the Maiden of God Mary, let us faithfully praise; for today she is led into the Holy of Holies, to be reared for the Lord! *Thrice.*

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 1. Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*
The torch-bearing virgins, * brightly accompanying the Ever-Virgin, * truly prophesy by the Spirit what is to come; * for being the temple of God, * the Theotokos, * with virginal glory, * as an infant is led into the temple.

As the fruit of a holy promise * and of honorable renown, * the Theotokos has truly appeared unto the world, * as being higher than all: * who, being piously led into the temple of God, * fulfills the prayer of her parents, * being preserved by the Divine Spirit.

Nourished by heavenly bread, O Virgin, * faithfully in the temple of the Lord, * thou didst bring forth unto the world the Bread of Life, the Word; * unto Whom, as a chosen and all-immaculate temple, * thou wast betrothed mystically by the Spirit, * espoused unto God and the Father.

Let the door * of the God-receiving temple be opened: * for Joachim, having dedicated to the Lord * her who was chosen by Him to be His Mother, * offers her today, having received within with glory * the temple and throne * of the King of all.

*Glory, and now: Tone 2.*
*By Leo the Master:*
Today the all-immaculate Virgin is led into the temple, to be the dwelling of God the King of all, and the nourisher of all our life; today the purest holiness, as a three-year-old heifer, is led into the Holy of Holies. Let us cry aloud unto her as the angel: Rejoice, thou who alone art blessed among women![^946]

*Great Doxology. And Dismissal.*
*Note:* The brethren are anointed with holy oil by the priest. And we sing the Idiomelon sticheron of the feast, whichever the ecclesiarch wishes.
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the canon: Ode 3, Tone 4, and Ode 6, Tone 1, on 8. After the Entrance, the Troparion of the feast. Glory, and now: Kontakion. Prokeimenon, Tone 3: The Song of the Theotokos: My soul doth magnify the Lord... Verse: For He hath looked upon the low estate of His handmaiden*[^947] [is sung]. Epistle to the Hebrews, section 320.[^948] Alleluia, Tone 8: Give ear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear. Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance.[^949] Gospel according to Luke, section 54.[^950] Communion Hymn: I will take the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of the Lord.[^951]

*It should be known: if the afterfeast of the Entry of the Theotokos falls on a Sunday, and the saint is celebrated on 4, or on 6:*
*At Small Vespers, on Saturday evening, the stichera are of the Resurrection and of the Theotokos, according to custom.*
*At Great Vespers, after the Kathisma, on "Lord, I have cried", the stichera of the Resurrection 3, and of the Anatolian 1; and of the feast 3, the appointed ones for that day; and of the saint from the Menaion 3. But if the saint is sung on 6, or if he has a Polyeleos, then we sing the stichera of the Resurrection 3, and of the feast 3, and of the saint 4. Glory: of the saint; but if not, Glory: of the feast. Both now: Theotokion of Tone 1. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day.*
*At the Litiya, the stichera of the feast, those of the Aposticha for that day; and of the saint if he has a Polyeleos. Glory, and now: of the feast. But if the saint has a Doxastikon, Glory: of the saint; Both now: of the feast. At the Aposticha, the stichera of the Resurrection. Glory: of the saint, if there is one; but if not, Glory, and now: of the feast.*
*At the Blessing of the Loaves, the Troparion: "O Theotokos Virgin", twice; and of the feast, once.*
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord", the Troparion of the Resurrection, twice; Glory: of the saint, if there is one; but if not, Glory, and now: of the feast. After the Kathismata, the Sessional hymns of the Resurrection with their Theotokia, and the reading from the Commentary Gospel. The Polyeleos, and the Troparia "The angelic council"; the Hypakoe, the Hymns of Ascent, and the Prokeimenon of the Tone; the Gospel of the Resurrection, and "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ", and the rest of the Resurrection.*
*The Canon of the Resurrection, with the Heirmos, on 4; and of the Theotokos on 2; and of the feast on 4; and of the saint on 4. If he has a Polyeleos, the Canon of the Resurrection with the Heirmos on 4, and of the feast on 4, and of the saint on 6. Katavasia: "Christ is born". After Ode 3, the Kontakion of the feast, and the Ikos; and of the saint, if he has one; and the Sessional hymn of the saint; Glory, and now: of the feast, and the reading. After Ode 6, the Kontakion of the Resurrection, and the Ikos, and we read the Prologue. At Ode 9, we sing "More honorable". The Exapostilarion of the Resurrection; Glory: of the saint, if he has one; if not, Glory, and now: of the feast.*
*At the Praises, the stichera of the Resurrection 4, and of the feast with its Doxastikon 4: the morning Aposticha stichera, with the verses of the feast. If the saint has stichera at the Praises, then we sing the stichera of the Resurrection 4, and of the saint with its Doxastikon 4, with his refrains. Glory: Evangelical sticheron; Both now: "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos". Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Troparion of the Resurrection only. And the Litanies, and the Dismissal. And the Catechetical Instruction* [Catechetical Instruction], and the customary procession into the narthex. Then the First Hour: at the First Hour, the Troparion of the Resurrection; Glory: Troparion of the feast; Both now: Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father", the Kontakion of the feast. At the Third Hour, the Troparion of the Resurrection; Glory: of the saint; Both now: Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father", the Kontakion of the Resurrection. Likewise also at the other Hours we say the Troparion of the Resurrection, always alternating with the feast and with the Troparion of the saint, if there is one. And the Kontakion of the Resurrection and of the feast we say alternating; if it is a Polyeleos, of the saint as well.
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Tone on 6; and of the feast, the appointed ode on 4. But if the saint has an ode in the Typikon: of the Resurrection on 4, and of the feast the appointed ode on 4, and of the saint Ode 6 on 4. After the Entrance, the Troparion of the Resurrection, and of the feast, and of the patron saint of the temple; and of the saint, if he has one. Then the Kontakion of the Resurrection; Glory: of the saint; Both now: of the feast. But if the saint has neither Troparion nor Kontakion: Glory: Kontakion of the Resurrection; Both now: Kontakion of the feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn of the day and of the saint, if he has them; but if not, then the Sunday cycle alone.*
*Be it known that this feast is celebrated for 5 days.*

*In the same month, on the 22nd day.*
*The Holy Apostle Philemon and those with him:*[^952]
*Stichera of the feast, Tone 8. Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*
O marvelous wonder! * The ineffable future * is now prefigured * in images today, * things perceived in what is seen; * for having shone forth as the divine Light unto the world, * she is led as a bride unto the holy temple. * Her let us praise as the most radiant temple of God, * holy and light-bearing, * of Christ the Giver of light!

Truly an acceptable first-fruit * did wise Joachim * with Anna offer * unto Him Who was moved to give them the divine fruit: * the Maiden of God, the pure Virgin Mary, * through whom the debt of sorrow was taken away. * Her let us hymn, rejoicing piously; * the mediatress of joy * has she become unto all the world!

Come, let us mystically gather together, * and let us now begin, * adorned with the tapers of faith, * the escort of the Virgin; * for she enters gloriously into the temple of God, * betrothed unto Christ the King of all. * Her fair solemnity do we celebrate, * all of us making divine feast, * at her entrance!

*Stichera of the Saints, Tone 2. Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Е҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
Being a branch of the living Vine, O glorious Philemon,[^953] thou didst drop the wine of divine knowledge unto those in sickness of soul; and thou didst gladden the hearts grieving under the darkening of deceit, and gripped by the darkness of idol-madness. Therefore, rejoicing, we celebrate thy light-bearing memory.

The city of Gaza honors thee, having seen through thee the light of knowledge, O blessed one; and Colossae, possessing thy divine body as wealth, receives healings and ever-flowing grace.[^954] Therefore, we who celebrate thy memory are preserved from perils, O glorious Philemon, by thy prayers.

In faith, with the honorable Apphia, let us praise Archippus the wise hierarch; singing hymns unto Philemon and Onesimus, the sacred preachers of God, the venerable teachers, who uprooted polytheistic deceit by the word and planted the knowledge of the truth in all who piously honor their memory always.

*Glory, and now: Tone 1.*
Let the heaven rejoice today from above, and let the clouds drop down gladness,[^955] at the exceedingly glorious marvelous works of our God! For behold, the gate looking toward the East, having been born of a barren woman who had no child according to the promise, and consecrated unto God for a dwelling, is led today into the temple as an immaculate offering. Let David rejoice, plucking the harp: "The virgins that follow her shall be brought unto the King; those near to her shall be brought within the tabernacle of God, within His mercy-seat, to be reared for a dwelling of Him Who was born incorruptibly of the Father before the ages, unto the salvation of our souls!"

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2. Podoben: "O House of Ephrathah" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Today after the manner of the psalms, * the assembly of virgins, * having kindled tapers, * go brightly before * the only All-Immaculate one.

*Verse: The virgins that follow her shall be brought unto the King; those near to her shall be brought unto thee.*
The noetic mountain, * and divine table, * the bridge and jar, * O prophet, receive: * the only All-Immaculate one!

...All-Immaculate one.

*Verse: They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing; they shall be brought into the temple of the King.*[^956]
Having opened the doors of the sanctuary, * O Zechariah the prophet, * receive in truth * the Mother of God, * and only Ever-Virgin!

*Glory, and now: The same Tone.*
*Idiomelon:*
Today the all-immaculate Virgin is led into the temple, to be the dwelling of God the King of all, and the nourisher of all our life. Today the purest holiness, as a three-year-old heifer, is led into the Holy of Holies. Let us cry aloud unto her as the angel: Rejoice, thou who alone art blessed among women!

*Troparion of the Apostles, Tone 3:*
Holy Apostles, entreat the merciful God, that He grant remission of transgressions unto our souls![^957]

*Glory, and now: of the feast.*
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord", the Troparion of the feast, twice; Glory: of the Apostles; Both now: of the feast.*
*After the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "When the stone was sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́танꙋ):*[^958]
Praise, ye virgins; mothers, celebrate; ye people, glorify; ye priests, bless the all-pure Mother of God! For being an infant in the flesh of old, she was brought into the temple as the holiest temple of God. Therefore, celebrating a spiritual feast, let us sing unto her as the advocate of the human race!

*Glory, and now: The same.*
*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Begin before God in the temple of God, and rejoicing receive our Queen, and cry aloud unto her: Enter, O Lady, enter through into the temple, whose glory is understood covertly, from whom Christ the Light is about to flow forth unto all of us!

*Glory, and now: The same.*

*The Canon of the feast, with the Heirmos, on 8; and of the saints on 4.*
*Canon of the feast, Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
I will open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I will utter a word unto the Queen and Mother; and I will appear brightly keeping festival, and rejoicing I will sing her entrance.[^959]

*Troparia:*
O all-pure one, we know thee to be the treasury of wisdom and the ever-flowing spring pouring forth the grace of understanding; we pray thee, O Sovereign Lady, rain down thy drops, that we may ever sing thy praise!

Having become higher than the heavens, O all-pure one, a temple and a palace, thou wast dedicated in the temple of God, to prepare thyself to be a divine dwelling for His coming!

Having shone forth the light of grace, the Theotokos has illumined all, and assembled us to adorn her most radiant solemnity with hymns; come, let us hasten unto her!

The glorious gate, impassable to thoughts, having opened the doors of the temple of God, now commands us who are assembled together to enjoy her divine marvels!

*Canon of the Saints, whose Acrostic is: "I glorify thee, O Philemon, who lovest Christ." A composition of Joseph.*[^960]
*Tone 2. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Come, ye peoples, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He led forth from the bondage of Egypt, for He has been glorified![^961]

*Troparia:*
Dancing joyfully in heavenly dwellings, O sacred celebrant, grant me grace, as I divinely hymn thy holy memory; for thou hast been glorified!

Having watered hearts with the streams of thy words, O blessed one, thou didst prepare them by faith to cultivate heavenly understandings, O most admirable Apostle Philemon!

Sacredly ministering the sacred Gospel in the radiance of the Spirit, thou didst illumine souls, having delivered them from the darkness of idol-madness, O wise apostle!

*Theotokion:*
That divine assembly of the prophets of old, with manifold figures, O pure one, truly prefigured from afar the only one who was to bear the Sovereign Lord.

*Ode 3, [Canon of the Feast]. Heirmos:*
Establish thy choir-singers who have gathered a spiritual company, O Theotokos, thou living and plentiful fount, and vouchsafe them crowns of glory at thy venerable entrance![^962]

*Troparia:*
A beautifier of brides has the fair temple and bridal chamber of the Virgin appeared today, having received the animate bridal chamber of God: pure, and immaculate, and brighter than all creation!

David, leading the chorus, leaps and makes merry with us, and calls thee the Queen adorned, O all-pure one, who standest, O all-venerable one, in the temple before the King and God![^963]

She through whom the transgression came forth of old unto the human race, from her has restoration and incorruption blossomed forth,[^964] as the Theotokos is led today into the house of God!

The angelic hosts and the multitude of all men leap for joy; and before thy face, O all-pure one, they run today as taper-bearers, crying aloud: "Thy marvelous majesty in the house of God!"

*Another [Canon of the Saints]. Heirmos: Establish* us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst slay sin, and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who praise Thee![^965]

*Troparia:*
Preaching the passions and resurrection of Christ, thou didst raise up men as from the grave of unbelief and deadness, O most glorious Philemon!

Let us praise with sacred hymnody divine Onesimus, and Philemon, Apphia, and Archippus, the stars who illumine the ends of the earth!

Having purified the contemplative faculty of the mind, ye attained unto divine vision of God, and turned back straying hearts unto knowledge, O most sacred ones!

*Theotokion:*
Having appeared pure and all-incorrupt, thou didst receive in thy womb God the Word, Who cleansed our nature which had been greatly defiled by the fall of sin.

*Kontakion of the Apostles, Tone 2. Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*[^966]
As all-radiant stars illumining the ends of the earth, let us praise the Apostles of Christ: glorious Philemon, and sacred Archippus, and Onesimus, and Mark, and Apollos; and with them the all-wise Apphia, crying aloud: Pray unceasingly for all of us!

*Then the Sessional Hymn, Tone 8. Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Plowing the fallow hearts with the plowshare of the word, O sacred celebrant, thou didst prepare them by good works to cultivate divine knowledge; and having cast down the idol shrines, thou didst build churches, O blessed one, unto the glory of thy Creator. Therefore, assembling together, we glorify thy holy memory, O Philemon, being sacredly enlightened, and with one accord we cry unto thee: Entreat Christ God that He grant remission of sins unto those who lovingly honor thy holy memory!

*Glory, and now: of the feast, the same Tone. Podoben: "That which was ordered mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́иннѡ):*
Let David the hymn-writer rejoice, and let Joachim with Anna make merry, for a holy fruit has come forth from them: Mary the light-bearer, the divine taper; and she rejoices entering into the temple. Seeing her, the son of Barachiah blessed her,[^967] and rejoicing cried aloud: Rejoice, O universal marvel!

*Ode 4, [Canon of the Feast]. Heirmos:*
Perceiving the unsearchable divine counsel of Thine incarnation from the Virgin, O Thou Most High, the Prophet Habakkuk cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^968]

*Troparia:*
Receiving today the impassable gate,[^969] the house of God caused all legal service to cease, as he that cries aloud truly appeared crying aloud unto those on earth: "The Truth!"

The overshadowed mountain which Habakkuk foresaw of old,[^970] having blossomed forth with virtues, he foreproclaimed as having been contained within the inaccessible places of the temple, and it covers the ends of the earth!

All the earth, seeing most glorious, strange, and marvelous things—how the Virgin, receiving food from an angel, bears the types of the divine dispensation!

Having appeared as a temple, and a palace, and an animate heaven, O Bride of God, the all-pure one is led today into the temple of the Law, being preserved for Him!

*Another [Canon of the Saints]. Heirmos:*
I sing unto Thee, O Lord, for I have heard report of Thee and was afraid; for Thou comest unto me, seeking me who have strayed: therefore do I glorify Thy great condescension toward me, O greatly merciful One![^971]

*Troparia:*
Taking wing with the sail of the Cross, thou didst cross unharmed the fierce deep of the temptations of life, O blessed one, having directed by divine grace many voyagers unto the haven of salvation!

The divine city of Colossae sets forth the light-bearing luminaries:[^972] the sacred Archippus, Philemon, and Apphia both, and glorious Onesimus, who illumine the ends of the world!

The divine river having welled up in thy heart, O speaker of God, thou didst stop the rivers and currents of godlessness, and with grace didst refresh the souls languishing under the heat of ignorance, O glorious one!

*Theotokion:*
In truth I hymn thee, O all-hymned one, who supernaturally didst bear the lauded God the Word; and I pray thee, heal the infirmities of my humble soul, as thou art good, O Bride of God!

*Ode 5, [Canon of the Feast]. Heirmos:*
All creation was amazed at thy venerable entrance; for thou, O Virgin who hast not known wedlock, didst go within the temple of God as a most pure temple, granting peace unto all who sing thy praise![^973]

*Troparia:*
A glorious sanctification and sacred offering, the all-pure Virgin having dedicated herself today in the temple of God, is preserved for our King and God alone as a dwelling, as He Himself knows!

Beholding of old the beauty of thy soul, O all-pure one, Zechariah cried aloud in faith: "Thou art deliverance; thou art the joy of all; thou art our recall, through whom He Who cannot be contained shall appear contained unto me!"

...beyond understanding are thy marvels, O all-venerable one! Strange is thy birth; strange is the manner of thy rearing; strange and most glorious are all thy things, O Bride of God, and ineffable unto men!

Being a many-lighted lamp-stand, O Bride of God, today thou hast shone forth in the house of the Lord, and thou dost illumine us with the honorable gifts of thy marvels, O all-hymned Theotokos!

*Another [Canon of the Saints]. Heirmos:*
O Giver of light and Creator of the ages, O Lord, guide us in the light of Thy commandments; for other than Thee we know no God![^974]

*Troparia:*
Those who suffered with the visible sores of evil, O glorious Philemon, suffering grievously of old from idol-madness, thou didst heal by thy efficacious word!

Unto those who had grievously strayed, thou didst show the paths of salvation, as a truthful guide, O Philemon; thou didst daily guide them to love the one Way, Christ!

Today the honorable Church of Christ of Colossae joyfully sings a radiant feast, honoring divine Archippus and the God-proclaiming Philemon!

*Theotokion:*
O Sovereign Lady, save us who are storm-tossed by the fierce surging of temptations, and by the relentless invasions of barbarians, and by the fierce assaults of demons!

*Ode 6, [Canon of the Feast]. Heirmos:*
Celebrating this divine and all-honorable feast of the Mother of God, come, ye godly-minded, let us clap our hands, and glorify God Who was born of her![^975]

*Troparia:*
He Who upholds all things by His word[^976] gave ear unto the prayer of the righteous; therefore, as He is tender-hearted, He loosed the disease of the barren woman, and granted them her who was the cause of joy!

Willing to reveal His salvation unto the nations, the Lord has now received from mankind the unwedded Maiden, the sign and renewal of reconciliation!

As thou art the house of grace, in which lie the treasures of the ineffable divine dispensation, O all-venerable one, thou didst partake of incorruptible sweetness in the temple!

Receiving thee, who art visibly a church, O Bride of God, the temple was enlightened, and advanced to higher things, beholding the fulfillment of the prophecies upon thee!

*Another [Canon of the Saints]. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unsearchable abyss of Thy tender mercy: bring me up from corruption, O God![^977]

*Troparia:*
Thou hast appeared as a heaven unto all, declaring the saving glory[^978] of Him Who glorified thee, and numbered thee among the Seventy disciples,[^979] O most rich martyr!

Departing from thy fatherland, by thy marvelous word thou didst catch those who had estranged themselves from God, and didst make them citizens of Sion, O Hierarch Philemon!

Shining with sacred virtues, and brightly well-pleasing unto God, Thou didst ascend unto the heavens, O Apphia, dancing with the angels!

*Theotokion:*
The Word is incarnate in thy womb, and through tender mercy is known as Man, that He might make man a god, O all-immaculate Maiden!

*Kontakion [of the Feast], Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*[^980]
The most pure temple of the Savior, the precious bridal chamber and Virgin, the sacred treasury of the glory of God, is led today into the house of the Lord, bringing with her the grace which is in the Divine Spirit; whom the angels of God hymn: "This is the heavenly tabernacle!"

*Ikos:*[^981]
Beholding the grace of the ineffable and divine mysteries of God manifested in the Virgin and fulfilled manifestly, I rejoice; and I am at a loss to understand the strange and ineffable manner: how the chosen and pure one alone has appeared surpassing all creation visible and intelligible? Therefore, wishing to praise her, I am greatly amazed both in mind and word. Yet daring, I proclaim and magnify: "This is the heavenly tabernacle!"

*Ode 7, [Canon of the Feast]. Heirmos:*
The godly-minded youths served not the creature rather than the Creator, but valiantly trampling upon the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers![^982]

*Troparia:*
Lo, today a joyful spring has shone forth unto the ends of the earth, illuminating our souls and thoughts and mind with grace: let us mystically keep feast today in the solemnity of the Theotokos!

Let all creation today bring gifts unto the Queen and Mother of God: heaven and earth, and the angelic ranks, and the multitude of men; and let them cry aloud: "Joy and deliverance is led into the temple!"

The Scripture has passed away, and the Law has failed like a shadow,[^983] and the rays of grace have shone forth, since thou, O pure Virgin-Mother, didst enter into the temple of God, being blessed therein!

Heaven and earth and the nether regions submit unto Thy birthgiving, O all-venerable one, as unto the Creator and God; and every tongue of mortals confesses that the Lord has appeared as the Savior of our souls![^984]

*BOOK OF THE MENAION*[^985]
*Month of September*[^986]

To the glory of the Holy, Consubstantial, Life-Creating, and Undivided Trinity: Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit; under the reign of the great King Augustus the Third;[^987] by the blessing of His Excellency, the Lord Sylvester Liubieniecki-Rudnytsky,[^988] Exarch of the Metropolitanate of Kyiv, Halych, and all Rus', Bishop of Lutsk and Ostroh; by the volition of the Most Reverend Lord Father Hieromonk Ipatii Bilynsky,[^989] Protoarchimandrite of the Order of Saint Basil the Great; by the diligence and expense of the monks of the same Order in the Holy Wonderworking Lavra of Pochaiv, published in print.
In the year from the Creation of the world according to the Greek chronographers 7269, and of the Nativity of Christ 1761.

*In the same month, on the 23rd day: Our Fathers among the Saints Amphilochius, Bishop of Iconium, and Gregory, Bishop of Agrigentum.*[^990]

*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Saints, on 6.*

*Stichera of Saint Amphilochius, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
Having inherited a self-governing character and a sovereign mind over passions, thou hast sovereignly given supremacy unto that which is better over the worse, O all-blessed one, having weighed them by the most righteous measure, O father. Therefore wast thou fit for the vision of God and the knowledge of God, O divinely-inspired hierarch!

Thou hast shattered the snares and destroyed the subtleties of heresies, O venerable one, by the straightness of dogmas and by the most certain theology; having avoided division and the confused constraint [of blending], O father.[^991] Remaining within the bounds of our pious faith, thou didst proclaim the Trinity in the unity of the Godhead.

Having skillfully made wise the ruler on earth, thou didst pass by his son without bowing unto him;[^992] wisely teaching that when the Son is despised without worship, the Father is moved to the warmest indignation—He Who begot Him before the ages beyond understanding and dispassionately, as incorporeal, as He alone knows, O venerable one!

*Other Stichera, of Saint Gregory, Tone 8. Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѽ пресла́внагѡ чудесѐ):*
O most marvelous wonder! From swaddling bands dedicated diligently unto God, Who by His unfailing nods created all things; and already illumined by Him, thou didst pass through the night of passions. And thou didst shine forth as a light of healings and of the grace of miracles, driving away chronic afflictions and deceitful spirits!

O marvelous Gregory! Shining purely with the most radiant beams of the mind, thou didst put to sleep the surge-tossed sea of passions; and flying by dispassion upon honorable wings, thou didst reach that place where there is ineffable and incomprehensible beauty; ever praying for us who praise thee with hymns!

O Gregory [glory] of fathers, rule of the priesthood, image of chastity, strength of monastics, establishment of the Church establishment, lamp of love, throne of feeling, fountain of miracles, fire-breathing tongue, sweet-speaking mouth, vessel of the Divine Spirit, and an intelligible paradise hast thou been, O divinely-blessed one!

*Glory, both now: Tone 4.*
Come, all ye faithful, let us praise the only immaculate one, who was foretold by the prophets and led into the temple; foreordained before the ages to be the Mother, and in the latter times made manifest as the Theotokos! O Lord, by her intercessions grant Thy peace unto us, and great mercy!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 4. Podoben: "Of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чино́въ):*
"Let the virgins be brought unto the King into the temple of the Lord after thee, O Virgin," says David, the forefather of God;[^993] celebrating with bright tapers, and bringing thee, O pure one, unto the Holy of Holies as the holy ark of God!

*Verse: The virgins that follow her shall be brought unto the King; those near to her shall be brought unto Thee.*[^994]
Let the doors of the temple of the Lord be prepared and opened; and rejoicing, let them receive the house of glory, the one higher than the heavens, who hath become beyond understanding, and let them hymn Christ the Savior!

*Verse: They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing; they shall be led into the King's temple.*[^995]
Let the doors of the most divine temple be opened, let them receive within the heavenly door! And let human nature make festival, and let the angels leap for joy, mutually celebrating with us the entrance of the Mother of God!

*Glory, both now: Tone 2.*
A joyful day and a most venerable feast hath shone forth! For today she who remained a Virgin before childbearing and after childbearing is brought into the temple of the Lord; and the elder Zacharias, the father of the Forerunner, rejoices and cries aloud with joy: "The protectress of the afflicted hath drawn near unto the holy temple, as holy, to be consecrated into a habitation for the King of all! Let Joachim the forefather make merry, and let Anna rejoice, for they have offered unto God, as a three-year-old heifer, the immaculate Sovereign Lady! Mothers, rejoice together; virgins, leap for joy; and ye barren, join the choir; for the fore-chosen Sovereign Queen hath opened the heavenly kingdom unto us! Rejoice, ye peoples, and be glad!"

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
O God of our Fathers, Who dealest ever with us according to Thy meekness, take not Thy mercy away from us, but by their prayers direct our life in peace!

*Glory, both now: of the feast.*
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord", the Troparion of the feast* of the feast, twice; Glory: of the Saints; Both now: of the feast.

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1. Podoben: "When the stone was sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́тану):*
Being the Holy of Holies, O Theotokos, thou wast worthily led to dwell in the Holy of Holies, as an animate ark of the Lord, and truly the divine receptacle of the Holy Spirit, O Virgin Mother! Therefore, He Who is Only-begotten with the Father and consubstantial with the Holy Spirit, Thy Son, took up His abode in thee without knowing man, divinizing all humanity.
*Glory, both now: the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou didst appear today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ):*
Today all the universe is filled with gladness on the auspicious feast of the Theotokos, crying aloud: "She is the heavenly tabernacle!"
*Glory, both now: the same.*

*Canon of the feast, Tone 4.*
*With the Heirmos on 6. Heirmoi twice.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us all sing a triumphant song unto God, Who hath done marvelous wonders with an high arm, and hath saved Israel, for He hath been glorified![^996]

*Troparia:*
Let us gather today, honoring the Theotokos with hymns, and let us celebrate a spiritual feast; for she is offered unto God in the temple as a gift!

Let us hymn with songs the glorious procession of the Theotokos; for today, as the temple of God, she is prophetically offered unto the temple as a most precious gift!

Anna the immaculate rejoiced, offering a most precious gift unto God in the temple as a mother; and Joachim makes festival brightly with her!

David thy forefather hymned thee of old, O Virgin Bride of God, calling thee the daughter of Christ the King; Whom having borne as a mother, thou didst suckle as an infant!

*And of the Saints, two canons, on 8.*
*Canon of Saint Amphilochius, its acrostic:*
*I laugh at deception as I sing of the shepherd. By Theophanes.*[^997]
*Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Having traversed the deep of the Red Sea with dryshod feet, Israel of old, by the cross-shaped hands of Moses, conquered the power of Amalek in the wilderness.[^998]

*Troparia:*
Illumined by the radiance of Orthodoxy, thou didst easily destroy the words and teachings of wicked heresies; wherein do thou preserve in a manner becoming holiness those who honor thee!

The Lord, Who ever desires the salvation of all, sets thee forward, O hierarch, as a guide of His sacred flock, shining forth preeminently by word and by life unto the Benefactor!

Having chosen lawfully to suffer for the Church of Christ, thou didst fence thyself about with the knowledge of God of the Cross, O father, and by grace didst appear as a victor and crown-bearer, O glorious one!

*Theotokion:*
The Word, co-beginningless and co-everlasting with the Father, and being the form of His essence unto Him Who begot Him, hast thou borne incarnate from thee ineffably, O unwedded Maiden!

*Another Canon, of Saint Gregory, its acrostic:*
*Marvel at the skillful Gregory. By Joseph.*[^999]
*Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Unto Him Who hath shattered battles with His arm, and led Israel through the Red Sea, let us sing, as unto our Deliverer and God, for He hath been glorified![^1000]

*Troparia:*
Ever illumined by the rays of the Spirit, O holy Gregory, and having become a radiant star, enlighten all of me by thy prayers, that I may hymn thee!

He Who foreknows all things, having graced thy mind with God-given illuminations, adorned thee from swaddling bands, O father, who wast destined to shine with divine virtues and miracles!

Having cast away the slumber of despondency from thine eyelids, a watchful lamp didst thou appear, O God-bearer; showing forth in deeds thy name, Gregory, being truly watchful![^1001]

*Theotokion:*
I confess thee properly and truly to be the Theotokos; for thou didst bear the Lord ineffably, understood in two essences and two wills, O most pure Virgin!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God, Who didst establish the second heaven above the waters, and didst found the earth upon the waters, O All-powerful One![^1002]

*Troparia:*
Let us make festival, ye lovers of feasts, and rejoice together in spirit on this holy feast, feasting today in honor of the King's daughter and the Mother of our God!

Rejoice today, O Joachim, and be glad in spirit, O Anna, as ye lead unto the Lord her that was born of you, three years of age, as a pure heifer, all-immaculate!

The habitation of God, Mary the Theotokos, is brought into the holy temple, being three years of age in the flesh; and the virgins bearing tapers run before her!

The innocent ewe-lamb of God, and the undefiled dove, the tabernacle that contained God, the sanctification of glory, hath chosen to dwell in the holy tabernacle!

*Another, Heirmos [of Saint Amphilochius]:*
Thy Church rejoices in Thee, crying aloud: "Thou art my strength, O Lord, and refuge and establishment!"[^1003]

*Troparia of Saint Amphilochius:*
The divine and radiant beaming of thy dogmas swallowed up the wicked heretical host, O glorious Amphilochius!

Being a fountain of life-giving [teachings], like a river filled from God, having become a high priest, whereby we the pious are watered.

Illumined with rich rays, thou didst cleanse the mind with the mysterious beauty of the dust of thy teachings.

*Theotokion:*
A radiant lampstand, and the soul-nourishing table of piety, and the ark, O most pure one, do all we faithful proclaim thee to be!

*Another, Heirmos [of Saint Gregory]:*
My heart is established in the Lord, my horn is exalted in my God; my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; I have rejoiced in Thy salvation![^1004]

*Troparia of Saint Gregory:*
Therefore having accepted thy labor, O father, the Creator led thee into the desert unto an elder, who taught thee, O Gregory, the interpretation of every scripture.[^1005]

Passing the entire week without food, O father, thou wast nourished with heavenly food; watered with the rain of thy tears, and divinely delighted!

From God, O hierarch, a spacious heart was given unto thee; for thou hast richly poured forth the most honorable waters of teachings, watering the hearts of the faithful!

*Theotokion:*
The voices of the divinely-speaking preachers have been fulfilled; for behold, the Virgin hath borne a young Child, older than Adam, and enthroned together with the Father!

*Kontakion of the feast, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Who wast raised up" (Вознесы́йся):*
The most pure temple of the Savior, the most precious bridal chamber and Virgin, the sacred treasury of the glory of God, today is led into the house of the Lord, bringing in the grace which is in the Divine Spirit; whom the angels of God hymn: "This is the heavenly tabernacle!"

*Ikos:*
Beholding the grace of the ineffable and divine mysteries of God clearly made manifest and fulfilled in the Virgin, I rejoice; and I know not how to understand the strange and ineffable manner: how the chosen pure one alone appeared greater than all creation, visible and intelligible? Therefore, wishing to praise her, I am greatly struck with awe in mind and in word; yet making bold, I proclaim and magnify: "This is the heavenly tabernacle!"

*And Kontakion of Saint Gregory, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou didst appear today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ дне́сь):*
With light-bearing radiance the Church of the Holy Spirit light-enriches those who celebrate thy radiant dormition, O venerable father, all-blessed Gregory!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone the same [Tone 4]. Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Thou dost enlighten the ends of the earth in thy memory, O wise one; for thy body pours forth a fountain of healings, O glorious Amphilochius! Therefore dost thou deliver from every infirmity those who come with faith unto thy venerable temple. For this cause, pray even now that we may be saved!

*Glory: Tone 8. Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Прему́дрости):*
From swaddling bands dedicated unto the Lord, like the most glorious Samuel of old,[^1006] likewise didst thou obey the Savior Who called thee; and having cleansed thy soul with the bounties of good things, thou didst worthily receive the grace of the priesthood. Therefore, having pastured thy flock on the pasture of divine knowledge, thou didst shine forth the operations of healings, O Gregory! Pray unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love!

*Both now, of the feast: Tone 4. Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
O Virgin, pass into the temple of God, and rejoicing receive our Queen, and cry aloud unto her: "Enter, O Lady, enter into the King's temple, whose glory is secretly understood; from whom Christ the Light is about to pour forth unto us all!"

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing in spirit the incarnation of the Word, O prophet Habbakuk, thou didst preach, crying aloud: "When the years draw near, Thou shalt be known; when the time comes, Thou shalt be shown forth! Glory to Thy power, O Lord!"[^1007]

*Troparia:*
O prophet Isaiah, prophesy unto us: who is the Virgin that hath conceived in the womb?[^1008] She who hath budded from the root of Judah, and was born from David the King, a holy seed, a blessed fruit!

Begin, ye virgins, and sing songs, holding tapers in your hands, praising the procession of the pure Theotokos, who now goes into the temple of God, celebrating together with us!

Rejoice now, O Joachim and Anna, leading into the temple of the Lord the pure Mother of God, who shall be the Mother of Christ the King of all, born of you, as a three-year-old heifer!

Being the Holy of Holies, O pure one, thou didst love to dwell in the holy temple; and conversing with the angels, O Virgin, thou abidest most gloriously, receiving bread from heaven, O nourisher of our Life![^1009]

*Another, Heirmos [of Saint Amphilochius]:*
Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Sun of righteousness the Church stood in her order, worthily crying aloud: "Glory to Thy power, O Lord!"[^1010]

*Troparia of Saint Amphilochius:*
Come, ye divinely-wise, let us clap our hands in faith at the sacred solemnity of the divine and divinely-speaking Amphilochius; being strengthened by his teachings and his theology!

Having become a conductor of the bride unto the Church which is in Christ, O God-bearer, Thou didst adorn her with the beauty of thy words, and didst make her radiant with the beauty of Orthodoxy!

Thy theological and divinely-speaking tongue made clear unto all the equal-in-honor dominion of the primordial Trinity, and taught all to honor one Godhead in three Hypostases!

*Theotokion:*
We understand thee to be the new tabernacle, O Virgin, and the pure sanctuary of the Master of all; for thou didst bear Him in the flesh according to hypostasis, having united [with our nature], O all-immaculate one!

*Another, Heirmos [of Saint Gregory]:*
I have heard, O Lord, the report of Thee, and was afraid; for by an ineffable counsel, being God everlasting, Thou didst come forth incarnate from the Virgin! Glory to Thy condescension, O Christ! Glory to Thy power![^1011]

*Troparia of Saint Gregory:*
Like good earth didst thou flourish, O father, an ear of corn yielding an hundredfold; and with the sickle of thy teachings thou didst harvest the heretical, wicked opinion; and thou didst appear as a champion of the Council, O venerable Gregory![^1012]

The heavenly judgment, O pleaser of God, shows thee forth as a hierarch to guide well the flock which Christ purchased with His blood; for He foreknew the brightness of thy soul!

Thou wast a temple of God, cleansed from the defilement of passions; and standing in the sacred temple, thou didst manifestly receive the descent of the Spirit in the appearance of a pure dove, Christ having glorified Thee![^1013]

*Theotokion:*
The human race hath been saved beyond understanding by thy childbearing; and they that sat in the darkness of corruption, O most pure Sovereign Lady, have beheld the light that shone forth from thy womb, O Maiden, the Author of our restoration!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Shine forth upon us Thy light everlasting, O Master, Lover of mankind, Christ our God, who rise early unto the judgments of Thy commandments![^1014]

*Troparia:*
Let us that are Orthodox wear bright vesture, all running together and glorifying the Mother of God; for today she is brought unto the Lord as an acceptable sacrifice!

Let the forefathers make merry today, O Sovereign Lady, and let her that bare thee rejoice together with thy father for their fruit is offered unto the Lord!

The much-hymned and most glorious immaculate heifer, as having borne in the flesh the divine Calf, let us all hymn, celebrating in faith!

The divine tokens of thy betrothal are inscribed today by the Holy Spirit in the house of God, surpassing understanding, O pure Virgin!

*Another, Heirmos [of Saint Amphilochius]:*
Thou, my Lord, hast come into the world as a light, a holy light turning those who hymn Thee in faith from gloomy ignorance![^1015]

*Troparia of Saint Amphilochius:*
Illumined by the light of the three-sunned Godhead, thou didst sit upon the throne of the hierarchate, O divinely-wise Amphilochius!

Thou didst sanctify thyself unto God, and didst become a loud-voiced preacher of God, O father, all-blessed Amphilochius!

A joyful and all-sacred feast of the divine and wise teacher hath shone upon us, illuminating the world!

*Theotokion:*
O most pure Mother of God, the comely adornment of all the faithful: wash away the defilement of my soul by thy prayers!

*Another, Heirmos [of Saint Gregory]:*
Dispel the darkness of my soul, O Giver of light, Christ God, driving away the primeval darkness of the abyss; and grant me the light of Thy commandments, O Word, that rising early I may glorify Thee![^1016]

*Troparia of Saint Gregory:*
With thine oil thou dost cleanse the foul infirmities of the leper who once came unto thee in faith; for from God thou didst receive the grace of miracles, O wise one, like the divine Elisha, O divinely-wise Gregory![^1017]

By thy prayer thou didst open the mouth and ears of the stammerer, O Gregory; having been enriched with the operation of healings, O all-blessed one, thou didst pour forth the depth of theology, drying up the sea of the godless!

Cleansed from earthly attachment, O father, like Peter the first-chosen Apostle, by thy shadow thou dost work healings, divinely curing those possessed by the attacks of grievous diseases![^1018]

*Theotokion:*
Without emptying the Father's bosom when becoming incarnate, O all-immaculate one, He is seen held in thy bosom as an infant; Whom do thou make merciful unto those who piously honor thee, O Virgin Bride of God!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Imitating the prophet Jonah, I cry aloud: Free my life from corruption, O Good One, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: "Glory to Thee!"[^1019]

*Troparia of the feast:*
Let us the faithful celebrate a spiritual feast of the Mother of God, hymning piously; for she is holier than the heavenly minds!

With spiritual songs let us the faithful praise the Mother of Light; for today she appeared unto us, going before into the temple of God!

The undefiled ewe-lamb and pure dove is led to dwell in the house of God, as immaculate, foreordained to be the Mother of God!

Into the temple of the Law the temple of God makes her entrance, the heavenly tabernacle; from whom light hath shone forth upon us that are in darkness!

*Another, Heirmos [of Saint Amphilochius]:*
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood that flowed for mercy's sake from Thy ribs![^1020]

*Troparia of Saint Amphilochius:*
Having put to death in the flesh earthly-minded zeal, thou wast clothed with the grace of dispassion, O father, initiate of sacred mysteries, and with all-honorable teachings didst proclaim the Trinity! *(Twice)*

Fenced about with divine fear, O receiver of God, and having kept thy soul pure from defilements, thou didst appear as the most sacred instrument of theology, O venerable one!

*Theotokion:*
Knowing thee to be the pure and holy habitation of the King of glory, and the temple and throne of the Most High, we pray that our souls may be saved, O all-hymned one!

*Another, Heirmos [of Saint Gregory]:*
Even as Thou didst deliver the prophet from the lowest depth, O Christ God, deliver me also from my sins, as Thou art the Lover of mankind, and direct my life, I pray Thee![^1021]

*Troparia of Saint Gregory:*
A maiden paralyzed in body for many years is strengthened by thy prayer, O venerable one, having come unto thee in faith; and she magnifies Christ, the Cause of all!

Following in the footsteps of the Master by an immaculate life, O glorious one: when unrighteously grieved and slandered, thou didst remain unweakened![^1022]

Living in malice, like fierce beasts they seized thee, the guileless lamb, and condemned thee unto prison, where thou wast preserved, O father, by divine grace!

*Theotokion:*
The mind cannot comprehend the great mystery of thy childbearing; for thou, O Ever-Virgin, hast borne God, Who became man incomprehensibly!

*Kontakion of Saint Amphilochius, Tone 2. Podoben: "Seeking the things on high" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Divine thunder trumpet of the Spirit, husbandman of faith, and axe of heresies, O hierarch Amphilochius, great servant of the Trinity: standing ever with the angels, pray unceasingly for us all!

*Ikos:*
The all-wise hierarch of Christ sealed the Church with the inspirations of the Holy Spirit. For possessing the operation of power, the glorious initiate of mysteries and acceptable teacher of faith, having heard the pious reading of the Divine Scriptures, by making the sign of the life-bearing and precious Cross, extinguished the fire and pit of Eunomius;[^1023] and having preached Christ, he prays unceasingly for us all!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The furnace, O Savior, was bedewed, and the youths rejoicing sang: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"[^1024]

*Troparia:*
Let us make choir today, ye lovers of feasts, let us hymn the pure Theotokos, worthily honoring Joachim and Anna!

Prophesy, O David, speaking by the Spirit: "The virgins shall be brought after thee, they shall be brought unto thee into the temple of the Queen-Mother!"[^1025]

The ranks of the angels rejoiced, the spirits of the righteous were glad, that the Mother of God is brought into the Holy of Holies!

Receiving heavenly food, she advanced in wisdom and grace, having become the Mother in the flesh of Christ God!

*Another, Heirmos [of Saint Amphilochius]:*
In the Persian furnace the Abrahamic youths, burned by love of piety rather than by the flame, cried aloud: "Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!"[^1026]

*Troparia of Saint Amphilochius:*
Attending with love unto thy most mystical divine declarations, O father, we have escaped the Arians' cutting-asunder of the Godhead; glorifying in faith the uncreated and consubstantial Trinity![^1027]

Beholding Macedonius refuted by thy teaching, O father, we glorify in faith the Good Spirit, worshipped together with the Father and the Son, and co-beginningless![^1028]

Having clarified by word the incarnation of the Word, which is beyond word, thou didst divinely-wisely teach us to honor one God in two essences, and to flee from division and confusion, O receiver of God![^1029]

*Theotokion:*
Let us all zealously praise the Theotokos! Come, ye who have been saved by faith through the Almighty Who was born of her, crying aloud: "Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate one!"

*Another, Heirmos [of Saint Gregory]:*
He Who saved the children from the fire by an Angel, and turned the rumbling furnace into dew, is blessed[^1030] [...Blessed art Thou,] O God of our fathers.

*Troparion:*
The Creator worked wonders when thou wast judged, O blessed one; for a harlot woman, seized by demonic impulse, showed thee forth unto all as pure, O Gregory.[^1031]

*Troparion:*
The light-bestowing, divine disciples of the Savior, appearing unto thee, O venerable one, loose thee when thou wast bound unto a tree, joyfully kissing thee.

*Troparion:*
The Master, heeding thy patience, O father, holily adorned thee with greater wonders, which drive away the darkness of infirmities.

*Theotokion:*
In a manner befitting a mother, thou hast given birth unto the Creator of all, and hast borne in thy hands, as a cherubic throne, Him Who upholds all things, O unwedded Maiden.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him Whom the Angels and the hosts of God dread as Creator and Lord, hymn, O priests; glorify, O youths; bless, O peoples, and supremely exalt unto all ages.

*Troparion:*
Joachim and blameless Anna rejoice brightly today; they offer unto the Lord God the sacrifice, the holy daughter given unto her from promise.

*Troparion:*
The saints David and Jesse boast, and Judah is honored; for from their root hath grown forth the fruit, the pure Virgin, from whom was born the pre-eternal God.

*Troparion:*
Mary, the all-pure and animate tabernacle, is brought today into the house of God; and Zechariah receives her with his hands, as a sacred treasure of the Lord.

*Troparion:*
As the saving gate, and the spiritual mountain, as the animate ladder, let us the faithful truly honor the Virgin and Mother of God, who is blessed by the hands of priests.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
Daniel, having stretched forth his hands, stopped the gaping mouths of the lions in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of fire, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.

*Troparion:*
Thy lips, adorned with song, clearly theologized the uncreated, unoriginate, consubstantial, unconfused Trinity in three Hypostases, O divinely wise father, unto Whom we cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.

*Troparion:*
Hypostatic Wisdom gave thee riches and precious glory, when thou didst piously theologize, O all-wise one, and didst cast down the pride of heresies, and with love didst sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.

*Troparion:*
He Who grants life unto all, as a faithful and divinely speaking hierarch speaking, brings thee, O venerable one, into the Church of the firstborn, as thou dost mystically minister as a priest, and faithfully singest:[^1032] Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.

*Theotokion:*
The Son is now manifestly revealed from the tribe of Judah as Ruler and Leader; for thou, O all-immaculate one, hast given birth unto Him, the very Expectation of the nations, Christ, unto Whom we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.[^1033]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
Thou Who coverest Thy high chambers with waters, Who settest the sand as a bound for the sea, and Who upholdest all things: the sun sings of Thee, the moon glorifies Thee, all creation brings a hymn unto Thee, as the Creator of all unto the ages.

*Troparion:*
The dread demonic afflictions were loosed through thy prayer, O blessed one, from the young girl who through the malice of the lawless men had slandered thee, the righteous one; and in the midst of the council, God, the Awarder of the contest, glorifies thee unto all ages.

*Troparion:*
They who maliciously conspired against thee, O father, were filled with dark gloom; and thy radiant life shines before the fathers, O Gregory, in whose presence, holding burning coals in thy hand, thou didst work wonders.[^1034]

*Troparion:*
As a most bright star hast thou truly appeared upon the height of the Church, O father; thou dost ever illumine us with virtues and with rays of wonders, as we sing of thy light-bearing memory, O divinely wise hierarch Gregory.

*Theotokion:*
Thy most glorious childbearing astonishes our minds, O only blessed one; for God received flesh from thee, remaining what He was, O Theotokos, unchangeable in essence, Whom we supremely exalt unto the ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The light-bearing cloud, upon which the Master of all descended as rain from heaven upon the fleece, and was incarnate for our sake, becoming man, the Unoriginate: all of us magnify as the pure Mother of our God.

*Troparion:*
From the righteous Joachim and Anna sprouted forth the fruit of promise, the Maiden of God Mary; and as acceptable incense, being an infant in the flesh, she is led into the holy sanctuary, to dwell as the Holy of Holies.

*Troparion:*
Her who is an infant by nature, yet revealed as beyond nature, the Mother of God, let us praise with songs; for into the lawful temple is she brought today unto the Lord, into an odor of sweet fragrance of unleavened offerings, as a spiritual fruit.

With the Angel, let us the faithful fittingly cry aloud the "Rejoice!" unto the Theotokos: Rejoice, all-comely Bride; rejoice, radiant cloud, from whom the Lord shone forth upon us who sit in the darkness of ignorance; rejoice, hope of all.

*Troparion:*
O Holy of holies and Mother of God Mary, by thy prayers, O pure one, deliver from the snares of the enemy, and from every heresy and affliction, us who faithfully venerate the icon of thy holy countenance.[^1035]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
A cornerstone was cut out from thee, the unquarried mountain, O Virgin, without hands: Christ, Who joined together the separated natures. Rejoicing therefore, we magnify thee, O Theotokos.

*Troparion:*
Having most piously theologized the one tri-hypostatic nature, the all-holy, divine, unsearchable Trinity, thou hast now been honored by It, O sacredly blessed Amphilochius.

*Troparion:*
Having boldness before God, as a God-bearing hierarch, ever remember, as thou standest before thy Master, those who celebrate thy sacred and light-bearing memory, O all-blessed one.

*Troparion:*
Grant me abundant grace, as with a fervent heart I weave praises unto thee, O divinely wise one, and ask remission of sins, as a most faithful hierarch, O venerable father Amphilochius.

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast indeed appeared as the granddaughter of Adam, yet art known as the Mother of God; for from the ages thou wast beloved, holier than all creation, O blessed all-pure one. Therefore do we all magnify thee.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, Who hath raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of His servant David; wherein the Dayspring from on high hath visited us, and hath guided us into the way of peace.

*Troparion:*
Behold the radiant celebration! Behold the sacred commemoration! Behold the grace pouring forth abundant healing unto all the faithful who have assembled! Let us draw near, for the shrine of Gregory gushes forth unto us ever-flowing enlightenment and immortality.

*Troparion:*
Like a river wast thou filled with the waters of Christ; like an olive tree dost thou pour forth the oil of life; like a palm tree hast thou grown on high, O Gregory; like a vine dost thou bear for us the clusters of thy virtues, from which we are watered with the wine of incorruption.

*Troparion:*
Let the assembly of the sacred, and the multitude of the venerable, and the ranks of all the Angels rejoice together with us today in thy memory; standing with them before the Creator, illuminated, O father, remember with love those who hymn thee.

*Troparion:*
Thou wast a sacred vessel of Christ, O father, a pillar of the Church, and a haven of the faithful; a sword severing delusion, an unquenchable lamp, and a shepherd of shepherds.

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth unto the timeless Light, Who shone forth from the Father, enlighten my soul and mind, O Maiden, driving far from me the darkness of passions, that I may call thee blessed, the ever-blessed hope of the faithful.

*Exapostilarion of Saint Amphilochius.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "With the disciples" (Uchenikom):*
Having become god by adoption[^1036] through the immaterial communion of the divine nature, O all-wise one, thou wast anointed by Angels as a hierarch of the divine clergy; mediating between the Creator and creation, O divinely receptive father Amphilochius. Therefore, celebrating thy memory, we hymn thee, being delivered by thy prayers from corruption and tribulations.

*Glory, of Saint Gregory:*
Having adorned thy life through asceticism, O wise father, thou didst appear as an honorable hierarch of the Church of Christ, O blessed Gregory, enlightening the Orthodox with the beams of thy teachings and with unutterable wonders. Therefore, ask by thy prayers salvation of soul for those who celebrate thy most holy dormition.

*Both now, of the Feast.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "Hear, ye women" (Zheny uslyshite):*
Her whom of old the prophetic company foreannounced as the jar, the rod, the tablet, and the unquarried mountain: Mary, the Maiden of God, let us faithfully praise; for today is she led into the Holy of Holies to be brought up for the Lord.

*Aposticha Stichera, Tone 2. Podoben: "O house of Ephratha" (Dome Evfrathov):*
The partition of the cities hath truly been gilded with gold by the divine entrance of the Theotokos; and we on earth are now united with the heavenly ones.

*Verse: The virgins that follow after her shall be brought unto the King; those near her shall be brought unto Thee.*
The virginal choirs sang a divine song, bearing torches as they escorted the only all-immaculate one into the house of God.

*Verse: They shall be brought in gladness and rejoicing; they shall be led into the King’s temple.*
Within the sanctuary, the Holy of Holies, as she is the true Theotokos, O Zechariah, receive her into the Holy of Holies.

*Glory, Both now, Tone 6:*
Today, let the assemblies of the faithful coming together spiritually keep festival, and the Maiden of God, the Virgin and Theotokos, being led into the temple of the Lord piously praise, forechosen from all generations to be the dwelling-place of Christ, the King and God of all! Bearing candles, O virgins, go before, honoring the venerable departure of the Ever-virgin! Having put away maternal sorrow, joyfully follow after her who becomes the Mother of God and mediatress of the world’s joy! Therefore let us all joyfully cry aloud with the Angel the "Rejoice!" unto her who is full of grace, who ever prays for our souls.

*At the Liturgy. The Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 4 and Ode 5, on 6.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:*
Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.
*Verse: What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me?*
*The Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 334 [Heb. 13:17-21].*
*Alleluia, Tone 2:*
Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice.
*Verse: The law of His God is in His heart.*
*The Gospel according to Matthew, Pericope 11 [Mt. 4:25-5:12].*
*Communion Verse: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.*

*On the 24th Day of the Same Month: The Holy Great-Martyr Catherine, and the Holy Great-Martyr Mercurius:*

*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Saint, Tone 1. Podoben: "Joy of the celestial ranks" (Nebesnykh chinov):*
Today the city of Alexandria rejoices, wisely possessing thy swaddling-clothes in thy divine temple, O martyr. Therefore, we also piously celebrate thy venerable memory, O Catherine; pray thou for those who honor thee.

Let us now celebrate the memory of Catherine; for she in truth valiantly cast down all the power of the enemy, both by word and by deed, and the opposition of the rhetors; but by her prayers deliver us, O God, from godless foes.

Rejoice, all-glorious and venerable martyr Catherine; for on Mount Sinai, wherein Moses saw the unburnt bush, Christ, having now translated thy God-pleasing body, keeps it preserved even unto the time of His Second Coming.[^1037]

*Other Stichera, of the Martyr [Mercurius], Tone 4. Podoben: "As one noble" (Yako dobla):*
By the assistance of the Spirit, O passion-bearer Mercurius, having overcome the adversary as an invincible soldier, with the weapon of faith thou didst cut down myriads of spiritual Ethiopians;[^1038] and having lawfully accomplished thy contest, thou wast crowned together with all the sufferers, O most blessed great-martyr.

From heaven an Angel was sent unto thee to heal thy wounds by the beck of the Divine Spirit; having been healed thereby, O right-renowned one, when thou wast pierced most fiercely with red-hot spikes, thou didst endure hanging and being stretched out, and being bound unto a heavy stone, and being bathed everywhere with thy blood, O martyr.

Serving as a soldier unto the earthly emperor, O Mercurius, when thou wast commanded by him to sacrifice unto demons, O divinely wise and blessed one, thou didst endure torments, burning with fire, and a violent death; and bearing a crown, thou didst ascend unto Christ, and wast joined unto the flock of martyrs, praying for the world.

*Glory, Tone 2:*
Let us run joyfully unto the festival of the divinely wise martyr Catherine, O lovers of the martyrs! And let us wreathe her with praises as with flowers, crying unto her: Rejoice, thou who didst expose the wild rhetoric of the errant orators, as being full of ignorance, and didst guide them unto the divine faith! Rejoice, thou who didst surrender thy body unto manifold tortures for the love of thy Creator, and wast not cast down, being an indestructible maiden! Rejoice, thou who hast inherited the heavenly mansions as the reward of thy afflictions, and dost enjoy eternal glory! Desiring which, may we, thy hymnodists, not fall away from our hope!

*Both now, Tone 8:*
After thy birth, O Bride of God and Sovereign Lady, thou didst come into the temple of the Lord to be brought up in the Holy of Holies as consecrated. Then Gabriel also was sent unto thee, the all-immaculate one, bringing thee food. All the heavenly ones were astonished, beholding the Holy Spirit dwell within thee. Therefore, O all-pure and undefiled Mother of God, who art glorified in heaven and upon earth, save our race.

*At the Aposticha, of the Feast, Tone 4. Podoben: "Joy of the celestial ranks" (Nebesnykh chinov):*
Come, all ye lovers of the feasts, let us honor with songs the only pure Theotokos and Virgin; for into the house of God is she led today to dwell brightly therein: the truly holiest temple of Christ, and the mediatress of joy and the mediatress of all joy.

*Verse: The virgins that follow after her shall be brought unto the King; those near her shall be brought unto Thee.*
Open the doors, therefore; receive with faith her who is led into the temple of the Lord, the praise of all Angels and men, and bright rejoicing, to dwell and dance with joy within, who is the temple of God and His dwelling place.

*Verse: They shall be brought in gladness and rejoicing; they shall be led into the King’s temple.*
The Theotokos Mary, being brought into the temple, appeared receiving bread from an Angel, who cried unto her: Rejoice! Thou shalt conceive the Son without knowing man, O Bride of God, blessed Virgin Theotokos, the noble inheritance and edification of earthly beings.[^1039]

*Glory, Tone 2:*
Having learned an immaterial life, when thou didst reach the godless judgment seat, thou didst stand firm, O venerable and victorious Catherine, bearing the flower of divine radiance; and clothed with divine power, thou didst deride the command of the tormentors, and didst silence the wandering speeches of the rhetors, O much-suffering one.

*Both now, of the Feast, Tone 8:*
David proclaimed thee beforehand, O all-pure one, foreseeing the sanctification of thine entrance into the temple; wherein the ends of the earth, keeping festival today, glorify thee, O all-hymned one. For she who before childbirth was a Virgin, and after childbirth remained incorrupt, the Mother of the Word of Life: today Zechariah rejoices in the temple, having received thee, O Sovereign Lady; and the Holy of Holies rejoices, having received thee, the fountain of our life. Therefore we also cry aloud unto thee with the children: Pray unto Thy Son and our God on our behalf, to grant us great mercy.

*Troparion of the Martyr [Catherine], Tone 4:*
Thy lamb Jesus, Catherine, cries with a loud voice: Thee, my Bridegroom, do I love, and seeking Thee I endure suffering, and am crucified with Thee, and am buried with Thee in Thy baptism; and I suffer for Thy sake, that I may reign in Thee, and I die for Thee, that I may also live with Thee; but as a blameless sacrifice accept me, who with love have sacrificed myself unto Thee. By her prayers, as Thou art merciful, save our souls.

*Or this Troparion, in the same Tone:*
By virtues as by sunbeams didst thou enlighten the unbelieving philosophers; and as the most bright moon for those walking in the night, thou didst drive away the darkness of unbelief, and didst convince the empress, while also exposing the tormentor, O divinely called bride, blessed Catherine. With longing hast thou ascended into the heavenly bridal chamber unto the fair Bridegroom groom, Christ; and by Him wast Thou crowned with a royal crown. Standing before Him together with the Angels, pray for us who observe thy venerable memory.

*Glory, of the Martyr, in the same Tone:*
Thy martyr, O Lord, Mercurius, in his contest received an incorruptible crown from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, he cast down the tormentors, and crushed the powerless boldness of demons; by his prayers save our souls.

*Both now, of the Feast.*

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord", Troparion of the Feast, twice; and of Catherine, once. Glory, of the Martyr; Both now, of the Feast.*

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "When the stone was sealed" (Kameni zapechatannu):*
Praise, O virgins! Celebrate, O mothers! Glorify, O peoples! Bless, O priests, the all-pure Mother of God! For being an infant in the flesh, she was of old brought into the temple, as the holiest temple of God. Therefore, celebrating a spiritual festival, let us hymn her as the protectress of the human race.

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "When the stone was sealed" (Kameni zapechatannu):*
Being the Holy of Holies, O Theotokos, thou wast worthily brought to dwell in the Holy of Holies, as an animate ark of the Lord, and truly a divine dwelling-place of the Holy Spirit, O Virgin Mother. Therefore, He Who is Only-begotten unto the Father and co-essential with the Holy Spirit, even Thy Son, dwelt within thee without knowing man, deifying all humanity.[^1040]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*

*Canon of the Feast, Tone 4, with the Heirmos on 6; and of both Saints, on 8.*

*Canon of the Feast, Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
I shall open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I shall utter a word unto the Queen and Mother; and I shall appear brightly keeping festival, and rejoicing I shall sing of her entrance.

*Troparion:*
We know thee, O all-pure one, as the treasury of wisdom and the fountain pouring forth grace, of ever-flowing understanding; we pray thee, O Sovereign Lady, shower down thy drops, that we may ever hymn thee.

*Troparion:*
Having become higher than the heavens, O all-pure temple and palace, thou wast dedicated in the temple of God, to prepare thyself therein as a divine dwelling-place of His coming.

*Troparion:*
The Light shining forth from the Father of grace enlightened all things, and united and united all to adorn her most radiant festival with hymns: come, let us hasten unto her!

*Troparion:*
The glorious door, impassable to thoughts, having opened the doors of the temple of God, now commands us who have assembled to enjoy her divine wonders.

*Canon of the Holy Martyr [Catherine], whereof the acrostic is: "I hymn in song the ever-memorable Catherine." By Theophanes. Tone 8.*[^1041]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The rod of Moses, working a wonder of old, striking the sea crosswise and dividing it, drowned the chariot-driving Pharaoh; and it saved Israel as a fugitive travelling on foot, as he sang a song unto God.

*Troparion:*
By the prayers of the all-wise martyr Catherine, O Christ, enlighten the darkened eye of my soul, granting me, O Master, the ray of Thy radiance, which consumes all the darkness of my soul-destroying falls.

*Troparion:*
Directed by divine commandments, O all-wise one, and inflamed with His love, thou didst hasten eagerly unto contests, and didst dismay the minds of the tormentors, O Catherine, by word, by wisdom, and by grace.

*Troparion:*
Guided by the strong right hand of Christ, O glorious martyr, thou didst escape the storm of idolatry, sailing dry-shod with the sail of the Cross and by the divine winds of the Spirit, singing a hymn unto God.

*Troparion:*
Rejoicing in virginal beauty, O wise Catherine, and possessing divine knowledge from heaven, thou didst put to shame the champions of knowledge falsely so called,[^1042] having boldly overcome them.

*Theotokion:*
He who proclaims thee to be the Theotokos, O all-pure one, has the repudiation of every heresy; for thou, O Mother of God, hast unchangeably given birth in the flesh unto Him Who is higher than all creation: the co-eternal Word of God.

*Another Canon, of the Martyr [Mercurius], whereof the acrostic is: "May the strength of Mercurius protect me." By Joseph. Tone 8.*[^1043]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
That which was cut severed the unquarried element, and the sun beheld the earth which it had not seen; the water drowned the fierce enemy, and Israel traversed the impassable deep. And a song was sung: Let us sing unto the Lord, for gloriously hath He been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Standing rejoicing with the heavenly choirs before the Fountain of good things, O Mercurius, and filled with divine sweetness, O ever-memorable one keep those who celebrate thy festival with love, as they sing unto the Lord: For gloriously hath He been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Courageously didst thou enter into the arena of martyrdom, O wise one, strengthened by the power of Christ, Who for our sake voluntarily endured the saving passions in the flesh; and rejoicing thou didst cry aloud: Let us sing unto the Lord, for gloriously hath He been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst fiercely rebuke the speech of the tyrant, being adorned with the confession of Christ, O blessed one; and rejoicing thou didst endure every form of pain, O Mercurius, crying unto Him Who strengthened thee: Let us sing unto the Lord, for gloriously hath He been glorified!

*Theotokion:*
From the Virgin Maiden didst Thou appear, being incarnate for our sake, having become man like unto us; and Thou dost reveal Mercurius, Thy valiant sufferer, as a faithful witness of Thy passions, who fervently sings unto Thee: Let us sing unto the Lord, for gloriously hath He been glorified!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Establish thy singers, O Theotokos, living and inexhaustible fountain, who have formed a spiritual choir; and in thine honorable entrance vouchsafe unto them crowns of glory.

*Troparion:*
The beautiful temple and bridal chamber of the Virgin was revealed today as an adorner of the bride, having received the animate bridal chamber of God: pure, undefiled, and more radiant than all creation.

*Troparion:*
David, beginning the choral dance, leaps and dances with us, and calls thee the Queen adorned, O all-pure one, standing in the temple before the King and God, O all-venerable one.[^1044]

*Troparion:*
