She through whom transgression of old came forth unto the human race, from her hath restoration and incorruption blossomed forth: the Theotokos who is brought today into the house of God.[^1045]

*Troparion:*
The angelic hosts dance, and the multitude of all men; and before thy face today, O all-pure one, the priests run before thee, proclaiming thy wonders in the house of God.

*Another Canon [of St. Catherine]. Heirmos:*
Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens with understanding, and didst found the earth upon the waters: establish me, O Christ, upon the rock of Thy commandments, for there is none holy save Thee, O only Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*
By thine own voluntary impulses didst thou enter into suffering, imitating the voluntary passion of Christ; and having brightly overcome the world-ruler of darkness, thou wast revealed as a crown-bearer, O divinely receptive Catherine.

*Troparion:*
By strength of mind thou didst expose the tormentors tossing about in the deep of godlessness, and passionately philosophizing against the dogmas of the knowledge of God; for as a martyr thou wast enlightened by the wisdom of God.

...made radiant, all-praised one.

*Troparion:*
For he who whispered equal status with God into Eve’s ear is now trampled down by a young maiden; for having fortified herself with the weapon of the Cross, Catherine the martyr put to shame those who boasted excessively of him.

*Theotokion:*
My deadened mind raise up, O only all-blameless Mother of God, by the operation of the Life that appeared unto the world from thee, destroying the wounds and arrows of sin.

*Another Heirmos:*
Thou art the affirmation of those who run to Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit sings of Thee.

*Troparion:*
Wholly inflamed with divine love, O glorious one, fire, bonds, swords, and torments thou didst account as a dream, O Mercurius.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst sing to the Creator while enduring cruel wounds, O wise martyr, and didst receive healing of thy stripes, O glorious one.

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by the divine rod, O valiant-minded martyr and sufferer, thou didst subdue the raging of the enemy by the power of God.

*Theotokion:*
That it might prefigure thy birthgiving surpassing the mind, O pure one, the bush appeared burning with fire yet never consumed.

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Who wast raised up" (Вознесыйся):*
The most pure temple of the Savior, the precious bridal chamber and Virgin, the sacred treasury of the glory of God, today is led into the house of the Lord, bringing with her the grace which is in the Divine Spirit; whom the angels of God hymn: this is the heavenly tabernacle.

*Ikos:*
Beholding the grace revealed in the Virgin of the unutterable and divine mysteries of God, and being filled with it plainly, I rejoice; and I am at a loss to comprehend the strange and unutterable manner: how the chosen pure one alone appeared more exalted than all creation, visible and intelligible? Therefore, wishing to praise her, I am greatly terrified in mind and in word. Yet daring, I proclaim and magnify: this is the heavenly tabernacle.

*Then the Kontakion of Mercurius, Tone 2. Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Явился еси днесь):*
In battles an invincible warrior, and in afflictions an unashamed defender, let us bless Mercurius with songs, glorifying him; for he delivers from afflictions and sorrows those who joyfully celebrate his memory.

*Sessional Hymn of the Saint, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Who wast raised up" (Вознесыйся):*

Having loved Thy Bridegroom, Christ, having brightly prepared Thy lamp, having shone with virtues, O glorious one; therefore thou didst enter with Him into the bridal chamber, and having received from Him the crown of suffering, deliver us from afflictions, O Catherine, who celebrate Thy memory.[^1046]

*Glory to the Martyr, the same Tone. Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Скоро предвари):*
The martyr Mercurius, having struggled, put the deceitful one to shame and became a valiant crowned one of Christ; therefore he is now numbered with the heavenly choirs, worthily partaking of unfading glory. For this cause we faithfully celebrate his sacred memory.

*Both now, of the Feast. The same Tone:*
Virgin, go before into the temple of God, and rejoicing receive our Queen, and cry aloud to her: Enter, Lady, enter into the temple of the King, whose glory is understood in a hidden manner, from whom Christ the Light will pour forth unto us all.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
The unsearchable divine counsel concerning the Incarnation of Thee, the Most High, from the Virgin, the prophet Habakkuk, beholding from afar, cried: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1047]

*Troparion:*
Receiving the impassable door today, the house of God caused all legal service to cease; for truly the Truth hath appeared, crying aloud to those who are holy upon the earth.

*Troparion:*
The overshadowing mountain which Habakkuk foresaw of old foreproclaimed her that is contained within the inaccessible places of the temple, blossoming with virtues, and covering the ends [of the earth].

*Troparion:*
All the earth, seeing marvelous and strange things, how the Virgin, receiving food from an angel, bears the types of the Dispensation.

*Troparion:*
Having appeared as the temple, palace, and animate heaven, O Bride of God of the King, today thou art led into the temple of the Law, being preserved for Him, O most pure one.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art both my power; Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who hast not left the Father’s bosom and hast visited our poverty. Therefore with the prophet Habakkuk I cry to Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind![^1048]

*Troparion:*
A martyr's resistance hast thou shown forth, O ever-memorable martyr Catherine, very patiently opposing the enemy, and having trampled him under thy fair feet by the power of the Cross, O passion-bearer, boast of martyrs!

*Troparion:*
A bride of Christ, O all-blessed Catherine, didst thou appear, enlightened by the light-radiant rays of divine beauty and shining with loveliness; therefore, rejoicing, thou singest to the Master: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst cast down the tyrant's arrogance, and by the divine word of thy wisdom, as from the depths of deceitful demon-worship, thou didst snatch away those who were deceived, teaching those who hymn Christ to cry: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
The divinely glorious and light-bearing solemnity of thy glorious memory, O all-praised one, having firmly trampled the enemy's boldness, shone forth as the sun, wherein we cry aloud to the Master: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:*
Now cast down the strength of those who reject the veneration of the icon, O maiden, that honors thee and the One incarnate from thee surpassing the mind Who hath enlightened all the world, and all the saints; and enlighten those who honor thee in faith, O only all-hymned one.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy Dispensation; I considered Thy works, and I glorified Thy Divinity.

*Troparion:*
Thou wast made Thine own by thy Creator through the sufferings of divine witness, O divinely wise one, and receivedst radiant crowns from Him, O glorious one, as one invincible.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast now clothed thyself, O martyr, in the robe woven of grace from on high, having stripped off the garments of corruption and deadness, O martyr.

*Troparion:*
Having resisted against sin even unto blood, O glorious one, thou wast shown forth as a victor and wast counted worthy of glory from on high, O Mercurius.

*Theotokion:*
Upon thee, O Ever-Virgin, the saving Word descended as a shower, and dried up the floods of polytheism.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
All things were amazed at thy venerable entry; for thou, O Virgin who knewest not wedlock, didst go within into the temple of God as the purest temple, granting peace to all who hymn thee.

*Troparion:*
A glorious sanctification and sacred offering, today the most pure Virgin, being offered into the temple of God, is preserved as a dwelling for God our King of all alone, as He Himself knows.

*Troparion:*
Beholding of old in faith the beauty of thy soul, O most pure one, Zacharias cried aloud: Thou art deliverance, thou art the joy of all, thou art our calling, through whom He Who cannot be contained seems to me to be contained.

*Troparion:*
Surpassing the mind are thy wonders, O all-venerable one! Strange is thy birth, strange the manner of thy upbringing; strange and most glorious are all things concerning thee, O Bride of God, and unutterable by men.

*Troparion:*
Being a many-lighted lampstand, O Bride of God, today thou hast shone forth in the house of the Lord, and thou illuminest us with the precious gifts of thy wonders, O pure one, all-hymned Mother of God.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy face, O Light unwaning, and alien darkness hath covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and unto the light of Thy commandments direct my ways, I pray.

*Troparion:*
Kindled with fire by love of thy Master, O all-glorious martyr, and seeking to behold His unsearchable beauty, by thine own voluntary resolve thou gavest thyself up to wounds, shining with the graces of virginity.

*Troparion:*
With most sacred arrows, O maiden of good deeds, having adorned thyself with seemliness, thou didst ascend to the heavenly bridal chamber of Christ, and now, rejoicing, thou art brightly united to thy Bridegroom, O all-blessed one.

*Troparion:*
An all-radiant maiden didst thou appear, having loved the One Desired One, and having accomplished the most valiant running after Him, into the fragrance of His poured-out intelligible myrrh thou didst cry aloud: I run, O my Bridegroom![^1049]

*Theotokion:*
Knowing thee all to be truly the Mother of God, O most pure Sovereign Lady, and knowing God the Word born of thee, we proclaim Him made known in two essences, in two sovereign wills, O Mother and Bride of God.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
Rising early at dawn we cry to Thee: Save us, O Lord, for Thou art our God, besides Thee we know no other.

*Troparion:*
Stretched on the rack and unceasingly cut by sharpness, O Mercurius, thou didst endure, enlivened by divine hopes.

*Troparion:*
Having strengthened thy heart with the spiritual rock, though weighed down with stones, thou wast not turned back, O glorious Mercurius.

*Troparion:*
Having become a partaker of the passions of thy Master, thou didst share in His glory and divine brightness.

*Theotokion:*
Put to death, O Virgin, the sin dwelling in me, having given birth to the Life that put death to death.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Celebrating this divine and all-honorable feast of the Mother of God, come, O ye divinely wise, let us clap our hands and glorify the God born of her.

*Troparion:*
Hearing the voice of the just, He heard the prayer of the righteous; therefore, as Thou art tenderhearted, Thou didst loose the barrenness of the infirm, and granted unto them the cause of joy.

*Troparion:*
The Lord, willing to make known His salvation to the nations, hath now received from men the Maiden who knew not wedlock, as a token of reconciliation and renewal.

*Troparion:*
As a house of holy grace, wherein lie the treasures of the unutterable divine Dispensation, O all-venerable one: in the temple thou didst partake of incorruptible sweetness.

*Troparion:*
Receiving thee, who art seen to be the Church, O Bride of God, the temple was illuminated and drew near to better things, beholding in thee the fulfillment of what was foretold.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
The abyss of sins and the storm of transgressions trouble me, and drag me into the deep of grievous despair; but stretch forth Thy strong hand to me as to Peter, O Helmsman, and save me!

*Troparion:*
Seeing thee wholly shining with beauty by the dawn of virginity, and reddened with martyr's blood, O maiden, the good and most pure Word settled thee in the heavenly bridal chambers.

*Troparion:*
By the Cross thou wast able to destroy the dominion of the tyrants, and having refuted the vanity of worldly wisdom, thou didst pour forth the dogmas of divinely inspired teaching, O greatly wise, ever-memorable Catherine.

*Troparion:*
Firmly enduring the pains of wounds, thou didst cast down to the earth him who of old by deceit drove Adam from the sweetness of Paradise, O all-glorious martyr, and thou wast crowned with the crowns of the Kingdom.

*Theotokion:*
By thy supplications, O Virgin Mother of God, make the Judge, Thy Son, merciful to me on the day of judgment, and make Him a deliverer from cruel things, O Mother; for in thee alone do I place my hopes.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
I will pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and to Him will I proclaim my griefs; for my soul is filled with evils, and my life hath drawn near unto Hades; and like Jonah I pray: Lead me up from corruption, O God!

*Troparion:*
The co-eternal Word enlivened thee, seeing thee enduring every kind of torture for His sake, O wise martyr; and through an angel He commanded thee to take courage, O Mercurius, and in no way to fear the resistance of the tyrants.

*Troparion:*
The multiform serpent was put to death, and trampled under the fair feet of the sufferer and noble warrior; for by voluntary impulse he entered into the wounds of torture unto death, filled with glory.

*Troparion:*
All-perfectly didst thou offer the disposition of thy heart to the Master, O martyr; and having for His sake endured crushings, as a victor thou wast crowned by Him, and now standest before Him in the heavens with all the martyrs, O Mercurius.

*Theotokion:*
By the angel's voice thou didst conceive the Angel of Great Counsel, O maiden; and incarnate from thy most pure blood, O all-blameless one, thou gavest birth to Him Who showed forth unto all the entrances of life, because of His ineffable mercy.

*Kontakion of the Saint, Tone 2. Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вышнихъ ищя):*
Form a sacred choir divinely now, ye lovers of the martyrs, honoring the all-wise Catherine; for in the stadium she proclaimed Christ, trampled the serpent, and subdued the intellect of the rhetoricians.[^1050]

*Ikos:*
Having received wisdom from God from childhood, O martyr, and having thoroughly learned all the external wisdom: having known therefrom the movement and creation of the elements according to reason, and having known Him Who from the beginning made these by His Word, she offered thanksgiving unto Him by night and by day; having cast down the idols and those who foolishly served them, and having subdued the intellect of the rhetoricians.[^1051]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The divinely wise served not the creation rather than the Creator, but having manly trampled upon the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, the all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers![^1052]

*Troparion:*
Behold, today a joyful spring hath shone forth unto the ends [of the earth], illuminating our soul and thoughts and mind with grace; let us be mystically banqueted today by the solemnity of the Mother of God.

*Troparion:*
Let all things bring gifts today unto the Queen, the Mother of God: heaven and earth, and the ranks of angels, and the multitude of men; and let them cry aloud: Into the temple are led joy and deliverance!

*Troparion:*
The scripture hath passed away, and the Law hath failed like a shadow, and the rays of grace have shone forth, when thou didst enter into the temple of God, O pure Virgin Mother, blessed therein.

*Troparion:*
Heaven and earth and the nether regions submit unto Thy birthgiving, O all-venerable one, as unto the Creator and God; and every earthly tongue confesses that the Lord hath appeared as the Savior of our souls.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

At the condescension of God, the fire was put to shame in Babylon of old; therefore the youths in the furnace, dancing with joyful step as in a meadow of flowers, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Boast of martyrs, thou wast a teacher of piety unto thy radiant Bridegroom, having brought a multitude of martyrs unto Christ; with whom thou criest, O all-praised one, singing: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Thy most wise word snatched many away from idol madness unto salvation, and showed them forth as light-bearing martyrs, crying with a loud voice with thee: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
The maiden following after thee was led to thee, beheaded with the sword, imitating thy most pure suffering; and crying to thee, her Creator, and saying: Blessed is the God of our fathers![^1053]

*Theotokion:*
The Holy of holies dwelt holily in thee, O pure Virgin Mother of God; incarnate from thee He is born in order to save those who cry in faith: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
The Hebrew children in the furnace boldly trampled upon the flame and changed the fire into dew, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Illuminated by the light of enlightenment from on high, O noble warrior, enlighten those who now hymn thee as they sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst sing to the Benefactor of all, inflamed with zeal for Him, O blessed one; and burned with physical fire, thou didst sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
They who offer honor to stones, having petrified senses, weighed down thy neck with a stone, O martyr, as thou didst cry, O Mercurius: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Mingling thy blood with the precious blood of the Master, the Lover of mankind, thou wast shown to be a partaker of His passions, crying, O Mercurius: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
The angelic ranks are astonished at the depth of thy mystery, O Mother of God; for God appeared incarnate from thee, unto Whom we sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Give ear, O maiden, pure Virgin, and let Gabriel declare the ancient, true counsel of the Most High: be ready for the reception of God, for through thee the Incomprehensible shall dwell with men. Therefore also rejoicing I cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Bringing the most pure temple into the house of God of old, Anna crying out in faith said to the priest: Receive now the child given me by God, and lead her into the temple of thy Creator, and rejoicing sing unto Him: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Beholding Anna of old, Zacharias said in the Spirit: Thou leadest the true Mother of Life, whom the prophets of God brightly proclaimed as the Mother of God, and how shall the temple contain her? Therefore, marveling, I cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
I was the handmaid of God, Anna answered him, calling upon Him in faith and prayer to receive the fruit of my travail; and having received her that was born, to bring her unto Him Who gave her. Therefore calling out I cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
A lawful deed in truth is this, the priest said unto her; but I marvel greatly at the strange matter, beholding her led into the house of God, who most gloriously surpasses the holy places by grace. Therefore also rejoicing I cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
Sevenfold did the Chaldean tyrant furiously kindle the furnace for the godly; but seeing them saved by a greater power, he cried to the Creator and Deliverer: Ye youths, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supreme exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Believing through thy teachings, the empress ran unto piety; and having firmly endured the sensation of pains, she was manifestly counted worthy of the heavenly, unfading Kingdom, crying to the Master: Ye priests, bless; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^1054]

*Troparion:*
With the martyrs let the petitions of the faithful be offered, for the passion-bearer stands before Christ, asking better things and intercessions of salvation for those who fervently celebrate her all-venerable and precious memory and faithfully sing: Ye people, supremely exalt Christ unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Having opened the doors of Paradise, the foremost of Bridegrooms receives thee, O all-wise one, and hath caused thee to dwell in the all-radiant bridal chamber, and shows thee forth as a partaker of the Kingdom and a companion of His passions. Standing before Him now as a King's daughter, brightly adorned, forget us not!

*Troparion:*
With subtle words the tyrant sought, and with coaxing speech the cruel one deceitfully flattered, hoping to weaken thy strength, O glorious one; but desiring to be betrothed unto Christ, Thou didst cry aloud to the Master: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Christ unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
More holy wast thou, O all-blameless Mother of God, than the otherworldly angelic ranks; for thou gavest birth to their Creator and Lord from a virginal and unwedded womb: in two natures, without confusion and without change, God incarnate in one Person.

*Another [Canon]. The same Heirmos:*
The choir of sufferers received thee as an addition, having become adorned and radiant with the honorable beauties of thy most pure sufferings and of thy pious and honorable witness; and now thou criest unceasingly: Ye priests, bless; ye people, supremely exalt Christ unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
In a godly-wise manner, O glorious one, didst thou finish the contest, and valiantly didst thou put the enemy to shame; and having taken the heavenly victory as a victor, thou now rejoicest with the angelic choirs. With them thou criest unceasingly: Ye priests, bless; ye people, supremely exalt Christ unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Having finished thy course by the sword, O all-blessed Mercurius, and having obtained the desired end that lay before thee, thou didst water the earth with the pourings of thy blood; and thy victorious and blessed body thou didst show forth whiter than snow, singing: Ye priests, bless; ye people, supremely exalt Christ unto the ages![^1055]

*Theotokion:*
As thou art the cause of our restoration, O most pure one, all we the faithful sing to thee: for beyond all cause thou gavest birth to God, the Cause of all, Who by His lovingkindness rebuilt the image that had been crushed by malice, O only most blessed and full of grace!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
As she is the animate Ark of God, let no hand of the profane in any way touch her; but let the lips of the faithful, unceasingly singing the voice of the angel to the Mother of God, cry aloud with joy: Truly thou art more exalted than all, O pure Virgin![^1056]

*Troparion:*
Having the beauty of soul-purity, O pure Mother of God, and being filled from heaven with divine grace, thou dost ever enlighten with the co-eternal Light those who cry with rejoicing: Truly thou art more exalted than all, O pure Virgin!

*Troparion:*
Thy wonder, O pure Mother of God, transcends the power of words; for in thee I contemplate a body beyond reason, not receiving the flow of sin; therefore thankfully I cry to thee: Truly thou art more exalted than all, O pure Virgin!

*Troparion:*
Most gloriously the Law prefigured thee, O pure one, as the tabernacle and the divine and the divine jar: a marvelous Ark, and the veil, and the rod, the indestructible temple, and the gate of God; therefore they teach us to cry unto thee: Truly thou art more exalted than all, O pure Virgin![^1057]

*Troparion:*
Singing of thee David proclaimed, calling thee the King's daughter, standing at the right hand of God in the beauty of virtues, seeing thee adorned; therefore prophesying he cried: Truly thou art more exalted than all, O pure Virgin![^1058]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
Heaven was amazed thereat, and the ends of the earth were astonished, that God hath appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens; therefore the hierarchies of angels and men magnify thee, O Mother of God.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast passed over into the light-bearing bridal chambers, adorned with bridal ornaments; having the virginal lamp in thy right hand, and holding in the other thy severed head; and now standing before Christ thy Bridegroom, preserve those who hymn thee![^1059]

*Troparion:*
Thy godly-wise prayer was accepted: for those who in faith name thy honorable name, O venerable one, the Master saves from temptations and grants good health, delivering from all manner of infirmities, both of soul and body; therefore rejoicing we call thee blessed, O Catherine.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast now arrived at the calm haven, having sailed across the worldly sea of tribulations favorably and lightly, O martyr, without being tempted [by disaster], O all-wise one: bringing unto Christ a manifold wealth, O virgin, a multitude of martyrs, O all-blessed Catherine.

*Troparion:*
Now keeping festival within the heavenly bridal chambers with virginal choirs, illuminated with martyr's rays, O all-wise Catherine, loose the bonds of my fallings, fervently entreating the Benefactor of all, for Whose sake thou didst pour forth thy blood.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst appear, O Virgin Mother of God, having supernaturally given birth in the flesh to the Good Word, Whom the Father poured forth from His heart before all ages as Good; Whom we now understand to be higher even than bodies, though He was clothed in a body.[^1060]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
Every hearing was terrified at the ineffable condescension of God: how the Most High voluntarily descended even unto the flesh, becoming man from a virginal womb; therefore, O most pure Mother of God, we the faithful magnify thee.

*Troparia of Ode 9 of the Canon:*
The purulent wounds of the martyrs now pour forth fragrance through grace, and by an ineffable word drive away our foul-smelling passions, and their bones pour forth waters of healings, and bedew the souls of those who sing of their marvelous deeds.

As a great pillar of Christ's Church, holily do we honor thee, as an unshakable wall, as a divine and unconquerable city, O martyr, as a mighty warrior of God the King of all, as a destroyer of enemies, as an intellectual and universal luminary.

Thou didst receive an angel of light as thy fellow companion unto suffering, O godly-wise one; therefore, though torn and scorched with torches, cruelly cut asunder and struck with the sword, thou wast not frightened, O most noble passion-bearer of Christ.

A day full of illumination, cheer, and joy has thy divine memory shone forth unto us who honor thee, O Martyr Mercurius; wherein remember us who celebrate thy memory, and deliver us from cruel temptations, tribulations, and passions.

*Theotokion:*
Illumine, O door of the Light, my soul blinded by passions, darkened by wicked thoughts, and in distress; and deliver me from temptations, tribulations, and sorrows, that I may glorify thee, the hope and confirmation of the faithful.

*Exapostilarion of the Saint, Tone 3, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋхо́мъ во ст҃или́щи):*[^1061]
Enkindled [with divine love], having rejected the worldly mind of women,[^1062] O all-honored Virgin Catherine, glory of passion-bearers: thou didst refute in God the cunning of the philosophers as being foolish prattle and fable, having truly acquired the all-undefiled Mother of God as thy helper.

*Glory, and now, of the Feast, Tone 2, Podoben: "As the disciples looked on" (Оучн҃кѡ́мъ зрѧ́щымъ):*
The angelic ranks and the choir of martyrs celebrate today with us, in the divine Entry of the Child of God and Mother of the Lord, born of Joachim and Anna, together with steadfast Mercurius and glorious Catherine; by whose prayers we pray that we may find remission of our many sins.

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4. Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ єси зна́менїе):*
As we celebrate the all-consecrated memory of thy honorable suffering, O all-praised Catherine, we glorify in unceasing voices Him Who granted thee steadfast endurance, and showed thee to be victorious, and gave thee speech that put in dread the rhetors: Jesus, the Lover of mankind, the Savior and the Lord.

O voluntary martyr, all-praised Catherine, having mightily rebuked the tormentor, and cast down the cruel frenzy of polytheism by the radiance of the knowledge of God and by divine grace; whence also, both as a martyr and as an undefiled virgin, Christ, the Savior of our souls, has crowned thee.

The grace of the Spirit, O all-praised Catherine, thou didst receive through the opening of thy mouth as a purification; by thine own manner of life and patient mind thou didst trample down the pride of the tormentors; and above bodily comeliness thou didst godly-wisely prefer the beauty of the soul, O adornment of sufferers.

*Glory, Tone 2. By Babylas the Monk:*[^1063]
Having learned an immaterial manner of life, and having arrived at the godless judgment-seat, thou didst take thy stand, O victorious and honorable Catherine, blossoming with the divine brightness; and clothed with divine power, thou didst scoff at the tormentor's command, and didst silence the foolish speeches of the rhetors, O much-suffering one.

*Both now, Tone 6. By Sergius the Hagiopolite:*[^1064]
Today, let the assemblies of the faithful having come together spiritually celebrate, and the Virgin Child of God and Theotokos, as she is led into the temple of the Lord, let us piously praise, who was forechosen from all generations to be the dwelling-place of Christ the King and God of all. Ye virgins, carrying tapers, go before her, honoring the honorable progression of the Ever-Virgin; ye mothers, having put away all sorrow, joyfully follow along with her who is becoming the Mother of God and the mediatress of the world's joy. Let us all therefore joyfully cry out with the angel: "Rejoice!" unto her that is full of grace, who ever prays for our souls.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме єѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Having kindled thee as a thrice-radiant light, O Theotokos, in the temple of glory, [He] sends thee heavenly food,[^1065] magnifying thee.

*Verse: Virgins shall be brought after her unto the King, her companions shall be brought unto Thee. [Ps. 44:15]*
From the root of David didst thou sprout forth, O Virgin; Gabriel, bringing thee joy, cried aloud: "Thou shalt give birth to God, O all-pure one!"

*Verse: They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing, they shall be led into the temple of the King. [Ps. 44:16]*
Blessed is the sacred and divine pair, Joachim and Anna, of whom the pure one was born; she has now been brought unto her Creator.

*Glory, and now, the same:*
O heavenly gates, receive the Virgin Mary, who knew not man, the pure Theotokos, from whom deliverance has come unto mankind.

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 7, and Ode 8,[^1066] on 4; and of the Saint, Ode 6. Prokeimenon, Tone 4: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel. [Ps. 67:36] Verse: In the churches bless ye God, the Lord from the fountains of Israel. [Ps. 67:27] Epistle to the Ephesians, Pericope 233 [Eph. 6:10-17]. Alleluia, Tone 1: The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them. [Ps. 33:18] Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 104 [Lk. 21:12-19]. Communion Verse: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous. [Ps. 32:1]*

*On the 25th Day of the Same Month.*
*Our fathers among the saints and hieromartyrs, Clement, Pope of Rome, and Peter of Alexandria.*
*Take note: On this day is the Apodosis of the Feast of the Entry of the Most Holy Theotokos.*[^1067]

*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѽ ди́внагѡ чꙋдесе́):*
Today, let us, the faithful, dance for joy, singing unto the Lord in psalms and hymns, and honoring His sacred tabernacle, the animate Ark that contained the uncontainable Word; for beyond nature she is brought unto the Lord as an infant in the flesh, and the great hierarch Zacharias receives her with gladness as the dwelling-place of God.

Today the animate temple of the holy glory of Christ our God, the only blessed and pure one among women, is brought into the temple of the Law to live in the Holy of Holies; and Joachim and Anna rejoice with her in the spirit, and the choirs of virgins sing unto the Lord, chanting in the manner of psalms and honoring His Mother.

Thou art the preaching of the prophets, the glory of the apostles, and the boast of the martyrs, and the renewal of all earthborn, O Virgin Mother of God; for through thee have we been reconciled unto God. Therefore do we honor thine entry into the temple of the Lord, and with the angel do we all cry out to thee in song: "Rejoice!", O all-pure one, being saved by thy prayers.

*Other Stichera of Saint Clement, Tone 2, Podoben:*

*Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
Having become a branch of the vine of life, O father and hierarch, thou didst bring forth by the Spirit fair clusters of dogmas, O all-wise one, which ever drip the saving wine of divine knowledge and gladden the hearts of all the pious who truly honor thee, O God-bearing and all-blessed Clement.

Having become a disciple of the pre-eminent Peter, O father, upon his rock thou didst build thyself as an honorable stone, O all-praised one; by the firmness of thy words thou didst completely overturn the edifice of polytheism, and didst erect divine temples in honor of the Trinity, for Whom thou didst struggle, O blessed one, and didst receive the crown of martyrdom.

Like a light-bestowing sun didst thou shine forth from the west, O father, illuminating the earth brightly with the beam of thy dogmas and thy wounds; and having reached the eastern lands, O thrice-blessed one, thou didst set when put to death, and didst shine forth, O Clement, unto Christ, being richly and unceasingly illuminated there by the rays through divine communion.

*Glory, and now, Tone 8:*[^1068]
After thy birth, O Bride of God and Sovereign Lady, thou didst come into the temple of the Lord to be reared in the Holy of Holies, as one sanctified. Then also Gabriel was sent unto thee, the all-undefiled, bringing thee food. All the heavenly hosts marvelled, beholding the Holy Spirit having taken up His abode in thee. Therefore, O all-pure and spotless Mother of God, who art glorified in heaven and on earth, save our race.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Feast, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*
Heaven and earth rejoice, beholding the noetic heaven approaching to be reared honorably in the divine house, the only and undefiled Virgin. Unto whom Zacharias, marveling, cried aloud: "O door of the Lord, I open unto thee the doors of the temple; rejoicing, dance for joy therein; for I know and have believed that the deliverance of Israel shall now manifestly come, and from thee God the Word shall be born, Who grants great mercy unto the world!"

*Verse: Virgins shall be brought after her unto the King, her companions shall be brought unto Thee. [Ps. 44:15]*
Anna, divine grace in truth, with gladness brings into the temple of God the pure Ever-Virgin given from grace, having summoned maidens carrying tapers to go before her, and saying: "Go, child, be an offering and a sweet-smelling incense unto Him Who gave thee; enter into the inaccessible places, and learn the mysteries; and prepare thyself to become a cheerful and fair dwelling-place of Jesus, Who grants great mercy unto the world!"

*Verse: They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing, they shall be led into the temple of the King. [Ps. 44:16]*
Within the temple of God, the temple that is to hold God, the all-holy Virgin, is dedicated, and maidens carrying tapers now go before her. The excellent pair of parents leaps for joy, Joachim and Anna dancing for gladness, because they gave birth to her who gave birth to the Creator; who, dancing in the divine tabernacles, and fed by an angel's hand, the all-undefiled, was shown to be the Mother of Christ, Who grants great mercy unto the world.

*Glory, and now, Tone 6:*
Today, let the assemblies of the faithful having come together spiritually celebrate, and the Virgin Child of God and Theotokos, as she is led into the temple of the Lord, let us piously praise, who was forechosen from all generations to be the dwelling-place of Christ the King and God of all. Ye virgins, carrying tapers, go before her, honoring the honorable progression of the Ever-Virgin; ye mothers, having put away all sorrow, joyfully follow along with her who is becoming the Mother of God and the mediatress of the world's joy. Let us all therefore joyfully cry out with the angel: "Rejoice!" unto her that is full of grace, who ever prays for our souls.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
O God of our fathers, Who dealest ever with us according to Thy meekness, take not Thy mercy away from us, but by their prayers guide our life in peace.

*Glory, and now, Troparion of the Feast: "Today is the prelude:" Leaf 115.*[^1069]

*Take note: It is fitting to know that if the Apodosis of the Feast of the Entry of the Most Holy Theotokos occurs on a Sunday, the office of Saint Peter is omitted and is sung whenever the ecclesiarch wills.*[^1070]
*On Saturday at Small Vespers, the Sunday stichera and those of the Theotokos according to custom. Troparion of the Resurrection and of the Feast.*
*At Great Vespers: After the customary Kathisma, on "Lord, I have cried", Sunday stichera, 3, and 1 Anatolian; and 3 Prosomoion of the Feast, Tone 1: "Today, ye faithful"; and 3 Prosomoion of Saint Clement. Glory, of the Feast, Tone 8: "After thy birth"; and now, the first Theotokion of the current Tone. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. At the Litiya, stichera of the Feast. Glory, and now, of the Feast. At the Aposticha, Sunday stichera. Glory, and now, of the Feast. At the blessing of the loaves: "O Theotokos and Virgin", thrice. Where there is no All-Night Vigil, we say* the troparion of the Resurrection. Glory, Troparion of Clement, Tone 4:
Most gloriously astonishing the ends of the universe with wonder-workings from God, O holy sufferer: beyond nature having caused a division in the compositions of the waters of the sea on thine honorable memory,[^1071] for those who ever run with fervor unto thy God-built church to thy miraculous relics; and after the procession of all the people, the sea marvelously forming a single passage, O most marvelous Clement, pray thou unto Christ God that our souls may be saved.
Both now, of the Feast.

*At Matins: At "God is the Lord", the troparion of the Resurrection twice; Glory, of Clement; and now, of the Feast. After the Kathismata: Sessional hymns of the Resurrection with their Theotokia. Polyeleos and the troparia: "The angelic assembly". Hypakoe of the Tone, and the Songs of Degrees. Prokeimenon and the Gospel of the Resurrection. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"; Psalm 50. Sticheron of the Resurrection. Canon of the Resurrection with its Heirmos on 4; and of the Theotokos on 2; and of the Feast of the First Tone on 4; and of Clement on 4. Katavasia: "Christ is born". After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Feast, and Ikos.*

*And Kontakion of Clement, Tone 2, Podoben: "The steadfast" (Тве́рдыя):*[^1072]
As a holily-vested vine of the divine vineyard wast thou shown unto all, dripping the sweetness of wisdom through thy prayers, O all-honored one, that we may offer unto thee, like a woven purple robe, a spiritual hymn, O holy Clement: save thy servants.

*And Sessional Hymn of the Saint; Glory, and now, of the Feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the Resurrection, and Ikos. At Ode 9, we chant the Magnifications. Photagogicon of the Resurrection; Glory, of the Saint; and now, of the Feast.*
*At the Praises: Stichera of the Resurrection, 4; and of the Feast with the Doxasticon on 4, with the refrains of the Feast; Glory, the Evangelical Sticheron; and now: "Most blessed art thou". Great Doxology. Troparion of the Resurrection only. Litanies and dismissal. And the First Hour. At the Hours, troparion of the Resurrection; Glory, of the Feast; and now, the Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father", the Kontakia of the Feast and of the Resurrection, alternating.*
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone on 6; and of the Feast, Ode 4 on 4. After the Entrance, troparion of the Resurrection, and of the Feast, and of the Saint. Then Kontakion of the Resurrection; Glory, of the Saint; and now, of the Feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel of the Tone and of the Feast. Communion Verse: "Praise ye the Lord", and of the Feast.*

*At Matins: At "God is the Lord", troparion of the Feast, twice; Glory, of the Saints:*
O God of our fathers:
*And now, of the Feast.*

*After the 1st Sticology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "The angelic choir" (Ли́къ а҆́гг҃льскїй):*
The righteous fruit of Joachim and Anna is offered unto God in the holy sanctuary, as an infant in the flesh, the nourisher of our Life, whom the sacred Zacharias blessed; let us all faithfully call her blessed as the Mother of God.
*Glory, and now: The same.*

*After the 2nd Sticology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆диви́сѧ їѡ́сифъ):*
Before conception, O pure one, thou wast sanctified unto God, and having been born on earth, thou hast now been offered as a gift unto Him, fulfilling the parental promise; and in the divine temple, as a divine temple in truth, having been given over purely from infancy with bright tapers, thou wast revealed as the receptacle of the unapproachable and divine Light. Truly great is thy procession, O only Bride of God and Ever-Virgin!
*Glory, and now: The same.*

*Then the Canon of the Feast with its Heirmos on 6; and both Canons of the Saints on 8. Canon of the Feast, Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us all sing a song of victory unto God, Who has wrought marvelous wonders with a high arm, and has saved Israel, for He has been glorified.

*Troparia:*
Let us assemble today to honor the Theotokos with hymns, and let us celebrate a spiritual feast; for into the temple she is offered unto God as a gift.

With hymns let us praise the glorious progression of the Theotokos; for today, as the temple of God, she is brought prophetically unto the temple, a priceless gift.

*Triadikon:*
O consubstantial Trinity: Father, and Word, and Holy Spirit! Thee do we faithfully glorify as the Creator of all, and unto Thee do we piously cry: "Save us, O God!"

*Theotokion:*
Having clothed Himself in purple from the crimson of thy blood, O all-pure one, the King and God, coming forth, has renewed all the human race by His tender compassion.

*Another Canon, of Saint Clement. A creation of Theophanes. Tone 8.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Traversing the water as dry land, and having escaped from the evil of Egypt, the Israelite cried aloud: "Unto our Deliverer and God let us sing!"

*Troparion:*
Having been instructed by the divine Peter, chief of the apostles, and having learned from him divine knowledge, O father, thou didst refute the deceit of the idols.

As a God-planted vine upon earth, bearing virtuous fruits of all-pious teachings, does Christ present Thee, Who truly is the flourishing Vineyard.

Unto all ends in truth has thy proclamation of divine victories gone forth, O wise Clement, and has enlightened all to glorify the Trinity in the unity of the Godhead.

*Theotokion:*
These prophetic proclamations concerning thee have truly received their fulfillment; for having conceived the Word without seed, O Parent of God, thou didst give birth to Him in the flesh.

*Another Canon, of Saint Peter, the acrostic whereof is: "I shall praise thrice-rich Peter."[^1073] A creation of Theophanes. The same Tone [Tone 8].*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us sing unto the Lord, Who led His people through the Red Sea, for He alone has been gloriously glorified.

*Troparia:*
Having thy dwelling in the most radiant habitations, grant me illumination by thy prayers, O all-blessed Peter.

Taught knowledge and adorned with the priesthood, O all-blessed Peter, thou didst offer thyself unto Christ by thy blood.

As an ornate adornment, as a precious dedication, thou wast granted by God unto the Church of Christ, O blessed one.

*Theotokion:*
O all-pure Theotokos, we sing of thee who beyond nature didst give birth to the incarnate, co-eternal, and transcendent Word.

*Katavasia: "Christ is born."*

*Ode 3 of the Feast. Heirmos:*
Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God, Who didst establish the second heaven above the waters, and didst found the earth upon the waters, O Almighty.

*Troparia:*
Let us celebrate, O lovers of the feasts, and rejoice together in spirit, being entertained today at the holy festival of the daughter of the King and Mother of our God.

Rejoice today, O Joachim, and be glad in spirit, O Anna, as ye bring unto the Lord her that was born of you, three years old, as a pure and all-undefiled heifer.

*Triadikon:*
Light is the Father, Light is His Son, Light is the Comforter Spirit; for as from one Sun the Trinity, shining forth, divinely illumines and preserves our souls.

*Theotokion:*
The prophets proclaimed thee, O pure one, to be the Ark of sanctification, the golden censer, and the lampstand, and the table; and we sing of thee as the tabernacle that held God.

*Ode 3 of the Canon to Saint Clement. Heirmos:*
Plant Thy fear, O Lord, in the hearts of Thy servants, and be Thou a confirmation unto us who truly call upon Thee.

*Troparia:*
Richly was the grace of the Spirit poured out upon thy lips, O wise one, wherewith thou didst enlighten all by thy divine teachings, and didst bring them unto Christ.

By the fire of abstinence didst thou burn up the fiery impulses of the passions, having made thyself a temple of the divine Spirit, O noble-minded father.

Ascending the mountain of divine virtues, and covered with the spiritual gloom, thou didst behold in thy pure soul the ineffable spiritual dawn.

*Theotokion:*
Ineffably didst thou conceive, O all-pure one, the Savior and Lord Who has delivered from cruel things us who truly call upon thee.

*Ode 3 of the Canon to Saint Peter. Heirmos:*
There is none holy as the Lord, and none righteous as our God, of Whom all creation sings: there is none righteous above Thee, O Lord.

*Troparia:*
Thou didst ascend, riding as upon a chariot by thy blood, O all-wise one, unto the heavens, whither our Forerunner Christ has entered, Who alone is sinless.

Thou didst forsake corruptible life and didst find immortal life, O blessed one, where, crowned, thou dancest for joy, praying that our souls may be saved.

Like a palm tree didst thou flourish most fruitfully, like a fruitful olive tree wast thou named, O God-inspired one, in the courts of the Lord, like myrrh and frankincense, and like sweetest-smelling ointment.

*Theotokion:*
As the saving gate and fair paradise, as the sacred cloud of the co-eternal Light, let us all sing unto the Virgin, saying unto her: "Rejoice!"

*Kontakion of the Hieromartyrs, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ дне́сь):*
As the unshakable and divine towers of the Church, the divine pillars of piety, truly mighty, O all-praised Clement together with Peter: by your prayers preserve all.

*Sessional Hymn of Saint Clement, Tone 8, Podoben: The same:*[^1074]
Thou hast shone forth like a ray of the sun, and shinest ever brightly upon all the world by thy teachings, O God-proclaimed, light-bearing Clement, boast of martyrs.

*Glory, of Saint Peter, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Having presided over the flock of the supreme tribunal of Christ, thou didst tend them upon life-giving pastures with thy most wise dogmas, having driven away heresy as a fierce wolf that had entered among them with godless teachings. Therefore didst thou also lay down thy life for them, and wast called a shepherd, as the Lord said: O blessed hierarch Peter, pray thou unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who lovingly honor thy holy memory.

*Both now, of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆диви́сѧ і҆ѡ́сифъ):*
The undefiled ewe-lamb and spotless bridal chamber, the Theotokos Mary, is gloriously led with gladness into the house of God; whom the angels of God faithfully escort,[^1075] and all the faithful ever call blessed, and thankfully sing unto her unceasingly with a great voice: "Thou art our glory and salvation, O all-undefiled one!"

*Ode 4 of the Feast. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing in spirit the incarnation of the Word, O Prophet Habakkuk, thou didst preach, crying aloud: "When the years draw near, Thou shalt be known; when the time is come, Thou shalt be shown. Glory to Thy power, O Lord!"

*Troparia:*
O Prophet Isaiah, prophesy unto us: who is the Virgin that has in her womb? She that sprouted from the root of Judah, and was born from King David, the glorious fruit of the holy seed.

Begin, ye virgins, and sing hymns, holding tapers in your hands, praising the procession of the pure Theotokos who is now coming into the temple of God, celebrating together with us.

*Triadikon:*
In three Persons, in one Nature, let us piously glorify the true God, of Whom the ranks and principalities of angels and archangels sing, as the Master of creation, and Whom men ever faithfully worship.

*Theotokion:*
Pray unceasingly, O all-holy, pure one, unto thy Son and God Whom thou didst bear in the flesh, to deliver all thy servants from the manifold snares of the devil, and from every temptation that befalls them.

*Ode 4 of the Canon to Saint Clement. Heirmos:*
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art my power, Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who, without leaving the bosom of the Father, hast visited our poverty. Therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: "Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!"

*Troparia:*
Coming from the west unto the east, O blessed one, thou wast united with the Apostle Peter, and enlightened by his divine splendors and teachings, together with him thou didst proclaim the saving word, and didst traverse all the western region.

Another Moses wast thou, O wise Clement, setting forth the divine laws unto all, and the sacred and writing sacred teachings, and thou orderest all the Church's fullness.[^1076] Therefore, having thee as lawgiver and teacher, all of us honor thee with faith.

*Troparion:*
Cleansed by ascetic labors, thou didst appear as a hierarch, O blessed one, leading all unto the pious faith of Christ by thy divine narrations; and having suffered lawfully, a crown was woven corresponding to thy suffering, O ever-memorable one.

*Theotokion:*
With God we have gained thee as protectress, for thou wast the Mother of God, of the Creator and Fashioner, Who took our likeness, O all-undefiled one, and saved it from corruption and death, and glorified it with divine glory.

*Ode 4 of the Canon to Saint Peter. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing Thee, O Word, with eyes divine from the overshadowing mountain, of the only Theotokos, when Thou wast about to become incarnate, the prophet with fear gave glory to Thy power.

*Troparia:*
Walking the path of virtues, O father, thou didst attain the mansions on high, O God-bearer, adorned with the anointing of priesthood and shining with the blood of martyrdom.

With the showers of the streams of thy blood, O blessed one, thou didst quench the furnace of deceit and didst destroy the darkness of the persecutors, O glorious hieromartyr.

A new Peter didst thou appear unto us, truly shining with apostolic gifts: a sacred celebrant and witness of the sufferings of thy Master, O all-wealthy one.

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth to the Fullness of all good things, fulfill our petitions, O Virgin, asking for us deliverance from sins, and enlightenment, and great mercy.

*Ode 5 of the Feast. Heirmos:*
Shine forth upon us Thy radiant, co-eternal light, who rise early to the judgments of Thy commandments, O Master, Lover of mankind, Christ our God.

*Troparia:*
Let us carry light, all we the orthodox, running together and glorifying the Mother of God, for today she is brought unto the Lord as an acceptable sacrifice.

Let the Forefather rejoice today, O Lady, and let her that bare thee be glad together with thy father, for their fruit is offered unto the Lord.

*Triadikon:*
Glorifying the pre-beginningless and co-eternal one Godhead, let us worship: in three Persons indivisible in essence, and equal in honor in glory.

*Theotokion:*
As a calm haven and an invincible rampart have we gained thy prayer in tribulations, O Mother of God, ever delivered from misfortunes and afflictions.

*Ode 5 of the Canon to Saint Clement. Heirmos:*
Enlighten us by Thy commandments, O Lord, and by Thy high arm grant us Thy peace, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparia:*
Walking in the light of the commandments of the Lord, a true and unfeigned child of His didst thou appear, O blessed one.

Thou didst renounce attachment unto that which is on earth, O hierarch, that thou mightest receive the future blessing and the splendors of the glory of Christ.

Adorned with the splendors of martyrdom, thou now standest with the angels, praying unto the Master for those who sing of thee.

*Theotokion:*
O Mother of God, deliver by thy prayers from tribulations those who sing of thee with faith, O Virgin, for we know thee as our protectress, O pure one.

*Ode 5 of the Canon to Saint Peter. Heirmos:*
Rising early, we cry unto Thee, O Lord, save us: for Thou art our God, and we know no other besides Thee.

*Troparia:*
Having mounted upon the rock of faith, O passion-bearer, thou didst remain unbent amidst adverse temptations.

With the fiery sword of the Holy Spirit, O hierarch, by divine judgment thou didst slay Arius the speaker of bane.

Strengthened by the might of the Savior, O glorious one, thou didst trample down the enemy's strength and power.

*Theotokion:*
We sing of thee as Virgin after childbearing, O Theotokos, for thou didst bear in the flesh the God-Word unto the world.

*Ode 6 of the Feast. Heirmos:*
Imitating the Prophet Jonah, I cry aloud: Deliver my life from corruption, O Good One, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: Glory to Thee!

*Troparia:*
Let us, the faithful, celebrate the spiritual feast of the Mother of God, singing piously: for she is more holy than the heavenly[^1077] minds.

With spiritual crowns let us, the faithful, praise the Mother of Light, for today she has appeared unto us, going before into the temple of God.

*Triadikon:*
Father, and Son, and right Spirit, three-hypostatic Unity, and undivided Trinity, have mercy upon those who worship Thy divine dominion.

*Theotokion:*
In thy womb was He contained Whom nothing can contain, having become the Mother of God; from thee He came forth, O all-pure one, twofold in nature, God and man.

*Ode 6 of the Canon to Saint Clement. Heirmos:*
Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and bring me up from the depths of evils, I pray, for unto Thee have I cried; and give ear unto me, O God of my salvation!

*Troparia:*
Kindled with zeal[^1078] for the love of the Lord, O wise one, Thou didst mightily refute the deceit of idols by verbal contentions and by miraculous manifestations, O all-praised one.

Thou didst watchfully preserve the eye of thy heart, in no wise slumbering unto malice, O glorious one, ascending by divine ascents unto the summit of virtues.

As an honorable hierarch who hast received power from the Savior Christ to bind and to loose sins, loose the debt of my many transgressions, leading me unto repentance.

*Theotokion:*
By thy supplications, O pure one, snatch me away from cruel misfortunes and calamities, and deliver me who pray to thee: for thou art an unbreakable rampart, and a haven, and a protection, and an unconquerable fortress.

*Ode 6 of the Canon to Saint Peter. Heirmos:*
Grant me a radiant robe, Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, O most merciful Christ our God.

*Troparia:*
Having lived chastely and righteously unto God, thou didst receive a blessed end from Him, O all-blessed Peter.

An all-perfect and acceptable sacrifice didst thou offer thyself, O marvelous Peter, unto God Who became a sacrifice for thy sake.

Filled with spiritual words, thou wast an instrument moved by the Spirit, singing of things ineffable, O speaker of divine words.

*Theotokion:*
O thou who alone by the Word didst bear the Word in the flesh, deliver our souls, we pray, from the snares of the enemy.

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*
The all-pure temple of the Savior, the most precious bridal chamber and Virgin, the sacred treasury of the glory of God, today is led into the house of the Lord, bringing with her the grace which is in the divine Spirit; whom the angels of God praise: This is the heavenly tabernacle.

*Ikos:*
Beholding the grace of the ineffable and divine mysteries of God manifested in the Virgin and plainly fulfilled, I rejoice; and I am at a loss to comprehend the strange and ineffable manner: how the chosen pure one alone has appeared above all creation, both visible and intelligible? Therefore, wishing to praise her, I am greatly filled with awe in mind and word. Yet daring, I proclaim and magnify: This is the heavenly tabernacle!

*Ode 7 of the Feast. Heirmos:*
The furnace, O Savior, was bedewed, and the youths, dancing for joy, sang:

...O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparia:*
Let us keep festival today, ye lovers of feasts, let us sing unto the pure Mother of God, worthily honoring Joachim and Anna.

Prophesy, O David, saying again:[^1079] "Virgins shall be brought after thee, they shall be brought unto thee into the temple of the Queen-Mother."

*Triadikon:*
Let us glorify the undivided Trinity, let us sing of the one Godhead, the Word together with the Father, and the all-holy Spirit.

*Theotokion:*
Pray unto the Lord Whom thou didst bear, for He is compassionate by nature, O Mother of God, to save the souls of those who sing of thee.

*Ode 7 of the Canon to Saint Clement. Heirmos:*
The pious youths in Babylon bowed not down unto the golden image, but bedewed in the midst of the fiery furnace, they sang a hymn, saying: O Thou Who art exalted above all, the God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou!

*Troparia:*
Like the dawn didst thou shine forth, enlightening all the ends of the earth and driving away the deceitful night of idolatrous godlessness, O God-proclaimed one: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Desiring to save him through thy prayers, God granted sight unto Sisinnius,[^1080] opening the eyes both of his soul and body, O father; wherefrom he is enlightened by the divine font.

Thou pourest forth streams of healings from thy divine reliquary, O glorious Clement, ever delivering from many passions those who have recourse unto thee, and who sing: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
It was fitting for Him Who was to be incarnate without seed to come forth from thee, O all-pure Virgin, for thou didst grow up pure and greater than all; therefore do we unceasingly cry unto thee: Blessed is the fruit of thy womb!

*Ode 7 of the Canon to Saint Peter. Heirmos: The same:*
Adorned with a life befitting God and enlightened with divine light, thou didst enter with rejoicing into the inaccessible heights of heaven, crying, O wise one, unto Him Who made thee: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*
That thou mightest graciously please Christ God, O God-blessed one, thou didst willingly deliver thyself into the hands of the lawless, singing, O all-wealthy one: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

All-enlightened, thou wast counted worthy to see Christ showing Thee His robe, cruelly torn, which was woven from above,[^1081] O venerable one, crying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
As one holy and pure didst thou receive in thy womb the Word being incarnate; but pray Thou Him to cleanse my soul and body of sins, O all-pure one, who run unto thee with pure faith.

*Ode 8 of the Feast. Heirmos:*
Him of Whom angels and all the hosts are filled with awe as Creator and Lord, praise, ye priests, glorify, ye youths, bless, ye peoples, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
Today Joachim rejoices brightly, and blameless Anna brings unto the Lord God as a sacrifice the holy daughter given unto her from the promise.

The holy ones, David and Jesse, boast, and Judah is honored: for from their root has sprouted the fruit, the pure Virgin, from whom was born the pre-eternal God.

*Triadikon:*
Let the Trinity be sung, the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the undivided Unity, the one Godhead holding all creation in Its palm, unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*
The beginningless Word begins in the flesh, born as He willed, both God and man, from the Maiden-Virgin: refashioning us who had fallen before, by reason of His extreme loving-kindness.

*Ode 8 of the Canon to Saint Clement. Heirmos:*
When the musical instruments sounded in unison, and the countless peoples worshiped the image in Dura, the three youths, refusing to obey, praised the Lord and glorified Him unto all ages.

*Troparia:*
Having become a disciple of Peter and imitating his divine ways, O Clement, sufferer: therefore didst thou truly show thyself the successor of his throne, enlightening all creation.

Having mystically reddened thy lips with the cup of wisdom, O Clement, thou didst pour forth an abyss of divine teachings, drowning demonic passions and welling forth salvation for the souls of men.

Having acquired thy divine statutes as a most precious adornment, the Church boasts in thee, and stirs up all to revere thy memory with faith unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*
O Mary, Virgin Theotokos, who didst bear God in the flesh as Savior unto men: save those who sing of thy childbearing with faith and supremely exalt it unto all ages.

*Ode 8 of the Canon to Saint Peter. Heirmos:*
Praise ye the Lord Who was glorified on the holy mountain, and Who in the bush by fire revealed the mystery unto Moses as a prefiguration, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

*Troparia:*
Thou didst extinguish the ruinous poison[^1082] of Arius's most wicked blasphemy, cutting him off from the assembly of the faithful and driving him away from the ecclesiastical sheepfolds, O God-wise one.

Peter appeared as the leader of the angelic choir, the divine prince, but thou wast a pillar of martyrs, O all-wise Peter, God-bearer, and a celebrant of the divine mysteries.

Having been taught the knowledge of future things by divine inspiration, O speaker of divine words, and having foreknown thy departure from the earth by martyrdom, unto Christ the Lord of glory on high, unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*
Sing ye unto the Lord Who took up His abode in the womb of the Virgin, and from her, awesomely and beyond word, renewed ancient Adam, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

*At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable", but we sing the Refrain of the Feast:*
*Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, her that is brought into the temple of the Lord and blessed by the hands of the priests.

*Ode 9 of the Feast. Heirmos:*
The light-bearing cloud, wherein the Master of all came down from heaven as rain upon the fleece, and was incarnate for our sake, becoming man, the Beginningless One: we all magnify as the pure Mother of our God.

*Unto these troparia, the same refrain is sung:*

*Troparia:*
From the righteous Joachim and Anna came forth the child of God, Mary, the fruit of promise; and as an acceptable censer, being an infant in the flesh, she is brought into the holy sanctuary, as holy, to dwell in the Holy of Holies.

Her that is an infant in nature, yet has appeared beyond nature as the Mother of God, let us praise with hymns; for today she is brought into the temple of the Law unto the Lord, as an odor of sweet fragrance of the righteous, as spiritual fruit.

*Triadikon:*
*Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, the dominion of the three-hypostatic and undivided Godhead.
The three-hypostatic Nature and undivided Glory, praised unceasingly in one Godhead in heaven and on earth, the inseparable Trinity let us glorify, piously worshiping the Father with the Son and the Spirit.

*Theotokion:*
*Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, the all-pure Virgin Theotokos, more honorable and more glorious than the heavenly hosts.
Those who have recourse with faith beneath thy compassionate tender mercy, and who piously worship thy Son, O Virgin Mother of God, as God and Lord of the world: pray thou to deliver them from corruption, and misfortunes, and all manner of temptations.

*Ode 9 of the Canon to Saint Clement. Heirmos:*
Truly we confess thee as the Theotokos, who are saved by thee, O pure Virgin, O pure one, with the bodiless choirs magnifying thee.

*Troparia:*
Having finished thy course through many struggles, and having kept the faith of Christ without doubting, thou hast been adorned with a righteous crown.

As Thou didst of old save the child[^1083] kept in the sea during the yearly cycle, O martyr of Christ: so also save me from the depths of sin.

Deliver from afflictions, and misfortunes, and sorrows those who honor thee with love, O passion-bearer Clement, praying unto Christ the Creator.

*Theotokion:*
Fill my heart with joy, O Virgin, who didst receive the Fullness of joy, doing away with the sorrow of sin.

*Ode 9 of the Canon to Saint Peter. Heirmos:*
That which was revealed on the mountain unto the lawgiver in the fire and the bush, the childbearing of the Ever-Virgin for our salvation as believers, with unceasing hymns do we magnify.

*Troparia:*
Let us sing of the marvelous Peter, foreordained to serve sacredly as hierarch, who gloriously received the end of the priesthood, and imitated the passion of Christ.

Let us sing of the God-bearing Peter, strengthened by the rod of the power of the Lord, who ministered as priest and was consecrated as priest, and offered himself as a sacrifice unto Christ.

Let us sing of God-acceptable Peter, who is completely mingling with the threefold ray and enjoying its most radiant illumination, and asking salvation for us.

Thou givest salvation abundantly unto my soul, for as high priest thou hast authority to bind and to loose the guilts of transgressions by thy most sacred supplications.

*Theotokion:*
Thou art our weapon and rampart, O Theotokos; thou art the protectress of those who have recourse unto thee; thee do we now stir up unto prayer, that we may be delivered from our enemies.

*Exapostilarion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены́ оу҆слы́шите):*
Now has an auspicious day appeared unto us, having the sacred successors of the sacred apostles, Peter together with Clement, the preachers of the faith and invincible martyrs, whose yearly memory all of us faithfully celebrate.

*Glory, both now, of the Feast:*
Her whom the company of prophets foretold of old as the jar, the rod, the tablet, and the unhewn mountain: Mary the Maiden of God, let us faithfully praise; for today she is led into the Holy of Holies to be brought up for the Lord.

*At the Praises, 6 Stichera: 3 of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*

Light-bearing virgins, escorting the Maiden brightly, truly prophesy by the Spirit that which is to come: for being the Mother of God, the temple of God is led into the temple with virginal glory, being an infant.

From the holy promise, a glorious fruit, the Theotokos truly appeared unto the world as higher than all; who, being piously brought into the temple of God, fulfills the vow of her parents, preserved by the divine Spirit.

Nourished by heavenly bread, O Virgin, faithfully in the temple of the Lord, thou didst bear unto the world the Bread of Life, the Word: unto Whom, as a chosen and all-undefiled temple, thou wast mystically betrothed in the Spirit, betrothed unto God and the Father.

*And 3 of Saint Peter, Tone 4, Podoben: The same:*
The consubstantiality of the transcendent Trinity, as of an uncreated Unity, O all-wise, all-blessed one: thou didst cast down Arius, showing us the indivisibility of the Son, as being of the same Godhead with the Father and the Spirit.

The murderous assault of the persecutors has ceased, the outpouring of blood has now come to an invisible end; both were sealed, O wise Peter, by thy sacred witness, as the flow of blood once ceased for Moses' child through the flint of Zipporah.[^1084]

Having lived as a shepherd, O hieromartyr of Christ, thou didst bravely display the struggles of martyrdom, receiving a single crown through both, adorned by both: by the priesthood and by the pains of suffering. Therefore pray thou that we may be saved.

*Glory, Tone 4. Idiomelon:*
Anointed by the hand of God unto the priesthood, namesake of the supreme Apostle, and partaker in his deeds: thou didst nourish the rational sheep with evangelical pastures, as a wise and true shepherd, and didst worthily appear as the successor of Mark, O passion-bearer; by thine own blood thou didst finish the course of faith, sacrificing thyself for the people and being conformed unto Christ, praying for our souls.

*Both now, of the Feast, Tone 2:*
Today the all-undefiled Virgin is brought into the temple, into the dwelling-place of God the King of all and the Nourisher of all our life. Today the most pure sanctuary, as a three-year-old heifer, is led into the Holy of Holies. Let us cry aloud unto her like the angel: Rejoice, thou who alone art blessed among women!

*Great Doxology. And Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Feast* from both canons of the Feast, Ode 9, on 8.[^1085] After the Entrance, the Troparion of the Feast, and of the Saints. Glory, Kontakion of the Saints; Both now, of the Feast. Prokeimenon, the Hymn of the Theotokos, Tone 3: "My soul doth magnify the Lord." Verse: "Because He hath regarded the lowliness of His handmaiden." Prokeimenon of the Saints, Tone 7: "Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones." Epistle of the Feast, to the Hebrews, section 320 [Heb. 9:1–7]. And of the Saints, to the Philippians, section 246 [Phil. 3:20–4:3]. Alleluia, Tone 8: "Give ear, O daughter, and see." Gospel of the Feast, Luke, section 54 [Lk. 10:38–42, 11:27–28]. Of the Saints, Matthew, section 31 [Mt. 9:9–13]. Communion Hymn: "I will take the cup of salvation." And of the Saints: "In everlasting memory shall the righteous be."

*On the 26th Day of the Same Month.*
*Commemoration of our Venerable Father Alypius the Stylite:*
*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Octoechos, or of the Theotokos; then of the Saint, Tone 4, Podoben: "All-praised martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*

All-blessed Alypius, from thy youth thou didst dedicate thy life unto Christ our God, by Whom being strengthened, thou didst subdue bodily passions unto the mind, subjecting the worse unto the better. Therefore pray thou that He grant unto our souls peace and great mercy.

O God-wise Alypius, Thou didst appear as a most great luminary, enlightening all under the sun with the rays of miracles and by divine deeds. Therefore after thy dormition, the never-setting Light received thee. Therefore pray Thou that He grant unto our souls peace and great mercy.

Thou wast an unshakable pillar of monks, O wise one, standing firm upon a pillar, afflicted by heat and frost, and by many fasts. Therefore thou didst also receive the divine gifts of the Spirit, to heal sicknesses and to drive away the most cruel passions. And now pray thou that He grant unto our souls peace and great mercy.

*Glory, both now, Theotokion, Podoben: The same:*
Rejoice, bush unconsumed,[^1086] who truly didst bear the Angel of Great Counsel, our Joy! Rejoice, O Maiden, the good pleasure of the honorable Trinity! Rejoice, confirmation of earthly ones! Rejoice, who didst bud forth the untilled Ear of wheat of paradise, the King and Lord, having escaped the malice of that sprout!

*Staurotheotokion, Podoben: The same:*
When the ewe-lamb and undefiled Lady saw her Lamb upon the Cross having neither form nor beauty, "Woe is me!" she cried, lamenting: "Whither has Thy beauty set, O sweetest One? Where is Thy comeliness? Where is the beaming grace of Thy countenance, O my most beloved Son?"

*Troparion of the Venerable One, Tone 1:*
Thou wast a pillar of endurance, having emulated the forefathers, O venerable one: Job in sufferings, Joseph in temptations, and while in the body living the life of the bodiless, O Alypius our father: pray thou unto Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*At Matins, both Canons of the Octoechos; and of the Venerable One on 4. Its acrostic:*
Rejoicing I praise the pains of Alypius. By Joseph.[^1087]

*Tone 5.*
*Ode 1 of the Canon to Saint Alypius. Heirmos:*
Unto Him Who shatters battles with a high arm, Christ Who shook horse and rider into the Red Sea and saved Israel who sang a song of victory.

*Troparia:*
Filled with grace, fill my soul with joy to praise thy life and conversation, O Alypius, by which, having labored, thou didst gladden all the angels.

As another Samuel did God sanctify thee from thy mother's womb,[^1088] O blessed Alypius, and made thee, O glorious one, to foresee future things as a divine prophet.

That God might reveal the brightness which Thou wouldst possess in the end, having struggled well, He filled the chamber of her that bare thee, O venerable one, with divine light beyond understanding.[^1089]

*Theotokion:*
The saying of the honorable prophet has received its end: for behold, the Virgin has borne God in the flesh, Who refashions men who were formerly crushed by sins and transgressions.

*Ode 3 of the Canon to Saint Alypius. Heirmos:*
Thou Who didst establish the earth upon nothing by Thy command,[^1090] and didst suspend its weight unsupported: establish Thy Church upon the immovable rock of Thy commandments, O Christ, Who alone art good and the Lover of mankind!

*Troparia:*
Placed like a lamp upon the lampstand of noble action by thy radiant virtues, O father, every soul that faithfully comes unto thee thou didst enlighten with pious wisdom, delivering it from the darkness of sin.

*Troparia:*
Directing the holy movements of thy mind unto the keeping of the divine laws of the Spirit, thou didst appear as an angel upon earth: having embraced the angelic life while in the flesh, O God-bearing father Alypius.

Wisely turning thy back upon worldly things,[^1091] O Alypius, thou didst appear as a solitary, and didst zealously enter upon the arena of ascetic life, showing forth thy heart as a dwelling of the Spirit, O venerable one.

*Theotokion:*
O pure Virgin, palace of the Word: show my soul to be a dwelling of the Spirit, and with the water of the life-originating spring give drink unto me who am burned by the heat of sin, that as is meet I may glorify thee.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
By the brightness of faith and by active light, thou didst truly appear equal to the angels upon earth, O venerable Alypius; thou didst courageously manifest the fortitude of thy mind, having conquered the assault of passions by fasting. Therefore, even after thy demise, being alive, pray thou that we may be saved.

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
O all-undefiled Virgin, who didst bear the pre-eternal God: together with the bodiless hosts unceasingly beseech Him to grant remission of transgressions and correction of life unto us before the end, who sing of thee with faith and love as is meet, O only all-hymned one.

*Staurotheotokion:*
O all-blameless Virgin, Mother of Christ God, a sword pierced thy most holy soul when thou didst behold thy Son and God voluntarily crucified; Whom cease not to implore, O blessed one, to grant us forgiveness of transgressions.

*Ode 4 of the Canon to Saint Alypius. Heirmos:*
Perceiving Thy divine condescension, Habakkuk cried out with trembling unto Thee, O Christ, with foresight: For the salvation of Thy people, to save Thine anointed ones, art Thou come.

*Troparia:*
Having embraced true love and wisdom,[^1092] faith, and steadfast hope, and an undefiled conversation, O father, thou wast well-pleasing unto Christ.

Standing upon the pillar, unmoved by contrary assaults, thou didst conquer the host of demons, and wast an unshakable confirmation for those who are tossed, O all-blessed one.

Having been filled with divine waters, thou didst bedew souls that were wasted by the heat of cruel sin, O God-wise, all-wealthy Alypius.

Thou didst appear truly fearsome and unapproachable unto all demons, striking them down with the wound of thy sacred prayers and driving them far away, O Alypius.

*Theotokion:*
Heal the passions of my soul, and enlighten my mind and my heart, O Lady, who didst bear the Giver of light, Christ the all-good God.

*Ode 5 of the Canon to Saint Alypius. Heirmos:*
Thou Who deckest Thyself with light as with a garment, unto Thee I rise early, and unto Thee I cry: Enlighten my darkened soul, O Christ, as Thou alone art tenderhearted!

*Troparia:*
Having committed thyself wholly unto the Almighty, standing for years without a roof, O father, suffering intensely from rain and heat, thou didst endure with zeal.

Exercising thyself in hymns and supplications, O venerable one, through purity of mind thou didst receive the grace of the thrice-radiant illumination, and didst flash forth the light of healings.

Having enclosed thy body upon the pillar, thou didst permit thy mind to journey unhindered unto Him Whom thou didst desire, O father, being filled with light.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst bear the holy God, Who became man through tender mercy, O holy Maiden, Who sanctifies those who in faith and fear sanctify themselves unto Him.[^1093]

*Ode 6 of the Canon to Saint Alypius. Heirmos:*
Raging with a soul-corrupting tempest, O Master Christ, calm Thou the sea of passions, and lead me up from corruption, as Thou art tenderhearted!

*Troparia:*
Openly striking thee with stones as thou didst keep thy standing upon the pillar, the spirits of malice in no wise shook thee, the firm rock.

Patiently didst thou endure, O venerable one, for the Lord granted Thee true endurance, and delivered Thee from all hardships.

Most gloriously, O venerable one, a light was seen above[^1094] the pillar, daily enlightening thy spiritual senses, O wonderworker.

*Theotokion:*
All of us have thee as a strong consolation in affliction, and a refuge, and a sure protection, O Theotokos: save thy servants from misfortunes!

*Kontakion, Tone 8. Podoben: "As the first-fruits" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ нача́тки):*
As the cause of virtues and the adornment of ascetics, the Church glorifies thee today and sings of thee, O Alypius. By thy prayers grant unto those who honor thy valiant deeds and struggles with love, deliverance from cruel transgressions, as one of like name.[^1095]

*Ikos:*

Come, ye priests, kings, and princes, monastics and all God-wise people, let us marvel at the divine and angel-like life of Alypius, and let us imitate his deeds, that by his supplications we lovers of the feasts may also be accounted worthy of his portion: for he sings a new[^1096] song grieflessly unto God, as one of like name.

*Ode 7 of the Canon to Saint Alypius. Heirmos:*
The supremely exalted Lord of the fathers quenched the flame and bedewed the youths as they sang in unison: Blessed art Thou, O God!

*Troparia:*
Most patient and steadfast Alypius, being tormented by winter's cold for many years, was most gloriously warmed by the heat of the Spirit.

Having thy conversation in the heavenly heights, thou didst take no thought for the body as being subject to corruption; and while it was rotting away, thou wast unconcerned about sufferings.
