Having rejected all voluptuousness, O father, contending against winter and burning heat, thou didst suffer without a roof, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
The Incomprehensible One took flesh, endowed with mind and soul, from thee, O Ever-Virgin, to save those who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God!

*Ode 8 of the Canon to Saint Alypius. Heirmos:*
Unto Thee, the Creator of all, the youths in the furnace, having woven a universal choir, sang: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
A new Samuel, foreseeing the future through purity of mind, thou didst appear, O Alypius, foretelling unto all, as a prophet of God, the things revealed unto thee by the Lord, O father.

The light-radiant pillar of the Church, the unshakable rampart, the indestructible wall of all men who have believed in God, Christ's favorite, Alypius: let him be honored!

Thou didst fall asleep well with the righteous sleep due unto all, O father, having first put to sleep manifold passions[^1097] by prayers and vigils; therefore, having thee now as a sleepless advocate, we are enriched.

*Theotokion:*
Thy childbearing has made barren the sin born through the serpent's malice, O Virgin, who alone didst abolish the curse; therefore do we honor thee unto all ages.

*Ode 9 of the Canon to Saint Alypius. Heirmos:*
Rejoice, O Isaiah! The Virgin had in her womb, and bare a Son, Emmanuel, both God and man; Orient is His name: Whom magnifying, we bless the Virgin.

*Troparia:*
Thy sacred life appeared unto Christ from swaddling clothes, shining with the light of virtues, O blessed one; and precious was thy death in the sight of God, O father Alypius, leader of monastics.

As a most radiant luminary thou dost enlighten the whole earth, driving away wicked passions and dispelling the darkness of sin, and enlightening with the divine brightness of healings those who sing of thee.

Thou didst accomplish thy standing upon the pillar for fifty-three years, O wise one: suffering most zealously as an athlete, and unflaggingly tormented by winter, frost, and heat, O father.

Thy holy memory, in the Holy Spirit, has encompassed[^1098] us, O wise one, who sacredly celebrate it and with faith praise thee therein, O father, as the protector and advocate of our souls.

*Theotokion:*
Grant me enlightenment, who am in the darkness of passions, wretched and sinful, and deliver me from evil deeds and from the flame that lies before me, O all-pure Lady, protectress of those who sing of thee.

*Exapostilarion. Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены́ оу҆слы́шите):*
Thou didst accomplish struggles surpassing man, O venerable father, by the power of Christ: for fifty-three years didst thou stand upon the pillar, O wise Alypius, tormented on all sides; and now, O blessed one, thou hast found the ultimate end of all good things.

*Theotokion:*
Thou art my protectress, O pure one, and a firm refuge; thou art my defense and shelter, and falling down before thee I cry: Deliver me from my sicknesses, as being able to do all things, and snatch me from the eternal fire, O Virgin, who place my hope in thee.

*On the 27th Day of the Same Month.*
*Commemoration of the Holy Great-Martyr James the Persian:*
*And of our Venerable Father Palladius:*
*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Martyr James, on 6, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*

Leaving behind the fair things of the world, nobility of birth, riches, and beauty, and casting away every earthly sensation, and being broken in pieces in body in body, by the imitation of His passions thou didst joyfully follow Christ, O James; for as a partaker in sufferings, so in truth hast thou become a partaker of glory and of the Kingdom now.

Having the members of thy flesh reaped, and enduring unbearable pains and wounds, O praiseworthy martyr of Christ, James, and having courageously trampled upon the ferocity of the torturers, thou didst receive a priceless crown of victory; wherewith now adorned, O blessed one, thou standest before the divine throne of thy Master, together with those who suffered with thee.

Having boldness toward Christ, thou dost warmly intercede for all who celebrate thy venerable feast with faith, O ever-memorable martyr, delivering them from misfortunes, freeing them from passions, rescuing them from every assault of cruel things, and granting salvation unto souls through thy divine prayers, that we may glorify thy radiant struggles.

*Glory, Tone 5:*
Thou didst astonish all, O James, by patiently enduring in torments; for when thy fingers, hands, and arms were cut off, and likewise thy feet and legs even unto the thighs, thou didst endure. At the last, as thou wast praying, they also cut off thy venerable head, O much-suffering martyr: cease not to pray unto Christ for us, that our souls may find mercy.

*Both now, Theotokion, or Staurotheotokion, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*
When the ewe-lamb of old beheld her Lamb hastening unto the slaughter, she followed Him zealously, crying aloud these things unto Him: "Whither art Thou going, O my sweetest Child, Christ? For what cause dost Thou run this swift race so unsluggishly, O long-suffering One? O Jesus most desired, sinless, most merciful Lord, give a word unto Thy handmaiden, O my most beloved Son! Overlook not in silence,[^1099] O compassionate One, her that gave Thee strange birth, O all-merciful God, Who grantest great mercy unto the world!"

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Octoechos.*
*Glory of the Martyr, Tone 8. By George Synkellos:*[^1100]
Assembling faithfully today, ye lovers of spectacles, behold the strange and extraordinary contest of sacred James from Persia, who has shone forth upon us like the star that appeared unto the Magi and guided them unto true knowledge. For that valiant man, in falling, struck down the combatants; and when the joints of his members were to be severed, he made the torturers powerless. Being strengthened by supreme providence, he cried out: "Even if ye cut off my physical limbs, yet I have Christ, Who intelligently becomes all things unto me!" Therefore, foreseeing the future life, through the death that lies before all men he hastened to pass over unto that life; wherein taking up his abode, he entreats from God the Bestower of crowns cleansing, enlightenment, and great mercy for us who celebrate his memory.

*Both now, Theotokion, or Staurotheotokion, Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*
"What is this sight that is seen, * which is beheld with mine eyes, O Master? * Thou Who upholdest all creation, * having been lifted up upon the Tree, * diest, Who givest life unto all!" * the Theotokos cried out weeping, * when she beheld Him Who had shone forth ineffably from her, * God and man, * lifted up upon the Cross.

*Troparion of the Martyr James, Tone 4:*
Thy martyr, O Lord, James, in his suffering received an incorruptible crown from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, he cast down the torturers, and crushed the powerless insolence of demons: through his supplications save our souls!

*Or this one, in the same Tone:*
By strange and fearful tortures, and by the valor of thy patience, thou didst exceedingly astonish all, O much-suffering one: over each joint of thy severed members thou didst utter marvelously grateful supplications unto the Lord. Therefore, having received a crown in thy suffering, thou hast ascended unto the throne of the heavenly King, Christ God, O James: pray thou Him that our souls may be saved.

*Glory, both now, Theotokion, or Staurotheotokion.*

*The Service of Saint Palladius is sung at Compline.*
*Canon, whose acrostic is: "I honor thy life, O all-blessed father. By Joseph."*
*Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^1101]
I will open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I will utter a word unto the Queen and Mother; and I will appear radiantly keeping festival, and will sing rejoicing of her wonders.

*Troparia:*
Illumined by divine brightness, O venerable one, dispel the cloud of my thought, that I may behold thy light-bearing life and the perfection of thy conversation.

Having risen early unto God, the Sun of righteousness, from infancy, O all-wealthy one, thou didst escape the darkness of bodily passions by abstinence, and wast enriched with the gift of wonders, O venerable one.

Having acquired mental purity through dispassion, thou wast a receptacle of the Spirit, O praiseworthy, all-blessed Palladius, adornment of the fathers, universal luminary.

*Theotokion:*
Thou alone, O Bride of God, didst hold in thine arms Him Who sits on high, Who became flesh; for thou art a worthy receptacle of the Ruler of all ages.

*Ode 3 of the Canon to Saint Palladius. Heirmos:*[^1102]
Establish thy hymnographers, O Theotokos, thou living and plentiful fount, who have gathered together in a spiritual choir; and in thy divine glory account them worthy of crowns of glory!

*Troparia:*
Offering all-night prayer unto God the Almighty with a vigilant mind, O father, thou didst put to sleep bodily passions; therefore thou hast become a sleepless intercessor for all of us.

Having mortified thy members through abstinence, O father, thou didst quicken thy soul with divine growths, being nourished by virtues through the all-effecting powers of the fathers, O father Palladius.

Having heard the voice of the good God, and partaking[^1103] of divine understanding, having accomplished thy life in silence, adhering irrevocably, O venerable one, unto our God, the Giver of light.

*Theotokion:*
With the drops of thy prayers, O Maiden, quench the coals of passions, O unwedded Mary, and kindle the extinguished lamp of my heart, O golden lampstand, all-undefiled one.

*Ode 4 of the Canon to Saint Palladius. Heirmos:*
Perceiving the unsearchable counsel of God, namely the incarnation from the Virgin of Thee, the Most High, the Prophet Habakkuk cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparia:*
And by the power and all-effecting grace of God the King of all, thou didst utterly escape the evil deceits of the bodiless enemies, O father Palladius, God-inspired one.

Let us rejoice spiritually as we celebrate the festive memory of our sign-bearing and venerable father, being delivered from hardships by his sacred supplications.

Thy shrine wells forth ever-flowing[^1104] healings, O glorious Palladius, cleansing the defilements, both bodily and spiritual, of those who approach, O father of fathers, acceptable unto God.

Deliver us by thy prayers, O venerable one, from all snares of serpentine temptations, and heal our cruel afflictions by thy supplications unto the Good One.

Truly thou didst appear as a temple capable of containing God, the King of all King, O all-undefiled Mother of God; therefore piously with faith we without doubting offer Gabriel's "Rejoice!"

*Ode 5 of the Canon to Saint Palladius. Heirmos:*
All things were amazed at thy divine glory: for thou, O Virgin who knewest not wedlock, didst hold in thy womb the God Who is over all, and didst bear the timeless Son, Who bestows peace upon all who sing of thee.

*Troparia:*
Thou didst disregard bodily passions,[^1105] O God-blessed one, through exceeding abstinence; therefore was divine grace granted unto thee to heal the passions of the faithful who approach thee, O father, O most glorious Palladius.

Having holily accomplished thy life, O all-blessed one, thou wast numbered with the saints who from the ages have served God; thou dost sanctify the souls of all who praise thy venerable marvelous deeds.

Truly blessed wast thou, O praiseworthy one; for thou didst walk in the path of the ordinances of the all-seeing God, being gentle and meek, and adorned with good ascents.

*Theotokion:*
Mankind had departed far from God, but since thou, O joyous one, didst ineffably conceive the Savior, it enters into Paradise again, blessing thee with faith, O all-hymned one.

*Ode 6 of the Canon to Saint Palladius. Heirmos:*
Celebrating this divine and all-honorable feast of the Mother of God, come, ye God-wise, let us clap our hands and glorify God Who was born of her!

*Troparia:*
Having embraced a pure life of abstinence as one bodiless, having accomplished all-night standing, unceasing prayer, O wise one, true faith, and divine humility.

Adorned with good contemplations, thou wast seen as an angel while living in the flesh; and having passed away, thou didst take up thy dwelling with the angels, O God-blessed father Palladius.

Having angels as helpers, thou didst shatter demonic imaginations and all craftiness; and without stumbling, O God-blessed one, didst thou traverse the path that leads unto life.

*Theotokion:*
When thou didst hear the words of divine Gabriel, O all-undefiled Maiden, thou didst conceive the Word in thy seedless womb, and beyond word didst thou bear Him.

Lord, have mercy (Thrice).
*Glory, both now, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1. Podoben: "While the stone was sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́танꙋ):*
Having lived the monastic life in a manner well-pleasing unto God, O our God-bearing father, by prayer and fasting thou didst seek God; and thou wast a pure receptacle of the Spirit, flashing forth upon the faithful the rays of virtues, wherewith thou dost enlighten all who honor thee. Glory to Christ Who glorified thee! Glory to Him Who strengthened thee! Glory to Him Who through thee works healings for all!

*Ode 7 of the Canon to Saint Palladius. Heirmos:*[^1106]
The God-wise youths worshiped not creation rather than the Creator, but valiantly trampling down the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of the fathers!

*Troparia:*
By most glorious tokens of wonders, O all-wealthy one, thou dost enlighten the souls of all who have recourse unto thee, by the grace of the Almighty, Who enlightened thy soul and showed it forth brighter than the sun.[^1107]

Having most perfectly loved the Lord with uprightness of mind, Thou wast also perfectly loved by Him, O all-wise one; Thou didst receive grace to drive away wicked spirits and to heal all infirmities.

Receiving the streams of thy tears, the all-seeing God made thee a partaker of angelic consolation, which they who served God with uprightness of heart received.

*Theotokion:*
Having borne the merciful Lord, O only God-favored one: pray thou that with His right hand He have mercy on my mind, O pure one, which is ever cruelly constrained by worldly cares.

*Ode 8 of the Canon to Saint Palladius. Heirmos:*
The childbearing of the Theotokos saved the pious youths in the furnace: then figured forth, but now brought to pass, it moves the whole world to sing unto Thee: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
By divine power thou didst destroy the ruinous demonic hosts, and thou didst receive grace to soothe[^1108] infirmities and to drive away unclean spirits, crying out: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Having lived in a manner well-pleasing unto God, O all-blessed one, thou hast now fallen asleep with the sleep of the righteous due unto all, and thou hast been brought unto unending enjoyment, O venerable one, crying out: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Thy shrine wells forth healings most gloriously unto those who hasten unto it, O father, checking infirmities and drying up passions; before which[^1109] bowing down, we sing of thy life, thy labors, and thy divine struggles, O blessed Palladius, luminary of monastics.

*Theotokion:*
Fill me with divine waters, O Virgin, who didst bear the Spring; deliver me from the burning heat of sin, and guide me unto life, O portal of divine life, who cry aloud: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9 of the Canon to Saint Palladius. Heirmos:*
Let every earthborn mortal leap for joy, being illumined by the Spirit; and let the nature of the bodiless minds keep festival, honoring the sacred triumph of the Mother of God, and let it cry aloud: Rejoice, O all-blessed Theotokos, pure Ever-Virgin!

*Troparia:*
Enabled by divine power and grace, O father, to conquer the serpent boasting in folly, to crush his pernicious head, and to trample him under thy feet: therefore, assembling with contrite soul, we bless thee.

Thou didst appear as a heaven by the height of thy life, adorned[^1110] with wonders as with divine stars, O all-wealthy one; and thou dost piously enlighten the souls of those who ever approach thee and honor thy struggles with faith, O God-bearer, most radiant luminary.

Thou didst check the flow of passions, O venerable one, by torrents of thy tears; streams of wonders dost thou pour forth unto those who hasten unto thee, O God-blessed one; thou dost ever cool[^1111] the burning heat of passions, O glorious Palladius, venerable adornment of the Church.

Thou didst blossom forth openly like a sweet-smelling rose in the Church of Christ, and with marvelous fragrances didst perfume the ends of the world; therefore do we celebrate thy divine memory: wherein ask thou for all of us remission[^1112] of our many sins, O God-bearer.

*Theotokion:*
The Light from Light shone forth from thy womb, O Mother and Ever-Virgin, and drove away the darkness of deception, and enlightened all the ends of the earth; therefore with faith we cry "Rejoice!" unto thee, O Theotokos, boast of the venerable.

*Stichera, Tone 1. Podoben: "All-praised martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мч҃нцы):*
*Refrain:* Venerable father Palladius, pray unto God for us.

Thy mind being enlightened by the light of the thrice-radiant Godhead, O all-blessed Palladius, thou wast a pure temple, intelligently receiving the divine rays of the Holy Spirit. Therefore pray thou that He grant peace and great mercy unto our souls.

Having the angels as helpers who strengthened thee, O wise one, thou didst shatter demonic imaginations and wicked deeds, O father, and didst traverse the path that leads unto divine rest. Therefore pray thou that He grant peace and great mercy unto our souls.

*Glory, Tone 1:*
In purity of soul, O wise, glorious God-bearer, unto the Pure having become like unto God and thy Creator: thou didst offer thyself as a living sacrifice unto Him, as a keeper of His commandments. Therefore pray that He grant our souls peace and great mercy.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
O all-pure temple of God, wider than the heavens, and holier[^1113] than the Cherubim, O maiden full of divine grace, all-holy: grace[^1114] my mind and enlighten the eyes of my heart, granting me by thy favorable intercession the forgiveness of all transgressions.

*Staurotheotokion, Podoben: "All-praised martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мч҃нцы):*
The undefiled Virgin of old, beholding upon the Tree God, Whom she bare from a seedless womb, unable to endure the maternal wounding, tearing herself cried aloud: "O Thou Who by Thy nod upholdest all creation, how as one condemned art Thou crucified upon the Cross, desiring to save all mankind?"

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos, without the martyria; and of the saint on 6; whose acrostic is: "The Persian martyr James do I hymn with songs." A work of Joseph. Tone 2.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Come, ye people, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He brought out of the bondage of Egypt; for He hath been glorified.

*Troparia:*
Standing now before the throne of Christ, O glorious crown-bearer, martyr James, grant unto me by thy prayers a light-bearing beam and grace from heaven.

Like a most radiant dawn thou didst shine forth upon us from the rising of the east, and hast enlightened the Church of Christ with the brightness of thy sufferings, O martyr James.

Having shown youthful resistance, as a victor thou wast accounted worthy of honor, and of the perfect reward,[^1115] and of eternal glory, O martyr James.

*Theotokion:*
The prophetic trumpets proclaimed thee, preaching the mystery concerning thee, O Virgin Theotokos, and beholding thy wonders from afar.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst slay sin, and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who sing of Thee.

*Troparia:*
Thou wast like a chosen vine of Christ, pruned by the sickle of torments, and bearing much fruit brought unto the winepresses of the Savior.

Thou didst prudently despise the corruptible and easily dissolved things of passing life, O crown-bearer, and as one keen of mind didst choose beforehand the unshakable nature of eternal things.

Thy body, being hacked in pieces by the cruelty of the torturers, mediated bright crowns for thee, O James, and the enjoyment of the food of Paradise.

*Theotokion:*
Humanity was manifestly shown mercy by thy divine childbearing, O Virgin, having been hypostatically united unto the Master of all, O Bride of God.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8. Podoben: "Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Christ caused a newly-revealed star from Persia to shine forth unto earthly dwellers: the divine James, the ever-memorable martyr; for whose sake He drove away the gloom of deception, and caused the grace of the Spirit to shine forth upon the faithful. Therefore, celebrating his memory, we faithfully keep feast, and cry aloud saying: O passion-bearer who didst suffer much, pray thou unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who honor thy holy memory with love. *(Twice)*

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
Having fallen into the mire of sins, and having no firm standing, the tempest of transgressions hath cruelly overwhelmed me. But as thou didst bear the Word, the only Lover of mankind, look down upon me thy servant, and deliver me from every sin, and from soul-corrupting passions, and from every affliction of the wicked murderer, O unwedded Theotokos; pray thou unto Christ God to grant me remission of sins, for in thee do I, thy servant, have hope.

*Staurotheotokion:*
The Virgin and Mother of the Redeemer, standing beside the Cross in pain, weeping with tears, cried out maternally: "What is this strange and most glorious thing, O Son? Thou Who pourest forth dispassion unto all men art crucified upon the Cross between condemned ones,[^1116] pierced in the side, and given gall to drink by him whose hands Thou didst fashion![^1117] But arise, and grant remission of transgressions unto those who sing in faith of Thy divine sufferings."

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I have heard, O Lord, the report of Thy dispensation, and I glorified Thee, O only Lover of mankind.

*Troparia:*
With the weapon, O glorious one, the armor of faith given unto thee by God, Thou didst utterly burn up all the delusion of the fire-worshipers.

Ask thou cleansing for us who celebrate thy honored memory, as one having boldness, O martyr[^1118] James.

The flowing streams of blood from thy limbs, O thrice-blessed one, quenched all the flame of deception, quenched.

*Theotokion:*
Direct my thoughts, O all-pure one, unto the calm harbor of thy dispassion and purity.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O Giver of light and Maker of the ages, O Lord, guide us in the light of Thy commandments; for besides Thee, no other God do we know.

*Troparia:*
Like good and truly fruitful earth wast thou, O wise one, broken up by the plow of bitter torments, bringing forth unto the Creator a tillage rich in grain.

Thou didst quench the fiery arrows of the enemy, O most excellent one, by the blood of thy severed bodily limbs, O thrice-blessed one; for thou didst appear sheltered by hope and faith.

Like a sheep without voice[^1119] unto Christ, O all-wise one, when thy limbs were cruelly severed, thou didst offer a song of victory and worthy praise at each one.

Thy sufferings grant cleansing from my spiritual defilements, O glorious martyr[^1120] of Christ, bestowing deliverance through the streams of thy blood, O all-praised one.

*Theotokion:*
Offering with heart and tongue a voice that witnesses unto thy honorable and awe-inspiring childbearing, we now name thee the pure Theotokos.[^1121]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Floating in the abyss of sins,[^1122] I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy tender mercy: lead me up from corruption, O God.

*Troparia:*
Sensibly accepting the instruction of thy kinsfolk, rejoicing thou didst hasten unto the struggles, O glorious one, and didst receive the crowns of victory.

As though suffering in an alien body, thou didst endure, O martyr James; and being severed limb by limb, thou didst send up a hymn unto the Master.

As a victorious martyr, O all-wise one, thou wast clothed in the garment of salvation and the robe of gladness, actively dyed with thy blood.

Having accomplished the crossing of the sea of suffering, therefore thou didst receive the sacred victor's crown; and now thou dost worthily dance in chorus with the ranks of the martyrs, O glorious James.

*Theotokion:*
Without knowing man, O Virgin, thou didst give birth, and remainest a virgin, manifesting the signs of the true Godhead of thy Son and God.

*Kontakion, Tone 2. Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Persuaded by thy good spouse, O patient-minded one, and having feared the dread tribunal, the Persian command and threat, O James, thou didst despise, and didst appear as an honored martyr, in body being pruned like a vine-branch.

*Ikos:*
From the soul let us all groan, shedding tears, as we behold the martyr bitterly dismembered. Like roaring dogs they came together and tore in pieces the limbs of the marvelous and valiant martyr among witnesses. What then is this? Let me tell it, if ye will, wait a little while, and I shall recount all unto you with diligence: how in one single day death came to pass, as James in body was pruned like a vine-branch.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
When the golden image was worshiped on the plain of Dura, Thy three youths despised the godless decree: cast into the midst of the fire, bedewed they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*
With mental strength and endurance of soul, when thy body was being dismembered, O martyr,[^1123] thou wast unchanged and unbending, strengthened by divine faith, crying out, O James: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!

Having directed thy thoughts toward the contemplation of the high calling, when drenched with torments thou wast not submerged; but willingly enduring the wounds of the lawless, and being cut in pieces, thou didst sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!

Blessed art thou, and well is it with thee now, O most blessed one, having conquered the untamed cruelty of the evil one and the rage of the torturer, as thou didst fervently cry: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast appeared as a golden-shining lampstand of the unwaning Light and torch of divine radiance, illuminating the whole world with the beam of honorable virginity, and saving those who sing: Blessed art thou who bare God in the flesh!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Unto God Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew youths, and changed the flame into dew: sing, ye works, as unto the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
Strengthened by the power of God, thou didst demolish the gatherings and battle-arrays of the wicked, O blessed one; and having powerfully driven them off, thou didst receive the crown of victory, crying out: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

The severing of thy limbs as an addition of good things didst thou behold, O martyr,[^1124] not looking at present afflictions, but looking toward the future: the fair crowning of martyrs[^1125] prepared by the righteous Judge.

Having acquired supernatural endurance firmly, like a pillar thou didst remain, O blessed one; fearlessly receiving the enemy's onrushes and arrows, crying aloud: Bless Christ unto all ages!

With great assault the author of evil, the soul-destroying foe, attacked thee, stirring up torturers to overthrow the strength of thy soul, but was not able, O glorious one: for thou didst clothe thyself with the armor[^1126] of Christ.

*Theotokion:*
We know thee, O Theotokos, as the clear well-spring of immortality, as having borne the Word of the immortal Father, Who delivered from death all those who supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
God the Word of God, Who by ineffable wisdom came to renew Adam who had fallen grievously into corruption through eating, and for our sake was ineffably incarnate of the holy Virgin: Him do we the faithful magnify with songs in oneness of mind.

*Troparia:*
Dancing in chorus with the martyrs as a martyr, O thrice-blessed one, and standing before the throne of Christ: deliver from grievous perils by thy prayers those who celebrate thy memory and today honor thy light-bearing feast with gladness.

Where the assemblies of martyrs dwell, where the choir of all the saints[^1127] is at rest, where the spirits of the righteous abide, where is the Church of the firstborn: thither hast thou now in truth taken up thy dwelling in the heavens as a martyr,[^1128] O James.

Light-bearing hast thou stood before the Savior of all, for Whose sake thou didst endure the hacking off of the limbs of thy body, and strongly didst disregard the testing of fire and wounds; therefore with faith and love do we all bless thee, O James.

Adorned now with a variegated purple robe, reddened with thy blood, thou reignest with Christ, O James; for by thy sufferings thou didst find the spring of dispassion, which to enjoy eternally thou hast been accounted worthy, O divinely blessed one.

*Theotokion:*
As having conceived God and truly become the pure Mother of God, we glorify thee, O Theotokos; clearly fitting the title unto the nature of things, and suitably offering unto thee a divine voice.

*Exapostilarion. Podoben: "In the spirit in the sanctuary" (Дх҃омъ во ст҃или́щи):*
Like a vine pruned by many torments did the Lord glorify Thee, as an honorable vineyard pouring forth wine from the springs of thy blood, O passion-bearer James, and protector of those who worthily celebrate thy all-sacred memory with love.

*Theotokion:*
There is no salvation in me at all, O Virgin, for evilly have I fallen into the depth of sin, and I await threat, and dread torment, and the lot of the goats; have compassion on me before the judgment, as thou art a fervent protection, O Theotokos.

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*
*Glory of the saint, Tone 2. By Studites:*
Patiently enduring in thy sufferings, O martyr James, thou didst surrender thy body for Christ God; and being dismembered in hands and thighs, and arms, and calves, and fingers, and finally thy head, thou didst take flight unto the heavens, reigning together with the King of all. Therefore, O most valiant among sufferers, fail not to pray that our souls may be saved from every alien harm.

*Both now, Theotokion, or Staurotheotokion, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
When the undefiled ewe-lamb beheld her Lamb led willingly as a man unto the slaughter, weeping she said: "Dost Thou now make me childless, O Christ, who bare Thee? What is this that Thou hast done, O Redeemer of all? Yet do I hymn and glorify Thine exceeding goodness that is beyond mind and word, O Lover of mankind!"

*At the Liturgy, Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* To the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath been marvelous in all His will in them. [Ps. 15:3]
*Epistle to the Ephesians, pericope 233.*
*Alleluia:* Many are the afflictions of the righteous. [Ps. 33:20]
*Gospel of John, pericope 50.*
*Communion Verse:* In everlasting memory... [Ps. 111:6] *On the 28th Day of the Same Month.*
*Memory of the Holy Venerable Martyr Stephen the New; and of the Holy Martyr Irenarchus.*

*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the venerable one on 6, Tone 6. Podoben: "Having set all aside" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*
Having set all aside from thy youth, thou didst dedicate thyself unto the Master, being outside the flesh and worldly love, O most sacred one. Having become a most excellent monk, O Stephen, and a receptacle of the Divine Spirit: for having shut thyself, O blessed one, within a most narrow hut, thou didst wing thy mind unto heavenly things, to behold the ineffable beauty of Christ the King and God; bowing down before Whose icon, thou didst suffer most valiantly.

Forty days like the Master didst thou fast, being kept in prison; thou didst prepare thyself for suffering, O sacred Stephen, foundation of monastics and ornament of martyrs.[^1129] Therefore, falling upon thee like pitiless wild beasts, dragging thee like a gentle lamb, they unrighteously tore thee asunder, who hadst lived among the lawless, who gavest up holy things valiantly, and who with boldness prayest for our souls.

A most lawless people, obeying the extreme lawlessness of the most iniquitous king,[^1130] O venerable one, unsparingly pelted thee with stones like the first-sufferer and honorable Stephen, and crushed thy holy head, O father; and dragging thee most cruelly through the streets, they poured out thy bowels, O all-blessed one, not having pity on thee even after death. O thy courage! O thy character! O thy great endurance! whereby thou didst receive an unfading crown, O Stephen!

*Glory, Tone 6. By Studites:*
From infancy thou didst dedicate thyself unto God, O most sacred Stephen, even as did the great prophet Samuel; and having ascended the mountain, in monastic manner thou didst please Him. And again, unto suffering thou didst manfully strip thyself; and for the sake of His icon thou didst endure banishments and afflictions most patiently, and didst suffer bonds and prisons; beaten, and pelted with stones, and crushed in the head, thou wast accounted worthy of crowns from Christ God: Him do thou entreat, for those who celebrate with love thy ever-honored memory, that they be delivered from passions and temptations, and from distressing afflictions, and that our souls may be saved.

*Both now, Theotokion, or Staurotheotokion. Podoben: "Having set all aside" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*
When of old the ewe-lamb, the undefiled and spotless Lady, beheld her own Lamb upon the Tree of the Cross, maternally she cried out, and marveling exclaimed: "O sweetest Child, what is this new and most glorious sight? How hath the graceless assembly delivered Thee unto the tribunal of Pilate, and condemned unto death the Life of all? Yet do I hymn Thine ineffable condescension, O Word!"

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*
*Glory, Tone 8:*
Having preserved that which is according to the image unharmed, O venerable father, for the sake of Christ's icon thou didst most manfully stand firm, not fearing the threats of the one named for dung;[^1131] but with the sword of the Spirit thou didst slay him. Therefore, having acquired boldness before God, save thy flock from all heresies, O much-suffering Stephen.

*Both now, Theotokion, or Staurotheotokion. Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*
"What is this sight that is seen, which is beheld with mine eyes, O Master? Upholding all creation, lifted up upon the Tree, Thou diest, Who givest life unto all!" the Theotokos cried out weeping, when she beheld Him Who had shone forth ineffably from her, God and man, lifted up upon the Cross.[^1132]

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Having trained beforehand in ascetical life upon the mountain, thou didst destroy the noetic battle-arrays of the enemies with the panoply of the Cross, O all-blessed one; and again unto martyrdom thou didst manfully arm thyself, slaying Copronymus[^1133] with the sword of faith: and on account of both thou wast crowned by God, O venerable martyr Stephen, ever-memorable.

*Glory, both now, Theotokion, or Staurotheotokion.*
*The service of the holy martyr Irenarchus is sung at Compline.*
*Canon, whose acrostic is: "Grant me peaceful grace, O martyr." Tone 6.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Traversing the deep on foot as on dry land, Israel, beholding the pursuer Pharaoh drowned, cried out: Let us sing a song of victory unto God!

*Troparia:*
From the scandals of this life[^1134] and from the passions that assail me, pacify my mind, O sufferer Irenarchus, and account me worthy quietly to praise thy memory.

By the streams of thy blood thou didst quench the flame of the persecutors, and didst water the thoughts of the faithful, so as to cultivate piously the desire for eternal life, O martyr Irenarchus.

Having received sacred victorious crowns as a sufferer, O Irenarchus, thou hast passed over from earth unto the tranquil world, and unto the true light and life, O most blessed one.

*Theotokion:*
Having borne within thy womb the uncontainable Word contained, O tent that contained God: deliver me, O pure one, from the surging tempest of grievous evils that constrain me.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
There is none holy like unto Thee, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and hast established us upon the rock of Thy confession.

*Troparia:*
Sheltered by divine strength, thou dost advance eagerly unto the struggles, O all-blessed one, enduring wounds and the tearing of the pursuers, O most valiant passion-bearing martyr.

Christ, the great Marshal of the contest,[^1135] gives thee strength to destroy deception and to put to shame the enemy who boasts shamelessly and rages vainly,[^1136] O martyr.

The choir of saints, having suffered valiantly and endured wounds and bonds by the power of the Holy Spirit, cast down the serpent, the author of evil, through manly sufferings.

*Theotokion:*
Let us hymn Mary the pure, the Palace of the Master, whom Jacob of old clearly beheld as a divine ladder reaching from earth unto heavenly height.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Christ is my power, God and Lord: the venerable Church divinely sings, crying out from a pure mind, keeping feast in the Lord.

*Troparia:*
Lawfully didst thou run, lawfully didst thou suffer, and lawfully wast thou crowned, being strengthened by the law of God, and keeping thyself unharmed, O most blessed one.

Unable to bear walking in deception, O glorious one, as a prudent man rejoicing thou didst hasten unto the divine rebirth, receiving intellectual light and showing thyself to be a luminary.

By no means did the deep cover thee[^1137] when it received thee, O all-blessed martyr,[^1138] having recognized thee, O Irenarchus, as a divine witness of the divine sufferings of Christ, the All-True.

Being offered as sacred sacrifices, and slaughtered beforehand, and scraped together, and burned on every side with fire, ye did not deny Christ, O marvelous passion-bearing women.

*Theotokion:*
A Virgin didst thou remain after childbirth, even as thou wast before childbearing, for thou didst bear God the Word, Who delivered us through thine intercession, O all-immaculate one.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
With Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine in love, I pray Thee, the souls of those who awake early unto Thee, that they may know Thee, O Word of God, as the true God, Who callest them from the darkness of sin.

*Troparia:*
The enemy was wounded by the spear of the strong endurance of the valiant-minded martyr, and was subjugated beneath his heels, and is seen to be a laughingstock and is put to shame.

Thy foot, O martyr,[^1139] hath stood upright manifestly according to the prophet, by unswerving understanding tripping up the crafty one, and being adorned by the paths of martyrdom.

Having appeared guileless and simple, O martyr Irenarchus, thou didst cast away the darkness[^1140] of the malice of the persecutors; and by the consummation of thy blood thou wast crowned with crowns of incorruption.

*Theotokion:*
The divinely-radiant choir of the prophets, understanding from afar in mystery the ineffable depth of thy divine childbirth, O Virgin Bride of God, prefigured thee with sacred types.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, fleeing unto Thy calm haven I cry aloud unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Greatly Merciful One!

*Troparia:*
Having stepped upon the waters, piloted by the life-originating right hand, O Irenarchus, thou wast saved through them, drowning the impieties of the persecutors by fervent prayer, O most purified one.

Testing great things through small, the sacred women gave themselves over unto great torments, having by the Spirit put to death Eve's deceiver, the serpent who was the author of evil.

Holy youths, pure lambs, and perfect offerings were brought as a sacrifice unto the true Lamb Who was slain for our sake, taking up their dwelling in the odor of sweet fragrance.

*Theotokion:*
Behold, now was the Lord incarnate from thy pure blood, O Virgin Mother, and is united unto men without turning,[^1141] working out our salvation according to His ineffable mercy.

Lord, have mercy, *(thrice)*.
Glory, both now.
Sessional Hymn, *Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*
Great peace brought [the Lord] unto thee, O martyr,[^1142] when thou didst overtake the enemy and vanquish the warfare of deception by divine grace, when thou didst strongly suffer. Therefore by faith we pray thee: Deliver from every harm those who honor thy holy memory, O Irenarchus.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
An angel made the furnace drop dew for the venerable youths, while the command of God, burning the Chaldeans, persuaded the tormentor to cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*
Having unyoked thy mind from love toward the flesh, O most blessed one, burned with flame and fire, O wise one, thou didst cry aloud with the song of the youths: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

Blessed was the divine assembly of youths and the holy sevenfold choir of women, having together strongly endured the flaying, fire, and wounds, and being vouchsafed heavenly goods.

The evil spirits are driven away at the mere invocation of thy name, having recognized thee, O Irenarchus, as Christ's invincible sufferer, singing fervently: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Held fast by despondency, raise me up unto the activity of divine deeds, O most pure one, strengthening me against the enemies who fiercely fight against me continually and beguile me with opposing thoughts.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
From the flame Thou didst shed dew for the venerable ones, and by water didst consume the sacrifice of the righteous one; for Thou dost all things, O Christ, solely by willing them. Thee do we exalt unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
Yet dripping with streams of blood, and adorned with the beauty of wounds, thou didst appear unto the Victor,[^1143] O Irenarchus, receiving from Him the honors of victory.

Elevated by the love of the Almighty, thou didst cast down the exalted pride of the persecutors, and didst humble the haughtiness of idols, O martyr, passion-bearer Irenarchus, most blessed one.

Vouchsafe me the divine tender mercy, O martyr, delivering from temptations and perils him who honors thee with fervent faith, O Irenarchus, and flees beneath thy shelter.

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O holy mountain traversed by God, [revelation] of ineffable things; rejoice, dread manifestation and hearing, a vision hardly to be beheld; rejoice, restoration of the fallen, O Virgin!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
It is impossible for men to see God, upon Whom the angelic hosts dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-immaculate one, the Word was manifest incarnate unto men; Whom magnifying, together with the heavenly hosts, we call thee blessed.

*Troparia:*
Thou hast attained the very ultimate and utmost of desires, O divinely-wise Irenarchus, and by participation didst become a god,[^1144] singing with the bodiless hosts: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O all-creating and all-powerful Trinity!

Having escaped the snares of those who hunted thee, thou didst take rest in the heavenly nest, O glorious one, and wast joined to the armies of the martyrs who suffered together with thee. Therefore we honor your memory, celebrating with exceeding joy.

Setting forth the strength and power of Christ, Thou didst sail across the cruel deep of torments and didst attain the haven on high, all adorned, all abundantly showered with the effusions of the light of the Spirit.

*Theotokion:*
Unable to comprehend the incomprehensible wonder of thy childbearing, O Virgin Mother, with silence we rather glorify it; and we hymn thee, the only all-blessed one, and fair among women, O all-immaculate one.

*Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*
*Refrain:* Holy Martyr Irenarchus, pray to God for us.
Duly praising the struggles of the venerable sufferer and the pains of Christ's weapon-bearer, ye faithful, let us cry aloud unto the Lord: By His prayers deliver us from every distress!

Great peace from the Lord came unto thee when thou didst suffer and pass through the tempest of cruel things, O all-blessed Irenarchus, valiant warrior and intercessor for those who praise thee!

*Glory...*
The choir of women suffered together with thee, and the divine assembly of children, together with Saint Acacius, stoutly accomplishing the struggle, diminishing the deception, O blessed Irenarchus.

*Both now... Theotokion:*[^1145]
Thou art my defense and shelter, O all-immaculate Theotokos; for I have thee as a helper in afflictions, sicknesses, and straits, and I glorify thee who art all-hymned.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding the most lawless people unjustly nailing Thee to the Tree, the Virgin and Thy pure Mother, even as Symeon foretold, was wounded in her inward parts, O Savior.

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos, and of the venerable one, on 6; whose acrostic is: "Christ crowns thee with a martyr's crown, O blessed one. By Joseph. Tone 6."*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Israel, having walked on foot through the deep with dryshod steps, beholding Pharaoh the persecutor drowning, cried aloud: Unto God let us sing a song of victory!

*Troparia:*
Having joyfully traversed the narrow path of fasting, by the breadth of martyrdom thou didst burn up the onslaughts of the enemy, and didst inherit spacious life, O blessed one.

A barren root brought Thee forth of old, eponymous of Anna, as of old Samuel; and she gave Thee back unto God Who gave Thee, signifying, O wise one, the grace of thy life.

Having joined the most sacred, divine rank of monks, thou didst shine forth through virtues like a most luminous star, mystically illumining the faithful, O venerable Stephen.

Having constricted thy body by enclosure in a narrow cell, thou didst give wings to thy mind toward the heavens, O wise one, nobly expanding in ascents.

*Theotokion:*
The impassable gate, the pure temple of purity, the fair among women, the holy Theotokos, with sacred voices let us, a sacred people, glorify!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established us upon the rock of Thy confession.

*Troparia:*
Thy mind, adorned by contemplation toward God, O father, appeared most fair, and truly filled with all grace, and a partaker of the divine brightness.

Venerating the honorable icon of Christ and of her who bore Him, O blessed one, thou didst abhor the vile decree of the wicked emperor,[^1146] by the power of the Holy Spirit.

With fetters did the exceedingly senseless one, having an iron heart, bind thee and send thee away into prison as a keeper of Christ's dogmas, O Stephen, most blessed one.

Mystically fair didst thou have thy feet, O venerable one, which stepped brightly unto the paths of martyrdom, crushing the heads of the enemy, O Stephen, much-suffering one.

*Theotokion:*
From thee alone, the pure one, the all-divine Word was incarnate as He knew, and He saved us from corruption who worship, because of His tender mercy, His divine condescension.

*Kontakion, Tone 8, Podoben: "To thee, the champion leader" (Взбра́нной):*

As a lover of the Trinity and divine, let us, ye feast-lovers, faithfully praise Stephen from the heart with songs, as one who honored the fair depiction of the Master and of His Mother; and with one accord now let us cry aloud unto him in love, rejoicing: Rejoice, O most glorious father!

*Then, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*
Thy blood, O wise one, mystically calls from the earth unto God, like that of Abel, O divinely-wise one; for it clearly proclaimed Christ's incarnation. Therefore thou didst put to shame the delusion of the icon-fighters,[^1147] and hast passed over into the heavenly chambers; pray thou to save us.

*Glory... Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (То́йже):*
Illumined by purification, like gold in the furnace thou didst shine forth, O wise one, through lawful suffering, and didst receive a crown corresponding to thy calling.[^1148] Therefore, rejoicing, we celebrate thy most holy memory, honoring thy struggles, O venerable-martyr Stephen.

*Both now... Theotokion:*
Unwedded, pure Virgin Theotokos, sole protector and shelter of the faithful, deliver all from perils, afflictions, and cruel circumstances who place their hope upon thee, O Maiden, and save our souls through thy divine prayers.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding Thee, O Christ, stretched out dead upon the Cross, the all-immaculate Mother cried aloud: O my Son, co-unoriginate with the Father and the Spirit, what is this Thine ineffable dispensation, whereby Thou hast saved the creation of Thy most pure hands, O Compassionate One?

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Christ is my power, God and Lord, the venerable Church sings in godly manner, crying aloud from a pure mind, keeping festival in the Lord.

*Troparia:*
Illumined by the light of the Spirit, through divine supplications thou didst grant light unto the blind, O father, imitating thy Master and God, O divinely-inspired one.

Thou wast seen from afar by those sailing upon the sea, piloting them, O blessed one, unto a calm haven by divine grace, as they faithfully invoked thy name, O father Stephen.

Sacrificed like a sacred slaughter, thou wast offered up unto Him Who was slain for thy sake, O Stephen, and in the mansions of the firstborn thou didst take rest, rejoicing.

By thy venerable word, he who was previously withered in his sides appeared whole and healthy, marveling, O martyr,[^1149] at the grace abundantly granted thee from on high for the correction of men.

*Theotokion:*
Upon thee, O all-immaculate one, have I set the hopes of my salvation, unto thy shelter have I fled; be thou a helper unto me, O Maiden, delivering me from cruel things.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
With Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine in love, I pray Thee, the souls of those who awake early unto Thee, that they may know Thee, O Word of God, as the true God, Who callest them from the darkness of sin.

*Troparia:*
With martyr's honors did our only God, the Marshal of the contest,[^1150] truly crown thy fasting labors, O venerable Stephen, strengthening thee against the murderers.

Struggling gloriously, in communion with a multitude of monks in prisons, O martyr,[^1151] thou wast found; for like stars they surrounded the unsetting Sun, being exceedingly illumined.

With divine words, we call blessed the sacred confessors and imitators of the divine passions, three hundred and forty and two,[^1152] who subjugated the godless.

The removal of noses in mockery, the cutting off of ears and hands, and the burning of bodily members for the sake of Christ's icon, did the most gloriously famous multitude of venerable ones endure.

*Theotokion:*
O [Throne],[^1153] who alone on earth truly didst bear the most holy God, sanctify and save through thine intercession those who ever proclaim thee as Theotokos.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, fleeing unto Thy calm haven I cry aloud unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Greatly Merciful One!

*Troparia:*
The inventor of malice could not endure the power of thy words; therefore he surrendered thee, O Stephen, unto scourges and wounds, and cruelly[^1154] unto a violent death.

Baked like bread by fire, and mercilessly suspended by the feet, thou wast wholly burned, O Paul, and offered as a sacrifice unto God, being vouchsafed co-dwelling with the martyrs.

Having lawfully suffered in imprisonment, and having departed this life by strangulation, the venerable monks in Ephesus, eight and thirty,[^1155] we call blessed in faith and love.

Thou didst stoutly resist the judge, and by torn wounds[^1156] unto thy body thou didst choose to die thou didst choose to die for Christ, the only Immortal One, O praiseworthy, great-named Peter.

*Theotokion:*
The only all-hymned, and fair among women, Mother of God, the unconquerable rampart of Christians, the most pure Theotokos, with doubt-free heart we call blessed.

*Kontakion, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*
From a barren root, O venerable one, thou didst sprout as a branch eponymous of the first sufferer; a great instructor of monks didst thou appear, O father, and didst not fear the rage of the emperor who was unwilling to venerate Christ's image; therefore, having finished thy course, thou didst receive a martyr's crown, O Stephen.

*Ikos:*
The father of envy and alien from God raised up against thee many temptations and tribulations, unable to bear the sight of thy godly life and upright, unswerving walk; the vile one framed knaveries against thee, feigning to be a disciple, as Judas of old; and he strove to deliver thee into the hands of the lawless, O father, who didst brightly proclaim Christ and bow down in love before His image; therefore thou didst receive a martyr's crown, O Stephen.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
An angel made the furnace drop dew for the venerable youths, while the command of God, burning the Chaldeans, persuaded the tormentor to cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*
Thy demise was revealed unto thee, O blessed one, by the all-creating will; therefore thou hast attained unto what is greater, and passest from glory to glory, slain for the sake of Christ Who is God over all.

Eponymously with the first sufferer thou wast glorified with him; for mercilessly struck with stones, dragged, and beaten, thou didst fill the earth with thy blood, and rejoicing didst commit thy soul unto the Lord.

Mercilessly dragged along the streets of the city, O martyr Stephen, thou didst smooth the path of martyrdom for the faithful; treading firmly upon which, they have manifestly attained unto the heavenly city.

*Theotokion:*
The most sacred prophets proclaimed most clearly, O pure one, the mystery of thy venerable childbearing; and now we, brightly understanding the fulfillment, piously call thee blessed.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
From the flame Thou didst shed dew for the venerable ones, and by water didst consume the sacrifice of the righteous one;

...for Thou dost all things, O Christ, solely by willing them. Thee do we exalt unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
Most fiercely, like wild beasts, did those who live in extreme lawlessness seize Christ's lamb, beating and slaying him, and burying him together with lawless men.

Mercilessly did the enemy crush thy head, which God crowned on high with a victorious crown, O much-suffering crowned one, glory of martyrs and of all the venerable!

Patiently opposing the tormentor, the divinely-wise Andrew is torn to pieces with wounds, and mercilessly put to death, the venerable one, singing: Bless Christ unto all ages!

Having become a most constricted dwelling, thou didst have Him Who rests above all the holy living in thy heart, O much-suffering Stephen, unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*
By the sprinkling of the divine blood poured forth from the rib of Thy Son and God, O full of God's grace, wash away, I pray thee, O Virgin, the defilement that hath accrued unto me through evil sin.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
It is impossible for men to see God, upon Whom the angelic hosts dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-immaculate one, the Word was manifest incarnate unto men; Whom magnifying, together with the heavenly hosts, we call thee blessed.

*Troparia:*
Beholding rejoicing the ranks of angels, patriarchs, venerable ones, prophets, sufferers, apostles, and all the righteous, O divinely-inspired one, being joined together with them: remember, protect those on earth who purely call thee blessed.

As light, as morning dawn, as a great sun, as a heaven studded with stars by the brightness of wonders and holy wounds hast thou been, O Stephen, truly adorning the thoughts of all who praise thee, O much-suffering martyr.

By the steadfast struggles of fasting, having first cast down the principalities of darkness, O father, and at the last having suffered stoutly, delivering them over unto utter ruin, O Stephen, beauty of martyrs and boast of the venerable!

Thy most glorious memory today, with the most radiant beams of the gifts of the Spirit, illumines the fullness of the earth. Enlighten and sanctify us who now joyfully celebrate it, O divinely-blessed Stephen.

*Theotokion:*
O receptive vessel of Light, full of God's grace, truly the confirmation of the sacred-martyrs and the boast of all the venerable, save us save us from perils, tribulations, and the assault of enemies, who hymn thee.

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "In the spirit in the sanctuary" (Ду́хомъ во ст҃или́щи):*
Through fasting pains thou didst put to death the author of evil, the serpent, to the end; and at the end having taken the crown of martyrdom, O Stephen, all-praised one, rendering veneration unto the honorable icons, as knowing that it manifestly passes over unto the Prototype, O all-blessed one.

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast the all-immaculate bride of an ineffable[^1157] childbearing, as a most sacredly pure temple, O Theotokos; for thou didst bear God the Word, the pre-eternal Light Who dwelt in thee. Singing of thy childbearing, therefore, we worthily magnify thee, O all-immaculate Maiden.

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Octoechos on 4; and of the saint, Ode 3, on 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 8:* The venerable ones shall boast in glory, and they shall rejoice upon their beds.[^1158]
*Verse:* Sing unto the Lord a new song.
*Epistle to Timothy, pericope 294 [2 Tim. 3:1-9].*
*Alleluia, Tone 8:* Blessed is the man that fears the Lord.
*Verse:* His seed shall be mighty upon the earth.
*Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 37 [Matt. 10:32-33, 11:1].*
*Communion Hymn:* In everlasting memory [shall the righteous be; he shall not be afraid of evil tidings].[^1159]

*On the 29th Day of the Same Month.*
*The holy Martyr Paramon; and the holy Martyr Philoumenos; and the venerable Acacius, who is attested in the Ladder.*[^1160]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Martyr, 3, Tone 4, Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*
Manifestly illumined by the illumination of light of the Holy Spirit, O all-blessed Paramon, thou didst utterly abhor the deepest darkness of polytheism; and having received an opportune time, O all-blessed one, thou didst come valiantly unto the set-forth sufferings, and didst appear as a trophy-bearer; thou didst cast down the proud adversary of all earthly ones, magnifying Christ: Whom do thou pray to save and enlighten our souls.

For the sake of God and King of all, a numerous multitude being slaughtered perceiving a numerous multitude being slaughtered for the sake of the God and King of all, O Paramon,[^1161] thou wast inflamed with divine zeal, and didst cry aloud: "I am ever a sincere servant of Christ! Know, O most lawless tormentors, that like an innocent lamb to be slaughtered, lo, now have I come unbidden. Be not anxious, therefore: I compel myself to become a sacrifice acceptable unto Him Who was slain in the flesh for my sake!"

Honored with a sevenfold decad, and thrice, O honorable one, a choir of hundreds of sufferers,[^1162] through faith thou didst overthrow the polytheistic deceit of the most lawless ones. Together with them thou wast crowned, having struggled valiantly, O Paramon, and rejoicing wast numbered with the choirs of the bodiless ones. Together with them pray thou that we be delivered from every affliction and misfortune, who honor thee and ever call thee blessed.

*If the superior decide to sing "Alleluia", let him sing these stichera to the Theotokos first. Tone and Podoben the same:*
From the unoriginate Father, the timeless Son, for the sake of condescension and the salvation of men, being God became man, that He might now give Paradise unto the first-created; then also shall all nature be delivered from the deception of the serpent, and He shall save the fallen image, as the Benevolent Transformer; and her He made His Mother, a pure Birthgiver of Heaven, as being undefiled; whom, as an anchor and haven, we all call blessed.

The incarnate Creator of all didst thou have within thy womb, O divinely-blessed one, Who restored man that fell of old through the transgression of the serpent. For thou didst bear God in the flesh ineffably for us, and didst deliver from corruption all nature that had grown old, through thy childbearing. Therefore we sing and glorify thy grace, O unwedded Virgin; cease not to pray that our souls may be saved.

That we may run[^1163] unto the multitude of thy tender mercy and goodness, do thou uncover unto us the boundless abyss [of mercy], and blot out the sins of thy servants, O [Mother] of God; for thou hast, O all-immaculate one, as holy[^1164] Mother of God, power over the creation, and dost guide all things as thou wilt by thy strength; for the grace of the Holy Spirit, manifestly dwelling in thee, ever cooperates with thee in all things, O most blessed one.

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
The Son Who is glorified together with the Father and the Spirit by the highest Seraphim, wishing again to renew the first-created wishing again to renew the first-created, ineffably emptied Himself wholly within thy womb, O all-hymned Theotokos; and having shone forth from thee, He illumined the whole world by His Divinity, delivered it from the idol-madness, deified it by Himself, and led mankind up unto the heavens, Christ God and Savior of our souls.

*Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "Called from on high" (То́йже):*
Weep not for Me, O Mother, beholding suspended upon the Tree Thy Son and God, Who uncontainably suspended the earth upon the waters and created all creation; for I shall arise and be glorified, and with power crush the kingdoms of Hades, and destroy his might, and deliver the bound from his wickedness, as One compassionate, and lead them unto My Father, as the Lover of mankind.

*At the Aposticha, of the Octoechos.*

*The service of the venerable Acacius is sung at Compline.*

*The Canon, whose acrostic is: "I sing in hymns Acacius, the chosen disciple." By Theophanes. Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The Red Sea's deep, with unwetted steps, Israel of old traversed on foot, and by Moses' arms stretched out crosswise, vanquished Amalek's power in the wilderness.

*Troparia:*
Clothed in a guileless disposition, thou didst acquire the comely beauty of virtues, imitating Christ's voluntary obedience even unto death, O all-blessed one.

Thou didst put to shame the inventor of malice by thy guilelessness; and by patience under temptations, O father, thou didst humble unto the earth his proud and exalted hostility, O all-blessed one.

Advancing in patient temperance, O venerable one, thou didst cut off the beginnings of the passions; afterward thou wast adorned with the garment of dispassion, being covered by divine grace.

Having strengthened the disposition of thy soul with steadfast patience and valiant mind, O all-blessed one, daily thou didst endure the struggle of martyrdom, and wast shown forth as a crowned victor.

*Theotokion:*
A creative power and song is God and Lord,[^1165] Who was incarnate and born of thee for our sake, even as Isaiah prophetically proclaimed good tidings, O most pure one.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge and my firm foundation!

*Troparia:*
Having committed thine entire self unto thy Creator and God, O venerable one thou didst endure tormenting humiliation.

Lawfully didst thou show forth a sufferer's endurance upon earth, O abstinent one; therefore heavenly rejoicing was given unto thee.

True humility, strict long-suffering didst thou keep, patience, abstinence, with obedience, O all-blessed one.

*Theotokion:*
The Maker of all is fashioned, having for our sake taken ensouled flesh from thee, O all-pure one, O most pure Bride of God.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Sun of righteousness, the Church stood in her order, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparia:*
Having put to death the wisdom of thy flesh, O father, thou didst give life unto thy soul and didst receive the crown of righteousness, crying aloud, O Acacius: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

Undergoing long struggles, thou didst show forth daily a patient resistance, O father; therefore after death, as one alive, thou didst cry aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

With steadfast mind thou didst endure torments for Christ, O blessed Acacius, contemplating Him nailed upon the Cross for the salvation of our race.

*Theotokion:*
Thou art purer than the heavens and the bodiless powers, O all-pure one, having given birth unto their Creator; therefore we cry unto thee: Rejoice, O all-hymned Theotokos!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou, O my Lord, didst come as a light into the world, a holy light turning from the darkness of ignorance those who in faith sing Thy praise.

*Troparia:*
Manfully protected by wounds and daily beatings, O venerable one, enduring valiantly, thou didst venerably repose.

Having finished the good course, O guileless Acacius, thou didst receive rest free from toils and pains.

Thy mind being steered by pure thought, O God-bearing Acacius, safely directed its course unto the Cause of all.

*Theotokion:*
Neither angelic nor human mind can recount thy childbirth, for it surpasses every comprehension of reason.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood that flowed in mercy from Thy ribs.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst fall asleep with a blessed sleep, O blessed one, and after death wast shown forth obeying those who questioned, O father saying that he who possesses obedience dies not.[^1166]

Having finished the struggles of good deeds, O namesake of guilelessness,[^1167] Thou wast truly counted worthy of incorruptible immortality, O God-wise one, where rejoicing Thou didst receive the crowns of victory.

The divine, good, and God-pleasing abstinence of thy life, O blessed Acacius, establishes many in divine fear and the desire of future good things.

*Theotokion:*
In truth as Theotokos do we glorify thee in faith, as having conceived God and given birth unto Him without knowing wedlock, Who was united through the holy temple received from thee.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Quickly anticipate" (Скорѡ предварѝ):*
By the brightness of faith and the active light thou wast shown forth on earth as equal to the angels, in truth, O all-wise Acacius; manfully didst thou display the fortitude of thy mind, and didst crush the assaults of passions by fasting; therefore even after thy repose thou wast shown forth as alive, O unconquerable one.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
In the Persian furnace the Abrahamic youths, consumed rather by the love of piety than by the flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparia:*
Following the Master with whole desire, enduring reproaches, dishonor, and wounds, O venerable one, thou didst cry aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

Thy mind meditating on the sufferings and crucifixion of the Good One, and yielding thyself unto death, when wounded thou didst sing: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

Dead in the grave, lying breathless according to the law of those who die, thou didst answer beyond nature unto him that spoke, crying aloud: I have not died! Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth unto the true Life, thou didst raise up those who were dead under the law by which we were held,[^1168] as they cry: Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Lady!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Daniel, stretching out his hands, stopped the mouths of the lions in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, girt with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Through steadfast abstinence it was granted thee to be joined unto God, O venerable one, being loosed from the bonds of the body and having brought the flesh into subjection; and by active contemplation, O father, thou didst cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, the Lord!

*Troparia:*
Numbered and ranked together with Christ's martyrs, O venerable one, unceasingly hymn the Lover of mankind, praying for us who praise thee and cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

Having lawfully suffered upon earth, thou didst find heavenly rest, rejoicing with the saints, O venerable one, becoming a partaker of their gladness and joy, and crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*
He Who before was bodiless is incarnate; the Maker is fashioned from thee, O all-immaculate one; for the Incomprehensible, entering into thy most pure womb, willed to be clothed in the circumscription of flesh; therefore we all bless thee, O Mary, Bride of God.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
A cornerstone was cut out without hands from thee, the unhewn mountain, O Virgin: Christ, Who joined together the divided natures; therefore rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Theotokos.

*Troparia:*
Thou didst yield thyself gently, O father, unto the Benefactor of all, being adorned with the beauty of guilelessness and shining with the loveliness of virtues; therefore we all call thee blessed.

Obeying the law of piety, thou didst bend thy neck to the struggle of monastics, and having become a victor, O father, thou didst attain unto perfect guilelessness, O all-blessed one.

Thou wast counted worthy to send up praise unto God with the bodiless hosts, having preserved their way of life and purity; and by patience in deeds thou didst receive the glory of the martyrs,[^1169] O all-blessed one.

Receive from us, O God-bearer, the hymn offered unto Thee from a pure heart, and through thy supplications grant in return remission of sins and salvation, O all-honored one.

*Theotokion:*
As the holy root of incorruption, in truth, and the confirmation of all the faithful, O Virgin, do we honor thee with praises, for thou didst bear for us hypostatic Immortality.

*Stichera of the Venerable one, Tone 4. Podoben: "As one noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
By abstinence thou didst put to death the wisdom of the flesh, and didst give life unto thy soul through fasting and the perfection of virtues; whence thou wast shown forth truly as alive after death; for death was accounted as sleep unto thee when thou didst depart unto God and commend thy soul into His hands, O glorious Acacius.

Thou didst lull to sleep the burning of the passions, O Acacius, having acquired all-night vigilance, ob edience and humility, the study of the divine Scriptures, a pure heart, and an untroubled mind; therefore thou becamest also a receptacle of the Holy Spirit, having shone forth rays of wonders unto the ends of the earth.

Utterly abhorring worldly attachment, thou becamest a vessel of dispassion; and by the active ascent of philosophy, O glorious one, thou didst rise unto the ultimate Desire Itself, and by mystical contemplation didst behold the incomprehensible and divine beauties of invisible things, O all-wise and blessed Acacius.

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
Him Who is consubstantial with the Father and enthroned together with the Spirit thou didst incarnate from thy pure blood, and beyond word didst bear Him Who is truly known in two active substances and wills;[^1170] pray thou Him, O all-pure Virgin, as thy Son and God, to save those who in pure faith call thee blessed.

*Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: The same (То́йже):*
When the Ewe that bare Thee beheld Thee, the Lamb and Shepherd, upon the Tree, she lamented and maternally spoke unto Thee: O beloved Son, how art Thou suspended upon the Tree of the Cross, O Long-suffering One? How were Thy hands and Thy feet nailed by the lawless, O Word, and how hast Thou poured out Thy blood, O Master?

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos, and of the saint to 4. Whose acrostic is: "Grant me now, O martyr,[^1171] grace to sing thy praise." By Joseph. Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The Red Sea's deep, with unwetted steps, Israel of old traversed on foot, and by Moses' arms stretched out crosswise, vanquished Amalek's power in the wilderness.

*Troparia:*
Celebrating thy light-bearing memory, O martyr Paramon, enlighten my heart with the illuminating rays of the Spirit, and strengthen me to abide in the divine statutes.

Most brightly wast thou enriched with the martyric glory, O blessed one, having shone forth with martyric beauties and being adorned with fair wounds, O Paramon; therefore in faith we call thee blessed.

Being full of the life-creating waters of the Spirit, thou didst bedew those who were fiercely languishing in the heat of godlessness, and didst guide them unto the water of refreshment,[^1172] O glorious one.

*Theotokion:*
In time thou didst bear the Timeless One, Who became man, Whom diligently beseech, O pure one, as thy Son and Lord, of my soul to heal the inveterate passions of my soul, O all-immaculate one.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge and my firm foundation!

*Troparia:*
Having humbled thyself for Christ's sake, thou didst cast down the enemy's haughtiness, and with the sword of patience didst hew down his legions.

Thou didst destroy the wicked counsel against our faith and didst suffer valiantly, O martyr and passion-bearer Paramon.

Thou wast strengthened by divine grace as a mighty warrior, and the cruel torments, O martyr, thou didst account as a dream.

*Theotokion:*
Strengthen my mind, led astray by many passions, O most pure Mother of God, that I may worthily glorify thee.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*
Through the endurance of the divine commandments thou didst cleanse thy soul from defilement, and didst attain unto the perfection of sufferers; for thou didst refuse to sacrifice unto deceitful idols; imitating Christ, thou wast pierced with a lance; but diligently pray thou Him for peace, O all-blessed Paramon.

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
Next to God, O Theotokos, I, the humble one, flee unto thy divine protection; falling down, I pray thee: Have mercy, O most pure one, for my sins have gone over my head,[^1173] and I fear the torment, O Lady, and tremble; make supplication, O pure one, unto thy Son, to deliver me from them.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
She that in the latter times bare Thee in the flesh Who wast begotten of the unoriginate Father, beholding Thee suspended upon the Cross, O Christ, cried aloud: Woe is me, O most beloved Jesus! How is it that Thou, Who art glorified as God by angels, art now willingly crucified by lawless men, O Son? I praise Thee, O Long-suffering One!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Sun of righteousness, the Church stood in her order, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparia:*
With thy heart fortified by courage, and kindled with boldness, O glorious one, thou didst account the intricate torments as the arrows of infants,[^1174] O right-minded martyr.

Beholding the sufferers put to death by the tormentor's command, the martyr Paramon, having received divine zeal even as they, came unto suffering Valiantly when thou wast racked and mercilessly pierced with lances, overcoming the wiles of the enemy, Christ the Contest-Master[^1175] crowned thee, O blessed Paramon.

Marveling at the endurance of the martyrs and admiring their perfection, O glorious one, thou didst partake of their zeal of faith and honorable suffering.

*Theotokion:*
Men having been slain by transgression, by thy life-bearing childbirth, O Virgin Mary, thou didst revive all; therefore we glorify thee and in God-befitting manner call thee blessed.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou, O my Lord, didst come as a light into the world, a holy light turning from the darkness of ignorance those who in faith sing Thy praise.

*Troparia:*
Having suffered, thou didst offer thine own self as a costly gift unto thy Creator, and having vanquished deception, O adornment of martyrs.

Thou didst shatter idols and demonic shrines, O wise one, having acquired a steadfast mind upon the rock of divine faith, O Paramon.

Thou didst manfully turn back the multitude of demons by the tearing of thy flesh, O noble-minded sufferer; therefore we call thee blessed.

*Theotokion:*
The Lord, Who is co-equal in honor with the Father and the Spirit, was incarnate from thy pure blood, O pure one, having become man.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood that flowed in mercy from Thy ribs.

*Troparia:*
Thou wast not slothful in the time of struggles, but rather aroused, and valiant for divine suffering; for this cause thou didst receive the crown of glory.

Thou didst join thyself unto the choir of martyrs who zealously finished their course before thy suffering, O ever-memorable one, and with them wast counted worthy of the heavenly bridal chamber.

Lances made thee an imitator of Christ, pierced by which, O martyr,[^1176] thou didst ascend unto Him as a crown-bearer, having slain the senseless by the weapon of endurance.

*Theotokion:*
Deliver me from worldly stumbling-blocks, O all-immaculate one, who am held fast in the night of ignorance by unfitting thoughts and ever darkened by the malice of the enemy.

*After Ode 6, the Martyricon of the Octoechos.*

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
In the Persian furnace the Abrahamic youths, consumed rather by the love of piety than by the flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparia:*
Brightly enriched by God with the grace of healings and wonders, O wise martyr,[^1177] thou healest those who cry: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

Thou didst disregard the stretched torments, having all thy care in the heavens, and crying aloud, O praiseworthy one: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

With the fire of thy blood, O sufferer, thou didst burn up all the wicked matter of godlessness, O glorious one; and with the dew of thy wonders thou dost bedew those who are in the heat of cruel afflictions, O Paramon, crying: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, thou that alone didst bring forth joy unto men! Rejoice, heaven and Cherubic throne, and most glorious palace of the King of all the ages, O all-immaculate Lady!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Daniel, stretching out his hands, stopped the mouths of the lions in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, girt with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparia:*
Having acquired thee as a vigilant guardian of our souls, we are enriched, for thou dost ever calm demonic phantoms and the wild waves of the flesh and the storm of thoughts, O much-suffering martyr, of those who cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!
