With the streams of thy sacred blood thou didst dye for thyself a purple robe that can in nowise suffer aging; and brightly adorned, thou dwellest in the heavens, crying aloud, O blessed one: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

As a pure sheep, an immaculate sacrifice, and an offering burnt with the coals of sacred suffering, O martyr, thou didst offer thyself unto Christ, the Founder of thy contest,[^1178] O wise one, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*
The shadows of the Law and the pure proclamations of the prophets prefigured thee, O pure one, that wast ineffably to become the Mother of our God, O full of God's grace and pure; unto Whom we all sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
A cornerstone was cut out without hands from thee, the unhewn mountain, O Virgin: Christ, Who joined together the divided natures a cornerstone was cut out: Christ, Who joined together the divided natures; therefore rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Theotokos.

*Troparia:*
From the radiant passion-bearer the light-manifest memory shone forth, enlightening by the Divine Spirit the hearts of all the faithful who joyfully keep festival and call him blessed in faith.

Being joined with seven decads and three hundreds of unconquerable martyrs,[^1179] with whom thy body lies, O martyr of Christ, with them pray thou that we may be saved.

Having passed through the painful course filled with diverse torments, and having brightly conquered with Christ Who conquered the world, ye crown-bearing martyrs dwell in the heavens.

Thou wast taken from the earth and didst receive the honors of thy struggles, and now thou pourest forth rivers of wonders unto us who honor thee and piously celebrate thy memory, O Paramon.

*Theotokion:*
Enlighten the pupils of my soul, darkened by the ignorance of corruptive sin, O most pure Theotokos and Lady;[^1180] for thou art the help of the faithful and enlightenment, O pure one.

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Же́ны ᲂу҆слы́шите):*
Let us piously hymn the unconquerable multitude of the army, the divine, unconquerable assembly of martyrs, having as commander the marvelous Paramon, who rebuked the tormentor, who with all the martyrs received the crown of glory.

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, palace of God! Rejoice, overshadowed mountain! Rejoice, unburnt bush! Rejoice, throne of glory! Rejoice, divine table! Rejoice, all-golden urn! Rejoice, all-radiant lampstand! Rejoice, light cloud, O Virgin-Mother Mary!

*On the same month, on the 30th day. Of the holy and all-praised Apostle Andrew the First-Called.*

*After the Introductory Psalm, we sing: "Blessed is the man", the 1st Kathisma antiphons. At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera to 8:*

*Tone 4, Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*
Shaped beforehand by the Forerunner's light, when He that illumines the flesh of the Father's glory appeared, desiring in His loving-kindness to save the human race, then first didst thou run unto Him, O glorious one, being illumined in thy mind by the most perfect ray of His Divinity; whence thou becamest also a herald and apostle of Christ our God; Whom beseech thou to save and enlighten our souls. *(Thrice)*

Instructed by the Forerunner's voice, when the all-holy Word became incarnate, granting us life, and proclaimed good tidings of salvation unto those on earth, then didst thou follow Him, O all-wise one, and didst dedicate thine uttermost and all-holy self as firstfruits unto Him; and having recognized Him, thou didst proclaim our God unto thy kinsman;[^1181] Whom beseech thou to save and enlighten our souls. *(Thrice)*

Having been a disciple of him that sprouted from the barren woman, when the virginal childbirth shone forth, the Teacher of piety and chastity, displaying purity, then didst thou become a most fervent lover of virtue, O blessed Andrew, laying up ascents in thy heart,[^1182] and wast lifted up from glory unto the ineffable glory of Christ our God; Whom beseech thou to save and enlighten our souls. *(Twice)*

*Glory, Tone 4. By Anatolius:*
Having abandoned the fisherman's netting, O apostle, thou dost catch men with the rod of preaching,[^1183] casting down the attraction of piety as a hook, and drawing up all the nations from the depth of deception, O Apostle Andrew, being of the same blood as the supreme one,[^1184] and together with him a loud-voiced herald of the universe; cease not to pray for us who ever praise thy venerable memory in faith and love, O all-praised one!

*Both now, of the Forefeast, Tone 4:*
Dance, O Isaiah! Receive the Word of God; prophesy unto the Maiden Mary that the bush burns with fire and is not consumed by the radiance of the Godhead! Adorn thyself well, O Bethlehem; open thy gates, O Eden; and go forth, ye Magi, to see the Salvation wrapped in swaddling clothes in a manger, Whom the star revealed above the cave: the Lord and Giver of life, Who saves our race!

*Entrance. Prokimenon of the day.*
*And the Readings, 3.*

*The Reading from the Catholic Epistle of Peter.[^1185]*
Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the elect strangers of the dispersion of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in the sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace unto you and peace be multiplied. Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Who according to His abundant mercy has begotten us again unto a living hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, unto an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fades not away, reserved in heaven for you, who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, ye have been grieved in diverse temptations, that the trial of your faith, being much more precious than gold that perishes, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honor and glory at the revelation of Jesus Christ; Whom having not seen, ye love; in Whom, though now ye see Him not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and glorified, receiving the end of your faith, the salvation of your souls. Concerning which salvation the prophets have enquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that should come unto you, searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ Who was in them did signify, when He testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow; unto whom it was revealed, that not unto themselves, but unto us they did minister these things, which have now been reported unto you by those who have preached the gospel unto you with the Holy Spirit sent down from heaven; into which things the angels desire to look. Therefore, beloved, having girded up the loins of your mind, being sober, hope perfectly for the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ; as children of obedience, not fashioning yourselves according to the former lusts of your ignorance; but as He Who called you is holy, be ye also holy in all your manner of life; because it is written: Be ye holy, for I am holy.[^1186] And if ye call on the Father, Who without respect of persons judges according to each man's work, pass the time of your dwelling here in fear, knowing that not with corruptible things, as silver or gold to be redeemed from your vain manner of life handed down from your fathers, but with the precious Blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot. He indeed was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for your sake, who through Him believe in God, Who raised Him up from the dead and gave Him glory, that your faith and hope might be in God. Having purified your souls in obedience to the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned brotherly love, love one another fervently from a pure heart, having been born again, not of corruptible seed but of incorruptible, through the word of God which lives and abides unto ages. For all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of the grass. The grass withers, and its flower falls away, but the word of the Lord abides unto ages. And this is the word which was preached as good tidings unto you. Laying aside therefore all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisy, and envy, and all evil speaking, as newborn babes, desire the rational and unadulterated milk, that by it you may grow unto salvation, since you have tasted that the Lord is good. Coming unto Him, a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen by God and precious, you also, as living stones, are built up into a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. For it is contained in the Scripture: "Behold, I lay in Zion a chief cornerstone, elect, precious, and he who believes on Him shall not be put to shame."[^1187]

*Reading from the Catholic Epistle of Peter (Pericope 58):*[^1188]
Beloved, Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example, that we should follow His steps: Who committed no sin, nor was guile found in His mouth; Who, when He was reviled, reviled not again; when He suffered, He threatened not, but committed Himself to Him Who judges righteously; Who Himself bore our sins in His own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by Whose stripes you were healed. For you were as sheep going astray, having no shepherd, but you have now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls. Likewise, you wives, be in subjection to your own husbands, that even if some do not obey the word, they without a word may be won by the manner of life of their wives, beholding your chaste manner of life in fear. Whose adorning, let it not be that outward adorning of braiding the hair, and of wearing gold, or of putting on of apparel; but let it be the hidden man of the heart, in the incorruption of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who hoped in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: even as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord; whose daughters you are, doing good, and not being afraid with any fear. Likewise, you husbands, dwell with your wives together according to knowledge, giving honor unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life, that your prayers be not hindered. Finally, be all of one mind, having compassion, loving as brethren, pitiful, tender-hearted, lovers of wisdom, humble-minded: not rendering evil for evil, or reviling for reviling: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that you are called unto this, that you should inherit a blessing.

*Reading from the Catholic Epistle of Peter (Pericope 61):*[^1189]
Beloved, forasmuch as Christ suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind: for He Who suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin; that he no longer should live the rest of his time in the flesh to the lusts of men, but to the will of God. For the time past of life may suffice you to have wrought the will of the Gentiles, when you walked in uncleanness, lusts, bestiality, evil thoughts, drunkenness, revelries, banquetings, and abominable idolatries. Wherein they think it strange that you run not together with them into the same excess of riot, speaking evil of you: who shall give account to Him Who is ready to judge the living and the dead. For for this cause was the Gospel preached also unto the dead, that they might be judged according to men in the flesh, but live according to God in the spirit. But the end of all things is at hand: be therefore sober-minded, and watch unto prayer. And above all things have fervent love among yourselves: for love covers a multitude of sins. Be hospitable one to another without murmuring. As each has received a gift, minister the same among yourselves, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God. If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God; if any man minister, let him do it as of the strength which God supplies: that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to Whom be glory and dominion unto ages of ages. Amen.

*At the Litiya, the Sticheron of the Temple, and of the Apostle, Tone 1. The Work of Andrew of Jerusalem:*
The first-called disciple and imitator of Thy Passion, conforming himself unto Thee, O Lord, Andrew the Apostle, who once drew up with the hook of Thy Cross those who were deceived in the deep of ignorance, brought them unto Thee. Therefore we, the faithful, having been saved, cry unto Thee: By his prayers, O All-Good One, pacify our life, and save our souls.

Let us, the faithful, hymn the kinsman of Peter, Andrew the disciple of Christ; for he who once explored the sea with nets, caught fish, but now with the rod of the Cross catches the whole world, and turns the nations from deception unto baptism; and standing before Christ, he asks peace for the world, and great mercy for our souls.

Having received within his heart the noetic Fire that enlightens the thoughts and consumes sins, the Apostle and disciple of Christ shines forth with mystical rays of teachings in the unillumined hearts of the Gentiles, and burns up anew the brushwood of the fables of the impious; for such is the operation of the Fire of the Spirit. O strange and fearful wonder! A clay tongue, a clay nature, a body of dust, has received noetic and immaterial knowledge! But O initiate of things unutterable, and beholder of heavenly things, pray that our souls may be illumined.

*Tone 8. The Work of Maurus:*[^1190]
Having seen the desired God walking in the flesh upon the earth, O first-called beholder of God, thou didst cry rejoicing unto thy kinsman: "We have found Him Whom we desired, O Simon!" And unto the Savior thou didst cry after the manner of David: "As the deer pants after the fountains of waters, so pants my soul unto Thee, O Christ God!" Therefore, adding desire unto desire, thou didst pass over by the Cross unto Him Whom thou didst desire, having become a true disciple and a wise imitator of His Sufferings by the cross. Therefore, having become also a partaker of His glory, pray fervently for our souls.

*Glory, Tone 8. By Andrew of Jerusalem, or Anatolius:*[^1191]
Let us praise Andrew, the preacher of the faith and minister of the Word; for he catches men from the deep, holding the Cross in his hands instead of a fishing rod, and letting down power like a cord, he draws up souls from the enemy's deception, and brings an acceptable gift unto God continually. Let us, the faithful, praise him in the choir of Christ's disciples, that he may pray with them, that He may be merciful unto us in the Day of Judgment.

*Both now, Theotokion:*

O Sovereign Lady, accept the prayer of thy servants, and deliver us from every necessity and sorrow.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 5. Podoben: "Rejoice:" (Радуйся:)*
Rejoice, rational heaven, ever declaring the glory of God! Having warmly followed Christ first when He called, and abiding with Him without departing, enlightened by Him thou didst behold the second Light, and those abiding in darkness thou didst enlighten with thy lightnings, imitating His goodness. Therefore we celebrate thy most holy solemnity, and joyfully kiss the shrine of thy relics, from which thou pourest forth salvation and great mercy unto those who ask.

*Verse: Their sound has gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.* [Ps. 18:4]
First discoverer of the virtues of Him Who for mercy's sake was clothed in our nature, O God-wise Andrew! Being joined unto Him with burning love, thou didst cry unto thy kinsman: "He Whom the Prophets proclaimed in the Spirit we have found! Come unto His beauty, that we may be drawn both in soul and in thought, so that, guided by His brightness, we may drive away the night of deception and the darkness of ignorance, blessing Christ Who grants great mercy unto the world!"

*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands.* [Ps. 18:1]
Nations that knew not God, as from the deep of ignorance, thou didst catch with the net of thy words; and clearly troubling the salty seas, thou didst appear as a most valiant horse of Him Who rules the sea, O ever-praised one; and thou didst dry up the foulness of godlessness, putting in thy wisdom as precious salt, at which they marveled, O glorious Apostle, who had joined themselves shamelessly to foolish wisdom, not knowing Christ Who grants great mercy unto the world.

*Glory, Tone 3. By Germanus:*[^1192]
Let us honor in songs Andrew the Apostle, the kinsman of Peter and disciple of Christ, the catcher of fish and fisher of men; for having instructed all in the dogmas by the teaching of Jesus, even as food for fish he surrendered his flesh unto the lawless, and caught them. By his prayers, O Christ, grant peace and great mercy unto Thy people.

*Both now, the same Tone:*
Tell us, O Joseph: How is it that the Virgin whom thou didst receive from the Holy of Holies, thou bringest with child unto Bethlehem?

"...lehem?" "Having searched the Prophets," says he, "and having received an answer from an Angel, I am persuaded that Mary shall bear God ineffably, unto Whom Magi shall come from the East to worship, ministering with precious gifts. O Thou Who wast incarnate for our sake, Lord, glory to Thee!"

*Troparion, Tone 4:*[^1193]
As the first-called of the Apostles, and true brother of the Primate, pray to the Master of all, O Andrew, that He grant peace to the universe, and great mercy to our souls.

*Glory, and now, Resurrection Theotokion.*
*At Matins, after the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1. Podoben: "Thy tomb:" (Гробъ твой:)*
As a divine disciple and first-called of all the disciples of Christ, we praise thee with love, O Andrew the Apostle, and faithfully cry unto thee: Deliver thy flock, which was entrusted unto thee by God, from all sorrow, and necessities, and stumbling blocks, and every affliction.

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
Having now stretched forth thy precious, holy hands in supplication, grant us help from the Holy Place, and grant that we may pass through life without harm, who glorify thy most holy Offspring, and describe thee, O Virgin Lady, as our hope and boast.

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3. Podoben: "Of divine faith:" (Божественныя вѣры:)*
Christ found thee first-called, an excellent initiate of mysteries, O blessed Andrew, and one who zealously exalted His commandments to the universe; like a winged creature, thou didst enlighten the gatherings of the nations. Entreat Him as God to grant us great mercy. *(Twice)*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
Thou wast the divine tabernacle of the Word, O only most pure Mother Virgin, who in purity didst surpass the Angels. Cleanse me, who above all have become dust, defiled by carnal transgressions, with the divine waters of thy prayers, O pure one, granting great mercy.

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5. Podoben: "The Word unoriginate:" (Собезначалное слово:)*
Let us all praise the Apostle as an eyewitness of the Word, and a divine preacher, and a spiritual catcher of the nations, as is truly meet: for Andrew the God-proclaimer has led us into the knowledge of Christ, being truly our great protector; and now he prays unceasingly that He may save our souls. *(Twice)*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*

As thou art a protection unto those who have unfailing hope in thee, O most pure Virgin, free us from diverse perils, and circumstances, and bitter calamities, praying unto thy Son with His Apostles, and save all who hymn thee.

*The Graduals, 1st Antiphon of Tone 4.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
*Their sound has gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.*
*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God.*
*Let every breath praise the Lord.*
*Gospel according to Matthew (Pericope 9).* [Matt. 4:18-23][^1194]
*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 8:*
Let us praise Andrew, the preacher of the faith and minister of the Word; for he catches men from the deep, holding the Cross in his hands instead of a fishing rod, and letting down power like a cord, he draws up souls from the enemy's deception, and brings an acceptable gift unto God continually. Let us, the faithful, praise him in the choir of Christ's disciples, that he may pray with them, that He may be merciful unto us in the Day of Judgment.

*Canon of the Theotokos with the Heirmos to 6, Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^1195]
Let us all sing a song of victory unto God, Who has wrought marvelous wonders with a high arm, and saved Israel, for He is glorified!

*Troparia:*
As the only one who in time gavest birth to the timeless Son incarnate, O all-holy, most pure one, heal all the temporal passions of my all-passionate soul.

The wounds of my soul, the hardening of my heart, the darkening of my thought, and the injury of my mind, wipe away, O most pure one, as thou art compassionate, through thy prayers.

O thou who gavest birth to the Light, my Redeemer, deliver me from the darkness and eternal torments there, O most pure one, that being saved, I may hymn thy greatness.

Drive away with thy light the darkenings of my mind, O all-praised one, who gavest birth to the Light that is beyond understanding, and grant me good things, that I may see the Light that has shone forth upon us from thee.

*And two Canons of the Apostle, to 8. The First Canon, the Work of John the Monk, Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^1196]
Thy victorious right hand has been glorified in power in a manner befitting God; for it, O Immortal One, as all-powerful, shattered the adversaries, forging a new way through the deep for the Israelites.

*Troparion:*
Cleanse my soul, troubled with thoughts and words, O Andrew, universal preacher of Christ's riches, through divine grace, that I may purely pour forth a worthy hymn unto thee.

The honorable Forerunner of Christ, who sprang from a barren womb, the supreme among his disciples, joyfully brought Andrew unto Christ, Who was born of the Virgin and is exceedingly glorified.

With desire and unswerving love, having begun the steps of virtue, and ever meditating upon ascending, thou didst attain from weak strength unto supreme power, O Andrew.

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, fountain of grace! Rejoice, ladder and heavenly gate! Rejoice, candlestick and golden jar, and unhewn mountain, who didst bear Christ the Giver of life unto the world!

*The Second Canon of the Apostle, the same Tone. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^1197]
He Who as God guided Israel with a pillar of fire and of cloud, divided the sea and covered the chariots of Pharaoh with the deep. Let us sing a song of victory, for He alone is glorified!

*Troparia:*
Taking them out from the deep of deception with the rod of the Gospel, O much-hymned Andrew, thou didst catch men, as Christ promised Who taught thee to catch men like fish.

The pillar of faith, the seat of the true dogmas of Christ, God-inspired Andrew, calls all the ends of the earth today to establish an annual feast: let us all, the faithful, therefore gather together.

Exploring the sea monster with nets, a fisher by art, with the net of the Spirit thou catchest nations, tribes, and peoples clearly through the Spirit, and the former deep thou plainly uncoverest unto us, O wonder-worker!

O citizen of the heavenly city, eyewitness and orator of the ineffable knowledge of Christ, who received from on high the Holy Spirit Who spoke, Who sits among the nations, dividing gifts with fire: pray that we may be saved!

*Glory, Triadicon:*
Unto the Trinity that is equally without beginning, the supersubstantial Unity, I bow down with faith, not dividing the Godhead; for It is uniform, simple, indivisible; and I unite It in essence, yet faithfully divide It in Persons.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
God becomes an infant from the Virgin, and renews those who were corrupted from Adam; and He destroys the middle wall of partition and the fence of enmity by His flesh; He blesses the curse of the foremother, having come forth from a most pure Mother.

*Katavasia: Christ is born Christ is born...*

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^1198]
Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God, Who didst establish the second heaven above the waters, and didst found the earth upon the waters, O All-Powerful One!

*Troparia of the Theotokos:*
Drive away all the barrenness of my barren mind, and show my soul fruitful in virtues, O all-holy Theotokos, helper of the faithful.

Deliver me, O all-immaculate one, from all condemnation, and from the many stumbling blocks of the serpent, from the eternal fire and darkness, O thou who didst bear for us the unwaning Light.

By the fearful judgment seat, O pure one, and by that unquenchable fire, and by the grievous answer, I am completely condemned: hasten to save me before the end, O good one, thy servant.

Blessed is the Fruit of thy womb, O all-praised Virgin; for those who were corrupted by the fruit of the tree, through His Cross He has made partakers of incorruption, by divine grace.

*Another. Heirmos:*[^1199]
Thou Who alone knowest the weakness of human nature, and didst mercifully take form therein, gird me from on high with power to cry unto Thee, O Holy One: The animate temple of Thine ineffable glory, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparia of Canon 1:*
Thou didst run with thirst, uncalled, O Andrew, but of thine own will unto the Fountain of life, even as a deer, and having found Him, thou didst proclaim Him unto all; and having drunk, thou didst water with the waters of incorruption the ends of the earth that were wasting away with thirst.

Having recognized the laws of nature, O Andrew worthy of wonder, thou didst take thy kinsman as partner, crying: "We have found Him Whom we desired!" And unto Him Who made a path for the birth of the flesh, thou didst recount spiritual understanding.

With the net of the word from the deep of deception thou didst catch rational fish, O Apostle, and didst bring a clean food unto the table of Christ, enlightened by grace, of Him Who appeared in the likeness of the flesh.

*Theotokion:*
Having conceived God in thy womb by the All-Holy Spirit, O Virgin, thou didst remain unburnt; for the burning bush clearly prefigured thee unto the lawgiver Moses, unconsumed, having received the unendurable Fire.

*Another [Canon 2]. Heirmos:*
Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God, Who didst establish the second heaven above the waters, and didst found the earth upon the waters, O All-Powerful One!

At the word of Him Who called: "Come after Me," Cephas along with Andrew immediately followed Christ, leaving their father, boat, and nets, as foresighted ones of faith.

Having transformed idol temples into temples of God, O all-honored one, Thou didst sanctify in them the sons of baptism, whom grace renewed with water and the Spirit.

Mystically thou didst set forth to the world the pearl of great price, hidden in the field of thy heart, O Apostle, which the nations, having found it, treasured up through faith.

Taking the Gospel into thy hands as a treasure, O much-hymned one, thou didst enrich the whole earth with divine preaching; therefore it honors also thy memory with thy sufferings.

*Glory, Triadicon:*
In the Trinity let us all sing in orthodox fashion of the one Power: the unoriginate, uncreated God, consubstantial, enthroned together, in three Hypostases, thrice-radiant, singing unto It.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Every mother, having given birth to a child, can no longer remain a virgin; but thou, O Virgin, having given birth to Christ, didst remain a mother, suckling our Life, and remaining pure.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8. Podoben: "Of wisdom:" (Премудрости:)*
As the first-called of all the disciples, and eyewitness and minister of the Word, O Andrew the Apostle, we honor thee as is meet; for with unwavering faith thou didst warmly follow the Lamb Who takes away the sins of the world. Therefore thou didst also show thyself a partaker of His Sufferings, Who for our sake willingly endured death in the flesh. Therefore we cry unto thee: Pray to Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate with love thy holy memory.

*Glory, another Sessional Hymn, the same Tone and Podoben:*
Having overthrown the savage fury of idols, and desired the Sufferings of the Savior, O blessed Andrew, thou didst show thyself an Apostle, pouring forth miracles from heaven upon all, and thou wast a teacher of the nations, O all-blessed one. Therefore, worthily honoring thy memory, in hymns we glorify and faithfully magnify thee, O Apostle of the Lord. Pray to Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate with love thy holy memory.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, fiery throne of God! Rejoice, maidenly royal seat, couch richly adorned and spread, gold and purple chamber, scarlet-dyed mantle, adorned temple, lightning-bearing chariot, brightly-shining lamp! Rejoice, O Theotokos, twelve-walled city, golden-forged gate, radiant bridal chamber, brightly gilded table, tabernacle adorned by God! Rejoice, glorious Bride dropping sunlight! Rejoice, only beauty of my soul!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^1200]
Foreseeing in spirit the incarnation of the Word, O Prophet Habakkuk, thou didst proclaim, crying: "When the years draw near, Thou shalt be known; when the time is come, Thou shalt be shown!" Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparia of the Theotokos:*
O all-holy Virgin, undefiled tabernacle, cleanse me who am defiled by transgressions, now with the purest sprinklings of thy compassions, and grant me a helping hand, that I may cry: Glory to thee, O pure one, glorified by God!

Thou didst appear as a consecrated temple of God, of God Who dwelt in thee beyond understanding, O Virgin: entreat Him to cleanse us from sinful defilement, that we may be known as a temple and dwelling-place of the Spirit.

Have mercy on me, O Theotokos, who alone gavest birth to the Fountain of mercy, and resolve the grievous disease of my soul and the perplexity of my heart, granting divine stream of tears and compunction before the end, through thy prayers.

Having recognized thee as a mountain overshadowed, O pure one, the Prophet described thee beforehand by the Divine Spirit; cleanse by thy mediation, O Virgin, who art the only restoration of men, those who are consumed by the flame of many sins.

*Another. Heirmos:*[^1201]
Perceiving with prophetic eyes the mountain overshadowed by the grace of God, Habakkuk proclaimed that the Holy One of Israel should come forth from thee, unto our salvation and renewal.

*Troparia of Canon 1:*
The divine power of the all-effecting and radiant Spirit, which destroys what is worse, having dwelt in thee in a manner befitting God, O Andrew, in the form of a fiery tongue, showed thee forth as a preacher of ineffable things.

Taking not carnal weapons for vengeance, nor for the casting down of strong enemy strongholds, O all-honored Andrew, but having armed thyself with Christ, having captured the nations, thou didst bring them into obedience.

The supernatural God, Who shared in what is ours, showed thee, O Andrew, as a mountain dropping noetic gladness, which destroys the bitter mountains of demonic arrogance by the power of the Spirit.

*Troparion:*
Unto those who celebrate thy memory with love in hymns, from the bountiful gift of thy Teacher Christ, O all-rich Andrew, cease not to fill them with the waters of spiritual gladness by thy prayers.

*Theotokion:*
We hymn thy great and awesome mystery; for having hidden Himself from the transcendent angelic ranks, He Who is ever-existent descended upon thee as dew upon the fleece, O all-hymned one, unto our salvation and renewal.

*Another canon. Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^1202]
Foreseeing in the Spirit the incarnation of the Word, O Prophet Habakkuk, thou didst proclaim, crying out: When the years draw nigh, Thou shalt be known; when the time is come, Thou shalt be shown. Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparia:*
Casting away thy nets and taking up the Cross, thou didst follow in the way Christ Who called thee; and spreading the net of the Spirit, instead of fish thou catchest men: glory to Him Who gave the Spirit unto thee!

Having received the flame of the Spirit upon thy tongue, O apostle, thou wast a God-bearing man, ascending to the heavenly beauties, and discerning the noetic excellences therein, and revealing these unto us.

Thou didst water the thirsty desert, O wise one, with thy divine words, and didst show it to be fruitful, bearing the children of the Church, the seed of preaching: glory to Him Who gave the Spirit unto thee!

Foreknowing Thine ineffable[^1203] goodness, O Jesus, Andrew brightly called his kinsman: O Peter, of one blood with me, we have found the Messiah, Who was proclaimed in the Law and the Prophets! Come, let us cleave unto the true Life!

*Glory, Triadicon:*
Let us the faithful hymn the Trinity in Unity, in one Godhead: the Father, and the Son, and the divine Spirit; one Essence and Nature, undivided, inseparable, impartible; for God is one in three Persons.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Having ineffably conceived in thy womb One of the Trinity, thou didst bear Him incorruptibly as Son; and the Trinity indeed received no addition whatsoever, and thou didst remain pure as thou wast before childbirth, intact, O Mother of God.

*Ode 5, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^1204]
Give us Thy peace, O Son of God; for we know no other God besides Thee; we call upon Thy Name, for Thou art the God of the living and of the dead.

*Troparion:*
Open the pupils of my heart, O pure one, that I may clearly behold the divine radiance and thine ineffable glory, that I may obtain mercy and eternal glory.

*Troparia:*
In two wills, O all-immaculate one, thou didst bear One of the pure Trinity, Who bears a single hypostasis: Whom do thou fervently beseech that we all may be saved.

O all-pure one,[^1205] as having given birth to the Savior and God, pray that from every affliction, and sickness, and mistreatment, thy unprofitable servant may be preserved saved.

Beseech Him Whom thou hast borne, O Virgin, beyond[^1206] comprehension, to save those who cry unto thee in faith: Rejoice, O all-immaculate Virgin; rejoice, O blessed one, protection of the world!

*Another canon. Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^1207]
O Christ, Who didst illumine with the radiance of Thy coming, and didst enlighten the ends of the world by Thy Cross: enlighten with the light of the knowledge of God the hearts of those who orthodoxly hymn Thee.

*Troparia:*
Thou hast received Him Whom thou didst desire, O Apostle Andrew, dwelling with Him in the incorruptible mansions, worthily reaping the sheaves of thy labors; therefore with hymns we glorify thee.

Thou didst love the Good, and didst swiftly run in His wake, guided by His steps unto life; and truly[^1208] imitating His passions unto death, O most honorable Andrew.

Having bent thee like a mighty arrow, O blessed one, the Lord released thee into all the world, wounding the demons and healing men who were wounded by impiety.

*Theotokion:*
The heavenly powers make merry, beholding thee; and the assemblies of men rejoice with them; for by thy childbirth they were united, O Virgin Theotokos, worthily glorifying thee.

*Another canon. Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^1209]
Dawn upon our mind, O God, with the light of Thy commandments, and by the brightness of Thy grace; grant unto us Thy mercies, O Good One, for Thy commands are light and peace.

*Troparia:*
Having desired[^1210] the Cross, O disciple of Christ, by thy cross thou didst receive the incorruptible kingdom, unto which thou didst draw all men by the Cross, O initiate of divine mysteries, granting an inheritance unto His theologians.

Thou didst bend down toward Christ, Who is truly Life, and having sought Him, thou wast the first to find Him; and having found Him, thou didst receive Him mystically; and receiving Him in the Giver Himself, thou becamest a treasury of incorruptible life.

The sounds[^1211] of thy divine thunderings poured forth into the world, and went through from the ends to the ends of the earth; for they circled about like a wheel, and thy lightnings were revealed, as David says unto the universe.

*Troparion:*
Remember us, O disciple of Christ, who celebrate thy memory and honor thy relics; pray ever fervently for the flock of which from the beginning thou hast been guardian and salvation.

*Glory, Triadicon:*
The Father, and the Son, and the Spirit, God, the undivided Trinity, the three-hypostatic Kingdom, let us the faithful glorify with one accord in unceasing theologies, faithfully hymning It.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Thou didst give birth to the Light, not knowing how, O all-radiant candlestick bearing the Light of the Sun; and thou wast the new receptacle of the immaterial Light, pouring forth upon all the earth the rays of the knowledge of God.

*Ode 6, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^1212]
Imitating the Prophet Jonah, I cry out: Deliver my life from corruption, O Good One, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: Glory to Thee!

*Troparia:*
Defiled as I am with many sins, I pray unto thee who art good and an undefiled tabernacle: wash me from every defilement by thy intercession.

Be a pilot unto me, O pure one, who am ever tossed upon the deep of evils by the temptations of life, and save me, guiding me unto the haven of salvation.

The tempest of thoughts, and the assault of passions, and the abyss of sins burden my wretched soul; help me, O holy Lady!

Christ hath ever done great things for Thee; Whom do thou ever beseech to magnify His rich mercies upon me, O thou who art full of divine grace.

*Another canon. Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^1213]
The uttermost abyss hath surrounded us, there is none to deliver; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter; save Thy people, O our God, for Thou art the strength of the weak and the restoration.

*Troparia:*
Sailing across the sea of life in the vessel of the body, thou didst find Christ, Who directs all things, as a pilot, O all-blessed one; and rejoicing, thou didst put in unto Him, O most honorable Andrew.

Spirits are driven away by a word, diseases flee, and the multitude of bodily passions are driven far away from the suffering by the grace given thee by God, O Andrew.

Like a tranquil wave, moved by a gentle spirit, O blessed one, thou didst dry up the evil seas of polytheism with divine streams, and didst pour forth rivers of the knowledge of God for all.

*Theotokion:*
[The forebears rejoice in thee, O all-pure Virgin...] The forebears of our race rejoice in thee, O all-pure Virgin, having through thee regained Eden, which by transgression they lost; for thou art pure both before childbirth and after childbirth.

*Another canon. Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^1214]
Imitating the Prophet Jonah, I cry out: Deliver my life from corruption, O Good One, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: Glory to Thee!

*Troparia:*
He Who leads forth from affliction summons us to celebrate, offering us his solemnity, the excellences of his struggles.

By trade a fisherman, but by faith a disciple, as one searching the depth of the hearts of the faithful, he casts down the hook of the word and catches us.

Carrying about in thy heart the fire of the love of Christ, O disciple, thou didst cry aloud with thy tongue: The flame of deception hath been extinguished, now that Christ hath truly appeared!

Having seasoned your mind with the salt of Christ, your foods became sweet to you, the clear dogmas and incorruptible sweetness.

*Glory, Triadicon:*
Unto the Father, and the Son, and the upright Spirit let us the faithful bow down, unto the three-hypostatic Nature, undivided, crying aloud: Glory to God in Trinity!

*Both now, Theotokion:*
By the good pleasure of the Father the Son was incarnate by the Divine Spirit in thy womb, O pure one, and He saved the former image, O pure Mother of God.

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "In prayers" (Въ молитвахъ):*[^1215]
Let us praise the namesake of courage, the proclaimer of God and follower of the Church supreme, the kinsman of Peter; for as once unto him, so now unto us he hath called aloud: Come, we have found the Desired One!

*Ikos:*
Of old indeed David forbids[^1216] the sinner, such as me, to recount the blessings and ordinances of God; yet he teaches faith again, and with abundant tears proclaims: For today if ye shall hear His voice, harden not your hearts, as once Israel provoked Him. And he adds the rest in the Psalm: Sing unto the Lord, all the earth! Come, we have found the Desired One!

*Ode 7, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^1217]
The fire touched not nor distressed Thy children in the furnace, O Savior; then the three, as with one mouth, hymned and blessed, saying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*
Purify my soul, O pure one, which is defiled with passions, being ever thy servant; and quickly destroy the cruel captivity of my mind, the hardening of my heart, and the assaults of demons.

Slain by carnal passions, O all-immaculate one, quicken my mind, and strengthen me to accomplish what is pleasing unto God, that I may magnify thee and ever glorify thy lovingkindness.

Slain as I am by carnal passions, O pure Lady, cleanse the cruel defilement of my humble soul, O Virgin, deliver me from the ensnarement of invisible foes, and save me.

Unto thee, O all-honorable, immaculate, and pure one, we thy servants ever fall down day and night, praying with compunction of heart that we may find deliverance from sins by thy prayers.

*Another canon. Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^1218]
We the faithful contemplate thee as a noetic furnace, O Theotokos; for as the Supremely Exalted One saved the three children, so He wholly renewed the world in thy womb: the praised and supremely glorified God of the fathers.

*Troparia:*
Truly and clearly hath Thy promise been fulfilled, O Christ; for rebuking the storms by a word, Thy most divine disciple turned them into a gentle calm, singing: Praised and supremely glorified is the God of the fathers!

Commanded to ascend the noetic mountain of Zion, O apostle, and receiving the cup of salvation, thou didst joyfully take it up, passing through death unto divine life, singing to the praised and supremely glorified God of the fathers.

The divine Water of life showed thee to be a spiritual river, drying up the torrents of the rivers of deception by thy blessed preaching, and giving drink unto those who cry: Praised and supremely glorified art Thou, O God of the fathers!

Being an earth-born man, O apostle, thou dost work supernatural wonders; for united in love, thou didst follow Christ Who loved thee, hymning: Praised and supremely glorified is God!

*Theotokion:*
Jacob prophetically understood thee as a ladder, O Theotokos; for through thee the Most High appeared unto men on earth and lived as He was well pleased: praised and supremely glorified is the God of the fathers!

*Another canon. Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^1219]
The fire touched not nor distressed Thy children in the furnace, O Savior; then the three, as with one mouth, hymned and blessed, saying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*
The fire of the Holy[^1220] Spirit descending from on high, O Apostle of Christ, commanded thee to speak His mighty works in new tongues wherein thou hadst never spoken, unto the ends of the world.

The preaching which ye trumpeted forth to the earth, O initiates of Christ and beholders of heavenly things, surpasses every thought; for as the twelve alone ye enlightened the darkness of the earth.

Thy grace was made marvelous, O Master Christ, in Thy God-wise disciples; for being small and simple men, they ran throughout all the earth, from its ends even unto all its borders.

Who taught thee so to speak, O apostle? Who enlightened thy mind to behold clearly the ray of unapproachable glory, shining forth the light of truth in our hearts?

*Glory, Triadicon:*
Let us the faithful hymn the Trinity, glorifying the unoriginate Father, and the Son, and the upright Spirit; the one unique Essence, which let us triply hymn: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou unto the ages, Amen.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
As One of the Trinity we glorify Thee, O Christ; for having been incarnate of the Virgin without wedlock, Thou didst endure all things as a man, yet not departing from the Father's Nature, O Jesus, even though Thou wast united unto us.

*Ode 8, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^1221]
Him of Whom the angels and all the hosts are in dread as Creator and Lord, hymn, ye priests; glorify, ye children; bless, ye people, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
The Bodiless One is incarnate of thee in God-befitting manner; Whom do thou beseech, O all-pure one, to put to death the passions of my soul, and to quicken it, slain of old by most wicked sin.

Thou hast healed the crushing of dust-formed Adam, having given birth to the Savior and God, O all-pure one; beseech Him to heal the wounds of my soul, which is incurably diseased.

Raise me up who lie in the depth of evils, and conquer the enemies that now war against me; despise not my soul, wounded by unfitting pleasures, O pure one, but have compassion and save me!

Heal the passions of my heart, O all-pure one, who didst bear the Physician of all, and show me to be a partaker of the lot of the righteous, O Virgin, by imploring Christ.

*Another canon. Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^1222]
From the furnace the children of Israel, as in a crucible, through the beauty of piety shone more purely than gold, saying: Bless all ye works of the Lord, hymn the Lord, and supremely exalt Him hymn, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
A light-bearing and joy-creating beam of healings, O Apostle of Christ Andrew, thy divine memory shines upon us who cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Having received human nature, thou didst surpass its laws, and didst pass over unto the angelic tabernacle, O Apostle Andrew, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

The inspiration of the Divine Spirit from on high, which of old enlightened thee with fire, shows thee, O speaker of God, to be a fervent orator, crying aloud to thy Christ: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Radiant like lightning, thou didst go forth into the light of the Gentiles, driving away the darkness of ignorance, and enlightening the faithful who cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O throne of God's glory; rejoice, O wall of the faithful, through whom Christ shone forth as Light upon those who were in darkness, unto those who call thee blessed and cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Another canon. Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^1223]
Him Who preserved the burning bush unconsumed on Sinai, and delivered the children from the midst of the burning flame, hymn, bless, and supremely exalt God unto all ages!

*Troparia:*
By the trade of fishing thou didst catch fish from the sea, O all-wise one; but now by faith thou catchest men for Christ from the deceit of the enemy; for deceit was once a deep, engulfing the nations in the tempest of ignorance.

Painlessly thou didst sail across the noetic depth of life, O apostle, flying across by the sail of the Spirit, by the faith of Christ; therefore thou hast reached the haven of life, rejoicing unto all ages.

When the Noetic Sun voluntarily set upon the Tree, the lampstand who was not less than the Sun, seeking to be dissolved and to set like Christ, was hung upon the Tree of the Cross, Andrew the great luminary of the Church.

O disciple and beloved of Christ, numbered with His apostles: when the Judge shall sit upon His throne to judge with you, the Twelve, as the promise says: be ye then a wall of lovingkindness unto us!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

*Triadicon:*
The thrice-radiant Unity and the co-enthroned Trinity let us bless, not dividing Them, but uniting Them as consubstantial; for truly one is the Essence united in three Persons without confusion.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Having conceived One Who is of the Trinity, thou didst bear Him incarnate of thee, Who renews the laws of nature by thy childbirth, O pure one; cease not ever to beseech Him as God for us, O Theotokos.

*Ode 9, Tone 4. Heirmos:*[^1224]
The light-bearing cloud, wherein the Master of all descended as rain from heaven upon the fleece, and was incarnate for our sake, becoming man, the Unoriginate: all we magnify as the pure Mother of our God.

*Troparia:*
Being a lover of sin, I abide in carelessness, and I tremble before the impartial judgment-seat, whereon by thy holy prayers, O Bride of God, preserve me uncondemned, that I may ever bless thee as my protectress.

I tremble before the judgment-seat, O Virgin, and before the unforgetting eye of thy Son; having wrought shameful deeds on earth, therefore I cry unto thee: O all-compassionate Lady, help me, and deliver me from the constraint of that hour, and save me, O pure one!

How awesome is the day of examination, O Maiden! How terrible the answer! How cruel the shame! Who can endure it, O all-pure Lady? Have mercy on my passionate soul, and grant me remission before the end, O pure one!

Having given birth to the Divine Light, enlighten me who am darkened by all kinds of assaults of the evil one and by all wickedness, and who have provoked God to wrath, O all-immaculate one, guiding me unto good deeds, as being the cause of all good things.

*Another canon. Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^1225]
The unburnt bush showed forth an image of thy pure childbirth; and now we pray thee to extinguish the furnace of temptations that assault us, that we may unceasingly magnify thee, O Theotokos.

*Troparia:*
As a most excellent disciple, following even unto death thy Master Who was crucified upon the Cross of His own will, thou didst ascend rejoicing unto the height of the Cross, journeying on thy way to the heavens, O blessed apostle.

The door of Eden was opened unto thee, and the heavenly ladder was set before thee, and the heavenly mansions received thee; and rejoicing thou didst stand before Christ the Giver of life, O apostle: a most excellent intercessor for the world.

*Troparia:*
Thou wast glorified by sufferings like unto those of thy Teacher, O blessed and all-wise Andrew; for by the cross thou didst receive a divine end, and by participation becamest a god; therefore we pray thee: Pray ever for us!

Rejoice, O most excellent pair, who have now inherited citizenship in the heavens: ye oversee the determination of crowns, overcoming their force, and enlightening with the brightness of divine gifts.

*Theotokion:*
From the root of David the prophet and ancestor of God didst thou spring forth, O Virgin; but thou also didst truly glorify David, having given birth to the Lord of glory foretold by the prophets: Whom as we hymn, we worthily magnify.

*Another canon. Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^1226]
The light-bearing cloud, wherein the Master of all descended as rain from heaven upon the fleece, and was incarnate for our sake, becoming man, the Unoriginate: all we magnify as the pure Mother of our God.

*Troparia:*
O thou who didst spread out the net of mystical vision of God, and like fish didst catch therein by the beauties of heavenly understanding: pray, O holy one, unto the Holy Trinity to pour forth cleansing upon us also!

We the nations who were enlightened through thee give thanks, who through thee were brought from earth unto heaven; for having fallen away from the service of the enemy, we have become communicants of the holy angels and partakers of the glory of the Lord.

O eyewitnesses of ineffable things and ministers of the Word, mystagogues and beholders of unsearchable things: pray, O apostles, that we also may be co-heirs of Christ's kingdom and partakers of His Godhead!

Having received power from Christ to bind and to loose: loose all men from the bonds of their many transgressions, when Christ shall come and ye twelve shall sit upon as many thrones to judge all the tribes of Israel.

*Glory, Triadicon:*
The three-hypostatic Nature and undivided Glory, praised in one Godhead unceasingly in heaven and on earth, let us glorify the inseparable Trinity: devoutly worshipping the Father with the Son and the Spirit.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Unto those who flee beneath thy lovingkindness in faith and devoutly worship thy Son, O Virgin Mother of God: beseech Him as God and Lord of the world to deliver them from corruption and dangers and every assault.

*Exapostilarion, Podoben:*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Духомъ во святилищи):*[^1227]
Having found thee, O all-blessed one, the Word Who is supremely without beginning showed thee to be the First-called of all the apostles, O ever-memorable Andrew; and following in His steps, thou wast shown to be a guide of the wandering, leading them unto that heavenly,[^1228] divine pathway.

*Glory. Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены услышите):*[^1229]
Let us gloriously praise the Apostle Andrew, Peter's kinsman,[^1230] the first of the disciples, who was an eyewitness and minister of the Word; for he enlightened the nations, and having been crucified, he underwent the end as a disciple of the Master.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Beseech God, Whom thou didst bear, O all-immaculate Virgin, together with the First-called Andrew, on behalf of all who devoutly honor thee, that they may obtain the divine radiance of thy Son, and the station of the elect and the saints; for thou canst do whatsoever thou desirest.

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Небесныхъ чинѡвъ):*[^1231]
Rejoice now, be glad! * For in thee from the mother's valley blossomed * the most sweet-smelling lilies, Peter and Andrew, * making the preaching of the faith fragrant unto all the world * by the grace of Christ, * Whose passions they also shared.

Rejoice and leap for joy, O Andrew! * For thou hast manifestly received * in the radiance of the Word, the Sun of glory, Christ the Giver of life, * and holding fast to Him, thou didst preach Him in faith. * Beseech Him unceasingly for us * who hymn thee in faith!

The mystical teacher of the divine dispensation of Christ, * chosen among the first * to be a disciple of the Word, Andrew the beholder of God, crying aloud says, * having recognized his kinsman Peter: * We have found the Messiah, * Whom the Scripture and the prophets foretold!

The city of Patras gained thee as shepherd * and divine ruler of the city, * and as a deliverer from every danger and guardian, O wise Andrew, * for those who honor thee with thanksgiving; * but pray unceasingly for it, * that it may be preserved unharmed!

*Glory, Tone 8:*[^1232]
Let us praise Andrew, the preacher of the faith and minister of the Word; for he catches men from the deep, holding the Cross in his hands instead of a rod; and letting down power like a rope, he draws up souls from the deceit of the enemy, and ever offers unto God an acceptable gift.

Ever let us, the faithful, praise him in the choir of the disciples of Christ, that he may pray with them, that He may be merciful unto us in the Day of Judgment.

*Both now, the same Tone:*[^1233]
Receive, O Bethlehem, the metropolis of God; for the unwaning Light comes to be born in thee! Ye angels, marvel in heaven; ye men, glorify on earth; ye Magi from Persia, bring most glorious gifts; ye shepherds, playing upon pipes, sing the thrice-holy hymn: Let every breath praise the Creator of all!

*The Great Doxology, and Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the canons, Ode 3 and Ode 6.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 8: Their proclamation has gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the universe.*[^1234]
*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands.*
*Epistle to the Corinthians, pericope 134.*[^1235]
*Alleluia, Tone 1: The heavens shall confess Thy wonders, O Lord.*[^1236]
*Gospel from John, pericope 4.*[^1237]
*Communion Hymn: Their proclamation has gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the universe.*[^1238]

*(Woodcut tailpiece: Two cornucopias flanking an armillary sphere, open book, and compass, surmounted by floral garlands with birds, upon an acanthus pedestal)*

### Notes

[^6]: Saints Cosmas and Damian of Mesopotamia (Asia), sons of Saint Theodota, unmercenary physicians who healed both men and beasts without charge. In the Byzantine calendar, their commemoration on November 1 is distinguished from the Roman martyrs Cosmas and Damian (July 1) and the Arabian martyrs Cosmas and Damian (October 17).

[^992]: An allusion to the famous historical encounter between St. Amphilochius and Emperor Theodosius I: when the Emperor hesitated to prohibit Arian assemblies, Amphilochius greeted the Emperor with profound respect but completely ignored his young son Arcadius, whom Theodosius had crowned Augustus. When the Emperor became indignant at the insult to his son, Amphilochius said unto him: "Thou seest, O Emperor, that thou canst not bear an insult to thy son; how then thinkest thou that the Heavenly Father can bear those who blaspheme His Only-Begotten Son?" Theodosius immediately acknowledged the lesson and enacted laws suppressing Arian conventicles (cf. Theodoret, *Hist. Eccl.* V, 16; Sozomen, *Hist. Eccl.* VII, 6).
